articleTitle: Enhanced Tunneling Performance of Magnetic Helical Robots Utilizing Pecking Motion Generated by Alternating Rotating Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic helical robots (MHRs) actuated by an external magnetic field have been regarded as a possible application to treat occlusive vascular disease. We propose a pecking motion of an MHR to tunnel an occlusive vascular lesion effectively. Pecking motion is composed of a rotational driving motion and a linear impulsive motion of the MHR actuated by alternating rotating magnetic field (ARMF). The minimum magnetic flux density to synchronize the MHR to ARMF was mathematically determined from the equation of motion of the MHR and experimentally verified. Finally, enhanced tunneling performance of the MHR with the application of pecking motion was verified by in vitro tunneling experiments with a pseudo thrombus.

articleTitle: State tomography for magnetization dynamics and coherence anomaly in Y3Fe5O12
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Precessional motion of magnetization around the magnetic field decays to thermal equilibrium due to magnetization damping after cutting of the excitation force. After the decay, the phase coherence of the precession motion of magnetization was thought to be completely lost. Here we developed state tomography technique for time-resolved magnetization dynamics in a thin disk of yttrium iron garnet (YIG). We revealed that the temporal evolution of the coherence after cutting off the driving ac magnetic field exhibits different time constant from the one evaluated by linewidth measurement of ferromagnetic resonance, which is supported by theoretical modeling.

articleTitle: Spin-orbit torque induced magnetization switching in perpendicularly magnetized MnGa/Fe bilayer grown on GaAs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We investigated the effect of inserting an ultrathin Fe layer between MnGa and GaAs on the growth of MnGa and the spin-orbit torque (SOT) induced magnetization switching in the MnGa/Fe bilayer. MnGa was epitaxially grown on Fe at room temperature without annealing, and MnGa/Fe showed a perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA). A clear SOT switching was observed in the structure consisting of Ta heavy metal layer and 2-nm-thick MnGa/Fe bilayer at room temperature, which is a promising spin source for semiconductor spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Multi-mode Excitation Analysis and Design of a New Hybrid Excited Modular Stator Permanent Magnet Switched Reluctance Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, a new hybrid excited modular stator permanent magnet switched reluctance (HE-MSPMSR) machine is proposed. The design and multi-mode excitation characteristics of the HE-MSPMSR machine are studied. Firstly, the structure, basic working principle and design ideas of the motor are summarized, and the stator of HE-MSPMSR machine not only includes the stator core and three-phase armature winding, but also includes the excitation coil and permanent magnet as the excitation source. The motor can change the air gap magnetic field flux size by controlling the on-off of the excitation magnetic source. On this basis, the HE-MSPMSR machine can achieve the torque multiplication effect under the condition of magnetization. Compared with the traditional switched reluctance motor, the motor has the advantages of low speed and large torque, high power density, high torque density and high efficiency, and its driving performance is better than that of traditional switched reluctance motor. After clarifying the design constraints and specifications, the preliminary design results based on finite element analysis are demonstrated. Finally, a prototype will be constructed, and the experimental study will be conducted to verify the validity of the design and analysis results.

articleTitle: Human Skull Implantable Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The growing demand for complex disease treatment techniques requires the development of accurate and robust engineering applications. In recent years biomedical implants have gained considerable attention for treatments of neurological diseases such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and refractory epilepsy through the implantation of control and monitoring devices. These devices can be wirelessly successfully powered by using magnetic couplings-based technology. The challenges of this technology are to provide enough energy to power the implanted device, reduce the device dimensions and optimize its efficiency. Therefore, this work presents a new geometrical shape for a wireless power transmission system, which is composed of a wearable transmitting coil that can be built on a hat or cap and is able to produce an approximately uniform magnetic field in the skull region for simultaneous feeding of more than one implant.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Co-Zr-Si-B melt-spun ribbons
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Co-Zr-Si-B alloys were produced by the melt-spinning technique and subsequent annealing. It was found that the small addition of Si to the Co-Zr-B alloys resulted in an increase in coercivity. The Co-Zr-Si-B alloy with a Si content of 2 at% showed a high coercivity of 5.8 kOe. XRD studies showed that the annealed Co-Zr-Si-B alloy consisted of the Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Zr phase. Thus, the high coercivity of the Co-Zr-Si-B alloys is believed to be attributable to the existence of the Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Zr phase.

articleTitle: An Inductance Testing Method of Dual Three-phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines Using Equivalent Electromagnetic Field Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Nowadays, in the test of permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) with traditional q-axis and d-axis inductances testing methods, the machine needs to be connected to a mechanical load, and the test must be performed in the normal operating situation. However, there are some problems existing in traditional q-axis and d-axis inductances testing methods for PMSMs, such as complexity of test systems, high testing cost, etc. It restricts the testing method development of PMSMs. In this paper, a normal method for testing q-axis and d-axis inductances of dual three-phase PMSMs is proposed based on its structural characteristics and AC standstill test. The key point of the proposed method is using equivalent electromagnetic field analysis. The advantages of this method are avoiding auxiliary equipment and considering the saturation effect. In the process of testing the q-axis and d-axis inductances of dual three-phase PMSMs, AC current with DC bias is excited in a set of windings of dual three-phase PMSMs. The DC current component is used to reflect the saturation of the magnetic circuit, and the AC current component is used for the inductance test; DC current is excited the other set of winding of the machine, and it is used to adjust and fix the rotor position. Finally, the method is validated in simulation and experiment, and the error analysis of the test results is performed.

Author Keywords: Dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous machines

articleTitle: Magnetic layer thickness influence on the anisotropy of magnetoelastic properties in Co2Fe0.4Mn0.6Si Heusler alloys thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The anisotropic magnetoelastic properties of the epitaxial Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Si Heusler alloys thin films with the thickness changing from 8 nm to 100 nm were studied using the strain modulated ferromagnetic resonance technique. Assuming the cubic symmetry of the magnetic layer, the first cubic magnetocrystalline constant K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and the two cubic magnetoelastic constants b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> were calculated. All investigated parameters were found to depend on the magnetic layer thickness. The thinnest magnetic layers have shown the strongest cubic magnetocrystalline anisotropy and the weakest anisotropy of the magnetic properties.

articleTitle: Application of Magnetic Composite Materials in Windings to Reduce Alternating-Current Resistance in Leakage Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: High-efficiency converters capable of low-loss switching are LLC resonant dc-dc converters. Leakage transformers that combine resonant inductors and transformers are effective for the miniaturization of LLC resonant dc-dc converters. However, leakage transformers have a substantial leakage magnetic flux due to low coupling between the primary and secondary windings. Leakage transformers have high alternating-current (AC) resistance because of the leakage magnetic flux acting on the windings. Thus, the authors propose an approach to reduce the AC resistance of leakage transformers by inducing leakage flux through the application of magnetic composite materials to the windings. In this study, magnetic field simulation is used to clarify the effect of the loading position of a magnetic composite material on the AC resistance of leakage transformers. The AC resistance at 1 MHz was reduced by 38% from 594 to 368 mΩ by loading the magnetic composite material at the appropriate position in the winding.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Adaptive Error-Correction Decoding for Spin-Torque Transfer Magnetic Random Access Memory (STT-MRAM)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spin-torque transfer magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM) is a promising emerging non-volatile memory (NVM) technology with wide applications. However, the data recovery of STT-MRAM is affected by the diversity of channel raw bit error rate (BER) across different dies caused by process variations, as well as the unknown resistance offset due to temperature change. Therefore, it is critical to develop effective decoding algorithms of error correction codes for STT-MRAM. In this paper, we first propose a neural bit-flipping (BF) decoding algorithm, which can share the same trellis representation as the prior art neural decoding algorithms, such as the neural belief propagation (NBP) and neural offset min-sum (NOMS) algorithm. Hence a neural network (NN) decoder with a uniform architecture but different NN parameters can realize all these neural decoding algorithms. Using such a unified NN decoder architecture, we further propose a novel deep learning (DL)-based adaptive decoding algorithm whose decoding complexity can be adjusted according to the change of the channel conditions of STT-MRAM. Experimental and simulation results demonstrate that our proposed DL-based adaptive decoder can work well over different channel conditions of STT-MRAM, with a dramatic reduction of the decoding latency and energy consumption compared to the fixed decoders.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Double Layer Coils Linear Motor with Series Magnetic Circuit Structure using for Linear Dynamic Loading Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Linear voice coil motor (VCM) has the advantages of high precision and high dynamic response, which fulfills the requirements of linear dynamic loading platform. In this article, a high thrust double layer series magnetic circuit linear voice coil motor is analyzed and designed. Based on 2-D FEM, the thrust and thrust ripple are optimized. Moreover, the damping force on coil support plate is analyzed and reduced by optimization of material and structure. Finally, a linear VCM prototype is manufactured and tested, the thrust results have good consistency with FEM results.

articleTitle: Anomalous Magnetism in Epitaxial Mn2RuxGa Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Thin films of Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ru<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ga grown by sputtering at low temperature, T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</inf> = 225 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup>C, are nearly defect free and have in-plane grain size exceeding 180 nm. A higher T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</inf> of 425 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup>C leads to an increased density of defects and reduced in-plane coherence. The near-perfect films grown at low temperature exhibit a pinched wasp-waist magnetic hysteresis that is a consequence of the frustration induced by exchange interaction and site-specific anisotropy. At higher temperatures, the long-range crystalline order is broken by the presence of defects and simpler square hysteresis loops are recovered.

articleTitle: Study on Magnetic Properties of La-doped Fe-Ga Polycrystalline Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper reports the effect of La composition on magnetic properties of Fe-Ga-La polycrystalline films toward improvement of magnetic softness and high-frequency magnetic properties of Fe-Ga polycrystalline films. The magnetic softness of Fe-Ga-La films got better as the La composition was increased. The saturation magnetostriction of these films slightly increased at the La composition of 0.9, whereas linearly decreased to 3.8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> at the La composition more than 0.9. Furthermore, the in-plane effective damping constant became lower as the La composition was increased, and their values were approximately one-half to one-quarter lower than that of Fe-Ga polycrystalline films. Thus, these results are revealed that both magnetic softness and high frequency magnetic properties of Fe-Ga-La films can be significantly improved by adjusting the amount of La.

articleTitle: Investigation of a New Split Stator-Permanent-Magnet Machine with Mechanical Manufacturing Consideration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The paper investigates the influence of mechanical manufacturing consideration on the electromagnetic performacnes of a new split stator-permanent-magnet (SPM) machine (SSPMM). The designed SSPMM is evolved from the conventional flux reversal machine (FRM), in which both of these two machines employ PMs placed on the top of stator teeth. The fixation methods of PMs will affect electromagnetic performance, which is not taken into consideration in machine design process. Then, the steady torques of the designed SSPMM and the conventional FRM are analyzed with four key parameters in two representative fixation methods selected as mechanical manufacturing consideration. The evolution process of SSPMM, operating principle and the investigated parameter defination are provided. The finite-element-analysis-calculated results show that the dovetail PM fixing and sticking fixing are suitable for SSPMM and FRM, respectively.

articleTitle: A multi-state memory device based on the Manipulation of a single skyrmion using spin-polarized current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Towards a multistate skyrmionic device, Firstly, the motion of a single skyrmion under spin-transfer-torque (STT) is studied in the conventional and constricted wire the study reveals the possibility to pin, depin and annihilate skyrmion. Later, a stepped nano-track with bottom and top confinements has been proposed, to stabilize the skyrmion in each confinement. The adjustment of the current density magnitude and its duration enabled the displacement of the skyrmion at any position. More interestingly, it was observed that only one skyrmion can be stabilized in each confinement when a large number is displaced by current pulses. These results open the way for large-capacity memory devices and neuromorphic computing.

articleTitle: Transmission spectra of magnetic fluids with magnetite nanoparticles in the visible and near-IR regions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The transmission spectra of magnetic fluids with magnetite nanoparticles in kerosene with a solid phase concentration from 0.01% to 1% in the range of 350–1050 nm have been studied. A transparency maximum was found in the region of 740-750 nm, which becomes more pronounced with increasing magnetite concentration. The spectra are interpreted on the basis of the theory of multiple light scattering and coherent propagation of electromagnetic radiation in close-packed media.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Magnetoelectric Nanoparticles With Varying Core-Shell Ratios and Their Effects On In Vitro Neuron Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetoelectric nanoparticles (MENPs) convert magnetic fields into localized electric fields, using a core-shell nanostructure based on a magnetostrictive core and piezoelectric shell. These nanoparticles can serve as biocompatible wireless nanotransducers for magneticbased brain stimulation. We examined the effects of changing the core-to-shell ratio in cobalt ferrite – barium titanate (CoFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) MENPs on their magnetic properties, and then we tested their performance in stimulating neurons in vitro. The nanoparticles with the highest anisotropy core and lowest core-to-shell ratio were the most effective at activating neurons.

articleTitle: Model of a Magnetic Waveguide for a Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The present work focuses on a novel mechanism for controlling the spin-wave (magnonic) signals in the ferromagnetic films that is promising to be a basic element for the realization of artificial synapses in hardware-based artificial neural networks. The general idea of this control is based on the effect of vanadium dioxide films exhibiting a metal–insulator transition on the propagation of magnon wave packets. A model of an artificial synapse has been built. In particular, various levels of microwave attenuation of spin waves transmitted through the investigated structure has been observed due to a variation of the conductivity of the vanadium dioxide film within a narrow temperature range. This feature makes it possible to control the strength of the connections between the individual neurons by dynamic controllability of an amplitude of the transmitted magnon signal.

articleTitle: Crossed Anisotropy Multilayered Nanogranular Films Combining High Permeability, Ferromagnetic Resonance Frequency, and Resistivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In-plane isotropic crossed anisotropy multilayer for high-frequency was fabricated using in-plane uniaxial anisotropic nanogranular film because of its high permeability, ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) frequency, and electrical DC resistivity. The multilayer exhibited in-plane isotropy and enabled us to combine permeability of 100, FMR frequency of 3 GHz, and resistivity of 5 μΩ∙m, and furthermore, low damping factor of 0.015 was obtained, and hence the multilayer can be available to us for a low loss up to 1 GHz. On the other hand, underlayer and cap layer were necessary for isotropy of the multilayer. These may contribute to the relaxation of interfacial stress.

articleTitle: An estimation method of magnetic coupling coefficient between two microstrip lines using machine leaning of near field information
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: An estimation method of magnetic coupling coefficients between printed-circuit-board-level traces using a near field information was investigated. Parallel two microstrip lines (MSLs) with different distances between the lines were used as a test bench. The current flowing in a signal line and its return current was modeled as a simple one-turn equivalent loop current model. First, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) for regression prediction was trained with the theoretical values of the magnetic near-field distribution generated from the loop current model. Next, the simulated magnetic near-field distributions above the parallel two MSLs at 1 GHz were input to the trained CNN to estimate the geometry of the loop current models. The magnetic coupling coefficient between MSLs is estimated through calculating the coupled magnetic flux between the estimated loop current models. The estimated results agreed with the simulation results within 10%, indicating the feasibility of the magnetic field coupling by the proposed method.

articleTitle: Effect of Helical Anisotropy on Magnetic Losses in Stacked Cores of Grain-Oriented and Non-Oriented Steels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic loss decomposition, going beyond the conventional power frequencies, and first-order reversal curve approach have been combined to assess the anisotropy of magnetization process inside the shifted ring stacks, made either of grain-oriented or non-oriented Fe–Si steel, endowed with helical distribution of easy magnetization axes. By applying the Statistical Theory of Losses, the loss contributions are analyzed as the functions of shift angle from DC to 2 kHz at peak inductions up to 1.5 T. The angle-dependent behavior of field-resolved domain wall processes is revealed in the micromagnetic maps of pinning and interaction fields.

articleTitle: Loss Model of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine with Series Iron-loss Resistance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) are widely used, because of the high power density and high efficiency. It is noted that the loss model of IPMSM is essential to analysis, and furtherly suppress the motor loss, especially for the loss-model based maximum efficiency control. The traditional loss model is the one with parallel iron-loss resistance, which has high-order and mixed parameters. Therefore, in order to identify the variable model parameters under the wide variation range of current vectors and speeds, some necessary simplifications or iteration solutions should be adopted, which may lead to the sacrifice of accuracy or time cost. In this paper, a loss model with series iron-loss resistance is introduced. This model is much mathematically simpler than the traditional one and is quite appropriate for parameters identification. Besides, considering the variable currents and speeds, the torque-related and loss-related parameters’ variation is discussed to improve the accuracy of torque and motor loss under different operating conditions. The analysis results are verified on a prototype IPMSM experimentally.

articleTitle: Semi-Analytical Non-Linear Physical Model of the Core Losses in Ferrite Ring Cores
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To calculate ferrite core losses based on a physical approach, non-linear material effects must be considered. To implement these effects in a fast and accurate way, a new semi-analytical model is proposed. It combines the solution of the wave equations in the core with advanced material models of ferrite into an iterative procedure. The results validate the approach, which enables a fast calculation of the core losses.

articleTitle: Development of High Efficiency PMSG with Extremely Thin Stator Lamination Materials for Electric-propulsion UAV
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) is gradually popular in the aero-electric propulsion system due to its high efficiency and high power density. In this paper, an efficient surface mounted PMSG is proposed for hybrid electric propulsion system of UAV. In order to get higher efficiency and power density, this paper not only optimizes the electromagnetic structure of the PMSG, but also compares the electromagnetic performance and weight with respect to different stator core materials and different stator lamination thicknesses. A 10kW and 20-pole and 45-slot prototype is manufactured with 0.1mm thick 1J22 material. Finally, the simulation and experiment results show that the PMSG has the highest efficiency under the premise of meeting the weight and volume requirements. The efficiency of the generator system can reach 92.5%, and the power density of the generator is about 2kW/kg.

articleTitle: Feasibility Investigation on Sinusoidal-Reluctance Rotor Contour in Variable Reluctance Resolver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this digest, a novel variable reluctance (VR) resolver with sinusoidal-reluctance rotor contour is proposed and its envelope feasibility is evaluated via the analytical and finite element (FE) analysis. Moreover, the third order harmonic suppression via flux leakage compensation is addressed to reveal the operation principle of the proposed VR resolver. Under 4 mm tooth width, the total harmonic distortion of the cosine envelope with the proposed rotor contour can be limited to only 0.56%.

articleTitle: Analysis on New Electromagnetic Shielding Structure and Shielding Effectiveness of Electric Vehicle Wireless Charging System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In order to reduce the electromagnetic leakage and without affecting the transmission efficiency, a new structure of electromagnetic shielding which is composed of ferrite and ultra-thin silicon steel(UTSS) is proposed. Considering the thickness and shape of the shielding plate, the air gap distance between the shielding plate, the shielding effect and transmission efficiency of the new electromagnetic shielding structure are studied. To verify the effect of the new shielding structure, a wireless charging platform is built. The test results show that the shielding effectiveness can reach 16dB and the transmission efficiency can reach 92.2%. The proposed structure can ensure the electromagnetic safety with high transmission efficiency, which is also suitable for high-power charging systems.

articleTitle: Frequency Sensing and Detection using Granular Vortex MTJ Nano Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A new paradigm in sensing and communication is emerging with Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), RF detection, object identification, and sensing capabilities for future Internet of Things (IoT) applications, such as automobiles, logistics, healthcare, and smart living. For sensing and detecting the required frequency, complex, large, and highly energy-consuming circuits based on CMOS technologies are required. Hence, here we propose a granular vortex magnetic tunnel junction nano oscillator for a compact and energy- efficient frequency sensing system. The granularity present in the free layer of magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) allows the identification of the natural frequency of the magnetic vortex core. Our study presents that as soon as the input frequency matches the natural frequency of the vortex core, the impact of grains on the vortex core is nullified. Otherwise, trapping of the vortex core in different grains produces varying output frequencies. The granular effect and the variation of the aspect ratio of the free layer are examined to determine natural frequency of the vortex core. Further, the frequency sensing and detection mechanism for a specific frequency are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Co2MnSi-based Heusler Alloy Glass-coated Microwires
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have successfully fabricated nanocrystalline Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnSi Heusler alloy glass-coated microwires with a metallic nucleus diameter of 10.2 μm and total diameter 22.2 μm by the Taylor–Ulitovsky technique. Magnetic and structural investigations have been performed to clarify the basic magneto-structural properties of the Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnSi glass-coated microwires. XRD showed a well-defined crystalline structure with a lattice parameter a = 5.62 Å. The room temperature magnetic behavior showed a strong in-plane magnetocrystalline anisotropy parallel to the microwire axis. The hysteresis loops showed unique thermal stability with temperature, with the coercivity (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) and normalized magnetic remanence exhibiting roughly stable temperature behavior.

articleTitle: A Novel Consequent-Pole Contra-Rotating Machine with Zero-Sequence Current Excitation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A novel hybrid excitation consequent-pole contra-rotating machine with zero-sequence current excitation is presented in this paper. The stator windings carry the DC field winding current and the AC armature current, making the machine more compact. Further, the flux can be weakened or enhanced without the risk of demagnetization by controlling the zero-sequence current excitation. Finally, the segmented stator can effectively reduce the iron loss and simplify the manufacturing process.

articleTitle: Development of anisotropic nanocrystalline ribbon core and powdered core for high frequency transformers and inductors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The rotation magnetization reversal enables to realize the eddy current loss minimum in the anisotropic metal-based magnetic materials magnetized in the hard magnetization direction. This digest describes the research and development on the anisotropic nanocrystalline ribbon core and powdered core for high frequency power transformers and power inductors.

articleTitle: CoFeB/MgO/CoFeB-Based Magnetic Tunnel Junction Using Soft Magnetic Composite Free Layer with TaFeB Spacer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: CoFeB/MgO/CoFeB-based magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) with a soft magnetic composite free layer have been studied for an ultra-sensitive magnetic sensor. Further improvement to the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) ratio is still required, which has been hindered by a trade off between the TMR ratio and interlayer exchange coupling (IEC) depending on the spacer thickness of the composite free layer. In this study, we developed a TaFeB spacer to replace the conventional Ta spacer in the sensor-type MTJ and solve the aforementioned trade off. The TaFeB spacer had a wider thickness window of the IEC than the case of pure Ta. This allowed us to increase the TaFeB thickness up to 1.0 nm, resulting in an improved TMR ratio of 234% which is higher than the case using the Ta counterpart. The TaFeB spacer enables us to break the ceiling of the sensor-type MTJs, leading to a higher sensitivity.

articleTitle: Vehicle Detection Using 2-axis MI sensors Based on Moving Vehicle Magnetic Field Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: With the number of vehicles increasing year by year, the development of Internet of Things (IoT) in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) is accelerating. Using magnetic sensors to detect vehicles on the road has been regarded as an efficient and cost-effective approach for traffic surveillance. In this paper, we propose a bar magnet model and a magnetic dipole model to simulate the magnetic perturbations during the vehicle movement. The characteristics of the two models were analyzed by comparing simulated signals to measured signals. We propose a detection method using a 2-axis magneto-impedance (MI) sensor and use an algorithm to calculate the dynamic threshold for detecting the car, achieved a 98% detection rate for a single lane and an 86% detection rate for the second lane included.

articleTitle: Accuracy Investigation of High-Frequency Core Loss Measurement for Low-Permeability Magnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, the effects of high-frequency core loss measurement for low-permeability magnetic material on the accuracy, which leads to high leakage flux during the measurement, is investigated using capacitive cancellation method. Moreover, a new correction method is proposed for obtaining accurate core loss for low-permeability materials. It was shown that the accuracy deteriorates with high leakage flux; however, the core loss was successfully corrected by the proposed method even when high leakage flux existed.

articleTitle: Study of Levitation Characteristic against Vertical Displacement at Minimum Levitation Velocity in the Electrodynamic Suspension System with Damper Coils
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The principle of the electrodynamic suspension (EDS) system is electromagnetic induction. The EDS system is used for levitation and guidance of JR Maglev. But a damping factor that only uses the EDS system is small. So, the passive damper system and the semi-active damper system are installed. The bogie starts levitating at 42[m/sec] in this system. The damping factor in that velocity is the smallest at the range of levitation. In this paper, the running simulation when the bogie that runs at minimum levitation velocity passes various vertical displacements is discussed. In the case of vertical displacement is small, the semi-active damper system converges oscillations more than 7[sec] shorter than the passive damper system. However, in the case of the vertical displacement becomes larger, the system that has a positive effect on oscillation suppression becomes passive damper system. The oscillation of the semi-active damper system does not converge. For this reason, the bogie obtains a large damping factor by shifting after reducing the oscillation.

articleTitle: Modeling of Wind Turbine Drive Trains for Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Wind turbine drive trains consist of mechanical components such as the gearbox, the bearings and the rotating shaft; and an electrical component, the electric generator. These components are electromagnetically and electromechanically coupled with each other and have continuously rotating parts, making them more susceptible to faults. Unfortunately, these components are individually modeled while performing finite element analysis, and the coupling effects are neglected, yielding approximations that are not acceptable for, e.g., modal analysis. This paper addresses that problem and presents the model of complete wind turbine drive train subsystem for finite element analysis. The proposed model takes a novel, one-of-a-kind approach design to analyze the drive train subsystem of a wind turbine in a holistic manner.

articleTitle: Spin-orbit torques in Co2MnGa magnetic Weyl semimetal thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Due to the nontrivial topology in their electronic band structure, topological quantum materials are known to exhibit unconventional surface states and anomalous transport properties. In the present study, the ferromagnetic Heusler alloy Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa, which breaks time-reversal symmetry, is studied to estimate its spin-orbit torque efficiency. Epitaxial thin films with high structural ordering are obtained, which show very high values of anomalous Hall conductivity. A spin-orbit torque efficiency of 0.13±0.01 is obtained in a 20 nm Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa film. The present results open the possibility to use these exotic materials in spintronic devices and beyond.

articleTitle: Model for Angular Dependency of the Intrinsic Coercivity Force of Ferrite Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In internal permanent magnet synchronous machines, the use of ferrite permanent magnets is being studied as an alternative to rare-earth elements-based permanent magnets, such as NdFeB. However, demagnetization measurements of ferrite magnets are rarely published and such information is crucial for an efficient electrical machine design with ferrite magnets. In this paper, we present measurements of partial demagnetization on ferrite permanent magnets subject to inclined external magnetic fields. From the measurements done, a mathematical model is developed that defines a relationship between the intrinsic coercivity and the inclination of the external demagnetizing field.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Rare-Earth Free High-Speed Multilayer IPMSM Using Dual-Phase Magnetic Material
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes the performance improvement of the rare-earth free high-speed multilayer (ML) IPMSM by using the dual-phase magnetic material (DPMM). To ensure mechanical stability, ML IPMSM should have many bridges. However, in the bridges, a significant leakage flux generates, and, due to this, the performance of the motor is decreased. Since the DPMM has magnetic and non-magnetic phases, to solve this problem, the non-magnetic phase is applied to the bridges of ML IPMSM. Through it, the leakage flux is decreased, and performance improvement of the motor is achieved. In this paper, the electrical parameters, torque, and efficiency are compared using finite element analysis for the motor with and without the DPMM. Finally, to verify the proposed method, the load test is conducted.

Author Keywords: high-speed multilayer (ML) interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM)

articleTitle: Precise transport of skyrmions by surface acoustic waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions in thin films with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy are promising candidates for magnetic memory and logic devices, making the development of ways to transport skyrmions efficiently and precisely of significant interest. Here, we investigate the transport of skyrmions by surface acoustic waves (SAWs) via several modalities using micromagnetic simulations. We demonstrate skyrmion pinning sites created at the anti-nodes of standing SAWs and skyrmion Hall-like motion without pinning driven by travelling SAWs. We also show how orthogonal SAWs formed by combining a longitudinal travelling SAW and a transverse standing SAW can be used for the precise 2D positioning of skyrmions. Our results also suggest SAWs offer a viable approach for the precise transport of multiple skyrmions along a multichannel racetrack.

articleTitle: Effects of Nb and B addition on intrinsic magnetic properties and phase of TbCu7-type Sm-Fe-Co-Nb-B alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The influence of Nb and B contents of TbCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>-type Sm-Fe-Co-Nb-B alloys on magnetic properties, including coercivity, saturation magnetization, and anisotropy field, was examined with the goal of enhancing coercivity of TbCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>-type Sm-Fe-Co-Nb-B alloy. Nb and B in the TbCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>-type phase were found to affect intrinsic magnetic properties such as the anisotropy field. Specifically, Nb and B addition decreased and slightly increased, respectively, anisotropy field of the TbCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>-type phase. The improved anisotropy field upon B addition contributed to realizing high coercivity for the Sm-Fe-Co-Nb-B alloys.

articleTitle: Reactive single-step hot-pressing and magnetocaloric performance of polycrystalline Fe2Al1.15-xB2GexGax (x = 0, 0.05) MAB phases
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Reactive single-step hot-pressing at 1473 K and 35 MPa for 4 h produces dense, bulk, near single-phase, low-cost and low-criticality Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.15</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.1</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</inf> MAB samples, showing a second-order magnetic phase transition with favorable magnetocaloric properties around room temperature. The magnetic as well as magnetocaloric properties can be tailored upon Ge and Ga doping, leading to an increase of Curie temperature and spontaneous magnetization. The maximum isothermal entropy change of hot-pressed Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.15</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in magnetic field changes of 2 and 5 T amounts to 2.5 and 5 J(kgK)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at 287.5 K and increases by Ge and Ga addition to 3.1 and 6.2 J(kgK)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at 306.5 K, respectively. The directly measured maximum adiabatic temperature change is improved by the composition modification from 0.9 to 1.1 K in magnetic field changes of 1.93 T. Overall, we demonstrate that hot-pressing provides a much faster, more scalable and processing cost reducing alternative compared to conventional synthesis routes to produce heat exchangers for magnetic cooling devices. Therefore, our criticality assessment shows that hot-pressed Fe-based MAB phases provide a promising compromise of material and processing cost, criticality and magnetocaloric performance, demonstrating the potential for low-cost and low-criticality magnetocaloric applications around room temperature.

articleTitle: Permeability of clustered soft magnetic narrow strips controlled by a surface normal magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A unique functionality was reported for a thin film soft magnetic strip having a certain angle of inclined magnetic anisotropy. It can switch magnetic domain by applying surface normal field with a certain distribution. The domain switches between single domain and multi-domain. Our previous study shows that this phenomenon appears even in case of adjacent configuration of the multiple narrow strips. In this report, magnetic permeability for alternating current (AC) was investigated. The result shows that the AC permeability changes drastically depending on the domain structure in the frequency range from 10 kHz to 10 MHz. This result leads to apply this phenomenon to a switched inductor working with low energy consumption or a sensor for magnetic field distribution.

articleTitle: Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Electrical Machine with High Torque Density: Research on the Influence of Combined-Halbach Array on YASA Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To increase power and torque density, a combined-Halbach array for the axial flux permanent magnet machines (AFPMMs) with yokeless and segmented armature (YASA) is presented in this paper. Firstly, the YASA machine models with conventional axial magnetized magnets and combined-Halbach array magnetized magnets are established using 3-D finite-element method (FEM). Then, the torque, torque per magnet-volume and no-load back-EMF are calculated, and the performance of two machines are analyzed and compared. It is demonstrated that the combined-Halbach array can improve the torque density of the machine and the utilization rate of the magnets. On this basis, the combined-Halbach array rotor is optimized, where the unequal thickness magnets rotor is established, and its torque density is calculated under different thickness. The results show that the combined-Halbach array with unequal thickness magnets can reduce the amount of permanent magnet materials, thus improving the utilization of magnets and reducing the costs.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design and Analysis of Low Speed High Torque Motor with Composite Rotor and Double Stator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a novel composite rotor double stator low speed high torque motor (CRDS-LSHTM). The rotor of the novel motor is composed of synchronous reluctance and surface permanent magnet. The salient feature of the composite rotor is the separation of permanent magnet torque and reluctance torque, which brings flexible control to the permanent magnet torque and reluctance torque components of the motor. The electromagnetic performance of the motor is simulated and analyzed by finite element method. The results show that the novel motor not only has the characteristics of high torque density and small torque ripple, but also saves permanent magnet materials and achieves the purpose of saving non-renewable resources.

articleTitle: 3-D Stray Loss Evaluation of Structural Component under Harmonic and DC-Biased Magnetization by Harmonic-Balanced Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Considering the anisotropic property of magnetic materials, the 3-D harmonic-balanced finite element method combined with the fixed-point technique is proposed and applied for simulating the TEAM P21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sup> model. TEAM P21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sup> is a model extended from the TEAM Problem 21 benchmark family for studying the stray loss of magnetic and non-magnetic components operating under the hybrid excitation of harmonics and DC-bias. The calculated results including leakage magnetic field as well as stray loss of components are compared with the measurement results of the set-up TEAM P21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sup> experiment platform. The investigation provides a new scheme for simulating the 3-D stray loss model of the large-scale power transformer in the harmonic domain.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Simulation For Smear Growth On HAMR Heads
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Modeling the smear growth in the write heads of the Heat Assisted Magnetic Recording (HAMR) Disk Drives is an essential tool for understanding the mechanisms of smear formation. In this paper, we present a novel method to simulate the growth of smear under the influence of thermophoretic and drag force. First, a time-averaged force field is generated using particle mechanics. Then, using evaporation and condensation parameters, we track the trajectory of random smear particles on the disk. The resulting particles that form smear on the head are plotted and compared with experimental results. The comparison reveals good similarities.

articleTitle: Effect of Phosphate Treatment on Corrosion Resistance of Nd-Fe-B Anisotropic Magnetic Powder
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Anisotropic Nd-Fe-B hydrogenation disproportionation desorption recombination (HDDR) powder with a high corrosion resistance was prepared by phosphoric acid treatment. The treated samples baked at temperatures higher than 250°C exhibited a high corrosion resistance; the change ratio of the coercivity (ΔH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cj</inf>) before and after the anticorrosion test was within 5%. Microstructural observations indicated that a uniform layer of phosphate with a small amount of Nd oxide could be formed at a high baking temperature.

articleTitle: A Topological Design Optimization Approach for Winding Oil Flow Paths in ONAN Transformers Based on a Fluidic-Thermal Coupled Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A power transformer is one of the most critical components in transmission and distribution systems. To extend the life-cycle while operating with enough reliability and controllability, thermal concerns of a transformer have attracted extensive research attentions. In this paper, a topology optimization (TO) methodology is presented for designing the coolant flow paths in a prototype oil-natural air-natural (ONAN) power transformer to maximize the winding heat dissipation capacity without any compromise on the flow resistance. First, the thermal and fluid flow characteristics in both the winding and the radiator of the prototype transformer are numerically investigated through a fluidic-thermal coupled field approach. The preliminary cooling effectiveness of the oil circulation system is initialized. Second, a material-density-based TO scheme is employed to realize the optimal design of the oil baffle structures. In the TO optimization, artificial Darcy frictional forces are applied to the solidified cells to block their internal flows in the fluidic calculations, while the thermal conduction coefficients in those cells are enhanced to separate the baffles from the flowing oil in thermal analyses. Finally, the fluid flow and thermal coupled fields of the prototype transformer winding region with structurally optimized oil baffles are numerically calculated to validate the TO effectiveness.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Magnetic Properties of Nd2Fe17N3 Magnetic Powders with Nano-α-Fe Phase-Separated Surface Layers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powders were coated with transition metals and rare-earth phosphate layers. The phosphate layers were subsequently phase-separated into outer Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and inner Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> layers via heat treatment in air. Simultaneously, phase-separated layers of nano-sized α-Fe and rare-earth rich phases were formed in the interface between the Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and phosphate layer. The resulting powder was classified into particle sizes of 20–38 µm, formed into a toroidal core shape, and then measured for magnetic properties in the MHz range. The real permeability µ′ and loss tangent tanδ values at 10 MHz were approximately 11.19 and 0.02, respectively. The treated powder exhibited a two-fold enhancement and 10-fold reduction in the values of µ′ and tanδ, respectively, compared to those of the untreated Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powder. The developed treatment protocols enable the synthesis of magnetic powders that possess both magnetic coupling and insulating properties, which will facilitate the development of MHz-range magnetic cores.

articleTitle: A Variable-Reluctance Based Wireless Sensing Module for Intraoral Pressure Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report a variable-reluctance based wireless sensing module to measure intraoral pressure for clinical orthodontic treatment. The wireless sensing module consists of two parts; first is a set of coils, i.e., a transmitting and a receiving coil and second is a variable- reluctance based pressure sensor. The coils are placed in a concentric arrangement at a certain distance from the sensor. An AC voltage is applied to the transmitting coil to produce AC magnetic flux and by electromagnetic-induction, an AC voltage is induced in the receiving coil. When the pressure inside the pressure chamber changes, the diaphragm of the sensor deflects towards or away from the coils, resulting in change of air-gap between the same. This causes the magnetic reluctance between the diaphragm and the receiving coil to change. Consequently, the output voltage of receiving coil is changed. Based on above principle, we fabricated above parts and conducted pressure sensing test. According to our results, the pressure can be successfully sensed. The pressure sensitivities of 3.62 µV/mbar and 2.66 µV/mbar is measured when the gap between the coils and the sensor is 10 mm and 20 mm respectively. Furthermore, to validate the viability that the pressure can be sensed in different regions inside the mouth, the sensor is placed on an inclined tooth and pressure sensing test is performed. For this case, the pressure sensitivities of 1.23 µV/mbar and 1.48 µV/mbar is measured when the gap between the coils and the sensor is 10 mm and 20 mm respectively.

articleTitle: Development of Optically Pumped Magnetometers towards Next Generation Biomagnetic Neuroimaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs) using alkali-metal atoms are capable of measuring extremely small magnetic fields. After describing principles of the pump-prove-type OPM, we introduce our newly developed compact OPM module having its noise floor was less than 20 fT<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</inf>/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> as well as results of magnetoencephalography (MEG) measurements. In addition, we introduce the first magnetic shieldless ultra-low-field MRI scanner with an OPM operating at a Larmor frequency of 300 kHz. The applicability of the OPM-based MEG-MRI fused system might provide important advancements of biomagnetic neuroimaging.

articleTitle: Basic Characteristics of Orthogonal-Core-Type Variable Inductor with Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Variable inductors, which consist of magnetic cores, primary dc windings, and secondary ac windings, can control the effective inductance of the secondary ac windings by the primary dc current due to the magnetic saturation effect. Therefore, they can be used as reactive power compensators in electric power systems. This paper presents a novel orthogonal-core-type variable inductor in which permanent magnets are inserted in the magnetic path of the primary dc flux. The proposed variable inductor can generate an arbitrary reactive power when the primary dc current is zero, and it can control the effective reactive power from lead to lag by changing the primary dc current from positive to negative.

articleTitle: Microstructural features of strip-cast Nd(Fe,Mo)12 based alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Nd(Fe,Mo)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> compounds have been considered as promising candidates for next generation permanent magnet materials because of their excellent intrinsic hard magnetic properties with a minimum usage of rare earth elements. However, achieving high coercivity in anisotropic microstructure is a big challenge, which hinders their practical applications. In this work we present the microstructural study of the strip-cast Nd(Fe,Mo)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>-based alloy. Detailed microstructure characterizations using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) indicate that addition of Cu leads to sub-micron size 1-12 magnetic grains with Nd and Cu segregated at grain boundaries. This work provides an evidence of the issues of the microstructure of these alloys for the development of the appropriate microstructure conducting to the high coercivity in the 1-12 alloys.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Increasing Torque Density by Magnetic Interaction in 500 N•m class IPM-type Magnetic-Geared Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic-geared motors (MGMs) can achieve high torque density without mechanical contact. Although interior permanent magnet (IPM) type MGMs have higher efficiency than conventional surface permanent magnet (SPM) type MGMs, a permanent magnet motor part and a magnetic gear part magnetically influence each other. In a previous paper, the magnetic interaction in IPM-type MGM was fully clarified. If the magnetic interaction is effectively used, then the torque density of IPM-type MGM may increase without additional magnets. This paper presents an experimental verification of increasing torque density by the magnetic interaction.

articleTitle: Compositional dependence of structure, magnetic and electrical conduction properties of CoxPt1-x alloy nanowires fabricated by electrodeposition into nanoporous templates
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report on compositional dependence of structure, magnetic and electrical conduction properties of CoxPt1-x alloy nanowires fabricated by electrodeposition into nanoporous polycarbonate templates. Scanning electron microscopy analysis shows that the wires have the average length and width of 9.0 μm and 130 nm, respectively, with x ~0.7. Anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) measurement of the nanowires with x ~0.7 carried out on Ni electrodes reveals that MR is ~0.11% with peaks observed near zero magnetic field, which is presumably associated with magnetic domain nucleation. Such findings should provide more insightful knowledge basis toward optimized construction of three-dimensional magnetic memory devices.

articleTitle: Analysis and Comparison of Novel Yokeless Double Rotor Mutually Coupled Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposed a new seven-phase, yokeless, two-rotor switched reluctance motor with flux between adjacent stator teeth. The motor adopts a two-rotor structure and increases the conducting area of each phase winding by using the self and mutual inductance between the windings, thus increasing the torque density and power density of the motor while reducing the motor torque pulsation. In this paper, the topology and operating principle of the proposed motor are firstly introduced. The motor model is established using the equivalent magnetic network method to further analyze the thrust characteristics of the motor, and the results are verified by the finite element method.Finally, the new motor proposed in this paper is compared with the conventional switched reluctance motor based on the analysis results.

articleTitle: Calculation of Iron Loss in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Based on PSO-RNN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) Recursive Neural Network (RNN) method independent of the empirical iron loss formula to analyze the iron loss in a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). This model establishes an iron loss calculation model considering high-order harmonic, rotating magnetization, and temperature factors. Considering the influence of multi-factors, the model studies the law of loss change under different magnetic flux densities, frequencies, and temperature conditions. To avoid the deviation problem caused by traditional polynomial fitting, the multi-layer RNN and PSO are used to train and optimize the neural network. Using the machine learning method, the iron loss model versus input parameters is established. The iron loss in complex cases beyond the measurement range can be estimated accurately. The proposed method helps achieve a PMSM iron loss calculation model with broad applicability and high accuracy.

articleTitle: Realization of zero-field skyrmions in a magnetic tunnel junction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The stability of skyrmions in zero external magnetic field is significant for promoting fundamental studies and device applications. Here, we develop a zero-field exchange-biased skyrmion material and integrate it into an MTJ device. An Ir layer is inserted between the antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic layers, which plays a key role in prohibiting interlayer diffusion under thermal annealing, resulting in simultaneous enhancement of exchange bias and thermal stability. The smallest zero-field skyrmions have a size of 100 nm scale at room temperature. The zero-field skyrmion material is then integrated into a perpendicularly-magnetized MTJ, leading to the first demonstration of zero-field skyrmions in an MTJ, which is an important step toward developing skyrmion-based spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of an Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine with Asymmetric and Auxiliary Slot Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) is widely used for electric vehicle driving applications since it has high torque and efficiency. However, torque ripple is very high which is a main drawback of the IPMSM. Its torque ripple can be reduced by designing the auxiliary slots on the rotor and stator surfaces and designing its permanent magnet and flux barrier with an asymmetric structure. Meanwhile, the design parameters will be increased greatly if the above design methods are employed for the IPMSM, which will make the machine difficult to design and optimize. In this paper, a four-stage multi-level optimization design process (FSMLODP) is proposed to optimize IPMSM with the double-layer asymmetric and rotor auxiliary slot structure for achieving low torque ripple performance. The effectiveness of the proposed FLMLODP is verified by three different IPMSMs, it can be seen that the torque ripple of IPMSM can be reduced greatly by taking asymmetric and rotor auxiliary slot design for the IPMSM. The torque performance of optimal IPMSMs using conventional asymmetric main parameter design optimization (CAMPDO) methods and FSMLODP was compared and verified FSMLODP is effective and efficient.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Modular Flux Switching Permanent Magnet Resolver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Permanent magnet (PM) resolvers are highly employed with the ascent of the electric machine speed. In this digest, a novel modular flux switching PM (FSPM) resolver is designed based on the FSPM machine. By removing the stator yoke, the flux path in each tooth coil is fixed and the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the output voltage is reduced to only 0.37%. Moreover, the proposed 12/16 FSPM resolver can be adapted to fit different rotor poles under the same mechanical support with different modular units (e.g., 6/8 and 10/8 FSPM resolver). Therefore, it can be applied in electric machines with variable rotor pole pairs.

articleTitle: Simulations of magnetic Bragg scattering in transmission electron microscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have modeled the magnetic Bragg scattering in two antiferromagnetic materials, NiO and LaMnAsO, using transmission electron microscopy. Experimentally, Loudon detected these weak magnetic phenomena in NiO. As a more difficult situation with a lower concentration of magnetic elements and higher concentration of heavier non-magnetic elements that significantly scatter, we did computations for the LaMnAsO compound in order to compare our computational replication of Loudon’s experimental data. Additionally, we have discussed the antiferromagnetic Bragg spot’s thickness and voltage dependency for both compounds. We used two computational methods, one assuming a static lattice with smeared Debye-Waller potentials and the other explicitly taking into account the atomic vibrations within the quantum excitations of phonons model (thermal diffuse scattering). According to the structural study, the antiferromagnetic Bragg spot in NiO is located between the (111) and (000) reflections. However, in LaMnAsO, it is located at the site of the (110) reflection in the diffraction pattern, which is a forbidden reflection of the crystal structure. According to calculations, the magnetic Bragg spot in NiO has an intensity that is much greater than thermal diffuse scattering at room temperature. The magnetic Bragg spot for LaMnAsO is weaker than the thermal diffuse scattering at room temperature, but its identification can be made easier at lower temperatures.

articleTitle: Large interfacial Rashba interaction and resultant dominating field- like torque in atomically thin metallic heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The hallmark of spintronics in the last decade has been the ability of spin-orbit interactions to convert a charge current into the spin current, and vice versa, most often in the bulk of heavy metal thin films. Here, we demonstrate how the insertion of a light metal element interface profoundly affects both the nature of spin-orbit torque and its efficiency in terms of damping-like (HDL) and field-like (HFL) effective fields in an ultrathin Co film. Indeed, we measure unexpectedly an HFL/HDL ratio much larger than 1 (up to 2.5) by inserting a nanometer-thin Al metallic layer in Pt|Co|Al|Pt as compared to a similar stacking including Cu instead of Al. From our modelling, these results strongly evidence the presence of a large Rashba interaction at Co|Al interface generating a giant HFL, which is not expected from a metallic interface. The occurrence of such enhanced torques from an interfacial origin is further validated by demonstrating current-induced magnetization reversal showing a significant decrease in the critical current for switching.

articleTitle: Mn4−xGaxN Thin Films for Ferrimagnetic Spintronics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Ferrimagnetic compensation in Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4−x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>N (0<x<0.27) thin films grown by sputtering on (001) MgO is determined from magnetisation and Anomalous Hall effect measurements and compared with results on the bulk material. Compensation appears in films with x >0.15 and it occurs at 235 K when x = 0.18. A greater amount of Ga-doping is required to achieve compensation in the bulk, where room-temperature compensation is at x = 0.26. The differences are discussed in terms of Ga site occupancy in the Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>N structure, and an effect of the change of easy axis of the triangular ferrimagnetic spin structure from [111] in the bulk to [001] in the tetragonally-distorted films.

articleTitle: Achieving Uniaxial In-Plane Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy to Enable Scalable SOT-MRAM Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, we examine in-plane spin-orbit-torque magnetic random-access-memory (SOT-MRAM) devices stabilized by in-plane uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy. This concept enables in-plane device stabilization without external fields or constraints on shape, paving the way for scalable and uniform magnetic memories, as well as novel spin-torque devices. Uniaxial in-plane anisotropy is generated through crystalline epitaxy between platinum and cobalt layers on a single-crystal substrate. The presence of in-plane anisotropy is confirmed by crystalline characterization and hysteresis measurements. Furthermore, we investigate the interaction between this uniaxial in-plane anisotropy and the spin-transfer torque in a spin Hall switching device – an interaction whose fundamental behavior is currently unknown. To this end, we fabricate an array of nanoscale pillar-and-channel switching devices from the epitaxial film stack and examine the angular dependence of the critical current pulse required to switch state.

Index Terms: Spin Orbit Torque Magnetic Random Access Memory

articleTitle: Stray Loss Evaluation of Power Transformers Using Simplified Air-core Model with Tank and Frame
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper reports stray loss generated in a tank, frames, and shields of a power transformer, and the shielding effect is qualitatively discussed for its design optimization. First, simplified transformer models composed of an air-core coil, a tank/frame, and a magnetic shield are newly proposed to reproduce stray loss generated in practical oil-filled power transformers. Then, accurate methods of measuring the stray loss in the proposed models were examined. The accuracy of the stray loss estimation based on a finite-element method was verified by comparing it with the measurement results.

articleTitle: Hybrid Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation and Deep Brain Stimulation in the Presence of an Implantable Pulse Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Due to promising research regarding the treatment of Parkinson’s Disease with Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS), the effects which TMS has in patients who have implanted Deep Brain Stimulators (DBS) needed to be accounted for. This is because many PD patients have DBS implants as a treatment to improve their motor control. TMS has also shown to improve long-term motor control of patients. But, TMS can negatively interfere with DBS probes, due to their high conductivity, potentially causing excess stimulation. Prior research regarding this phenomenon is highly conflicting and needs investigation. This study aims to reconcile this conflicting research by using a highly accurate finite element analysis approach in Sim4Life to determine the electric field distribution in patients with DBS probes undergoing TMS therapy. After considering proper DBS geometry by creating high-accuracy models of Medtronic 3389 DBS, including an Implantable Pulse Generator (IPG), high-voxel resolution, and multiple loops at the exit point of the cranium, which previous studies lack, we produced electric field results high enough to indicate hybrid DBS and TMS is unsafe.

articleTitle: Preparation of Sm-Fe-N hard magnetic nanopowder from micron-sized Sm-H and Fe mixed powder
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Metastable TbCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>-type phases of Sm-Fe-N nanopowder were successfully prepared. The Sm-H fine powder prepared by a jet mill process and Fe mixed powder were used as a raw material for nanopowder preparation by the recently developed low oxygen induction thermal process. The particle size was around 100 nm. Most of the obtained nanopowder consists of a core/shell structure. The core is Fe and the shell is Sm or Sm-Fe alloy, as observed by microstructure analysis. The coercivity of nitrided nanopowder is only 0.16 T at 300 K, which is due to the existence of a large amount of Fe core in the nanoparticle. The thermal plasma process is therefore a unique process with potential for one-through synthesis of nanocomposite powders by controlling the iron core size.

articleTitle: Switching Field Distributions in MRAM Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work we have measured the distribution of the easy axis orientation of MRAM elements using a technique based on the angular dependence of the coercivity. Large arrays of pillars with diameters of either 20 nm or 60 nm have been studied. A simple Stoner-Wohlfarth model that accounts for the dispersion in the easy axis distribution has been used to fit the data yielding a distribution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9.0^{\circ}$</tex> for the 20 nm pillars and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.5^{\circ}$</tex> for the 60 nm pillars. In the full paper the effect on the distribution of switching fields will be discussed together with measurements of the activation volume for both samples.

articleTitle: 3D-printed Magnetic Iron Material Modeling for High Speed Actuators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents the modeling procedure of a particular 3D printed iron material appropriate for low cost production of cores of actuators, a trend which is recently popular in the research community, with direct interest for the relevant industry. The characteristics of cores manufactured by a commercially available magnetic iron polylactic acid filament with low mass and cost are determined by considering a magnetic circuit of toroidal core geometry. A permanent magnet actuator prototype is then constructed by using equally 3D printing procedure to manufacture also the machine's casing and other individual parts by using a polyethylene terephthalate material. The motor's behavior is evaluated through finite element analysis in conjunction with equivalent surface impedance technique to account for the supply higher harmonic losses and the obtained results are validated by measurements.
