articleTitle: Detection of Metal Surface and Back Surface by Rectangular Wave Eddy Current Testing with Magneto Resistive Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Eddy current testing (ECT) at different frequencies can identify surface and back-surface defects caused by the skin effect. Therefore, we present the development of a rectangular wave eddy current testing (RECT) system using a magneto resistive (MR) sensor. The system uses rectangular wave excitation, which can generate both low and high frequency signals, and an MR sensor to detect the magnetic field components. A 12-mm thick aluminum plate with an artificial circular defect of 10 mm in diameter and 6 mm in depth was used as a specimen. The measurement results reveal that the developed system can effectively and quickly distinguish between surface and back-surface defects.

articleTitle: Resistance-Sum Architecture for Voltage-Controlled SOT-MRAM based Computing-in-Memory With Hybrid References
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To address the combination of computing-in-memory (CIM) architecture and magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM), a spin-transfer torque MRAM based resistance-sum-column architecture has been proposed to alleviate the low resistance problem that exists in the 2-terminal MRAM for CIM. In this paper, we propose a resistance-sum-row architecture with a hybrid reference based on the high performance 3-terminal voltage-controlled spin-orbit torque MRAM (VC-SOT-MRAM). This new architecture allows one-step parallel XNOR operation, and thus enabling ultra-high integration and throughput. The use of hybrid reference, which combines self-reference and auxiliary reference, is shown to effectively overcome the read errors. Our scheme is evaluated on a 28 nm technology node, showing extremely low latency (0.9 ns/write, <1 ns/read), low energy consumption (<3 fJ/bit), and high integration level (18 MTJ/Row), which make it a competitive candidate for Binary Neural Network (BNN) hardware.

articleTitle: A Novel Double Stator Hybrid-Excited Flux Reversal Permanent Magnet Machine with Halbach PM Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Flux modulated permanent magnet (FRPM) machines have been recognized as a promising candidate in various applications that require high torque density. Here, we propose a novel double-stator (DS) hybrid-excited (HE) FRPM machine with Halbach PM arrays. The sensitivity of the structural variables of the proposed machine was analyzed, and then the design variables were optimized using multi-objective optimization to achieve the design goals, including high torque density, high flux regulation capability, low cogging torque and torque ripple, and high efficiency. It was found that our proposed DS-HE-FRPM machine achieves significantly improved electromotive force, electromagnetic torque, and flux regulation capabilities. The rationale behind this improvement was given. The proposed machine can be utilized in EV applications.

articleTitle: Analytical Inverse Preisach Model and Its Comparison With Inverse J-A Model in Terms of Accuracy and Computational Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Inverse hysteresis model with magnetic flux density and magnetic field intensity as input and output respectively is more preferred, compared with the forward one, for resolving the electromagnetic problems of the electrical equipment in terms of magnetic vector potential, or for analyzing the electromagnetic issues of electrical equipment with voltage sources. And an inverse hysteresis model with high accuracy and high computation speed both has broader range of applications. However, the classical Preisach hysteresis model that is well known is formulated with the forward form, and involves the double integration of its distribution function, making it inconvenient and unpractical in the electrical engineering. In this paper, an analytical inverse Preisach model is proposed in this paper for the first time. To derive it, the analytical expressions of permeability for the initial magnetization curve, descending and ascending branches of hysteresis loop are derived using one closed form of Everett integral function. Subsequently the analytical inverse Preisach model is derived by the difference method, considering the reversible magnetization component that classical Preisach model cannot simulate with an odd function analytically. The experiment of one grain oriented silicon steel sample and one non-oriented silicon steel sample, under different magnetic excitation levels is conducted, and the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed analytical inverse Preisach model are confirmed by comparing its simulated hysteresis loops with the experimental ones and that computed with widely used inverse Jiles-Atherton hysteresis model.

articleTitle: Magnetic Analysis and Control of Three-phase Wireless EV Charging System Based on Quasi Z-source NPC Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The three-phase wireless charging system has the advantages of uniform magnetic fields, compact coil structures, and less output current ripple. In this paper, a novel three-phase wireless EV charging system based on a quasi-Z-source neutral point clamp (NPC) inverter is proposed to obtain a wide input voltage range with both voltage boost and buck abilities. The inverter operates with non-shoot-through mode and shoot-through mode and uses a specific space vector sequence to regulate the output power. The system model and modulation method are illustrated in detail. Furthermore, the working principle and magnetic feature of the three-phase coil system are simulated by finite element analysis. Finally, circuit simulations are conducted to prove the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Influence of Thickness on Eddy Current Losses in Materials Used as Clamping Structures in High-Power Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In the high-power electrical machines, different materials are used for clamping structures with given geometric dimensions. This paper studies the influence of the thickness of the clamping plate on eddy current losses for different materials at different frequencies. A simple configuration has been chosen in order to experimentally validate the numerical model of eddy current losses calculation and to highlight the effect of the thickness. A parametric study is presented and some interesting findings are discussed.

articleTitle: Impact of SOT & STT stress on MTJ degradation in SOT-MRAM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: SOT-MRAM devices are promising due to a decoupled read and write path. As such, SOT-MRAM is considered robust against MgO breakdown of the MTJ. However, during switching, high current densities flow through the thin metallic SOT layer causing significant self-heating of the MTJ. We investigate the degradation of the MTJ during hybrid SOT & STT stress. The resilience to breakdown is impacted by the SOT stress because of the elevated MTJ temperature, supported by thermal simulations.

articleTitle: Electrodeposited CoPt multilayered-nanowire for 3D memory device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, we construct composite structures of CoPt multilayer alloy nanowires by electrodeposition using a polycarbonate template membrane (PT). The holes in PT are subsequently filled with CoPt multilayer alloy films to form nanowires. The composition of the films can be controlled by modifying the potential to produce high anisotropy CoPt alloy multilayer nanowires. The CoPt multilayer nanowires have a periodic structure like bamboo with a chemical composition of (Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf>/Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</inf>Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">70</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. Polycrystalline and ferromagnetic characteristics were visible in a single layer of Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> nanowire. A vertical 3D magnetic domain wall memory has a ferromagnetic bit layer and a domain wall layer. Thus (Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf>/Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</inf>Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">70</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> multilayer nanowires can be used in domain wall controlled 3D memory devices like racetrack memory.

articleTitle: Structural and Magnetic Properties of CoFe/Sn-Doped Ge/Co2FeSi for Vertical Spin-Valve Devices on Si
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: For the vertically stacked semiconductor spintronic devices on Si, we develop a low-temperature growth technique of an epitaxial Ge layer with Sn doping on a Co-based Heusler alloy, Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>FeSi grown on Fe3Si/Si(111). Thanks to the Sn doping, the growth temperature for the Ge layer is significantly reduced down to ~110 °C, resulting in the suppression of the atomic interdiffusion between Ge and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>FeSi. The chemically abrupt interface leads to the improvement of magnetic properties of the all-epitaxial CoFe/Ge/Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>FeSi/Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Si/Si(111) structure. This study will pave a way for high-performance Ge-based spintronics devices on Si.

articleTitle: Domain-wall Tilting Angle Dependence on Current Pulse Width
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Domain-wall tilting in magnetic wires is accompanied when the domain-wall motion is driven by current. Theoretical research on the domain-wall tilting with respect to current densities has been extensively studied. However, experimental research on the current-driven domain-wall tilting has been received little attention due to various artifacts. In this paper, we report experimental results for the domain-wall tilting angle dependence on the current pulse width. Even if the sets of consecutive pulses have the same total length of the pulse widths and current density, the shorter pulses cases show less domain-wall tilting angles than the longer pulse cases.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Magnetic Field Energy Imaging of Magnetic Recording Head by Alternating Magnetic Force Microscopy with Superparamagnetic Tip
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Recent progress of high frequency (HF) magnetic materials and devices requires the precise imaging of HF magnetic fields. We have designed Alternating Magnetic Field Microscopy (A-MFM) with a superparamagnetic (SP) tip as a method to image HF magnetic field energy (MFE) near sample surface. The spatial resolution of MFE was confirmed to be better than that of magnetic field itself, due to shorter range interaction. In this work, we applied the method to image the MFE of magnetic writing head of perpendicular magnetic recording system. We applied amplitude modulated HF current with low modulation frequency of 89 Hz to the head and we imaged HF MFE by using the frequency modulated cantilever oscillation which was caused by low frequency magnetic force from the interaction between SP tip and the field.The imaging has been performed in a broad carrier frequency range 0.1 - 1000 MHz with minimal detectable wavelength of about 20 nm. We demonstrated the absence of image quality degradation with increasing field frequency. The magnetic spot size was close to the geometrical pole dimension, indicating the low tip-sample distance and minimal distortion.

articleTitle: Numerical and Micromagnetic Investigation of Strong Magnon-Magnon Coupling in Magnetic Insulator Bilayers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnon-magnon coupling between two ferromagnetic thin films is usually established by interlayer exchange interaction, which works as a boundary condition and in cases of strong interaction leads to the phenomenon of "anti-crossing". Previous studies have been devoted to ferromagnetic metal/magnetic insulator (FM/MI) bilayers; however, the level of damping in FMs here is usually 1-2 orders of magnitude greater than in MIs, causing a decrease in coherence time. Here, we show, for the first time, a strong coupling with a cooperativity of more than 10 between two MIs with experimentally relevant parameters via the finite element method in the frequency domain, consistent with our numerical method. This anti-crossing coupling in low-damping MI bilayers could pave the way for exciting prospects such as low-energy consumption magnonic devices.

articleTitle: Fast and Accurate Modelling of Laminated Cores in Electrical Machines using Homogenization and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Eddy currents induced in the individual laminations of ferromagnetic laminated cores are usually disregarded in conventional electrical machine simulations, and magnetic losses are then only evaluated a posteriori, by means of Steinmetz-like formulas. This approach yields however seriously inaccurate computed fields and losses whenever the operating frequency increases, or in the presence of higher harmonics, which is an issue of growing importance in industrial R&D. In this contribution we introduce a significantly improved and effective approach based on homogenization and neural networks. The method can be easily implemented in standard finite element packages.

articleTitle: Realization of Different Anisotropy Direction for Each Thin-film Magnetoimpedance Element on the Same Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have attempted to provide different anisotropy locally on the same substrate, i.e., different directions of easy axis in each area by combining simple Joule heating and the application of a magnetic field with permanent magnets. Orthogonal thin-film magnetoimpedance elements were fabricated on the same substrate, and the easy axis was successfully induced parallel to the width direction of each element, respectively. Each element shows the double-peak impedance profiles which is important to obtain higher sensitive magnetic field sensor. The results contribute to realizing multifunctional thin-film magnetic devices on substrates.

articleTitle: Magnetic, physical and chemical properties of consolidated Mn-Al-C bulk magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Rare-earth free permanent magnetic materials attract attention to reduce the dependency of critical materials for technological applications. Among others, Mn-Al based systems are stepping front due to their relatively good magnetic properties for specific application where the "gap" in the energy product are considered. In this work we investigate the structural, microstructural, magnetic and corrosion properties of Mn-Al-C material system which are of interest for application purposes.

articleTitle: Dynamic magnetization and specific loss powers of commercial magnetic nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, the heating properties of magnetic nanoparticle (MNP) samples were comprehensively examined. We quantified the specific loss power (SLP) values from dynamic magnetization measurements performed over wide ranges of intensities and frequencies of the applied AC magnetic field. SLP values of approximately 0.1–300 W/g were obtained over these ranges with the magnitudes depending on these field parameters, which could not be achieved from temperature measurements. Because we used commercial magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs), our results were compared with previously reported heating properties. This is important for developing the research on MNPs for hyperthermia. The intrinsic loss power (ILP) was also calculated. The specific features unique to the properties of each MNP sample were clarified from the intensity and frequency dependences of the ILP.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Monoclinic Fe3Se4 doped with transition metals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report density functional theory (DFT) study of the magnetic properties of Fe3Se4 doped with transition metals, TM (Co, Cr, Ni and Mn), where TM ions are doped in Fe sites to yield Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3−x</inf>(TM)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (x = 0.5). Screening of the exchange coupling interaction and magnetization modifications were performed upon the substitution of Fe by 3d-transition metals at various Fe sites in the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> structure. Our study reveals that doping of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> with 3d-elements at Fe sites does not remove antiferromagnetic (AFM) coupling across layers. Although a slight increase in magnetization can be obtained at low Ni-doping. The origin of this increase could be attributed to the AFM superexchange coupling of Fe across the Se planes. This coupling is exhibited by elements with more than half-filled electron shell, i.e. Fe is such an element. Moreover, the exchange coupling between layers of Fe increases strongly as function of interlayer spacing (a lattice parameter) for both pristine and TM-doped Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, while the magnetizations of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> alloys do not change significantly.

articleTitle: Tunable Creation of Bimerons in Confined Circular Nanodots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A magnetic bimeron consisting of a meron and an antimeron is considered as analogues of skyrmions in the in-plane magnetized systems and possess great application potential in spintronic based devices. Here, we explore the static properties of bimerons which are stabilized during the magnetization reversal process in confined circular nanodots. We also show the tunable control of topology of bimerons by applying an out of plane bias field of varying strength and direction.

articleTitle: Spin waves softening in thin films with perpendicular anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Mode softening is an important issue for phase transition-related phenomena. An example of such a phase transition is the spin reorientation transition between a uniformly magnetized system and a domain pattern. Here, we theoretically investigate the effects of the value of perpendicular magnetocrystalline anisotropy, the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, magnetic field bias values, and damping on spin wave propagation in uniformly magnetized thin films. We report that perpendicular anisotropy induces the formation of a minimum in the dispersion relation of Damon-Eshbach-type waves for a non-zero wave vector. The frequency of this minimum significantly deepens as the value of the magnetic field decreases and becomes the global minimum of the dispersion relation. We demonstrate, that the value of damping as well as the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction have an important influence on the mode softening process. Finally, we show that as the magnetic field decreases and the mode softening strengthens, the amplitude of the response of the softened SWs increases significantly. Our results are important both for the fundamental understanding of spin wave mode softening and spin reorientation transition and in applications such as sensors.

articleTitle: Anomalous magnetic anisotropy behaviour in Co-rich and Fe-rich glass-coated microwires under applied stress
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this article we study the effect of annealing temperature and applied stress on magnetic properties of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">71.80</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13.27</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11.02</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.99</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.92</inf> and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">65.34</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12.00</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10.20</inf>Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8.48</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.90</inf>Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.08</inf> microwires. An anomalous behaviour of the coercitive field is observed with applied stress indicating nontrivial changes in the magnetostriction constant of the microwires. The possible effect of applied stimuli on the magnetic anisotropy and magnetostriction constant in both microwires is also discussed.

articleTitle: Optimum Air Gap Selection in Powder Core Inductors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The requirements of magnetics for power electronics are high power density and low power losses, driven by the need for more compact and more efficient power converters. Metal powder materials are a common choice for high power and high frequency inductors subject to a magnetic field bias applied because of the high saturation flux density and their "distributed" air gap property that allows adopting these materials in un-gapped core configurations. Nevertheless, in certain conditions, a concentrated air gap could maximize the overall inductance factor for a given winding configuration (i.e. the number of turns). Therefore, this paper proposes a straightforward procedure to maximize the inductance factor of metal powder magnetic cores by selecting the optimum air gap length for a specified design operating point. The proposed methodology is theoretically described and then experimentally validated on an XFlux 60 core from Magnetics<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>.

articleTitle: Contribution of Nd-rich alloys to the multi-main-phase LaCe-based sintered magnets with high coercivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, we prepared MMP-LaCe35 sintered magnets with excellent coercivity by regulating the composition of Nd-rich Nd-Fe-B alloys. The origin of the high coercivity and the variation in magnetic properties caused by the addition of Nd-rich alloys with different compositions were revealed through detailed analysis of phase composition, microstructure, and magnetization reversal characteristics.

articleTitle: Writing information by current pulses in antiferromagnetic Mn2Au
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Antiferromagnets (AFMs) are promising for future spintronic applications because of their fast dynamics and lack of stray fields. For the required switching of the Néel vector (staggered magnetization), a current induced bulk Néel spin-orbit torque (NSOT) is most promising. Here we demonstrate current pulse induced complete, remanent, and reversible Néel vector switching of epitaxial Mn2Au(001) thin films. A current polarity dependence demonstrates an NSOT acting on AFM domain walls. We correlate direct imaging of the Néel vector reorientation by x-ray photoemission electron microscopy with measurements of the associated anisotropic magnetoresistance [1].

articleTitle: Strain effects on magnetic compensation and spin reorientation transition of Co/Gd synthetic ferrimagnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Synthetic ferrimagnets are an attractive material class for spintronics as they provide access to all optical switching of magnetization and, at the same time, they allow ultrafast domain wall motion at magnetic compensation. In this work, we study systematically the effects of strain on the magnetic compensation and perpendicular magnetic anisotropy of Co/Gd and Co/Gd/Co/Gd synthetic ferrimagnets. Firstly, the spin reorientation transition of a bilayer system is investigated in wedge type samples and we report an increase in the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in the presence of in-plane strain. Secondly, the magnetic compensation of a quadlayer is studied. We find that magnetic compensation of this multilayer synthetic ferrimagnetic system is not altered by strain. This confirms that magnetic compensation in this type of system is not affected by magnetoelastic anisotropy, making this material system ideal for applications where resilience against strain is required.

articleTitle: Perpendicular Magnetization Switching in Heusler Alloy Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Electrically manipulating magnetic moment by spin-orbit torque (SOT) has great potential applications in magnetic memories and logic devices. Although there have been rich SOT studies on magnetic heterostructures, low interfacial thermal stability and high switching current density still remain an issue. Here, highly textured, polycrystalline Heusler alloy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Mn}_{\mathrm{x}}\text{Pt}_{\mathrm{y}}\text{Ge}$</tex> (MPG) films with various thicknesses are directly deposited on thermally oxidized silicon wafers. The perpendicular magnetization of the MPG single layer can be reversibly switched by electrical current pulses with a magnitude as low as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.1\times 10^{10}\text{Am}^{-2}$</tex>, as evidenced by both the electrical transport and the magnetic optical measurements. The switching is shown to arise from inversion symmetry breaking due to the vertical composition gradient of the films after sample annealing. The SOT effective fields of the samples are analysed systematically. It is found that the SOT efficiency increases with the film thickness, suggesting a robust bulk-like behaviour in the single magnetic layer. Moreover, a memristive characteristic has been observed due to multi-domain switching property in the single layer MPG device. This work proves that the MPG is a good candidate to be utilized in high-density and efficient MRAM devices and other novel spintronics.

articleTitle: Theoretical demonstration of the electron spin wave filter in semiconductor two-dimensional electron gas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Electron spin waves (ESWs) [1], [2] are spatial spin structures realized by persistent spin helix (PSH) state [3] originating from momentum-dependent effective magnetic fields in a semiconductor two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG). The ESWs are attracting much attention as new information carriers with wave properties in semiconductors. Based on the nature of the ESWs, multiplexing, simultaneous transfer, and filtering functions are expected for parallel information processing applications [4]. In this study, we theoretically focus on the filtering functions and demonstrate an ESW filter by means of Monte Carlo (MC) simulation to clarify its feasibility.

articleTitle: Synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction study on nucleation and growth of nanocrystalline phase in Fe-Si-B-P-Cu-C amorphous alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Fe-Si-B-P-Cu-C nanocrystalline alloys are soft magnetic materials with high saturation magnetic flux density and low loss. Since the magnetic properties change depending on the heat treatment conditions, there has been interested in the close correlation between the heat treatment meathod and the magnetic property. In order to obtain excellent magnetic properties, it is important to derive the optimal heat treatment condition for nanocrystallization during the nucleation and growth process of the α-Fe. In-situ observation of the nucleation and growth of the nanocrystalline phases using synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction provides direct evidence that the grain growth rate and final state grain size vary with annealing temperature.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Rotor Bridge and Fixing Hole for Spoke-Type PMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of the spoke-type permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) for driving systems. The electromagnetic performance of the PMSMs with different rotor bridges and fixing holes is studied, including the no-load characteristic, cogging torque, output torque, and torque ripple. The location of the fixing holes in the rotor core is optimized to increase the output torque capability. The results show that the output torque of the single side bridge is increased due to the reduction of the leakage flux compared with the double side bridge structure. The inner side bridge design of three rotor structures has the highest output torque but will lead to a larger torque ripple. Furthermore, the mechanical strength of the different rotors at the maximum speed is investigated by finite-element analysis (FEA) to verify the feasibility of the structures. Finally, a 3000r/min 10kW prototype has been manufactured and the experimental results validate the analysis methods in this paper.

articleTitle: Investigation of Resting Motor Threshold Variabiliy in Schizophrenia Patients during Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a noninvasive neuromodulation technique utilized to treat several neuropsychiatric disorders. Schizophrenia patients typically experience positive and negative symptoms which are commonly treated with antipsychotic medications. Repetitive (r)TMS is being tested as a treatment to alleviate these symptoms by increasing the cortical stimulation. TMS stimulation strength is determined by the resting motor threshold (RMT) which is collected from single pulse stimulation to the M1 brain region. However, the effective stimulation intensity within the cortex is dependent on many individual factors. In this study, 23 Schizophrenia participants' magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were used to create anatomically accurate head models. These head models were then used to calculate the coil to cortex distance (CCD), and finite element analysis (FEA) was performed to calculate the induced electric field on the gray matter. Functional MRI was also performed to evaluate functional connectivity. These MRI derived parameters were then evaluated to establish their relationship with empirically collected RMT. CCD did not correlate with RMT suggesting CCD alone is not indicative of patient specific cortical architecture. Simulated electric field strength (EFS) negatively correlated with CCD suggesting the induced electric field in the brain is influenced by the CCD. We also observed a negative linear relationship between RMT and functional connectivity suggesting functional connectivity influences TMS treatment outcomes. Future investigations into RMT variability should incorporate quantitative fMRI Independent Component data with a larger sample size to further establish the relationship with RMT.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of α" -Fe16N2 nanopowder
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The α"- Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nitrides are known to be a potential candidate for use as rare-earth-free magnets. Since the new production technique of the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanopowder is developed and the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanopowder is now available, the structures and magnetic properties of the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanopowder are characterized in this study. It was found that the average particle size of the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanopowder was found to be around 50 nm and the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanopowder consisted of the α"- Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> phase. The magnetic measurements revealed that the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanopowder exhibited a high saturation magnetization of 168 emu/g and a relatively high coercivity of 2.65 kOe.

articleTitle: Thermal noise magnetometry as an emerging magnetic characterization technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This contribution gives an overview of recent advances in thermal noise magnetometry (TNM), an emerging method for the characterization of magnetic nanoparticles. This method is unique as it does not rely on measuring the response to an external field excitation. Instead it passively measures the fluctuations in the magnetization of the particle ensemble in thermal equilibrium. Through theoretical and experimental advances, we show how TNM can now be applied to a variety of applications in a practical and accessible manner. Specifically, we show how TNM can be used to study aggregation processes in biological media.

articleTitle: Fundamental study of Magnetic Particle Composite Core made by Fused Deposition Modeling Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Fused deposition modeling method (FDM) using resin material is one of the additive manufacturing techniques, and low cost equipments are available as 3D printer. However, magnetic materials are difficult to use as materials for FDM because of high melting point. In this study, a material composed of magnetic particles and thermoplastic resin was prepared and its magnetic properties after processing were evaluated. First, a linear filament material was produced and then processed into a magnetic device by the FDM. The shape of devices are toroidal and cubic block with narrow slits. The relative permeability after processing was 1.5. A shape anisotropy has been induced by a three-dimensional shape, the anisotropy was small due to weak coupling between particles inside.

articleTitle: Study of recycle process of Sm2Fe17N3 bonded magnet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have studied the recycling process of Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> injection molded bonded magnets. When sprue runners generated during injection molding were mixed with new pellets and put into the injection molding process, Br did not decrease, iHc did not decrease more than 10%, and mechanical strength did not decrease more than 5%. We also conducted experiments assuming the market recovery of Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> bonded magnets. It was proven in principle that the material can be recycled back to the three locations of the Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> production process by dividing it into cases based on magnetic properties, mechanical strength, and the amount of foreign matter.

articleTitle: Temperature dependent spin gap in multiferroic 2D-XY antiferromagnet Ba2CoGe2O7 under applied magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report an inelastic neutron scattering study on the low-energy magnetic excitations of Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CoGe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf> single crystals under applied magnetic fields for several fixed temperatures. Recently, a spin gap of about 0.1 meV has been observed under zero magnetic field and interpreted as an effect of spin-nematic interaction [1]. However, we have predicted such gap via linear spin wave theory by introducing the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction in the spin Hamiltonian. We have observed a spin gap of 0.105 meV in energy at 2 K under zero magnetic field and the gap energy decreases with increasing temperature. Temperature dependent spin gap also evolves under an applied magnetic field. Our results enlighten the discussion on understanding the origin of the zero-field spin gap in details.

articleTitle: Examination of Thinning Inspection Method for Ferromagnetic Steel Tubes using Velocity Effect of Static Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: When an electromagnetic sensor composed of a static excitation coil and a detection coil is moved in a steel tube at high speed, an eddy current is generated in the steel tube. If a defect is present in the steel tube, the defect may be detected by the change in the eddy current. Generally, the ferromagnetic heat transfer tubes in oil and chemical plants are inspected for defects by moving an internally inserted electromagnetic sensor at a high speed of about 1 m/s. Although there have been some past research reports for the detection of localized thinning in the steel tube, there are no reports for a wide range of thinning in the steel tube. Therefore, in this research, it is investigated a thickness measurement method for a wide range of thinning on the steel tube using only static magnetic field. As a result, it was shown that it is possible to measure the thickness in the steel tube by flux density inside the detection coil of the proposed static magnetic inspection sensor moving at 1m/s. The flux density in the steel tube is evaluated by the 3-D nonlinear FEM considering the velocity effect.

articleTitle: Application of various materials with negative saturation magnetostriction to vibration power generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Various materials with negative saturation magnetostriction were applied to an U-shaped unimorph device for vibration power generation using inverse magnetostrictive effect. When a fcc Fe-Ni metal with the positive saturation magnetostriction was attached as an unimorph core to the front side of the U-shaped frame, larger values of the open circuit voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">op</inf> were obtained in comparison with that of the frame core device without the sample. However, when a fcc Ni metal with the negative saturation magnetostriction was attached to the front side of the U-shaped frame, the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">op</inf> value of this device was smaller than that of the frame core device. Larger V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">op</inf> values were obtained by attaching a fcc Ni metal to the back side of the U-shaped frame. Similar behaviors were observed in the devices using a bcc Fe metal and a hcp Co metal with negative saturation magnetostriction. Therefore, the back side setting is effective for the application of materials with negative saturation magnetostriction to the U-shaped unimorph device.

articleTitle: Magneto-electric signal due to microwave heating in ferromagnetic/nonmagnetic bilayer system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetic voltage due to the microwave heating effect in a CoFeB/W bilayer system has been investigated experimentally. We find that the contribution from the microwave heating effect is comparable to that from the heating due to the ferromagnetic resonance at the specific field direction. We also comfirm that the magnetic signal is caused by the entanglement between anomalous Nernst and inverse spin Hall effects. This result provides an important aspect in future energy hervesting devices based on spin.

articleTitle: Field angle-dependent bubble lattice formation in Re/Co/Pt multilayers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Formation of bubble lattices stable at room temperature is investigated in asymmetric epitaxial [Re(1 nm)/Co(d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Co</inf>)/Pt(1 nm)]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> multilayers with thickness of the Co component layer, d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Co</inf>, ranging between 0.8 nm and 2.0 nm. This thickness range covers uniaxial anisotropy transition from perpendicular to in-plane with d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Co</inf> increase. We study evolution of domain structure at remanence depending on the sample magnetic history described by: (i) applied field inclination angle measured from the sample plane and (ii) the field strength. The bubble lattice appears only in a narrow field inclination angle range, being specific for d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Co</inf>. With increase in d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Co</inf> the required inducing field rotates from parallel to perpendicular orientation relative to the sample plane. The maximum density of the bubble lattice decreases from 18 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> to 1 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> with d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Co</inf> increase from 0.8 nm to 2.0 nm. Interpretation of the experimental results is supported by density-functional theory calculations and micromagnetic modelling. Obtained experimental and theoretical results suggest that the observed bubbles are topologically protected skyrmions.

articleTitle: Toroidal Nanocrystalline Powder Core with Trapezoidal Cross Section
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This digest proposes a toroidal nanocrystalline powder core with a trapezoidal cross section. The non-uniform magnetic flux density distribution of toroidal cores with different shapes of cross section is discussed, and inductance calculation equations are derived. The local electromagnetic interference (EMI) radiation at the inductor edge is investigated by simulation, and evident EMI reduction is observed in the toroidal core with a trapezoidal cross section. A 10-turn coil is wound on the cores, the measured inductance values show a good match with the simulation and calculation values. By adopting the trapezoidal cross section, a 30 % reduction of the material can be achieved in compromising 17 % inductance.

articleTitle: Development of BiFeO3-Based Multiferroic Thin Films with Excellent Magnetic Properties and Investigation of Their Etching Resistance for Magnetic Nano Device Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The control of magnetization using electric field is a key solution to reduce energy consumptions of magnetic devices against the operation method with magnetic field and spin current. BiFeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (BFO) based multiferroic thin films can be used as a candidate material for this application. But the antiferromagnetic (G-type) configuration in pure BFO is a barrier from application point of view, therefore magnetic properties of BFO based materials should be improved by using substitution elements. We fabricated (B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i,L</inf>)(Fe,Co)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (L = La, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd, Dy, Er) thin films and also found some suitable film materials with excellent magnetic properties for various magnetic nano device applications. Following successful sample manufacturing, we investigated the resistance of the films against etching for microfabrication to apply the films in magnetic nano devices.

articleTitle: A Spinwave Time-Multiplexed Ising Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We present a spinwave-based time-multiplexed Ising Machine (SWIM) where artificial Ising spins are formed with ns-long spinwave RF pulses propagating in a delay line based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5-\mu m$</tex> thick Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG) film. The phase of artificial Ising spins is binarized using an off-the-shelf phase-sensitive microwave amplifier and the coupling between spins is implemented with microwave delay cables. Thanks to the very low spinwave group velocity, the 7-mm long YIG delay line can host an 8-spin MAX-CUT combinatorial optimization problem and solve it in less than 4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu s$</tex> while consuming only 7 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu J$</tex>.

articleTitle: Reduction of Iron Loss on Motor Stator Cores by means of Secondary Current Heating Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, the “secondary current heating method,” which has been proposed in the previous reports, was used to heat-treat the laminated stator cores of actual motors to reduce iron loss. To evaluate the magnetic properties of the laminated stator cores including the teeth, an inner core was installed inside the stator to form a closed magnetic path with the two teeth, back yoke, and inner core. The air gap between the stator and the inner core causes the B-H loops to be tilted compared to the one of the back yoke, though, it was found that the iron loss was reduced by about 30% in the laminated stator core after heat treatment.

articleTitle: A Study on the Shape of a Small Wind Turbine with Fractional Slot Concentrated Winding to Realize Zero Cogging Level
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A typical wind turbine has a slot structure. This structure causes a permeance difference in airgap. And this permeance difference creates cogging torque, which acts as a brake when driving the wind turbine. Therefore, the size of cogging torque should be small in order to operate even in breeze. In this paper, in order to reduce cogging torque, first, a comparison of pole slot combinations was performed. In addition, a pole slot combination with a small cogging torque was selected, and a study on the pole arc ratio of a turbine having a FSCW (fractional slot concentrated winding) was conducted. Next, the pole arc ratio and the output characteristics according to the stator and rotor tapering models were examined for the FSCW model. Then, the output characteristics such as cogging torque and efficiency were analyzed by changing the variable of a turbine. Finally, a model that can realize the level of 'zero cogging' was designed and the output characteristics of each model were compared through FEA.

articleTitle: Thickness Measurement of Nickel Plating on the Back Side using a Combined Magnetic Field with AC of Two Different Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Nickel plating is used on the surface of rolled steel plates in paper mills. And it is important to monitor the thickness of the nickel layer of the nickel plating plate. In this research, the electromagnetic inspection method for the thickness of the nickel plating using the difference in electromagnetic properties between the nickel and the base material steel is proposed. On the other hand, the nickel plating plates have mechanical limitations in the papermaking process, so it is necessary to evaluate the thickness of the nickel layer from the back side of the nickel plating plate. Therefore, the electromagnetic inspection method for measuring the thickness of nickel plating on the back side using a combined magnetic field of two different frequencies is proposed. In this proposed method, it is possible to measure the nickel plating thickness of about 50 μm from the back side of the nickel steel plate.

articleTitle: Microscopic Calculation of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction in a Rashba Ferromagnet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We theoretically study the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in metallic magnets with strong spin-orbit interaction. We derive a general formula for the DMI in free energy in terms of Green’s functions. Generally, the DMI coefficient in free energy can be different from that in spin-wave dispersion. We show the relationship between these coefficients. Using the general formula, we investigate the DMI in a Rashba ferromagnet. We observe that the DMI coefficient shows a strong dependence on electron density and a higher-order dependence on the spin-orbit interaction.

articleTitle: Magnetic Nanowires versus nano/micro-particles for Cancer Cell Destruction by Magneto-mechanical Actuation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magneto-mechanical actuation induces the most destruction on cancer cells when employed on magnetic nanomaterials with shape anisotropy as well as high values of saturation magnetization. The aim of this study is to compare the effects of magnetic nanoparticles and magnetic nanowires on human osteosarcoma cells. In this paper we present the results obtained using Fe-(Cr/Ti/Mn)-Nb-B magnetic nanoparticles and Ni-Fe and Co-Fe nanowires for cancer cell destruction using magneto-mechanical actuation.

articleTitle: Single layer spin-orbit torque in Mn2Ru09Ga
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The full magneto-galvanic tensor of the non-centrosymmetric Heusler alloy Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ru<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">09</inf>Ga in thin film form was determined. The samples are expected to exhibit single layer spin-orbit torques due to the lack of a crystal centre of inversion and due to the broken symmetry at the thin film interfaces. By analysing the first and second harmonic response of the longitudinal and transverse voltages we extract the magnitude and symmetry of the current-induced spin-orbit torque as well as the contributions originating from thermal gradients induced by the bias current. The dominating torque term is damping-like (τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DL</inf>), due to the thin-film geometry, and reaches a magnitude of τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DL</inf> = 4.38 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−14</sup> TA<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Effect of Substitution in the Heating Efficiency of CuFe2O4 Nanoparticles for Magnetic Hyperthermia Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Superparamagnetic nanoparticles have undergone detailed research for decades and have been investigated for potential use in magnetic hyperthermia and certain other biomedical applications. In this work, we have synthesized Cobalt-substituted CuFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanoparticles (Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, x=0.1, 0.3, 0.5) by co-precipitation method. The structural properties of the samples are studied using X-ray diffractometer, Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, and Energy dispersive X-ray technique. To validate the possible suitability of the fabricated samples in magnetic hyperthermia application, magnetic and induction heating analysis is also performed. Comparing the computed specific absorption rates for each sample, it can be shown that Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> with an optimal concentration of 1 mg has the maximum heating efficiency.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Quantum Systems with Magnetic p-bits
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The slowing down of Moore’s Law has led to a crisis as the computing workloads of Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms continue skyrocketing. There is an urgent need for scalable and energy-efficient hardware catering to the unique requirements of AI algorithms and applications. In this environment, probabilistic computing with p-bits emerged as a scalable, domain-specific, and energy-efficient computing paradigm, particularly useful for probabilistic applications and algorithms.In particular, spintronic devices such as stochastic magnetic tunnel junctions (sMTJ) show great promise in designing integrated p-computers. Here, we examine how a scalable probabilistic computer with such magnetic p-bits can be useful for an emerging field combining machine learning and quantum physics.

articleTitle: Effect of B-site Substitution Element and Substitution Amount on Magnetic Properties in (Bi,La)(Fe1-yMy)O3 (M = Co, Ni) Ferromagnetic and Ferroelectric Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: High saturation magnetization, perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, and high Curie temperature are required for ferromagnetic/ferroelectric thin films to apply to highly integrated magnetic devices driven by electric field. To improve the magnetic properties of the BiFeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based ferromagnetic/ferroelectric thin films, (Bi,La)(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-y</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> or (Bi,La)(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-y</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films were fabricated. Here, the amount of substituted La for Bi in the A-site was fixed at about 50 at%, and the amount of substituted Co or Ni for Fe in the B-site was varied from 0 to 35 at%, respectively. As a result, high saturation magnetization and high perpendicular magnetic anisotropy were obtained in the thin films with Co substitution of 28 at% or Ni substitution of 30 at%. Especially, the high saturation magnetization of 78 emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> was obtained in (Bi,La)(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.72</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.28</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, and high normalized coercive force of perpendicular to the film plane by coercive force of parallel to the film plane (perpendicular magnetic anisotropy) of 4.1 and high Curie temperature of more than 475 °C were obtained respectively in (Bi,La)(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.70</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.30</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>.

articleTitle: Spin Logic and Emergent Spin Phenomena in 2D Materials Heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials and their van der Waals heterostructures represent a new platform to realize novel spin-based phenomena and device applications. We demonstrated robust spin interconnect, spin multiplexing, and multifunctional spin logic operation using large-area CVD graphene based spintronic devices. In order to control the spin polarization in graphene, we engineered 2D material heterostructures by combining the best of different materials in one ultimate unit and realized strong proximity induced spin-orbit coupling and magnetism. We showed that the graphene-based heterostructures are also useful for the detection of current-induced spin-polarization in topological materials and proximity interactions. Finally, room temperature spin-valve devices could be realized using van der Waals ferromagnet in heterostructures with graphene. These findings open a new platform for electrical creation and gate-control of spin polarization and provide new opportunities for all-2D heterostructure spintronic devices and integrated spin circuits.

articleTitle: Resonant microwave absorption in Mo-doped LaMnO3 investigated using a vector network analyzer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We investigated the magnetization and magnetic field dependent microwave absorption for multiple frequencies (f = 10 MHz to 7 GHz) at room temperature in LaMn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> series from x = 0.0 to 0.1. We focus on the parent compound and 6% Mo-doped LaMnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Mo-substitution transforms the parent compound from the antiferromagnetic insulator to a ferromagnetic conductor by inducing a mixed valence of manganese ions (Mn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> and Mn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>) which give rise to the double exchange interaction. The transition temperature was found to increase drastically from T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> = 140 K (Neel temperature) to T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> = 240 K for x = 0.06. Microwave transmission measured using a network analyzer shows a dip at a specific field for a frequency f greater than or equal to 2 GHz and it shifts up linearly with frequency, which we suggest to resonance microwave absorption due precessing spins (paramagnetic resonance). The dip shows a maximum amplitude for x = 0.06 in the series, and a minimum amplitude for x = 0.0. The resonance field and linewidth at 6 GHz was found to have no correlation with increasing content of Mo cation.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Magnetic Induction System Development with Synchronous MPI Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, a pre-clinical magnetic induction system for drug delivery was designed for bladder cancer of tiny animals. Firstly, to ensure the induced drug-modified magnetic particles (MNPs) were visible in magnetic particle imaging (MPI), the drug delivery capacity of several types of superparamagnetic MNPs, which were suitable for MPI imaging were evaluated under different magnetic conditions. Experimental result showed that the Nanoeast 30nm MNP showed the best performance, that was, when the field strength was more than 260mT, and the field gradient was 1.6T/m, the inducting velocity of MNPs is up to 2mm/s under physiological conditions. Further, epi, mmc and hcpt which were frequently used in bladder cancer treatment were selected and modified to the Nanoeast MNPs, and the CCK8 and microscopic cell experiments showed the effectiveness of the drug modified MNPs. Moreover, 20ug Fe of modified MNPs was well imaged in a home-made open-bore MPI system. Finally, a multi-coil structure was designed according to the necessary magnetic conditions considering magnetic field strength, field gradient and animal size. The three narrow coils are closely arranged coaxially and equidistantly. The MNPs were well induced and convergence length of 5mm in a blood vessel.

articleTitle: Room-temperature magnetic antiskyrmions and anisotropic fractal magnetic domain textures in (Fe,Ni,Pd)3P with S4 symmetry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Antiskyrmions, new topological spin textures with a topological number of the opposite sign to that of skyrmions, have attracted much attention in the research field of topological magnets. Here, we review our recent progress on a new antiskyrmion-host material with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> symmetry. We find that the magnetic anisotropy of schreibersite (Fe,Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>P is significantly modified by chemical doping, and Lorentz transmission electron microscopy shows that stable antiskyrmions form above room temperature in thin plates of (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.63</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.30</inf>Pd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.07</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>P. The size of the magnetic domain textures increases with increasing the crystal thickness, and sawtooth-shaped fractal magnetic domain patterns appear near the surface of thick crystals as revealed by magnetic force microscopy. Furthermore, recent small-angle neutron scattering measurements characterize anisotropic fractal nature of the magnetic domain walls in bulk crystals. These results demonstrate that uniaxial magnetic anisotropy and magnetic dipolar interaction in addition to Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction play an important role in this material.

articleTitle: High-throughput determination of structure-property relationships of magnetic nanoparticles using a multi-detector chromatographic approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic nanoparticles (MNP) possess unique magnetic properties which makes them highly suitable for various biomedical applications, including magnetic particle imaging (MPI). The magnetic behavior of MNP in a particular application depends largely on their size, morphology, structure, and surface modification. Therefore, it is essential to use various characterization techniques to systematically optimize MNP to achieve the desired magnetic effect and ensure the reproducibility and quality of commercial products. However, MNP samples typically exhibit a dispersion of particle properties (e.g. size) that may increase in biological environments. While ensemble methods provide acceptable results, they are not selective when applied to mixed particle populations. To reliably characterize MNP, we use a combination of chromatographic separation techniques with coupled complementary detectors for structural and magnetic characterization.

articleTitle: Vibronic excitations in the resonant inelastic x-ray scattering spectra of spin-orbit Mott insulators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) spectroscopy is a powerful tool to investigate elementary excitations in spin-orbit Mott insulators. Recent RIXS data of cubic Ru<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>+ and Ir<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>+ antifiluorites show puzzling features that cannot be explained by spin-orbit theories: the relevance of the dynamic JahnTeller effect was mentioned, whereas the evidence and its fingerprints in the RIXS spectra are unknown. Here, we address these issues based on ab initio calculations. We simulated the RIXS spectra fully taking account of the dynamic Jahn- Teller effect, which shows a good agreement with the experimental spectra, confirming the presence of the dynamic Jahn- Teller effect in the excited states. We revealed that the experimental RIXS spectra have several peaks that come from the dynamic Jahn- Teller effect rather than the standard crystal-field splitting. Our results suggest that the dynamic Jahn- Teller effect is an important factor in adequately interpreting the RIXS spectra of spin-orbit Mott insulators.

articleTitle: Investigation on Wide-Speed Operation of a New Five-Phase Fault-Tolerant Interior Permanent Magnet Motor from Perspective of Flux-Intensifying Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, a new five-phase fault-tolerant interior permanent magnet (FT-IPM) motor with flux-intensifying effect for wide-speed operation is investigated. Since the demagnetization fault and the weak saliency characteristic of the conventional FT-IPM motors, a new design idea about "magnetic-barrier guidance" is proposed for improving the characteristic of the inverse saliency. Consequently, the wide-speed operating capacity and the lower risk of irreversible demagnetization can be well achieved with the new design method. Futhermore, to ensure high-reliability operation of the drive system, good fault tolerance can be well implemented simultaneously. Then, the wide-speed operating capacity and saliency ratio of the traditional FT-IPM motor and the proposed five-phase FT-IPM motor with flux-intensifying effect are investigated and compared. The experimental results show the good performance of the back EMFs, fault-tolerant operation, and high-speed operation, which verifies the validity of the proposed five-phase FT-IPM motor.

articleTitle: Design Optimization using Asymmetric Rotor in IPMSM for Torque Ripple Reduction considering Forward and Reverse Directions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In the interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM), an asymmetric rotor is used as a design method to reduce torque ripple or cogging torque by adjusting the saturation of the rotor core. The advantage of an asymmetric rotor is that it can reduce torque ripple or cogging torque in the forward direction while maintaining the average torque or output power. However, when driving in the reverse direction, the torque ripple or cogging torque can be increased. Therefore, the asymmetric rotor produces different characteristics in the forward and reverse directions. In this study, the asymmetric rotor shape is designed using an optimization technique taking into consideration the rotating direction. The optimum design is performed based on the symmetric rotor as the base model. When rotating in the forward direction, the asymmetric rotor has a lower torque ripple than the symmetric rotor, and when rotating in the reverse direction, the asymmetric and symmetric rotors are designed to be similar. The kriging surrogate model was used to determine the optimum design point that satisfied the constraints. Finally, a symmetric and asymmetric rotor was manufactured and evaluated through tests.

articleTitle: Electrically controllable exchange bias via interface magnetoelectric effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Exchange bias is an unidirectional magnetic anisotropy that often arise from interfacial interaction of a ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic layers. In this article, we show that a metallic layer with spin-orbit interaction can induces an exchange bias in the neighbouring ferromagnetic layer via an interface magnetoelectric effect. In linear response regime, the interface magnetoelectric effect is induced by Rashba spin-orbit interaction at the interface. Due to the interface magnetoelectric effect, the exchange bias can be controlled by electric field.

articleTitle: Structural Phase Transformation and Magnetic Properties Induced by Thermal Analysis with Different Gaseous Environments in Iron-Doped Manganese Oxide Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We used a facile thermal treatment process to explore the structural phase transformations and magnetic behavior of iron-doped manganese oxide nanoparticles. The structural phase transformations, as well as magnetic properties, strongly depend on the gaseous environments. For samples prepared in the reducing gas, the tetragonal phase dominated the structure. The obtained saturation magnetizations and coercive force are about 20.7-21.4 emu/g and 75-100 Oe, respectively.

articleTitle: Large spin conversion in the Fe/graphene/Pt interface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The realization of novel memory devices is essential due to the increasing requirements in data storage and processing. The optimization of spin-to-charge interconversion is currently one of the most sought-after topics in spintronics, since spin-orbit torque devices promise a very fast an efficient framework to develop them. In this work, we show a large enhancement, twenty times, of the spin-to-charge current conversion when inserting an atomically-thick epitaxial graphene between epitaxial iron and platinum layers. We measure this using the spin-pumping (SP) ferromagnetic resonance technique. This work opens wide possibilities for spin conversion engineering 2D materials.

articleTitle: A Novel Speed-Sensorless Wireless Universal Motor with Bidirectional Movement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel wireless universal motor. By eliminating the motor controller and position sensor, the secondary side is very simple and robust. Besides, bidirectional movement can be achieved. The key is to employ a self-driving circuit at the secondary side. Also, the advantages of the small size and large starting torque of universal motors can be retained. Hence, the proposed wireless universal motor is very suitable to be sealed and employed in isolated environments, such as pipeline pigging. A series of simulations have been conducted, which confirms that the secondary side can be self-driven, and the motor speed can be detected at the primary side.

articleTitle: Heat magnetizing method for high-performance neodymium magnets for EV and HEV motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In recent years, there has been much research on magnets used in EV and HEV motors. Magnets used at high temperatures require a large coercivity and a maximum energy product.
