In addition, the development of magnets that do not use heavy rare earths has been active due to the problem of rare earth resources, and the use of magnets with smaller grain sizes and hot-deformed magnets has increased. These magnets require the application of a large magnetic field for magnetization, and the conventional pulse-type magnetization method requires a large-capacity capacitor and a large charging voltage. In order to use the pulse-type magnetization method safely and securely, we propose the magnetization by heating the magnet as a new magnetization method. We report on basic tests of this heated magnetization method and also introduce equipment for practical use.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Linear Permanent Magnet Flux Switching Machine for Use in Dry Gravity Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This study evaluates a linear permanent magnet flux switching machine (LPM-FSM) for use in dry gravity energy storage application where electrical energy is stored as potential energy in piston masses. The designed machine is optimised for efficiency and power factor. The optimisation is carried out using non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II). The results indicate that the LPM-FSM has a good power factor and efficiency, which make it cost-effective when used as the main drive unit in the linear electric machine gravity energy storage system. Furthermore, in order to reduce the force ripple, the machine is sectioned and step positioned. In comparison to the vernier machine, the LPM-FSM provides better performance in terms of power factor and efficiency.

articleTitle: Effect of Cu addition on the crystal structure and magnetic properties for Mn-Ga thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Rare earth magnets are known to possess high maximum energy products and a large magnetic moment. However, the countries of origin of those rare earth elements are unevenly distributed, and they are expensive and anxious about sustainable supply. Therefore, there is a need to develop rare-earth-free permanent magnets. Mn-Ga alloy films with L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> structure have attracted much attention for application to rare-earth-free permanent magnets and spin-transfer-torque magnetoresistive random access memory (STT-MRAM). In this study, In order to see the effect of Cu addition on the crystal structure and magnetic properties of L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> Mn-Ga thin films have been investigated. The samples were prepared on MgO (100) single crystal substrates using an ultra-high vacuum magnetron sputtering system. It was found that the addition of a small amount of Cu (0.75 ~ 1.5 vol. %) increased the peak intensity attributed to the L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> phase, but further addition resulted in a decrease in peak intensity and the value of saturation magnetization increased from 529 in w/o Cu to 637 emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> in 0.75, 1.5 vol. % Cu. However, the value of coercivity was decreased by the addition of small amount of Cu.

articleTitle: Electric field modulation of spin-flop behaviors in Co/Ru/Co/PMN-PT(011) artificial multiferroic heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Various attempts to realize electric field controlled energy-saving spintronic devices have been made in recent years. Artificial multiferroic heterostructures have attracted much attention because of its ability to control magnetization by an electric field due to the inverse magnetoelectric effect. In this study, as a new artificial multiferroic heterostructure, we investigate the electric field effects on the magnetic properties of a synthetic antiferromagnet composed of Co/Ru/Co deposited on ferroelectric (011) oriented Pb(Mg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-PbTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Spin-flop transition, which is characteristic of interlayer coupled synthetic antiferromagnets, is observed. The magnetic field direction at which the spin-flop behavior occurs is rotated by 90° upon the application of an electric field. The results are promising to be used in next-generation spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Additional Magneto Motive Force of Spoke-Type Vernier Permanent-Magnet Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Traditional permanent magnet (PM) magneto motive force (MMF) / specific permeance model has been widely applied to analytically predict the magnetic field of vernier permanent-magnet machines (VPMs). However, it fails to accurately predict the performances of spoke-type VPMs. This paper clarifies the intrinsic reason, i.e. the spoke-type VPMs have a large additional PM MMF introduced by the stator slotting, while the traditional model neglects it. In this paper, the additional PM MMF is analytically calculated and its influence on performance is comprehensively investigated. It shows that the additional PM MMF leads to reductions in the airgap flux density, back-EMF and torque density of spoke-type VPMs. Finally, a spoke-type VPM prototype is built and tested to verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Sub-picosecond magnetization reversal in fully ferromagnetic spin valves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The discovery of spin-transfer torque (STT) has paved the way for controlling the magnetization direction in magnetic devices within nanoseconds using an electrical current solely. However, current-induced STT switching below a few hundred picoseconds with low power consumption while maintaining high thermal stability is challenging. Ultra-short optical pulses can induce spin angular momentum transfer in a ferromagnetic spin valve, resulting in different demagnetization time depending on its magnetic configuration within less than a picosecond. However, magnetization reversal in ferromagnetic spin valves by a single femtosecond laser pulse has not been achieved. Here we demonstrate an optically induced sub-picosecond magnetization reversal in archetypical rare-earth-free spin valves of [Pt/Co]/Cu/[Co/Pt] that are used for current-induced STT switching. Our findings may provide a new route to ultrafast magnetization reversal by further bridging concepts from spintronics and ultrafast magnetism.

articleTitle: Inductance and capacitance emerged from topological electromagnetism
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We theoretically propose novel functionalities of inductance and capacitance in heterostructures of topological insulators and magnets. Topological insulators show anomalous responses between electricity and magnetism, which are described not by the conventional Maxwell’s equations, but by topological quantum field theory. Based on topological quantum field theory, we establish a unified theoretical framework applicable in arbitrary dimensions, to extract inductance and capacitance in topological insulators. We demonstrate the emergence of inductance and capacitance in several magnetic heterostructure setups, and show their advantages in achieving high operation frequency and high power efficiency.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal Magnon Hanle Effect in Antiferromagnetic α-Fe2O3
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The precession of the magnon pseudospin about the equilibrium pseudofield, the latter capturing the nature of magnonic eigenexcitations in an antiferromagnet, gives rise to the magnon Hanle effect. Its realization via electrically injected and detected spin transport in an antiferromagnetic insulator demonstrates its high potential for devices and as a convenient probe for magnon eigenmodes and the underlying spin interactions in the antiferromagnet. Here, we observe a nonreciprocity in the Hanle signal measured in α-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> using two spatially separated Pt electrodes as spin injector and detector. Interchanging their roles alters the detected magnon spin signal. The recorded difference depends on the applied magnetic field and reverses sign when the signal passes its nominal maximum at the socalled compensation field. Our findings unlock the high potential of antiferromagnetic magnonics towards the realization of electronics-inspired phenomena.

articleTitle: Rotor Position Estimation for PMSM Based on Hall Interval Angle Compensation and Phase-Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of large rotor position estimation error caused by Hall installation error of PMSM motor, this article proposes a rotor position estimation method based on Hall interval angle compensation and phase tracking. Firstly, a Hall rotation vector coordinate transformation method with three phase differences / is proposed. Secondly, a compensation angle estimation method for the Hall interval under non-uniform speed conditions was proposed using three-phase rotation vectors and an improved SOGI. Finally, the improved SOGI is applied again to extract the accurate rotor position information. This method can effectively reduce the rotor position estimation error caused by Hall installation error in both steady-state and dynamic operation of the motor. And it does not depend on the parameters of the motor system and has high engineering application value. The correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A Built-in Integrated Magnetorheological Fluid Brake Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, a built-in integrated magnetorheological fluid brake permanent magnet synchronous motor (BIMRFB-PMSM) is proposed, which integrates MR fluid brake and PMSM with a relatively simple structure to improve space utilization while meeting the braking requirement. Based on the design of outer stator with armature winding and inner stator with braking winding, the proposed machine has two switchable working states: rotation state and brake state. After a detailed description of the machine topology and operation principle of the proposed machine, the electromagnetic performance of the proposed machine is analyzed by finite element (FE) analysis. Simlulation results show that the brake torque in brake state satisfies the brake requirements of the proposed machine and the integrated topology can effectively improve the space utilization.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Inductor Modeling Technique Using Parametric Circuit Simulation and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Optimization of magnetic components design, such as power inductors and transformers, is most needed to improve the performance of future power electronics. However, power electronics designers are faced with the problem of not having sufficient magnetic component models available for their designs. In this paper, we propose a method to construct a unique nonlinear magnetic component model using parametric circuit simulation and deep learning.

articleTitle: Spin-transfer Torque MRAM - Status and Outlook
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spin-Transfer-Torque (STT) MRAM is an emerging memory technology with a unique combination of non-volatility and high write endurance. STT-MRAM products have been commercially available for both standalone memory and eFlash-replacement applications by successfully integrating magnetic tunnel junctions with CMOS technology. This talk will first give a brief overview of the current status of the STT-MRAM technology and then focus on materials innovations and remaining challenges to further expand STT-MRAM's application space.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Multiport Field Modulated Axial Flux Generator for Wave Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Direct drive wave power generation devices have the problems of low power density and low wave utilization efficiency. To solve these problems, a multiport field-modulated axial flux generator(MPFMAFG) structure is proposed. Based on the adjustable-speed magnetic gear with electric excitation, the dual-port axial flux generator is integrated. The new structure proposed in this paper broadens the working range of the system in different sea conditions. The MPFMAFG has the characteristics of strong reliability and high power density. The rationality and validity of the structure are well verified by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Comparison between Conical and Axial Flux Geometries of High-Speed Permanent Magnets Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A multiphysics design has been largely investigated for high-speed radial flux machines. In contrast, few articles discuss high-speed axial flux machines. Engineers face many thermal, mechanical, and magnetic challenges when designing such structures at high rotating speeds. The torque produced is proportional to the square and cube of the outer rotor radius for radial and axial flux machines, respectively. Simultaneously, especially at high speed, the centrifugal force strongly constrains the outer rotor radius for both radial and axial machines. In this digest, a conical rotor-stator-rotor structure is proposed, which could help enhance the torque production capabilities while preserving the rotors mechanical integrity at a high rotational speed. The conical structure is compared with a traditional axial flux machine regarding the electromagnetic aspect and a heterogeneous rotor disk’s mechanical behavior at high speed.

articleTitle: Scalable Spin-to-Charge Conversion Effect in the Inverse Spin Hall Nanodevice
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A major challenge to realizing a highly energy-efficient magneto-electric spin-orbit (MESO) logic device is the small signal response of ferromagnetic spin state readout by inverse spin Hall (ISH) effect, which makes it difficult to meet the practical device design. Here, we present a scalable T-shape W/CoFeB ISH device with tunable spin-to-charge conversion effects. The ISH signal appeared to increase with reducing the W channel width, achieving 40mΩ with a channel width down to 95nm. Tuning the sputtering dc power can further adjust the ISH signal. Our finding provides a pathway to improve the ISH signal in patterned devices that is beneficial for developing next-generation spintronic logic devices.

articleTitle: Improving Repeatability of Tests for Iron Loss Prediction and Electrical Machines Model Calibration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Prediction of of iron loss in electric machines is known to be a challenging task. The concept of a building factor to account for discrepancy between predicted and measured loss is widely used. This paper describes an extensive experimental campaign on permanent magnet synchronous machines at no-load, with magnetized and dummy rotors. Several identified challenges may be addressed by repeatabilty investigations combined with temperature monitoring of rotor core and bearing temperatures. For accurate prediction of iron loss impacted by manufacturing (cut edge or shrink-fit for example), current models require electrical steel properties (BH and iron loss density) as a function of tensile and compressive stress/strain. Such measurements have not yet been standardized. Repeatability issues with a bespoken single sheet tester were reduced by pre-cycling at three tensile stress levels. Analysis of measured impact of stress for different grades confirmed that a specifc set of data per grade and supplier may be required.

articleTitle: Spin-orbit torques of three spin polarizations in magnetic trilayers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Three spin polarizations of spin-orbit torques are theoretically available in ferromagnet/normal metal/ferromagnet trilayers. We report the quantification of spin-orbit torques of these spin polarizations via harmonic Hall voltage measurement. Furthermore, we show that using all three polarizations reduces the field-free spin-orbit torque (SOT) switching current of a perpendicular magnetization by employing a bottom ferromagnet with a tilted easy-axis in trilayer systems.

articleTitle: Generation probability of point defects considering microscopic elastic scattering cross-sections in rare-earth permanent magnets via first-principles calculations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, the generation probability of point defects was obtained from the formation energy of the point defects based on first-principles calculations and the microscopic elastic scattering cross-sections. From the results, the generation probability of point defects of Nd2Fe14B and Sm2Co17 both rose sharply when the incident energy was around 10 eV. When the incident energy became higher than 10 eV, the point defect generation probabilities both became close to 1. However, since the incident energy at which the point defect generation probability exceeded 0 was higher for Co than Fe, Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf> was found more stable than Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>B under high energy.

articleTitle: Principle and Analysis of Structure of Low-Speed High-Torque Gear Meshing Motor Driven by Radial Force
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a new motor structure based on electromagnetic radial force drive, which converts the radial electromagnetic force into output torque through the meshing action of the gear pair, resulting in a significant increase in torque density. Firstly, the basic structure of the motor is introduced, and then the working process of the stator magnetizing structure and the gear pair is analyzed separately. The process of radial electromagnetic force change caused by magnetic field change and the transmission process of gear pair are also introduced. The analysis process demonstrates the feasibility of the structure. The proposed motor structure offers significant advantages in space-constrained low-speed and high-torque applications.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Multi-Magnon Scattering in Ensembles of Nanomagnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Arrays of nanomagnets known as artificial spin ice have recently been discussed in the context of functional magnonic materials, where an interplay between geometry, material properties, and reconfigurability determines the magnon spectrum. Magnons are the fundamental quantum-mechanical bosonic excitations of magnetic solids, whose number does not need to be conserved in scattering processes. Microwave-induced parametric magnon processes have been believed to occur in magnetic thin films only, where quasi-continuous magnon bands exist. Here, we demonstrate the existence of such nonlinear multi-magnon scattering processes and their coherence in artificial spin ice. These systems exhibit effective scattering processes akin to those observed in continuous magnetic thin films. The experimental investigations using microwave and Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy are combined with numerical simulations to understand the evolution of modes. Our results show that harmonic magnon modes can be excited in artificial spin ice subject to sufficiently strong microwave power. This excitation leads to a spatial modification of modes enabling nonlinear processes that is unique to artificial spin ice. Our results suggest that tunable directional scattering is possible in these structures opening new avenues for manipulating magnon populations in reconfigurable nanomagnetic networks.

articleTitle: Effect of Instability of Ferrofluid for enhanced EMI shielding in Ku-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Ferrofluid is a type of smart material consisting of stable colloidal suspensions of magnetic nanoscale particles dispersed in a nonmagnetic carrier liquid. It is known that ferromagnetic nanoparticles may improve the magnetic and dielectric properties of host materials, which exhibit novel functionality to provide better microwave absorption properties. A ferrofluid layer subjected to an external magnetic field resulting in cone-shaped structures may further enhance the reflection loss of the incident electromagnetic wave. This study investigates the effect of the ferrofluid crests on the enhancement of the electromagnetic wave shielding effectiveness in the range of 12-18 GHz. It is noted that such a ferrofluid has significant shield effectiveness at the frequency of 16 GHz. When the magnetic field is applied to create the ferrofluid crests, the value of shielding effectiveness initially increases, then decreases as the field strength is further increased. The variation of the EMI shield effectiveness is dominated by the arrangement of the ferrofluid crests array, which is closely related to the thickness, composition of the ferrofluid layer, and the field strength uniformity.

articleTitle: Study on smoothing generated voltage in the vertical linear vibration generator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In recent years, it has been expected to create sustainable society using renewable energy sources. In this study, we focus on mechanical vibration. The method of converting vibration energy to electric energy is examined. The generated voltage obtained from the vibration energy has many different frequency components. Therefore, the optimal smoothing capacitor for rectifying and smoothing the generated voltage will also be examined. In this study, the vertical linear vibration generator was made to investigate the basic characteristics. The generation voltage increased with an increase in coil turns N. However, it did not follow Faraday’s law of induction due to the increased thickness of the coil, resulting in decrease in the generation voltage. The smoothing of the generated voltage by the capacitor is analyzed. The optimal smoothing capacitor was examined. As a result, the ripple of the generated voltage was decreased by up to 59%.

articleTitle: Influence of Split Ratio on Field Modulation Effect in Consequent-Pole Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of split ratio on air-gap field modulation effect (AGFME) on consequent-pole permanent magnet (CPPM) machine. Because of the doubly sided opening slotting effect, the CPPM machine exhibits an abundant air-gap flux density working harmonics for torque production. To identify and quantify the torque contributions of the various air-gap field working harmonics, the Maxwell stress tensor method (MSTD) is employed to illustrate their contributed torque components and proportions. The simulated results show that the split ratio exhibits a great influence on AGFME on CPPM machine. Finally, a CPPM machine prototype is manufactured and tested to validate the finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Effect of Tensile Stress Application on Magnetic Properties of Fe0.8Co0.2 Alloy and Martensitic Fe0.8Co0.2NxAlloy System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We investigated the change in magnetic properties of an alloy foil composed of a mixed phase of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}_{0.8}\text{Co}_{0.2}\mathrm{N}_{x}$</tex> martensite (FeCoN) and Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>ferrite (FeCo) when a tensional force was applied in the direction parallel to the magnetic field. FeCo foil was nitrided with ammonia gas and quenched to form nitrogen martensite on the surface of the sample. The obtained FeCoN foils featured lower maximum relative permeability and higher elastic limit than FeCo. When the iron loss was measured in an alternating magnetic field while tension was applied to this foil, it was found that the iron loss decreased as the tension was increased until the elastic limit was reached. On the other hand, when the elastic limit was exceeded, an irreversible increase in iron loss due to plastic deformation was confirmed. Therefore, in FeCoN foil, which is an FeCo alloy foil with nitrogen martensite introduced, it was experimentally clarified that iron loss can be reduced up to 50% by applying a tensional force up to 160 MPa parallel to the magnetization direction.

articleTitle: Open-Delta Flux-Modulating Consequent Pole Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a new variable-flux permanent magnet (PM) motor, named the "open-delta flux-modulating consequent pole motor (OFCM)." The armature winding of the proposed OFCM is connected in open-delta and is also used as a field winding by simultaneously supplying a three-phase armature current and a DC field current. The flux linkage of the armature winding can be adjusted by changing the field current. The flux-regulation capability of the OFCM is confirmed through three-dimensional finite element analysis (3-D FEA) and experiments conducted on a prototype machine.

articleTitle: Anisotropic magnetostriction for low-frequency energy harvesting applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In the framework of energy conversion devices for energy harvesting, magnetostrictive materials are an attractive alternative solution to the brittleness and geometrical limitations of piezoelectric materials. So far, the anisotropy of magnetostriction has never been studied to improve an energy harvesting system's performance. In this work, we investigated the performances of an oriented grain electrical steel material in an energy harvesting context. Well-known magnetic properties, including low magnetostriction and significant anisotropy, characterize this material. We combined experimental and predictive simulation results and discussed the possibility of increasing the energy level by playing with the orientation of both the magnetic and the mechanical stimuli.

articleTitle: Influence of Additional Air Gaps Between Stator Tooth and Back-iron on Acoustic Performance of Spoke-type Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of additional air gaps between stator tooth and back-iron on the acoustic performance of spoke-type permanent magnet synchronous motor (STPMSM) is studied. It is found that the existence of these gaps can reduce the electromagnetic vibration noise, and its sound pressure level decreases by 2.3dB. By comparing radial electromagnetic forces acting on the stator, it is found that the additional air gap will weaken the 2-order radial electromagnetic force in space, which is the main source of electromagnetic vibration noise. Under the same additional air gap length, different stator tooth segments and back-iron segments are studied. The results show that the structure with triangular separated stator tooth and back-iron has better acoustic performance.

articleTitle: Demagnetization of Nd-Fe-B Sintered and Ferrite Magnets Derived from Magnetic Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic-domain-wall motion determined the coercivities of Nd-Fe-B sintered and ferrite magnets according to their alignment dependencies. The alignment dependences of coercivity and the angular dependences of the coercivity were correlated. The alignment dependence of the coercivity indicated that, in the aligned magnets, several grains formed a cluster of reversed magnetization at the coercivity. In the demagnetization process, the aligned magnets behaved as though they were magnets with low alignment because of cluster formation. The calculated angular dependence of the coercivity using the results of the alignment dependence of the coercivity agreed well with experimental data. From the recoil curve of these magnets, minor demagnetization occurred in a weaker demagnetization field than the coercivity. The magnetic measurements yielded a demagnetization process that started with a weak demagnetization; a cluster of reversed grains then formed, and the coercivity resulted from the cluster growth.

articleTitle: Skyrmion dynamics and the Skyrmion-Excited Spin Wave Fractal Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are topologically protected spin textures which have been of interest for both their fundamental qualities as well as applications in data storage and logic technologies. Recently, there has been an emphasis on dynamic modes in the skyrmions. These investigations have revealed a rich collection of fundamental physics, including a variety of discrete excitation modes far beyond simple gyration and breathing mechanisms. In this work, we perform small angle neutron scattering (SANS) while performing in-situ ferromagnetic resonance (FMR), using the reciprocal space diffraction pattern as a direct probe of the skyrmion dynamic modes. The observations revealed the fairly benign conclusion that the skyrmion lattice remained largely unchanged during its dynamic modes, however, additional scattering was observed at ultra-small angles. This scattering was well fit by a mass-fractal model, which is generally representative of a network constructed from monodisperse elements, such as a polymer matrix. Using micromagnetic modeling to support our investigation, this network was revealed to be the consequence of spin waves and spin wave interference, forming a spin wave fractal network.

articleTitle: Impact of Soft Magnetic Material on Electromagnetic Force and Vibration of Permanent Magnet Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Electromagnetic vibration is excited by the radial electromagnetic force generated by the air-gap magnetic field acting on the stator core. In this paper, an analysis and reduction of electromagnetic force in high-speed permanent magnet electrical machines with different stator cores are investigated. A fast and accurate calculation method of air gap flux density and radial force density distribution are derived. The radial force density including amplitude, frequency, and order is obtained by a two-dimension fast Fourier transform. Then, the effect of the different PM segmentation on radial force is summarized.

articleTitle: Odd spin frustration in ultrathin Cr(001) films studied by spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: 3-nm-thick Cr(001) films have been fabricated successfully with atomically flat and clean terraces. Images of both the topological and magnetic structures of the Cr films were obtained at 300 K using spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy. The observed magnetic image of the Cr(001) surface indicated that the topological antiferromagnetic (AF) order appeared in a series of adjacent terraces with two types of spin frustration caused by screw dislocations leading to the modification of the topological AF order. One type of the spin frustration is accompanied with the narrow domain wall between two screw dislocations. The other type is due to complex spin frustration caused by a cluster of odd number of screw dislocations, which is explained through a micromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Damping-Like Spin-Orbit-Torque Efficiency in Synthetic Antiferromagnetic System using Pt-Cu Alloy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Damping-like spin-orbit torque (SOT) efficiency (effective spin Hall angle: ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DL</inf>) is investigated in synthetic antiferromagnetic (AF) systems using Pt-Cu alloy/Ir/Pt-Cu alloy spacer layers. AF interlayer exchange coupling through Pt-Cu alloy/Ir/Pt-Cu alloy spacer layers was observed. We also found that the magnitude of ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DL</inf> for synthetic AF system using Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">57</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">43</inf> alloy/Ir/ Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">57</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">43</inf> alloy spacer layer is larger than that for synthetic AF system using Pt/Ir/Pt spacer layer, comparing to devices with nearly similar magnitudes of interlayer exchange coupling of 0.11 mJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The observed maximum magnitude of ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DL</inf> is 19.9% for the synthetic AF system using Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">57</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">43</inf> alloy/Ir/Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">57</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">43</inf> alloy. The synthetic AF system will be a promising building block for future nonvolatile high-speed memories and logic circuits using the spin Hall effect.

articleTitle: Measurement and Evaluation of Magnetic Barkhausen Noise of Oriented Silicon Steel Sheet under Mechanical Stress
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetization and loss properties of magnetic material are closely related with the residual stress in the material, and the stress state in the material is hard to determine in advance. Magnetic Barkhausen noise (MBN) can be used to evaluate the microstructure changes, stress states, micro-damage defects and so on within a certain depth of ferromagnetic materials, and to realize the evaluation of fatigue, micro-cracks and other early performance degradation. In this paper, the measurement methods and detection platform of Barkhausen noise signal of oriented electrical silicon steel sheets under mechanical stresses are presented, and the Jiles-Atherton hysteresis model is combined with the Barkhausen noise evaluation model to propose a method to evaluate the mechanical stresses states of oriented electrical silicon steel sheets.

articleTitle: A Compact and Integrated Magnetic Coupler Design with Cross-coupling Elimination Utilizing LCC-LCC/S Compensation Network for Building Attached Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A compact and integrated wireless charging system is presented in this digest for the purpose of charging a photovoltaic system attached to a building. In such an integrated system, cross-coupling interference presents a challenge, which is addressed by using DD coils and Q coils. Moreover, since cross-coupling has been eliminated, it is convenient and efficient to design corresponding compensation networks. The theoretical analysis shows that the well-designed LCC-LCC and LCC-S compensation structures can provide load-independent constant current and voltage outputs, respectively.

articleTitle: Enhancement of non-destructive evaluation by combining induction thermography and eddy current testing techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Induction thermography (IT) and eddy current testing (ECT) are non-contact, non-destructive evaluation (NDE) techniques that can be coupled by the eddy currents. The two inspections can share the same energy source. By taking the synergized effects of the two techniques, we can detect a larger variety of defects and improve detection and sizing reliability. The two methods were analyzed in the view of energy flow. The clarification of the mechanism provides the basis for effective hybrid of IT and ECT.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Magnetic Properties of Novel Sm–Mo–Fe Phosphate-Coated Fe–X (X = Ni and Mn) Magnetic Powder Cores
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, we developed a new magnetic powder core using Fe–X powders, which has a coercivity of less than 80 A/m and a saturation magnetization that is comparable to that of pure iron powders. Fe–X powders doped with 4 at% nickel and 0.1 at% manganese were fabricated by the reduction of Ni–Mn doped ferrite (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.959</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.04</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.001</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanopowders with hydrogen gas at 1323 K. The magnetic powder cores were fabricated from Fe–X powders coated with the novel-developed phosphate insulators containing rare earth and transition metals. The insulator was more heat resistant than conventional phosphate insulators and maintained its properties even after annealing at 873 K. The magnetic powder core of Fe–X (X = Ni and Mn) powders coated with the Sm–Mo–Fe phosphate insulator, compacted at 1.47 GPa with heat treatment at 793 K and having a density of 7.62 Mg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, exhibited magnetic flux density at 10 kA/m of 1.66 T. Iron loss W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10/400</inf> (B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> = 1T, f = 400 Hz) was 38 W/kg and W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5/20k</inf>(B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> = 0.05 T, f = 20 kHz) was 43 W/kg.

articleTitle: Comparative study of Mechanical and Electrical Characteristics on High-Strength Steel and Conventional Steel for EV Traction High-Speed Multilayer IPMSM Using Rare-Earth Free PM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this article, the electrical and mechanical characteristics are compared with multilayer IPMSM (ML-IPMSM) using ferrite permanent magnet (PM) when driven at high-speed according to electrical steel. In high-speed operation, in the case of ML-IPMSM, the mechanical and electrical characteristics change depending on the number of PM layers, PM shape, the number of bridges, and bridge thickness. In addition, ferrite PM has a lower coercive force than Nd PM, therefore irreversible demagnetization (ID) must be considered, and it is affected by the number of layers and PM shape of ML-IPMSM. Therefore, when designing a multilayer IPMSM using ferrite PM for electrical vehicle (EV) traction, all the characteristics must be considered. Compared to conventional electrical steel (CES), High-strength electrical steel (HSES) has advantages in mechanical properties, allowing the ML shape to be relatively free. Accordingly, it is possible to design a shape that is advantageous in electrical performance compared to CES by adjusting ML shape. In this article, all characteristics of each ML-IPMSM applied with HSEC and CES are reviewed through finite element analysis (FEA), and the advantages of HSEC applied motors for high-speed driving motors are presented. To verify the validity of the review contents of this article, experiments are conducted on the manufactured motor, FEA results are compared with the test results.

articleTitle: A Novel Rotor-Step Skewing Method for Vibration Mitigation in Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a novel rotor-step skewing method to effectively mitigate vibration in the interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM). Firstly, the analytical models of the radial force and bending moment are established. Then, the effects on the vibration mitigation are discussed for different combinations of the skewing mode and skewing angle, and the optimal skewing angle of each skewing mode is determined. On this basis, the performance is compared by the finite element (FE) calculation, and a novel model with 4-type skewing rotor is proved to have a significant effect. Detailed performance parameters, including electromagnetic (EM) torque, air-gap magnetic field, vibration, are analyzed for the 4-type, conventional straight and V-shaped rotor-step skewing structures. Finally, a vibration experiment of the prototype is conducted to further prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Energy-efficient optoelectronic domain-wall motion for logic computing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Logic computing in magnetic domain walls is investigated using the interplay of all-optical helicity-dependent switching and current-induced spin-orbit torque switching. By simultaneously controlling current and laser pulses, logic functions of AND, OR, NAND and NOR are experimentally demonstrated through anomalous Hall effect. The optoelectronic domain-wall motion is energy-efficient compared to the traditional all-current approach and provides another degree of freedom for the realization of logic applications.

articleTitle: The Role of Heat Capacity Anomaly on the Magnetocaloric Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: It has been shown that for the accurate determination of magnetocaloric effect the specific heat capacity should be accounted. This is because during phase transitions, the magnetocaloric effect is typically accompanied by peaks in specific heat capacity that strongly depend on temperature and magnetic field. If this dependence is ignored, the resulting adiabatic temperature change will be significantly overestimated. A method for calculating the magnetocaloric effect during ferromagnetic-antiferromagnetic phase transition in Fe-Rh alloys has been proposed, and has been found to agree well with experimental results.

articleTitle: Increase of Saturation Magnetization Flux Density in Nitrogen Defective Fe16Nx
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Saturation magnetization flux density of nitrogen defective Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> was investigated by means of the first-principles density functional theory. The structures of nitrogen defective Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> were prepared by introducing randomly distributed point defects of nitrogen. We examined that the change in the cell volume obeys Vegard’s law, since the relaxed cell volume of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> decreased almost linearly with an increase of the point defects. We found that the dispersion of the magnetic moment is large around a nitrogen concentration of 5 at.%. Based on these behaviors of the cell volume and the magnetic moment, it revealed that the saturation magnetization flux density around the nitrogen concentration of 5 at.% shows higher value than that of α-iron and Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Growth and terahertz conductivity of epitaxial Mn3Sn thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetic Weyl semimetal has Berry curvature in the momentum space near Fermi level, leading to large anomalous Hall effect, anomalous Nernst effect and magneto-optical effect in such materials. It is still challenging to grow high quality epitaxial Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn thin films with transport and optical properties comparable to their single crystal counterparts. Meanwhile, the anisotropic conductivity has not been studied on Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn in THz frequencies. Here, we report the structure, magneto-optical and transport properties of epitaxial Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+x</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf> thin films fabricated by pulsed laser deposition (PLD). Highly oriented Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+x</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf> (0001) and $\left({11\bar 20}\right)$ epitaxial films are successfully growth on single crystalline Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and MgO substrates. The terahertz conductivity in Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn films is investigated by polarization-resolved spectroscopy. Our work demonstrates strong terahertz conductivity in epitaxial Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+x</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf> films, paving the way for future optical and spintronic device applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Fully Printed Implantable Rectenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a novel compact implantable rectenna for far-field wireless powering low-consumption biomedical sensors. A circular PIFA antenna resonant at 900 MHz was designed, by using CST software, manufactured, and characterized. In order to produce a less invasive rectenna, a double voltage rectifier circuit topology, composed only of a 2862 HSMS Schottky diode, is proposed. No other discrete electronic components are used. The rectification process is completed by employing printed capacitors. The rectifier circuit design was performed by using ADS software at low input powers, ranging from -20 dBm to 0 dBm. The antenna and rectifier circuit geometrical parameters were optimized to find matching condition at 50Ω. Numerical and experimental results obtained confirm the ability of the proposed system to supply implantable low-consumption sensors.

articleTitle: Power-aware Quantization Circuits in Analog In-Memory Computing with STT-MRAM Macro
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a low power quantization circuit in analog in-memory computing (IMC) with spin transfer torque magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM) macro, in which a successive approximation (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with reconfigurable 3/4-bit resolution and 250MS/s sampling rate addresses the need of high speed and low power for analog IMC. By using 28-nm CMOS process, simulation results show that the proposed ADC consumes only 31.6 µW at a 900mV supply and 250MS/s. 10.4-25.7 TOPS/W is realized with 2-bit input, 1-bit weight, and 4-bit output convolution neural network (CNN).

articleTitle: Spin Hall Magnetoresistance in Antiferromagnetic Insulators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Antiferromagnetic materials promise improved performance for spintronic applications, as they are robust against external magnetic field perturbations and allow for faster magnetization dynamics compared to ferromagnets. The direct observation of the antiferromagnetic state, however, is challenging due to the absence of a macroscopic magnetization. We show that the spin Hall magnetoresistance (SMR) is a versatile tool to probe the antiferromagnetic spin structure via simple electrical transport experiments by investigating the easy-plane antiferromagnetic insulators α-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (hematite) and NiO in bilayer heterostructures with a Pt heavy-metal top electrode. While rotating an external magnetic field in three orthogonal planes, we record the longitudinal and the transverse resistivities of Pt and observe characteristic resistivity modulations consistent with the SMR effect. We analyze both their amplitude and phase and compare the data to the results from a prototypical collinear ferrimagnetic Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>/Pt bilayer. The observed magnetic field dependence is explained in a comprehensive model, based on two magnetic sublattices and taking into account magnetic field-induced modifications of the domain structure. Our results show that the SMR effect allows to readout the spin configuration and to investigate magnetoelastic effects in antiferromagnetic multi-domain materials. We demonstrate that the SMR amplitude scales with the sum of the absolute sublattice magnetizations in ferrimagnetic and antiferromagnetic materials. In α-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Pt bilayers, we find an unexpectedly large SMR amplitude of 2.5 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, twice as high as for prototype Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>/Pt bilayers, making the system particularly interesting for room-temperature antiferromagnetic spintronic applications.

articleTitle: Finite size effect and dimensional crossover in antiferromagnetic epitaxial Cr2O3 thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We explore the finite size effect on the Néel temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>) and the dimensional crossover in the antiferromagnetic epitaxial Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films. T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> and the critical exponent (β) were experimentally determined based on the temperature dependent anomalous Hall effect (AHE) emerging at the Pt/Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> interface. T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> decreases with decreasing Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thickness: ~285 K above 40 nm and ~240 K at 5.2 nm. The decrease of T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> is prominent below 15 nm, and it is accompanied with the decrease of β Above 40 nm, β is about 0.325 (3D Ising model), and decreases about 0.25 around 15 nm, 0.125 (2D Ising model) below 10 nm. The thickness regime for the finite-size effects to emerge is higher than the reported cases of metallic ferromagnets probably because of the long-range exchange interactions between Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> spins in Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>.

articleTitle: Anomalous Reduction in Magnetization of Sm2Fe17N3 Anisotropic Sintered Magnets during Pressure Current Sintering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: It has been suggested in a previous publication that the magnetization of Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> anisotropic sintered magnets prepared from jet-milled powder is unexpectedly low. This study was conducted to clarify the cause of the reduction in magnetization from a metallographic point of view. Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powders prepared by jet-milling in a low oxygen atmosphere were aligned in a magnetic field and then sintered by pressure current sintering method. The smaller the grain size, the worse the crystallinity because of the milling damages on the raw powders. Magnetization of the sintered bodies decreased as the crystallinity got worse, which is qualitatively similar to the trend for the powders, but the absolute values converged to a fairly lower level. Based on the results of microstructure analysis, it is inferred that the damaged regions with high dislocation density are converted into isotropic nanocrystals under the influence of heat and pressure upon sintering, resulting in a certain loss of crystal alignment, which is considered to be the principal cause of the reduction in magnetization.

articleTitle: A Novel Counter-rotating Axial-flux Hybrid-excitation Permanent Magnet Machine with Dual-rotor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of unbalanced load in the operation of counter-rotating propeller(CRP), a novel counter-rotating axial-flux hybrid excitation permanent magnet machine(CR-AFHEPMM) is proposed, which combines the high torque density of the axial-flux permanent magnet machine(AFPMM) and the flexible flux regulation of the hybrid excitation machine. Firstly, the structural features and operation principle of the CR-AFHEPMM are presented. Then, the influence of slot-pole combination, permanent magnet(PM) arrangement and key structural parameters of the CR-AFHEPMM are studied. Finally, an optimal structure of the Halbach array consequent-pole PM rotor is further proposed and analyzed. The results show that the proposed CR-AFHEPMM is a promising candidate for the application of CRP.

articleTitle: Switching Dynamics of In-Plane Magnetized Spin-Orbit Torque Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In-plane magnetized spin-orbit torque (SOT) devices offer the possibility of low energy memory applications by utilizing the spin Hall effect in a heavy metal write lead for efficient spin torque switching of the bistable ferromagnetic element. One challenge is the optimization of the switching dynamics despite spatial variation of the internal magnetic field of the memory element, its magnetization and the write current. In turn this introduces a spatially dependent torque from the spin accumulation at the ferromagnet-heavy metal interface, and from the Oersted magnetic field associated with the write current pulse. The combination of spatial and temporal variations within an individual element can lead to complicated switching dynamics via formation of spin textures for very fast write pulses, which can slow the complete switching. In this work we use a combination of time-resolved magneto-optical microscopy and micromagnetic simulations to explore the requirements for optimal switching. This work provides additional insight for the most efficient operation of SOT memory elements by directly probing the dynamic magnetization with sub-micron resolution on picosecond timescales.

articleTitle: Effect of YIG nanoparticles addition on the magnetic properties of manganese ferrite
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, manganese ferrites with YIG nanoparticles added were developed for MHz frequency applications. The effect of YIG additive on the power loss, initial permeability and cut-off frequency of Mn ferrites was investigated. A small quantity of added YIG effectively reduces the power loss and concurrently increases the initial permeability. Compared to the results for the Mn ferrite with no YIG addition, the optimal Mn ferrite with 600 ppm added YIG exhibits a reduction in the power loss at 25 °C of 56.4% and 36.6% at 1 MHz/50 mT and 3 MHz/10 mT, respectively, and a 13.9% increase in the initial permeability. This sample also exhibits a good stability of the power loss against temperature. The power loss remains below 205 kW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> over temperatures ranging from 25 to 140 °C. The effect mechanism of YIG addition on the magnetic properties of Mn ferrites was studied. An analysis based on the equivalent circuit model showed that the reduction in the eddy current loss and power loss mainly results from the increase in the grain boundary resistance caused by the addition of highly resistive YIG.

articleTitle: Study on Electromagnetic Vibration Characteristics in Fractional Slot Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The fractional-slot motor can produce more serious vibration problems because the spatial order of electromagnetic force in this type of motor is lower compared with integer-slot motors. In this paper, an electromagnetic structural coupling model is built to study the electromagnetic vibration characteristics of a surface permanent magnet (SPM) synchronous motor. First, the electromagnetic force of the SPM motor is evaluated using finite element analysis (FEA). Then, the stator mode and the harmonic response of the motor are simulated to study its modal parameters and vibration characteristics. Finally, the result shows that the main electromagnetic vibration source of the motor is 5-order radial electromagnetic force wave. The model developed can predict the electromagnetic vibration characteristics of different motors and provide guidance for suppressing vibration.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a New Synchronous Reluctance Machine with Hybrid Cores
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: As no permanent magnet (PM) material is required and only silicon sheets are needed on the rotor core, the synchronous reluctance machine (SynRM) has received tremendous research attention in the past and it can be used for many driving applications. However, compared with the electrical machine with PM excitation, its torque density, efficiency, and power factor are both low. In this paper, a novel SynRM with hybrid cores (Hybrid-SynRM) is proposed. Specifically, its rotor core is made by the combination of non-grain-oriented (NGO) silicon sheet cores and grain-oriented (GO) silicon sheet cores. The magnetic circuit characteristic of the proposed Hybrid-SynRM is improved by taking the super high magnetization characteristic of the GO silicon sheet along its rolling direction. To verify the performance of the proposed SynRM, the traditional SynRM with NGO silicon sheet cores (NGO-SynRM) is determined as the benchmark machine. For obtaining fair comparison results, both these two machines are optimized under the same conditions. Through the comparison, it can be seen that the torque ability, efficiency, and power factor can be improved greatly by employing the GO silicon sheet block in the SynRM. Therefore, the Hybrid-SynRM can output better performance than the NGO-SynRM especially when the applied electrical loading is high.

articleTitle: AC Magnetic Field Detection of Coplanar Line Type Thin Film Magnetic Field Sensor with Optimized Narrow Slits
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have proposed coplanar line type thin-film magnetic field sensor with narrow slits. The slit is employed to flow more carrier current on the signal line by improving the impedance matching. Several sensors having 6, 10, 26, 36, and 50 μm slit widths were fabricated and evaluated from the phase and the amplitude of the transmission coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) and reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) measured by the network analyzer. The amplitude of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> with slit was improved about five times larger than the sensor without one at around 2 GHz. The appropriate slit width was evaluated as around 10 μm for the coplanar line type thin film magnetic field sensor and the sensitivity will enhance more than 10 times higher than the sensor without slits.

Author Keywords: Coplanar Line Type Thin Magnetic Field Sensor

articleTitle: An Integrated Axial-Flux Magnetic-Geared Double-Rotor Machine Using Harmonic Current Injection Method for HEVs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Axial-flux magnetic-geared double-rotor machines (AMGDRMs) have been proved a promising candidate for the electrical-continuously variable transmission (e-CVT) in hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). However, an additional permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) is needed for torque compensation in the e-CVT system. In this paper, a novel integrated AMGDRM based on harmonic current injection method is proposed to improve compactness further. By carefully designing pole-pair number combination and adopting the phase-shift structure, the proposed machine can enable both MGDRM and PMSM operations without significant torque ripple. First, the topology and operation principle are investigated. Second, the torque ripple suppression mechanism is analyzed. Finally, 3-D FEA simulations are carried out to validate the proposed machine.

articleTitle: RF Signal Processing with Magneto-acoustic Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We present advancements in novel rf signal processing techniques which combine the benefits of high-Q, high-linearity, and large dynamic range of acoustic wave devices with the tunability and nonlinear functionality of spin wave devices. The design and implementation of two such magneto-acoustic devices, a tunable high-overtone bulk acoustic resonator (HBAR) and a rf signal correlator are discussed. The devices are implemented on yttrium iron garnet (YIG), chosen for its low damping of both spin and acoustic waves and magnetoelastic properties for coupling them.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Mn-Ni Powders Prepared by Hydrogen Reduction of Wet-Synthesized Ferrite Nanopowders
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We synthesized soft magnetic Fe-X powders with different Ni compositions (Ni = 0, 2.2, 4.4, 6.7, and 8.8 at%) on a 1 kg batch scale and investigated the effect of Ni content on their magnetic properties. The coercivity increases as the Ni content decreased. The saturation magnetization was maximum for a Ni content of 4.4 at%. The magnetic properties of the Fe-X powder synthesized in this study on a mass production scale achieved a coercivity of 0.77 Oe and a saturation magnetization of approximately 222 emu/g at a composition of 0.1 at% Mn and 2.2 at% Ni content.

articleTitle: Thermo-elastic Martensitic transformation in off-stoichiometric Co2Fe0.5Ti0.5Si quaternary Heusler alloy thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This work discusses the effect of composition and the growth conditions on the magnetic and transport properties in off-stoichiometric Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Si (CFTS) Heusler alloy thin films. CFTS thin films of 100 nm thickness were deposited on Si (100) substrate at different substrate temperatures (Ts) 350°C, 450°C and 500°C by ultra-high vacuum magnetron sputtering technique. Depending upon their growth conditions and stoichiometry, CFTS films exhibit thermo-elastic martensitic phase transformations. The begin and end martensitic and austenite transformation temperatures change with deposition conditions. The magneto-transport properties depend sensitively on the fraction of martensitic and austenite phases.

articleTitle: Perpendicular magnetic anisotropy based spintronic devices in Pt/Co and Pt/Co/X/Pt stacks under different hard and flexible substrates
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetic properties in Pt/Co and Pt/Co/X/Pt multilayers (with X= different caping materials), such as perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA), are of particular interest for spintronic devices. In particular, it is important to obtain a strong PMA on the flexible substrate in the field of wearable devices and structural health monitoring. However, the different stack structures and growth conditions influence the magnetic properties of the film. Here, we investigate the magnetic properties in Pt/Co/Pt and Pt/Co/X/Pt structures deposited by sputtering with different substrates (hard and flexible), layer thicknesses, different deposition temperatures of the buffer layer, different capping layers, insertion of a thin interlayer and irradiation by He+ ions. We exhibite conditions for better crystallinity, enhanced PMA, homogeneous domain wall motion and stronger DMI. The experimental results also show that the optimized film conditions can also yield strong PMA on the flexible substrate.

articleTitle: Prediction of Tunneling Magnetoresistance and Spin-Transfer Torque Effects in Antiferromagnetic Tunnel Junctions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) is a conventional spintronic device exploiting tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) to read-out and spin-transfer torque (STT) to write-in the information that is stored in magnetization of ferromagnetic layers. With the advantages of antiferromagnets being robust against magnetic perturbations, producing no stray fields, and exhibiting ultrafast dynamics, it would be desirable to realize an antiferromagnetic (AFM) tunnel junction (AFMTJ)—an MTJ analog for AFM spintronics. Here, we predict that large TMR and STT effects with the strengths comparable to these in commercial MTJs can be observed in RuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/RuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> AFMTJs. We argue that both phenomena can be interpreted in terms of the Néel spin currents, i.e., staggered spin currents flowing through different magnetic sublattices, which effectively transfer current carrying spins between the RuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> AFM electrodes across the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> barrier. Our work uncovers the unexplored potential of antiferromagnets for the efficient writing and reading of information in AFM spintronics.

articleTitle: Effect of film thickness on microwave assisted switching behavior
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We study the effect of magnetic film thickness t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mag</inf> on microwave assisted switching (MAS) behavior in CoCrPt-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> granular film. Magnetization switching behaviors are evaluated by measuring the anomalous Hall effect of the granular film under microwave field application. The thermal stability factor for magnetization reversal is varied from E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> = 85 k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>T to 110 k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>T by changing the film thickness t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mag</inf> =10 nm to 15 nm. The slope of the frequency dependence of the coercivity becomes slightly gradual and the critical frequency shifts toward a few GHz higher by decreasing film thickness. Such film thickness dependencies are well explained by considering the thermal activation based on the effective energy barrier height under excitation with a microwave field.

articleTitle: Improvement Torque ripple characteristics of Dual-Winding Square wave Brushless DC Motor with phase difference drive
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Dual winding machine is known as having fault tolerant characteristics, so it is got much attention especially for application which needs failure tolerance like aircraft including Electro Mechanic Actuators (EMAs). Controlling each winding by independent inverters leads not only fault tolerance but also improvement drive characteristics, so it is widely considered nowadays. Moreover, Square Wave Excitation BLDCM is more simple control method than FOC, so it makes EMAs reliability increase. In this paper, we use 2 inverters controlled by 1 microcontroller for driving 10poles-12slots dual winding PMSM, operate the motor with current phase difference under square-wave excitation. Then we examine improving the BLDCM torque characteristics experimentally.Finally, it is confirmed that dual-winding BLDCM used in this paper with driving by 2 inverters found that it is possible to reduce torque ripple by current phase differential drive. In this test motor, it is found that the torque ripple and RMS current can reduce by exciting current having 30degree lead of phase difference to the motor.

articleTitle: All optical switching in transition metal synthetic ferrimagnetic multilayer systems with enhanced interlayer exchange coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Nickel-platinum based synthetic ferrimagnets (SFi’s) offer a highly tunable system in which to study ultrafast all-optical control of magnetisation, without the requirement for rare earth materials. This study explores the behaviour of a transition metal SFi in which a [Ni/Pt] multilayer and a single Co layer, both of which possess perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA), are antiferromagnetically coupled. Helicity-independent all-optical switching (AOS) between the two antiparallel magnetisation states (AP+ and AP-) is demonstrated. The tunability of the [Ni/Pt] layer allows the strength of the PMA to be increased and for AOS to be achieved at higher temperature than in SFis based on NiPt alloy layers.

articleTitle: Dynamics of magnetization under spin-lock pulse with T1 relaxation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To overcome temporal limitation of functional MRI, researchers have investigated novel principles independent of hemodynamics to measure brain function. Among them, we focused on spin-lock sequences to measure tiny neural magnetic fields using magnetic resonance. Although several spin-lock sequences are proposed, the difference depends on visualized component of magnetization. Thus, it is important to investigate the dynamics of magnetization during spin-lock pulses. In this paper, we modified our previous analytical solution of the Bloch equation by distinguishing rotating frames to derive homogeneous and particular solution. Then, we compared the analytical solutions to numerical simulation using 4th-order Runge-Kutta method and observed decrease of errors on vertical magnetization components to spin-lock axis.

articleTitle: Novel Slot-opening-PM Variable Reluctance Machine with High-order-harmonic Winding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To combine the advantages of permanent magnet motor and electric excitation while overcoming the drawbacks of both, a hybrid excitation doubly salient reluctance motor is designed in this paper. To further improve the performance of the motor and distinguish it from the conventional concentrated winding distribution, a short-pitch distributed winding connection with improved fifth-order harmonics is newly applied to this machine in this paper. The electromagnetic performance is analyzed by finite element analysis.
