The simulation results demonstrate that the slot PM can effectively alleviate the magnetic circuit saturation phenomenon and the proposed winding arrangement can effectively improve the back EMF as well as the motor output torque density compared to the conventional centralized winding distribution.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Magneto-Elastic Effect on the High-Speed Capability of Rotors in Synchronous Machines with Buried Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Buried permanent magnets are secured against centrifugal forces by the rotor lamination sheets. The magnet bridges have to guarantee the mechanical strength of the rotor at high-speed operation. However, a large bridge thickness leads to increased leakage flux within the rotor, hence reduces the efficiency of the machine. The permeability of electrical steel reduces with mechanical stress due to the magneto-elastic effect. The consideration of this effect in the design process could allow larger bridge thicknesses and therefore increased mechanical strength at constant leakage flux. The effect is evaluated based on a V-arrangement of permanent magnets where the bridge thicknesses and the magnet angle are varied.

articleTitle: Microstructure and Magnetic Characterization on Ball-milled Fe-based Nanocrystalline Alloy Sheet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To realize the effective utilization of the end material and its application to a soft magnetic composite, Fe-based nanocrystalline alloy sheets were ball-milled, and platelet particles were obtained, in this work. Instrumental analyses revealed that although a micro strain was introduced into the nanocrystalline α-Fe grains in the achieved alloy powder, almost no changes were found in the amorphous part filled among the grains. The ball-milling treatment greatly increased the coercive force of the pulverized nanocrystalline sheet. Although the coercive force of the alloy powder decreased after the heat treatment, the coercive force remained to be approximately 10 times higher than that of the heat-treated alloy sheet without the ball-milling treatment, even after the heat treatment. The magnetic process of the ball-milled and heat treated nanocrystalline alloy powder will be discussed in detail in the conference based on the obtained results and Lorentz transmission electron microscopy.

articleTitle: Field-free switching enabled by interplay of spin-orbit torque and interlayer Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Realizing field-free perpendicular magnetization switching driven by spin-orbit torque (SOT) in a system compatible with sophisticated technology of magnetic random-access memory (MRAM) is challenging and crucial for the development of SOT-MRAM. Here, making use of an interlayer Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction(iDMI) effect in the classic Pt/[Co/Pt]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>/Pt multilayers and Pt/Co/Pt/Ir/Pt/Co/Pt synthetic antiferromagnetic (SAF) structures with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA), we achieved the desired field-free switching in a maximized degree as current applied colinear with a D vector. In contrast, the switching was fully disabled by an orthogonal configuration between the current and the D vector. These rules reproducible theoretically define a new SOT symmetry breaking law for the chiral magnets with the iDMI under zero applied field. Moreover, our work can also broaden usage of the classic [Pt/Co]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> multilayer system and the SAF structures from a passive pinned layer in a spin-transfer torque MRAM to an active data-storage layer in a perpendicular SOT-MRAM and expedite the development of the practical and efficient SOT devices.

articleTitle: Investigation of EEG Functional Connectivity Relationship with TMS Response in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury Patients
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: TMS is widely utilized as a treatment method for a variety of neurological and psychiatric disorders. The standard dose parameter for administration of TMS is known as the resting motor threshold. Several researchers have explored the effect of neuroanatomy on resting motor threshold. However, functional state of the brain has also been shown to influence resting motor threshold. This study explores the applications of EEG analysis in obtaining functional connectivity parameters and correlating them to the resting motor threshold. The data was collected from EEG recordings of mild traumatic brain injury patients undergoing TMS treatment. Various time frequency and power spectra values were derived from the TMS EEG data to examine the relationship between resting motor threshold and brain-scalp distance.

articleTitle: Novel Electrically Excited Doubly Salient Variable Reluctance Machine with High-order-harmonic Winding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: DC excited doubly salient variable reluctance machine has received more and more attention due to its robust rotor structure, low cost and easy heat dissipation. In this paper, a short-pitch distributed winding connection with improved fifth order harmonic is newly applied in this kind of machine to enhance the torque production. Its electromagnetic performance is analyzed by finite element analysis. The simulation results verify that compared with the traditional centralized winding distribution, the proposed winding arrangement can effectively improve the back electromotive force as well as the motor output torque density.

articleTitle: Room-Temperature Magnetoresistance in Nanojunctions Consisting of C8-BTBT Molecules Sandwiched Between Two Magnetic Thin-Film Edges
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We fabricate magnetic nanojunctions using Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">78</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf> (Py) thin-film edges which sandwich the high-mobility molecules, 2,7-dioctyl[1] benzothieno[3,2-b][1]benzothiophene (C8-BTBT) and investigate spin transport properties. As a result, a clear positive magnetoresistance (MR) effect is observed in Py/C8-BTBT/Py nanojunctions at room temperature. In addition, the observed positive MR effect can reveal that the magnetization curves of the thin-film edges are different from those of the thin film measured by magneto-optic Kerr effect spectroscopy. These findings offer a new insight into high-mobility molecular nano-spintronics, leading to the creation of functional spin devices.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable spinwave dispersion in continuous magnetic layer induced via artificial spin ice based magnonic crystal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spinwaves are a promising candidate for information processing in future computing technologies. Diodes and switches are routinely used in modern electronic circuitry and the hunt for spinwave equivalents is underway. Here we simulated a system which has many functionalities including anisotropic spinwave propagation, spinwave diode with frequency dependent propagation direction and the ability to prevent propagation. This is achieved by selecting the microstate of the reconfigurable artificial spin ice which is dipolar coupled to a continuous layer which supports spinwave propagation.

articleTitle: Permanent-magnet-free Variable Flux Reluctance Machines: Towards a Nonlinear Magnetodynamic Modeling Framework for Heavy-duty Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Nonlinear modeling of soft-magnetic laminated steels is critical for electromagnetic devices operating under magnetic saturation. Although it is possible to introduce the single-valued saturation curve of the soft-magnetic material in the 2-D modeling utilizing an iterative nonlinear solver, the modeling of dynamic magnetic field intensity components, i.e. eddy current and excess fields, requires solving the diffusion equation in 3-D. This article proposes a novel 2-D nonlinear finite element analysis coupled with the dynamic field components using the weak formulation. The proposed technique is applied to a variable flux reluctance machine to develop 100 Nm electromagnetic torque for heavy-duty applications. It is observed that the local flux density discrepancy between the proposed magnetodynamic and conventional magnetostatic models reaches 0.5 T, which causes a 51% discrepancy in the iron loss calculation.

articleTitle: Overlapping-skyrmions based racetrack memory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetic skyrmion is expected to be used as a binary digit of a domain motion type magnetic memory such as a racetrack memory. When two or more skyrmions are aligned on a track, a space is needed between each skyrmion. Thus, we propose the use of overlapping skyrmions for the binary. One of the overlapping skyrmion is known a biskyrmion. The biskyrmion is two overlapping skyrmions and its skyrmion number is 2. We simulate the overlapping skyrmions produced in the perpendicularly magnetized nanowire by using the micromagnetic approach. The two or more overlapping skyrmions can be stabilized in the wire. These were moved by the spin-polarized current flowing through the wire in a similar manner to the skyrmion.

articleTitle: Investigation on Inclination Angle of Inserted Permanent Magnets in Double-Stator Vernier Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Different permanent-magnet (PM) arrangements possess great influences on the machine performances. In this digest, investigation on the inclination angle of the inserted-PM sets in double-stator (DS) vernier machines is carried out. Through changing the flux concentration mode, the PM inclination affects the harmonic spectrum distribution and torque performance. Specific conclusions are revealed through comparative study with representative machine topologies, and thus the optimal PM arrangement candidates for DS-PM vernier machines have been obtained.

articleTitle: Biocompatible Nanoparticles for DDS with Field-Dependent Radical Pair System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, we used 2,2’-azobis(isobutyronitrile) (AIBN) as a radical pair-forming agent to investigate whether magnetic fields can control a liposomal drug release through differences in the physical properties of biomembranes. Judging from the overall result of seven kinds of prepared nanoparticles, the drug release potentials with magnetic field effects obtained using a static field of 0.25 T were more extensive on the order of 16-32%, than those obtained at geomagnetic fields. We strongly propose a novel photomagnetic controlled drug-release technology using these liposomal nanoparticles equipped with magnetic controls, because magnetic field effects on RPMs are known as the one and only phenomenon by which magnetic fields can switch over chemical reaction paths despite of their low energies.

articleTitle: Magnetic materials prediction, high through put, artificial intelligence versus materials intuition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Most of the time great scientific achievements are accidental, this is also true for material science, examples are high temperature superconductivity, colossal magnetoresistance and hard magnets. So far, inverse design has been realized only to a limited extent. Experience and intuition in materials science have also played a role in the discovery of new materials for basic science and application. The new research field of topology, that it is based on a single-particle model has been very successful in terms of the theoretical prediction of topological properties. However, the prediction of topological magnetic materials is already more challenging. In my talk I would like to illuminate the active research field of machine learning from my point of view for the areas of "new materials for magnetism and topology".

articleTitle: Chemical order, unit cell volume, and spontaneous magnetization in vapor-quenched single crystalline Fe0.6Al0.4 alloy thin film
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To investigate the influence from chemical order to the spontaneous magnetization and unit cell volume in partially ordered B2 Fe-Al system, the vapor quenched single crystalline films of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf> were systematically studied. The X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that the chemical order in Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf> was changed from long to short range B2 order with lowering the deposition temperature. This chemical order changing accompanied the strong enhancement of spontaneous magnetization with the expansion of lattice volume.

articleTitle: An Experimental-Numerical Approach for Energy Loss Separation of Grain-Oriented Electrical Steels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Energy loss analysis of the magnetic cores of electrical machines and power transformers, requires an accurate figure of energy loss mechanism and components. This paper proposes an advanced experimental-numerical approach to further understanding the magnetising process of Grain-Oriented (GO) electrical steels with predominant focus on energy loss separation. As the main contribution of this work, static hysteresis loop (SHL) of the material can be constructed for energy loss analysis, and dynamic modelling purposes. The proposed approach is in line with the magnetic hysteresis and phenomenological concepts of rate-dependent and rate-independent energy loss components of ferromagnetic materials under time varying magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Analysis and Monitoring Method for Inter-turn Short Circuit Fault for PMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposed a monitoring method for inter-turn short circuit (ITSC) fault for PMSM. The paper analyzes the electromagnetic behavior of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) under single-phaseITSC fault working condition. On this basis, a new diagnosis method for ITSC fault based on 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> ripple of d-axis and q-axis current is proposed. Furthermore, the amplitude of the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> ripple of d-axis and q-axis current can be used to identify the seriousness of ITSC fault. The correctness of the proposed method is verified by prototype experiment.

articleTitle: Iron oxide nanoparticles as a new tool for treating cardiovascular diseases
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Thrombotic events are a major cause of death and disability worldwide. Thrombolysis with the clot busting drug tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) or thromboprophylaxis using anticoagulants such as heparin are frontline treatments for thrombotic diseases. However, they account for important limitations in terms of effectivity and safety, producing in some cases unwanted bleeding episodes in patients. Magnetic hyperthermia (MH) mediated by magnetic nanoparticles, targeted to localized tumors, has been used to treat cancer. Here we demonstrate that MH mediated by functionalized magnetic nanoparticles can act to improve the efficacy of antithrombotic and thrombolytic treatments. Iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) functionalised with the PAC-1 antibody (f-IONPs) were prepared for clot targeting, and the potential of MH to enhance diffusion of antithrombotic drugs into the clot was demonstrated. We found that clot-targeted MH increased the efficacy of clot-busting drugs in ex vivo-derived human blood clots, leading to a significant reduction in clot weight. Our results demonstrate that surface-localized MH could be applied to enhance the action of antithrombotic and clot-busting drugs.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation and Low-Order Component Optimization of Axial Electromagnetic Force for an Axial Flux Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The low-order high-amplitude component of axial electromagnetic force is the leading cause of electromagnetic vibration and noise of axial flux permanent magnet (AFPM) motors. In this paper, based on the analytical calculation of the axial electromagnetic force for a 20-pole 24-slot AFPM motor, the low-order axial electromagnetic force component is weakened by optimizing the motor’s electromagnetic structure. First, the three-dimensional structural model of the motor is equated to a two-dimensional analytical model, which is used to calculate the magnetic fields generated by each of the armature winding and permanent magnet (PM). Then, combined with the Maxwell tensor method, the axial electromagnetic force analysis waveform in motor loaded condition is further obtained, and the target low-order high-amplitude component is extracted by two-dimensional Fourier analysis. Finally, taking this axial electromagnetic force component minimization as the optimization target function, considering the output torque and ripple as constraints, the genetic algorithm is used to search for the optimal point by varying the structural parameters of the motor. The results show that the target low-order high-amplitude component of the axial electromagnetic force of the optimized motor is effectively suppressed, and the output torque ripple decreases with slightly increased torque amplitude, which provides a practical method for vibration and noise reduction of AFPM motors.

articleTitle: Comparative study on the origin of spin Hall effect in poly and single crystalline α-W in W/CoFeB bilayers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work we have aimed to deposit polycrystalline and epitaxial α-W films and estimate the spin Hall angle (SHA) of the above-mentioned phases of W. We have employed spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR) technique to understand the origin of spin Hall effect (SHE) in polycrystalline α-W and compare it with the epitaxially grown α-W in W/CFB bilayers. We have observed that the polycrystalline film of α-W has shown contributions from both extrinsic and intrinsic origins of SHE while the epitaxial film of α-W has majorly shown contributions from intrinsic origin of SHE.

articleTitle: A Novel Planar Magnetic Flux Concentrator and Its Application in Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a planar magnetic flux concentrator (MFC) for reducing the leakage flux and increasing the power transmission in the wireless power transfer (WPT) system. The magnetic field distribution in WPT and eddy current distribution in MFC are investigated. The Finite Element Method (FEM) based simulation results show that the magnetic flux density is increased around the centre hole area of the Tx and Rx coils and decreased in the outer area of the Tx and Rx coils. The experiment results demonstrate that the power transfer and magnetic coupling coefficient are increased by using a planar MFC in WPT system. The equivalent circuits of WPT transformer with and without a planar MFC are also proposed based on the impedance measurement and analysis.

articleTitle: BH curves of Anisotropic Alnico Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents the measurement results of the BH curve of the Alnico 8 (LNGT40) with recoil loops. The measurements were handled in a Vibrating Sample Magnetometer (VSM). The magnet samples have a cubic shape with 3 mm sides. BH curves in preferred (easy) and transverse (hard) directions and recoil loops were measured and compared to Alnico 9 as well as to the data from the supplier. The loading point of the cubic magnet in 0 A/m applied magnetic field was found.

articleTitle: Development of an Optical Probe Current Sensor for Local and Narrow Area Measurement Using Magnetic Domain Reversal in Bi-Substituted Rare-Earth Iron Garnet Crystal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The authors have developed an optical probe current sensor using a Faraday effect of granular magnetic film as a new current sensor to replace a current transformer and a Rogowski coil. However, the sensitivity for small current fields in the previously developed sensor was low, and the signal was buried in the floor noise, making accurate measurement impossible. In this study, we investigated a sensor using magnetic domain reversal of Bi:RIG crystal for Faraday element to solve the previous problem and succeeded in developing a sensor with excellent linearity and a high signal-to-noise ratio by optimizing the Bi:RIG crystal thickness and the light-beam diameter to be irradiated.

articleTitle: Thermal Characteristics and Cooling Methods of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors with High Flux Density
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To make electrical aircraft practical, a high-power density motor is needed. Therefore, we used finite element method (FEM) to investigate the power density and thermal characteristics of an 8 poles 9 slots permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The motor has a 0.3mm copper plating on rotor’s surface, which can reduce the penetration of harmonics in the magneto-motive force produced by the armature windings, cause less eddy current losses and heats. Some cooling methods were quantitatively evaluated to suppress the rotor and magnet’s temperature rise more efficiently. Simulation results show that the power density of the PMSM can be enhanced by using copper plating and appropriate cooling method.

articleTitle: Millimeter-sized, ultra-sensitive planar Hall effect gradiometer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We present a miniature, ultra-sensitive magnetic field gradiometer in the form of a single elliptical planar Hall effect sensor that allows measuring magnetic field at 9 different locations on a 4 mm length scale [1]. The gradiometer detects magnetic field gradients with equivalent gradient magnetic noise levels of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 958, \sim 192, \sim 51$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 26\ \text{nT}/\mathrm{m}\surd$</tex> Hz at 0.1, 1, 10, and 50 Hz, respectively, and tested under ambient conditions by measuring the field gradient produced by an electric current flowing through a straight wire. The compact size, low noise level, versatility, simple design, and low cost of this gradiometer makes it a suitable choice for detecting magnetic field gradients in small, confined spaces such as current probes or wearable electronic medical devices.

articleTitle: Permanent Magnet Linear Machines with Asymmetrical Tooth Tip
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a slotted permanent magnet linear machines(PMLMs) with asymmetrical tooth tip, which has high thrust density and low thrust ripple. The topology structure is firstly introduced, and then the sensitivity of structure parameters is investigated. Finally, the optimal structure is optimized, and validated by experimental results.

articleTitle: Influence of filler fraction and morphology on magnetic performance of polymer bonded magnets produced by laser powder bed fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Bonded permanent magnets are key components in many energy conversion, sensor and actuator devices. These applications require high magnetic performance and freedom of shape. With additive manufacturing processes, for example laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), it is possible to produce bonded magnets with customized stray field distribution. Here, the behavior of large Sm-Fe-N platelets with a high aspect ratio as filler material and its influence on the arrangement and the resulting magnetic properties are examined in comparison to a spherical magnetic filler. The platelet-shaped particles align themselves perpendicular to the buildup direction during the process, which offers a new and cost-effective way of producing composites by LPBF with anisotropic properties.

articleTitle: Modeling of Multi-Level Spin-Orbit Torque-MRAM: Scalability, Stochasticity, and Variations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, we, for the first time, demonstrate a comprehensive model of the multi-level Spin-Orbit torque (SOT)-MRAM. Scalability, stochasticity, and variations of the multi-level SOT-MRAM are captured within a unified model framework based on the modified Preisach model of hysteresis. The model functionalities are verified by experimental data from four types of multi-level SOT devices fabricated by us and others, including the major switching loop, minor loops, device-size dependence, and the variation of intermediate states.

articleTitle: Spin Wave Decoherence in the Presence of Dispersive Shock Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The processes for generation, amplification, and protraction of oscillating signals - often for information transfer - are inherently associated with dispersive decoherence and nonlinear phenomena. One such example are shock waves, which can be generated alongside, or instead of, the desired signal while dispersion and broadening can limit the propagation range of spin waves. Here, we develop a numerical model to investigate a generation process which results in dispersive shockwaves (DSW) being observed. In contrast to previous work, our system is strictly linear and does not require surface spin waves to observe DSW. We demonstrate how decoherence associated to DSWs is an inherent property of signals propagating through spin wave systems. We then discuss use cases for this behaviour.

articleTitle: Fast Propagation and Merger of Magnetic Domain Walls in Low Magnetostrictive Amorphous Submicrometric Wires
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Here we report on the magnetic domain walls associated with the magnetization reversal process in cylindrical amorphous submicrometric wires prepared by rapid quenching from the melt. Such domain walls can reach significantly high velocities, of up to 4000 m/s, under axially applied magnetic fields. We also show that, by means of an accurate control over the nucleation and propagation phenomena, one can force the generation of additional domain walls, and even have these walls moving towards each other. Domain walls moving in opposite directions will eventually merge, as shown by a double peak amplitude detected in a suitably located pick-up coil. The merger of domain walls could be employed for simple domain wall logic operations and for magnetic sensing applications.

articleTitle: Spin-Gapless Semiconducting Properties in a Polycrystalline CoCrFeAl Heusler-Alloy Film
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Heusler alloys have been investigated intensively over the last decades due to their almost indefinite possibilities to demonstrate a broad range of magnetic properties, including a half-metallic ferromagnet, antiferromagnet and topological insulator. Recently, a CoCrFeAl Heusler alloy has been predicted as a spin-gapless semiconductor according to first-principles calculations. In this report, we deposited a polycrystalline CoCrFeAl film using sputtering with precise control in the stoichiometry. We confirmed the growth of the CoCrFeAl films in the A2 phase at least after annealing at 400°C for two hours. These films exhibited clear ferromagnetic properties only after their crystallisation. We will report the corresponding spin Hall signals at our presentation.

articleTitle: Inductive heating based on VHF-ISM radio band frequencies as technology platform for efficient heating of metallic micro-scaled bonding layers in MEMS packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a method for selective and energy-efficient induction heating of metallic microstructures to support and enhance metal bonding technologies for MEMS packaging. The technological challenges include the use of miniaturized coils for homogeneous heat distribution, the implementation of VHF-ISM radio band frequencies up to f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> = 40.68 MHz for the generation of high frequency electromagnetic fields and the integration of the inductive equipment into a heating and bonding system. FE simulation and infrared (IR) thermography were used to characterize the inductive process with low coil currents of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> < 30 A and very fast heating rates of ∆T = 150 K/s. As a result, bonding times and pressures can be reduced significantly.

articleTitle: Ultra-low-current Spin Hall Nano-oscillators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report on the magnetodynamic properties and the magnetization auto-oscillations of ultra-low current 20 nm width nano-constriction spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) fabricated on different substrates and seed layers. Combining an optimized W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">88</inf>Ta<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> alloy, low damping CoFeB, and a moderate perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, we push the threshold current down to 35 µA in the best devices. The best overall magnetodynamic properties and lowest threshold currents are obtained when using a 3 nm thick AlOx seed layer in between the high-resistance Si substrate and the W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">88</inf>Ta<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> layer.

articleTitle: Analysis and Magnetic Field Calculation Method for Motor with Saliency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The effect of rotor with ‘saliency’ on magnetic field is important to the performance of propulsion motors. Thus, a novel analytical model and magnetic field calculation method that can consider the saliency effect is proposed, and the different effects of the saliency structure on the d- and q-axis magnetic field and principle of corresponding energy conversion are investigated. Then, taking synchronous reluctance motor and reluctance motor with simple salient pole as an example, the calculation and analysis process of d- and q-axis magnetic fields and the mapping relationship between their difference and energy conversion are elaborated. Finally, the accuracy of the proposed method is verified by finite element analysis (FEA) under the combination of various parameters. The results show that the proposed method is in good agreement with the results of FEA in a wide range of parameters.

articleTitle: A Path Integral method for numerical simulations of Spin Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Following the way paved by path integral molecular dynamics, we build a classical spin model from which we can compute expectation values of a spin whilst taking into account its underlying quantisation, in the presence of a magnetic field. We express the spin algebra in terms of coherent spin states, which enable the transition from a discrete quantum system to an equivalent continuous classical model, and recast the quantum mechanics in the framework of path integrals. We approximate the path integral in the high-temperature limit and derive an effective classical Hamiltonian. The quantized nature of the spin manifests itself as an anisotropic effective field. Solving the effective classical model using atomistic spin dynamics, we calculate thermodynamic observables and show that our effective classical model produces accurate quantum expectation values within its relevant temperature range.

articleTitle: SNR Impact of Magnetic Capping Layer in Granular FePt-L10 Media
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, we present a micromagnetic modeling study on a scheme to enhance medium signal-to-noise ratio in heat assisted magnetic recording. By adding a relatively thin magnetic capping layer on top of FePt-L10 granular thin film, recording performance can be significantly improved, especially at high linear densities, provided the capping layer has significant magnetic moment during recording.

articleTitle: Sub-harmonic excitation in passive spintronic diodes based on magnetic tunnel junctions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spin-torque diodes based on magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) are devices with a wide range of potential industrial and technological applications. The nanoscale size of MTJs allows to efficiently exploit phenomena such as voltage controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) to manipulate the ferromagnetic state and excite resonant modes in the device. In this work, we predict a fractional parametric resonant response in passive spintronic diode excited simultaneously by spin-transfer torque and VCMA by means of micromagnetic simulations. This resonance mechanism can be used for frequency divider and compact demodulation schemes.

articleTitle: Large low field magnetocaloric effect in Laves phase intermetallic compounds R'0.33Ho0.33Er0.33Al2 (R' = Gd, Tb and Dy) and Gd0.33Dy0.33Ho0.33Al2
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Polycrystalline Laves phase intermetallic compounds Dy<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Ho<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Er<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Tb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Ho<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Er<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Gd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Ho<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Er<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Gd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Dy<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Ho<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.33</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> have been synthesized and characterized by the means of magnetization measurements. The samples crystalize in MgCu2- type cubic structure (space group Fd-3m) and order ferromagnetically at ~30 K, ~45 K, ~60 K and ~85 K (TC) respectively. Large low field magnetocaloric effect is obtained for these compounds. A combination of these four materials can help build a magnetic refrigerator for hydrogen liquefaction.

articleTitle: Spin diode effect in extended magnetic insulating films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive study of the nonlinear transport properties of magnons, which are electrically emitted or absorbed inside extended YIG films by spin transfer effects at a YIG|Pt interface. Our purpose is to experimentally elucidate the pertinent picture behind the asymmetric electrical variation of the magnon transconductance analogous to an electric diode. The feature is rooted in the variation of the density of low-lying spin excitations via an electrical shift of the magnon chemical potential. As the intensity of the spin transfer increases in the forward direction (regime of magnon emission), the transport properties of low-energy magnon go through 3 distinct regimes: i) at low currents, where the spin current is a linear function of the electrical current, the spin transport is ballistic and set by the film thickness; ii) for amplitudes of the order of the damping compensation threshold, it switches to a highly correlated regime limited by magnon-magnon relaxation process and marked by a saturation of the magnon transconductance. Here the main bias, that controls the magnon density, is thermal fluctuations beneath the emitter. iii) As the temperature under the emitter approaches the Curie temperature, scattering with high-energy magnons dominates, leading to diffusive transport.

articleTitle: The correlation between skyrmion size, shape and device geometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This study calculates the radius of the skyrmion for nanotracks with varying widths, exploring the effect of device geometry on the size of the skyrmion. While previous studies have evaluated the skyrmion radius for materials with different properties, less work has focused on the impact of device width. Numerical calculations based on the Landau-Lifshitz Gilbert equation were conducted, and it was found that the skyrmion radius was strongly influenced by both material and device geometry. The study presents and discusses the reduction of skyrmion size with device width, as well as the transition from skyrmion to a warm-type magnetic domain. These findings are examined in terms of the effect of edge force

articleTitle: Nd-Fe-B films prepared by low temperature process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Although sputtering-fabricated Nd-Fe-B films have been reported to achieve excellent magnetic properties, the films require an annealing process such as substrate heating and/or post annealing. This study focuses on Nd-Fe-B films' preparation by low temperature process. In detail, laser-induced forward transfer technique using two targets (target A: pulsed laser deposition-fabricated Nd-Fe-B films, target B: Nd-Fe-B sintered magnets) were conducted. Fundamental properties were examined for the films prepared by each target in the study.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Planar Power Inductor for Beyond 10 MHz Using Fe-based Composite Magnetic Core
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A planar power inductor for a beyond 10MHz switching DC-DC converter was fabricated and evaluated. A closed magnetic circuit consisting of Fe-based composited magnetic core and a PCB based planar coil were used for planar inductor with a 4.8×3.2×1.84mm in size, and the fabricated inductor exhibited a high-quality factor of over 40 in 10~20 MHz frequency range. The planar inductor was implemented into a beyond 10 MHz switching GaN-FET two-phase buck converter with 24 V input, 5 V-3 A output, and the converter had an efficiency of 81% when 15 W output.

articleTitle: Reduced Switching Current with a Light Metal in a Tri-layer Spin-orbit Torque Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The use of a tri-layer structure and light metals have each received much research attention in spin-orbit torque (SOT) technology. We combine these two approaches by placing an ultra-thin (1 nm) Cu adjacent to the bottom ferromagnetic layer in a tri-layer SOT device. This can reduce the switching current by ~30% compared to the conventional bi-layer device due to enhanced SOT efficiency. This advantage is more obvious under a unipolar condition and it is attributed to a slightly asymmetric interface caused by the Cu insertion. By magneto-optical Kerr effect microscopy, we also observe a domain reversal mechanism distinct from the bi-layer case.

articleTitle: Evaluation of microstructure and magnetic performance of Fe- 6.5 wt% Si soft magnetic powder core
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper reports microstructure and magnetic performance of Fe-6.5wt% Si (Fe-Si) soft magnetic powder cores. Fe-Si powder core showed the extremely high saturation magnetization in the range from 186.1 to 192.2 emu/g depending on the annealing temperature. The permeability of the powder core at the frequency of 20 kHz gradually increased from 33.9 to 46.1 as the annealed temperature of the core was increased from 400 to 800 °C. The total core loss at the maximum magnetic flux density of 100 mT shows the increased tendency as function of frequencies in all annealed cores. In particular, the high saturation magnetization of 192.0 emu/g and lowest total core loss 267 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> measured at 20 kHz and 100 mT were obtained for the annealed powder core at 800 °C, suggesting that it is one of the promising candidates for high frequency power electronic devices.

articleTitle: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Using a Magnetoresistive Sensor with a Flux Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, we developed a signal detection unit composing a magnetoresistive (MR) sensor and flux transformer circuit for ultra-low field magnetic resonance imaging (ULF-MRI). The equivalent noise level of the detection unit was reduced to approximately 1/20 using the flux transformer comparing to the original MR sensor. We also demonstrated an ULF-MRI measurement using a phantom. The obtained results confirmed the potential of the MR sensor-based detection unit for the ULF-MRI measurements.

articleTitle: Mechanical Spin Current Generation via Intrinsic Spin-Orbit Interaction with Spatial Inversion Symmetry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We microscopically show that a spin current is generated from dynamical lattice distortion via intrinsic spin-orbit interaction in a system with spatial inversion symmetry. We consider a tight-binding model of s and p electrons on a simple cubic lattice, and examine the effects of lattice distortion microscopically. Effects of lattice distortion are incorporated through local modulation of hopping integrals. Using the linear response theory, we calculate the spin current in response to dynamical lattice distortion. The obtained spin current has mutually orthogonal flow and spin-polarization directions, as in the case of the spin Hall effect. The spin current is generated from the longitudinal component of elastic wave and is proportional to lattice displacement and frequency and the square of wave number of elastic wave.

articleTitle: Human Error Verification during ELF stimuli: Retinal Receptivity of ELF-Inducing Phosphenes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Needless to say, considerations for details in the retinal receptivity of the extremely low frequency (ELF)-inducing blindsight-like phosphenes are of great importance. In this paper, a further detailed validation of human reliabilities during the ELF stimuli was carried out. In the results of our analysis using signal detection theory, we found that the supraliminal effect had a certain amount of persistence for the flicker in the central part of the visual fields. Our results definitely revealed precious findings about an actual control of retinal activities with blindsight-like phosphenes induced by ELF stimuli, which may be able to provide preventive solutions for serious artificial mistakes and/or human errors.

articleTitle: Topological spin memory of antiferromagnetically coupled skyrmions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: I will discuss our recent discovery of a spin memory effect that stems from the topology of antiferromagnetically coupled skyrmion pairs in [Co/Gd/Pt]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> multilayered films (Wang et al., 2022). Photoemission electron microscopy imaging shows that these bubble skyrmions that are stable at room temperature evolve into complex in-plane spin textures as the temperature is lowered and reform completely when the sample is warmed back up. Micromagnetic simulations reveal that the topological charge is preserved throughout the spin reorientation transition (SRT) and furthermore demonstrate the key role that the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interactions play in this topological spin memory effect.

articleTitle: Current-induced magnetization switching in magnetic multilayers with interlayer exchange coupling by dual spin-orbit torque
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The current-induced magnetization switching was investigated for Pt/Co/Ir/Co/Pt films. The measurements based on the conventional four-probe method and the domain structure imaging revealed that the macroscopic switching process for Pt/Co/Ir/Co/Pt is considerably dependent on magnetic structures. The dynamics of spin-orbit torque switching are also shown using the macrospin numerical calculation for both the antiferromagnetically- and ferromagnetically-coupled cases sandwiched by spin Hall layers. The present results provide the macroscopic and microscopic pictures of switching mechanism for the interlayer exchange-coupled systems with dual spin-orbit torque and a guideline to design a spintronic device with high-efficient operation.

articleTitle: Ultrasmall Fe3O4@Au Composite Nanoparticles with Different Sizes of Fe3O4 for Magnetic Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We reported the synthesis and characterization of ultrasmall iron oxide/gold composite nanoparticles (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@Au NPs) with different sizes of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, and the evaluation of their heating efficiency for potential use in magnetic hyperthermia application. The Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs were synthesized using the thermal decomposition method with three types of sizes of ~5 nm, ~10 nm, and ~13 nm. Gold was then deposited onto the surface of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs by reducing gold acetate at 190°C. The synthesized Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and their Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@Au NPs were characterized using TEM, EDX, XRD, and VSM analyses. The magnetization of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs increased with increasing their size with 74.7 emu/g for ~13 nm. The mass percentage of Au in Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@Au NPs estimated from the magnetization values were 94.3, 96.3, 77.0wt% for Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ~5 nm@Au, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ~10 nm@Au, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ~13 nm@Au, respectively. The specific absorption rate (SAR) increased with increasing size of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> with the maximum values of 136.7 and 23,4 W/g under an applied magnetic field of 25.7 kA/m and 267 kHz for Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ~13 nm, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ~13 nm@Au NPs, respectively, exhibiting high heating efficient capabilities and indicating potential use for magnetic hyperthermia.

articleTitle: Temperature-dependent spin dynamics in WSe2/Pt/CoFe trilayers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, magnetic anisotropy and magnetic damping factor (α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) were studied at different temperatures (T) for the tungsten diselenide (WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)/Pt/CoFe heterostructure samples with various WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> monolayer numbers (n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ML</inf>). We observed that the WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> underlayer could weaken the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy due to the increased interfacial roughness and decreased orbital hybridization effect. In particular, the insertion of WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> leads to a rather high α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>, which mainly arises from the contributions of interfacial two-magnon scattering (TMS) and spin pumping by the WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer. When T is gradually reduced below 200 K, the magnetic damping factor of WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Pt/CoFe exhibits a much strong temperature dependence, as compared with the single CoFe films or Pt/CoFe bilayer. We consider the significant drop in damping at T<200 K is due to the decreased TMS scattering since the interfacial random spins become ordered. Our work elucidates the significant implications of two-dimensional materials on the magnetic properties, which will be valuable for the development of transition-metal dichalcogenides based spintronics devices.

articleTitle: Effect of an antiferromagnetic order on tailoring Dzyaloshinskii- Moriya interaction in Pt/Co/IrMn trilayer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Antiferromagnet (AFM) has currently participated in the spin-orbit torque (SOT) magnetoresistive random access memory (MRAM) technolopgy due to its great potential to be applied to the field-free SOT switching and promote the thermal stability of MRAM. However, effect of the introduction of AFM into the basic structure of SOT-MRAM composed of a heavy metal/ferromagnet (FM) bilayer was still not comprehensively understood. This work reports the effect of how an antiferromagnetic (AFM) order modifies the strength of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in a heavy metal (Pt)/FM (Co)/AFM (IrMn) trilayer, studied by SOT switching and loop-shift method. Increasing the AFM order reflected on exchange bias (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf>) through increasing the thickness of IrMn appears to significantly reduce the DMI strength of the trilayer, which leads to the reduction of the external field for yielding a complete SOT switching. The reduced DMI strength may ascribe to the Hex-hosted uni-directional anisotropy suppressing the neighboring spin canting in the FM layer. This stabilization for the magnetic moments via the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf>-hosted uni-directional anisotropy also improved the stability of SOT switching on the random read/write characterization, in which the strong AFM order would promote the memristivity for neuromorphic application and the weak AFM order would give rise to the stochasticity for the purpose of physically unclonable functionality. This work demonstrates the significance of an intrinsic tuning over the AFM order would serve as a switch to turn the SOT device into a stochastic/memristive cell to bridge probabilistic and neuromorphic computing.

articleTitle: Atomistic simulations on the effects of grain size in HAMR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Using atomistic models, L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> FePt systems were modeled undergoing heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR), while varying grain diameter and height. To investigate properties relevant to the application of FePt in HAMR, atomistic simulations were done to calculate temperature dependent anisotropy scaling, Curie temperature, magnetic switching profiles for grain diameters ranging from 3nm to 12nm, and grain heights ranging from 5nm to 10nm. The results section highlights some key findings in the magnetic switching data obtained, alongside a holistic comparison of various HAMR recording tracks which have undergone a writing process.

articleTitle: Mode hopping impact on NFT protrusion measurement in HAMR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In terms of head media spacing control in heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR), it's important to measure laser power induced protrusion in writing. Near field transducer (NFT) in the head provides confined heat to media. However, heat generated by laser diode is partially absorbed in NFT which leads to localized protrusion (NFT protrusion). Since NFT protrusion area is narrow, it's difficult to measure by conventional touch down based method. Burst writing scheme (BWS) is one of the proposed methods for NFT protrusion measurement [1]. BWS implements two writing modes, steady state writing in which NFT is fully protruded and burst writing in which NFT protrusion is quite small. Read back amplitude curve as a function of TFC power in each writing mode is used for NFT protrusion calculation. Read back amplitude usually increases as TFC power increases, however for steady state writing, unintentional amplitude drop has been observed in some heads and it affects the result of NFT protrusion directly. From the relation between read back amplitude and thermal sensor output which reflects NFT temperature, we find that laser mode hopping causes the amplitude drop. Since mode hopping happens several times in 1 revolution continuous writing, average amplitude is expected to include several laser modes. We successfully mitigated amplitude drop by using amplitude average in continuous writing. As one example, NFT protrusion measured by this method was twice as large as the one by conventional method by avoiding small NFT protrusion estimation caused by amplitude drop. In the future we plan to understand mode hopping in burst writing for accurate NFT protrusion measurement even though mode hopping effect was not observed in burst writing.

articleTitle: Atomic Scale Visualization of Magnetic Coupling at Individual Defects in Functional Materials by Spatially Resolved Electron Magnetic Circular Dichroism
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Atomic-plane resolved (APR) electron magnetic circular dichroism (EMCD) in a ferrimagnetic Sr2FeMoO6 based on the groundbreaking combination of spatially resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy technique with chromatic/spherical aberration correction. With the spatial resolution up to atomic scale, EMCD enables us to study local magnetic properties of individual defects. Direct measurement of local magnetic coupling at individual antiphase boundary was achieved, reduction in Fe and Ni EMCD signal is experimentally observed.

articleTitle: Effect of Radial and Axial Magnet Segmentation on PM Eddy Current Losses for Brushless Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: One of the major issues in the design of high-speed permanent magnet (PM) motors is the magnet losses. Magnet eddy-current losses are one of the significant loss components and it is related to the motor frequency directly. In this paper, a detailed analysis of a high-speed brushless permanent magnet synchronous motor is performed. Magnet losses as well as other loss component such as iron and copper AC and DC losses are also investigated comprehensively for the reference motor selected.

articleTitle: Restricted grain growth and role of Nb precipitates in Nd-Fe-Nb-B melt spun ribbon
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Microstructural evolution of Nd12Fe80.5Nb1.5B6 isochronally annealed Nd-Fe-Nb-B sample at various temperature 200 – 900 °C is probed to understand the role of Nb in restricting grain growth and its concomitant effect on the measured magnetic properties. The grain size (~25 nm) and coercivity (~ 12.5 kOe) was found to be invariant for samples annealed up to 700 °C. Grain size was found to increase for higher annealing temperature and correspondingly coercivity was found to decrease. 3-dimentional atom probe tomography revealed the presence of Nb clusters pinning the grain boundaries and subsequently coarsening for higher annealing temperature.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Novel Double-Stator Hybrid Flux Machine for Direct-Drive Electric Traction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The transverse-flux machine (TFM) is an ideal candidate for direct-drive traction due to its short effective flux path and high torque density. However, TFMs normally suffer from large longitudinal size, while the toroidal coils are hard to arrange for ordinary inner-runner machines. The configuration of phases leaves tricky in TFMs. To this end, this study sets out to propose a novel double-stator hybrid flux machine (DS-HFM) topology in order to make direct-drive machines more compact and powerful. In the DS-HFM, the poly phases are distributed along the circumferential direction with physical isolation end regions. Conventional toroidal coils are redesigned to concentrated coils. The operational principle is introduced and analyzed. Through 3-D finite element analysis, the quantitative performance evaluation verifies the effectiveness of this idea.

articleTitle: VCMA-MTJ: towards Ghz operation low power MRAM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: With STT-MRAM now in mass production for embedded flash memory replacement at several foundries, research shifts towards lower power switching mechanisms. We review opportunities and challenges of voltage controlled MRAM through the VCMA effect. We present the material research needed to improve VCMA coefficient in production-relevant magnetic tunnel junctions. We also review precessional switching mechanism and constrains it poses on device operation and propose several solutions and in depth studies carried out on 300mm integrated VCMA-MTJ devices.

articleTitle: Tunneling magnetoresistance effects based on van der Waals room-temperature ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Lately, van der Waals (vdW) magnetic heterostructures have caught increasing research attention in spintronics. However, the development of vdW materials in practical spintronics devices has been largely hindered by the lack of room-temperature magnetic order. Inspired by the recently discovered vdW ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2, which has been shown to exhibit considerable perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and magnetic order above room temperature, we investigate the basic electronic structure and magnetic properties of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>GaTe2 and tunneling magnetoresistance effect in magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) with structure of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>GaTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Insulator/Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>GaTe2 by using first-principles calculations. It turns out that Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>GaTe2 with highly spin-polarized Fermi surface ensures that such magnetic tunnel junctions may have substantial tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) effect at room temperature even comparable to existing conventional MgO-based MTJs. Our findings reveal that Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>GaTe2-based MTJs may be the promising candidate for realizing long-waiting full magnetic vdW spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Theory for Temperature Dependence of Tunnel Magnetoresistance: Crucial Role of Interfacial s-d Exchange Interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Large reduction of tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) ratios with increasing temperature is a long-standing problem in the field of spintronics. We here theoretically demonstrate that the s-d exchange interaction at interfaces of magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) is a possible physical origin of this phenomenon. We calculate the TMR ratio at finite temperature in Fe/MgO/Fe(001) by constructing a tight-binding model with the s-d exchange interaction. It is shown that the calculated TMR ratio sharply decreases as a function of temperature, consistent with experimental results. The s-d exchange interaction propagates thermally induced spin fluctuations from d- to s-electron state, which breaks the half-metallicity in the Δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> state and reduces the TMR ratio significantly. We also propose a nonempirical method for estimating the coupling constant of the s-d exchange interaction J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sd</inf>, which is the key parameter for the temperature dependence of the TMR ratio. The estimated values of J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sd</inf> for bcc Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> successfully explain the material dependence of the TMR ratio at room temperature obtained in previous experiments.

articleTitle: Magnetization dynamics of [Co60Fe40/Pt]5 multilayers synthesized over varying Pt buffer structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have investigated in time and frequency domain the magnetization dynamics of a set of [Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</inf>/Pt]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> multilayers which were sputtered over varying Pt buffer structures and present perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. The results showed clearly the strong effects on magnetization dynamics of changing substrate preparation and that in the case of small damping and angle oscillations both frequency and time-domain approaches agreed in characterizing magnetization dynamics of [Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</inf>/Pt]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> multilayers.

articleTitle: Dipolar core-shell cells with enhanced write speed and reduced cross-talk of perpendicular shape anisotropy MRAM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The concept of Perpendicular Shape-Anisotropy Spin-Transfer-Torque Magnetic Random-Access Memory (PSA-STT-MRAM) tackles the downsize scalability limit of conventional ultrathin magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJ) below sub-20 nm technological nodes. It is based on a thick storage layer, enhancing the thermal stability factor ∆ of the device via perpendicular shape anisotropy. However, this comes at the expense of a tendency for a non-reversal mechanism, increasing the switching time and capping the stability of the device versus aspect ratio. Besides, the high aspect ratio and volume supporting thermal stability significantly increase the stray field in neighbouring bits in comparison with the conventional MTJs, in the case of dense arrays. In this work, we show that, by making use of a dipolar-coupled core-shell structure as a storage layer for the PSA-MTJ, both the reversal mechanism and stray field challanges are largely improved. We use macrospin simulations in an array to show the decrease in stray field, and micromagnetic simulations to show the faster switching times while avoiding the domain-wall limit, for a given thermal stability.

articleTitle: Negative spin polarization of Mn2VGa Heusler alloy thin film studied in current-perpendicular-to-plane giant magnetoresistance devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>VGa (MVG) ferrimagnetic Heusler alloy possesses negative spin polarization, meaning that the spin direction of the spin-polarized conduction electron is the opposite of the magnetization direction. This characteristic is technologically important because it can increase freedom in the structures of spintronics devices and improve their performance. We fabricated current-perpendicular-to-plane giant magnetoresistance (CPP-GMR) devices consisting of MVG/Ag/CoFe by sputter deposition and demonstrated negative MR, which provided evidence of negative spin polarization of MVG. The observed negative MR ratio reached -1.3%, the highest value among the reported negative MR in CPP-GMR devices. This result suggests relatively high negative spin polarization of MVG.

articleTitle: Strain Effects on the Magnetic Ordering in A-Type Antiferromagnetic Pr0.5Sr0.5MnO3 Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In order to understand the origin of the strain effects on the magnetic ordering of layered manganite, high quality Pr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>MnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films are grown on different substrates with pulse laser deposition. In addition to the regular magnetization and transportation measurements, ferromagnetic resonance technique is applied to investigate the internal field of PSMO films. In cooperated with magnetization and high resolution X-ray diffraction, the distinct magnetic and electronic transport behaviors are attributed to the strain modulated orientations of laminar FM layer because of the interfacial strain.

articleTitle: An ELF magnetic Control Study of Metamorphic Qualities in T4-Administrated Axolotls (Ambystoma mexicanum)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate extremely low frequency (ELF) magnetic effects with different exposure timings on the forced metamorphosis of Mexican axolotls, which is induced by a function of thyroxine (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>). One hundred and forty axolotls (about 5 months old, approximately 80 mm) were individually kept in appropriate square boxes containing a dechlorinated water without aeration. Following a soak with T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> for 60 h, the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> solution was displaced by a dechlorinated water, employing an original water-renewing system. Exposures of T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-administrated axolotls to ELF fields (5.0 mT at 10 Hz) were performed using an air-cored coil system. The water temperature was strictly controlled at 24°C. The morphological changes and the survival rates of the axolotls affected by the prestimulation of the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> were monitored every day. In consequence, we discovered that the initiation timings of ELF field exposure did influence the speed of the morphological changes, as well as the survival rates of the following salamanded axolotls. As a point worthy of special mention, there was a close connection between the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-corresponding survival rates and serious indigestion/anorexia in the salamanded bodies. Our data could prove to be helpful for future reference with respect to a magnetic control study of tissue-regeneration.

articleTitle: Challenge of Media Noise Suppression with Oxygen Control in Granular Structure for CoPtCr-based Sputtered Tape towards 400 Gb/in2
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A sputtered tape that uses a CoPtCr-based granular recording layer was developed for practical application in the next-generation of large capacity magnetic tapes. The role of oxides in CoPtCr-oxide composite targets in forming nanostructure consisting of magnetic grains and grain boundary oxides for the recording layer was investigated under the distinctive conditions of the roll-to-roll sputtering system. It was confirmed that 1) increasing the amount of Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> in the CoPtCr-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> composite target improved the magnetic anisotropy of the recording layer and the magnetic isolation between magnetic grains, 2) the addition of 1.2% Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> content to the target improved the broadband signal-to-noise ratio (BB-SNR) for the tape by 3.0 dB compared with that sputtered by a target without Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> at a linear density of 353 kfci, which was brought by a suppression of noise, and 3) a further added cap layer to this sample brought the higher BB-SNR of 2.3 dB than that for the sample fabricated with the CoPtCr-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> composite target reported by us in TMRC2017. This SNR improvement was estimated to have the potential to achieve an areal density of 375 Gb/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in the case of the application to the latest track-following technology.

articleTitle: Characterization and multiscale modeling of the magneto-elastic behavior of Galfenol
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The properties of giant magnetostrictive materials (GMM) in actuation, sensing or energy harvesting applications are very sensitive to pre-stress levels. This work presents the experimental characterization of the magneto-mechanical behavior of Galfenol under static compressive and tensile stress. A multiscale modeling tool is then used to model the magnetic and magnetostrictive responses. The results demonstrates the high sensitivity to stress of the magneto-mechanical behaviour of Galfenol and the ability of the proposed multiscale approach to capture these effects.

articleTitle: Antiferromagnetic Droplet Soliton in a Nano-Contact Spin-Transfer Torque Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We demonstrate that a spin current flowing through a nano-contact into a uniaxial antiferromagnet with first- and second-order anisotropy can excite a self-localized dynamic magnetic soliton, known as a spin-wave droplet in ferromagnets. In this case, the frequency of the Néel vector precession lies below the antiferromagnetic resonance and decreases with the applied current. Above a certain threshold, the soliton mode disappears, and the oscillator instead emits spin waves propagating in the antiferromagnetic layer.

articleTitle: Effect of C replacement on magnetic properties and nanostructure of FePt-nitride granular film for HAMR media
