publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The effect of adding carbon (C) grain boundary material (GBM) on magnetic properties and nanostructure of FePt-nitride granular films with various nitrides is reported. Saturation magnetization of FePt-nitride-C granular films shows similar tendency with that of FePt-nitride granular films which varies almost linearly against volume averaged melting point (${T_{\text{m}}}^{{\text{ave}}}$) of the GBM. The value of perpendicular anisotropy for all FePt-nitride granular films is enhanced when nitride is partly replaced with C. By replacing nitride with C, the grain to grain separation is promoted significantly. When ${T_{\text{m}}}^{{\text{ave}}}$ of the GBM increases from around 2500 to 3500°C, in general, the average cluster size and cluster boundary decreases from around 13 to 9 nm and from 12 to 5 nm, respectively. Considering of ${T_{\text{m}}}^{{\text{ave}}}$ of the GBM, these results suggest that the GBM with high ${T_{\text{m}}}^{{\text{ave}}}$ will solidify prior to FePt which acts as the nucleation site to reduce the CD, which is similar to CoPt-based alloy granular films. In conclusion, the combination of nitride with C is more effective than single nitride to promote the grain isolation, while keeping higher degree of phase separation than C GBM.

articleTitle: Conductor Design Method considering AC Resistance for High Efficiency of PMSM using High Fill Factor Winding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes the design method of conductor considering AC resistance for high efficiency of PMSM using high fill factor winding. To achieve high power density of the motor, high fill factor winding such as hairpin winding is used. MSO coils were also developed for the same purpose. However, AC resistance is generated in the high fill factor winding used in the motor, which adversely affects the efficiency of the motor. For high efficiency of the motor using high fill factor windings, the AC resistance must be reduced. Therefore, in order to reduce the AC resistance, a design method in which the size of the respective conductor layers are different is proposed. In this paper, the method of reducing AC resistance is verified through analytical methods and FEA. Next, the validity of the proposed method is verified through performance evaluation of the prototype motor designed through the proposed method.

articleTitle: Atomistic simulations of ultrafast, optically induced switching dynamics in antiferromagnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: One of the most promising routes to both ultrafast and energy-efficient spintronics applications is the use of antiferromagnets. They have intrinsically faster eigenfrequencies than ferromagnets, but also incoherent, thermally driven dynamics, like de- and remagnetisation, are faster in antiferromagnets. Here, we present ab initio parameterised atomistic spin dynamics simulations that lay out a way to realise all-optical magnetisation switching procedures in antiferromagnets. We propose a coherent switching process that works without quenching of the magnetic order and hence requires less laser power, and consequently less heating, than all-optical switching processes in ferro- and ferrimagnets. The realisation of such a switching mechanism holds great potential for the development of fast and efficient magnetic memory devices.

articleTitle: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Voltage Distribution in MFTs with Foil Windings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, a voltage distribution model for MFTs with foil windings is presented. The model aims to compute the effects of harmonics in high dv/dt pulses from semiconductor switches, and consists of an equivalent circuit and FEM to quantify the impedance matrix. In order to verify the accuracy of the model, a test benchmark is manufactured and a comparison of experimental and calculation results are performed. The results of this comparison shows good agreement between the model and the test benchmark, indicating that the model is practical to compute the effects of high dv/dt pulses on MFTs.

articleTitle: Effect of Ar-N2 sputtering gas on structure and TMD effect in Co–(Si–N) nanogranular films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have investigated the effect of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> ratio in Ar-N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sputtering gas on tunneling magneto-dielectric (TMD) effect in Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf>–(Si–N)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">81</inf> nanogranular films. Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf>–(Si–N)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">81</inf> films were deposited by co-sputtering Co and Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> targets in Ar-x vol.%N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mixture gas with different x of 0 to 30. All deposited films have nanogranular structure composed of Co nanogranules with a diameter of 2 ~ 3 nm embedded in Si –N matrix, and we realized TMD effect in the film for x ≥ 3.3. The film deposited in Ar-6.6 vol.%N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas showed the highest TMD response. Moreover, we found the two types of change in both nanostructure and the frequency dependence of TMD effect. This study provides the new way to tailor the frequency response of TMD effect.

articleTitle: An MRI-Compatible Implantable Magnet Design with Self-Realigning Orientation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Patients with "MR Unsafe" rating magnetic implants are required to undergo implant removal surgery before they can take an MRI scan. Implants labeled as "MR Conditional" can stay in the patient’s body for MRI scan under specific conditions. In this article, the authors propose an MRI-compatible implantable magnet design with orientation that can be self-realigned or with an external homing magnet. This design can be readily adopted to most of the breast tissue expander implants on the market, upgrading them from "MR Unsafe" to "MR Conditional". Prototypes are tested to verify the design. Magnetic orientation realignment effectiveness is evaluated.

articleTitle: Entropy change and the magnetocaloric effect in R2Cu2Cd
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, we use a model Hamiltonian with two magnetic sub-lattices to study the magnetocaloric effect in the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cd compounds. In the model, the interactions of the magnetic moments were analyzed within the framework of the mean field theory. The model was applied to the compounds Gd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cd, Er<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cd, and Tm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cd. Our theoretical calculations are in good agreement with the experimental data.

articleTitle: Spin-current Driven Magnetic Meta-atoms for Time-varying Permeability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We study spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR) of magnetic meta-atom consisting of Ta/Co/Pt trilayers for time-varying permeability (µ). An alternating current (AC) at GHz frequencies is injected to the meta-atom under a direct current (DC) magnetic field to launch ST-FMR in the Co layer. In addition, a DC current is injected to modify the resonance condition. As the DC current increases, the ST-FMR signal becomes narrow owing to spin-current injection. The narrowing leads to the spin-current induced µ variation. The present result represents a major step forward in the integration of spintronics with metamaterials, thus opening a door to time-varying spintronic metamaterials as light sorces for the 6th generation mobile communication.

articleTitle: Magnetic Switching Properties for Synthetic Antiferromagntic Layers with Perpendicular Easy Magnetic Anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetic properties and switching behavior have been investigated for synthetic antiferromagnetic (SyAF) layers with perpendicular to the film plane easy magnetic anisotropy. We investigated the magnetic properties of SyAF layers using LLG micro-magnetic simulation, and found that square shape hysteresis in low magnetic field was observed for samples with anisotropic field of 1 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> and 1 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> erg/cc and coupling strength of 0.15 μerg/cm. We also investigated the magnetic switching properties for SyAF (CoFeB 1.2 nm/Ru 0.3 nm/CoFeB 0.6nm) films by using anomaly Hall effect, and found the switching current density of the sample was smaller than that of CoFeB 1.2 nm single ferromagnetic film by spin orbit torque with a W under layer.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and XAFS Analysis of PEG-coated Gd-doped ZnO Magnetic Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In recent years, spintronics has attracted much attention due to the charge and spin properties of electrons. Zinc oxide (ZnO) is known as a wide bandgap semiconductor with high exciton binding energy. In our study, we have prepared diluted magnetic semiconductors by doping into ZnO nanoparticles with 3d transition metals. In this study, we aimed to prepare diluted magnetic semiconductors with higher magnetic properties by doping ZnO nanoparticles with Gd, which has seven unpaired electrons among 4f rare earth metals. The local structures of the samples were analyzed by X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) measurements, and the changes in saturation magnetization and atomic coordination depending on the doping amount of Gd were discussed.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Study of Highly Spin-Polarized Heusler Alloys at Finite Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Strong reduction of magnetoresistance (MR) ratio in Heusler alloys based MR devices at finite temperature raises the need for the development of new highly spin-polarized Heusler alloys. However, recent high throughput expoloration and machine learning studies combined with first principles calculations to find prospective Heusler alloys are only performed with 0 K assumption, which lead to the significant discrepancy of material prediction with experiments. In this work, we carried out the finite temperature first-principles calculation combined with machine learning to find new highly spin-polalized Heusler alloys. We employed Bayesian optimization for the machine learning algorithm and the disordered local moment method for the finite temperature first-principles calculations, respectively. We successfully found several new prospective Heusler alloys with high spin polarization at finite temperature such as Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>As<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf> and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>FeAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>. Additionally, the effect of composition modulation on the temperature dependence of Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>As<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-y</inf> and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>FeAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-y</inf> was also studied.

articleTitle: Distant Excitation of Spin-Waves—How Electromagnetic Cross-Talk Impacts on Hybrid Magnonic Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This work uncovers the impact of electromagnetic cross-talk in hybrid magnonic devices using inductive spin-wave (SW) transducers. We present detailed electrical spin-wave spectroscopy measurements showing the important signal contributions to be considered in magnonic device design. Both the cross-talk and the distant SW excitation are modelled using the Hertzian dipole for a straightforward estimation of parasitic electromagnetic field components. Additionally, we visualize the distant SW excitation via time-resolved MOKE imaging in the forward-volume configuration in a 100nm Yttrium-Iron-Garnet (YIG) system. Our effective cross-talk estimation and in-depth understanding of distant SW excitation allows for a robust design of hybrid magnonic devices.

articleTitle: High Gradient Magnetic Separator Design with Hybrid Poles and Increased Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this article, we analyze the efficiency of high gradient magnetic separator (HGMS) designs in terms of efficient use of magnetic energy. Combining analytical analysis and Boundary Element Analysis software, we evaluate the characteristics of quadrupole design, specifically, the magnetic field limits, the energy and gradient distribution, and the design efficiency. To increase the design efficiency, we present a high gradient magnetic separator (HGMS) design with partial soft magnetic steel pole pieces. The use of nearly saturated soft magnetic pole pieces increases the magnetic field in the region of interest. And the use of pole pieces also increases the efficiency of the design. Magnetic separators with and without pole piece are built to evaluate the effectiveness of the pole piece.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Effect of the Oxidation Depth of Co/CoO Films on the Relative Constant of Interfacial Interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In the approximation of the "mean spin" theory, the influence of the thickness of the antiferromagnetic layer on the temperature dependence of the relative constant of the exchange interaction Ain/A in Co/CoO films grown on a palladium substrate was simulated. It is shown that in each CoO layer, the magnetic moments of cobalt ions are ordered antiferromagnetically. It is found that in the low temperature region (kT < J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Co</inf>/2), the magnitude and sign of the magnetic moment of the boundary antiferromagnetic layer, as well as the relative constant of the interfacial interaction Ain/A, change many times. The maximum values of the constant Ain/A decrease linearly with increasing temperature with increasing oxidation depth.

articleTitle: Analysis and Modeling of a Flux-Switching Transverse-Flux Permanent Magnet Tube Linear Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The flux-switching transverse-flux permanent magnet tube linear motor (FSTFPMTLM) has a variety of outstanding advantages, such as high thrust density and small detent force. However, the different thrust of the motor is coupled together, and it is time-consuming to take the three-dimensional (3-D) finite-element method (FEM) to analyze the thrust. To solve these above problems, this paper proposes a solution method for decoupling the electromagnetic thrust, in which the thrust of the motor can be divided into winding reluctance force, cogging force, and electromagnetic thrust. Firstly, the relationship between the different thrusts and the corresponding equivalent permeances of each magnetic source is obtained. Secondly, equivalent two-dimensional (2-D) finite-element FEM is proposed to quickly solve various equivalent permeances. Then, the expression of electromagnetic thrust can be determined, and the electromagnetic thrust characteristics are obtained and analyzed. Finally, the 3-D FEM analysis and experimental results verify the validity and correctness of the design method of the machine.

articleTitle: Magnetic nanopillars in self-organized magneto-dielectric nanocomposite thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents the magnetic properties of perpendicularly aligned magnetic nanopillars in magneto-dielectric nanocomposite films fabricated by tandem sputtering methods with an optimized substrate rotation speed. Since the film consists of self-assembled Co nano-pillars about 2.3 nm in diameter separated by Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>O matrix of 2.2 nm-spacing, Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">43</inf>-Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">41</inf> film exhibits perpendicular magnetic anisotropy attributed to the shape anisotropy of pillar shape of Co. These self-assembled nanopillar fabrication process may potentially assist the selective formation of perpendicular magnetic random-access memory architecture.

articleTitle: Investigation of Maximum Torque of Interior Permanent Magnet Type Magnetic-Geared Generator Based on Magnetic Interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic-geared generators (MGGs) are expected to be applied to wind-power generation because of high torque density and efficiency. Among them, an interior permanent magnet (IPM)-type MGG shows different characteristics compared to a surface permanent magnet (SPM)-type MGG. The reason is that since its high-speed rotor (HSR) does not have the iron yoke, the magnetic flux from the stator coil gets through and modulated by pole-pieces (PPs). Eventually, the modulated flux reaches the low-speed rotor (LSR). Since the stall torque of the magnetic gear is determined by the modulated flux, the stall torque of the IPM-type MMG would be influenced by the magnetic flux generated by the stator coil. This phenomenon is called magnetic interaction. This paper investigated the change of the maximum torque of the IPM-type MMG based on the of magnetic interaction by using both a three-dimensional finite element method (3D-FEM) and experiment.

articleTitle: Spin-Orbit Torque-Induced Field-Free Switching of a Perpendicular Antiferromagnet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The field-free spin-orbit torque induced 180° reorientation of perpendicular magnetization is a key step to the development of ultrafast magnetic memory based on the antiferromagnetic material (AFM). In this paper, we propose a trilayer AFM/Insulator/Heavy Metal structure as the AFM memory device and achieve field-free switching by using two orthogonal currents. These two currents provide uniform damping-like torque and stagger field-like torque, respectively. A current density of 1.79×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup>A/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is sufficient to induce the switching within 40 picoseconds. The device and switching mechanism proposed in this work offer a promising approach to deterministically switch the AFM with perpendicular Néel vector.

articleTitle: Identification of Nonlinear Reader Distortion in Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The ‘extracted dipulse’ technique is widely used in magnetic recording to characterize both the linear and the various nonlinear components in the readback signal. However, it is not always straightforward to identify the exact source and nature of the distortions since they may arise during either the writing process or the readback process. This paper analyses the distortion caused by the read sensor. Reader asymmetry and saturation are described by quadratic and cubic components, respectively. We compute the exact positions and shapes of the resulting ‘echo’ responses that appear in the extracted dipulse. It is important that the positions be identified exactly as this can help distinguish reader distortion from distortion during writing. The shapes of the echo responses are also important. The widths of echoes caused by reader distortion are significantly narrower than those that arise from the writing process and they become progressively narrower as the order of the reader distortion increases. Also, by reconstructing waveforms from the linear and nonlinear terms in the extracted dipulse, the sensor distortion can be directly visualized graphically.

articleTitle: Microstructural and magnetic properties of low-energy ball milled LTP-MnBi powders via melt-spinning and gas-atomization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: LTP-MnBi alloy presents many possibilities as a ‘gap-magnet’ material due to its excellent magnetic properties compared to M-type ferrite. However, the LTP-MnBi alloy has a critical problem of the phase decomposition in a milling process for improving magnetic properties. In this study, the MnBi alloy was manufactured by both the melt-spinning process and the gas-atomization process to overcome the above problem. As a result, it was confirmed that single-phase LTP-MnBi powders were obtained through heat treatment even in gas-atomization with a relatively low cooling rate. In addition, these MnBi powders had a spherical shape of about 20 μm or less even before milling. Thus, it was possible to minimize the decomposition of the LTP-MnBi phase. These powders showed an excellent maximum energy product (11.3 MGOe).

articleTitle: An Electromotive Force in Pt/VO2/Ni80Fe2o Tri-Layer Junctions Under the Ferromagnetic Resonance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: An electromotive force (EMF) in Pt/VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2o</inf>(Py) tri-layer junctions under the ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) of the Py layer was generated. The inverse spin Hall effect (ISHE) of the Pt layer, in the ISHE of the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer, the self-induced ISHE of the Py layer and so on, were considered as the possible origins of the EMFs under the FMR of the Py film. The temperature dependence of the EMF generated in the tri-layer junctions under the FMR of the Py layer were evaluated across the metal-insulator transition temperature of the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films. The results suggest the spin transport from the Py film to the Pt layer via VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin film has been achieved.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of skyrmionic magnetic tunnel junction and its on-chip learning application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Chiral magnetic skyrmions are topological swirling spin textures that hold promise for future information technology. The electrical nucleation and motion of skyrmions have been experimentally demonstrated in the last decade, while electrical detection compatible with semiconductor processes is still considered one of the most crucial gaps regarding the use of skyrmions in real applications. In this study, we report the direct observation of nanoscale skyrmions in CoFeB/MgO-based magnetic tunnel junction devices at room temperature by using high- resolution magnetic force microscopy (MFM) imaging and tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) measurements. This skyrmionic magnetic tunnel junction (SK-MTJ) shows a stable nonlinear multilevel resistance thanks to its topological nature and tunable density of skyrmions under current pulse excitation, which can represent the variations in the synaptic weights in the neuromorphic computing. Our chip-level simulation shows that such Sk-MTJ synapse array could be utilized to implement on-chip learning to solve image recognition task such as with CIFAR-10.

articleTitle: Extended Virtual-Signal-Injection MTPA Control of New Five-Phase Flux-Intensifying Interior Permanent Magnet Motor with Compensation Factor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: For the maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control system of the five-phase interior permanent magnet (IPM) motor, its MTPA control accuracy is greatly affected because of the cross-coupling and saturation effect of the motor, which cannot meet multiple operating requirements for electric vehicle applications. Motivated by this, an extended virtual-signal-injection MTPA (VSI-MTPA) control strategy is proposed in this paper. A new five-phase flux-intensifying interior permanent magnet (FI-IPM) motor with obvious inverse saliency effect is adopted to suppress the influence of cross-coupling and saturation effect on the tracking accuracy of MTPA point. In addition, for the inverse saliency of the five-phase FI-IPM motor, a VSI-MTPA control strategy with the compensation factor is proposed from the perspective of control algorithms to further improve the dynamic and steady-state performance of the motor drive system. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified by analysis results.

articleTitle: Giant magnetocaloric effects of 2nd order phase transition utilized for liquefaction of hydrogen near 20 K
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This work focuses on the magnetocaloric effect (MCE) in the temperature range of 77 ~20 K, which is required for magnetocaloric liquefaction of hydrogen pre-cooled by liquid nitrogen. Heavy rare-earth intermetallics compounds exhibit two distinguished features in this temperature range, both maximum magnetic and adiabatic temperature changes (ΔS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and ΔT<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ad</inf>) increase with decreasing Curie temperatures (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>) and a giant maximum ΔS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and ΔT<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ad</inf> in the vicinity of 20 K is observed. With heavy rare-earth Laves phases RAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and RNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as examples, a mean-field approach is developed, confirming the $T_C^{ - 2/3}$ linear relation and rationalizing these features. In a next step, inspired by the sharply increasing trend of MCE near 20 K, we tuned T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> of the light rare-earth Laves phases RAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to the hydrogen condensation point. Successfully, a light rare-earth intermetallic series covering the full temperature range required by magnetocaloric hydrogen liquefaction is achieved.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Properties of Mn–Pt and Mn–Pt–B Melt-Spun Ribbons
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To design new potential magnetic materials, Mn–Pt and Mn–Pt–B melt-spun ribbons were prepared, and then their structures and magnetic properties were surveyed. Samples that were prepared at a peripheral speed of 52 m/s were all MnPt single-phase nanocrystals with or without boron. With 10 mol% and 20 mol% additions of boron, crystal structure lattice constants a and c increased and decreased, respectively. These materials are expected to exhibit a variety of magnetic properties. The samples showed paramagnetism on application of a magnetic field up to 5 kOe at room temperature.

articleTitle: Fitting of X-Band CW FMR in Exchange-Biased [Co/Pt] Multilayers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The use of additional fitting terms, accounting for the conductive losses and instrumental time response in the X-Band CW FMR spectrum of an exchange-biased multilayers of [Co/Pt]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> is motivated and implemented. Regression shows the conductive losses are most aptly described by Voigt function heavily weighted towards a Gaussian, and the second derivative of a Lorentzian accurately describes the acquisition equipments low pass filter response time. The resonance field of the sample was determined to be 0.312(2)T, and the broadening term was found to be 0.0781(3)T. It is hoped this work can be extended to fit angle and field magnitude dependent absorption data sets, to reveal highly detailed information about the exchange-bias distribution in perpendicular media.

articleTitle: Effects of the Rotor Mechanical Offset Angle on the Electromagnetic Performance of Dual Stator Wound-Field Flux Switching Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This study is concerned with the effect of the rotor mechanical offset (MO) angle on the electromagnetic performance of dual stator wound-field flux switching machines (DSWFFSMs). The focus is to find the optimum initial rotor position so that control of the machine can be facilitated. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and based on a cocktail of simulations, key electromagnetic performance indices such as average torque, torque ripple, power factor and efficiency are studied under dynamic on-load state, with the optimum MO angle established at 8°. The experimental test prototype has been developed and the test results are promised future extended paper version.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Performance Analysis of a Bearingless Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor by Model Order Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents an electromagnetic performance analysis method for fast dynamic simulation of a bearingless permanent magnet motor (BPMSM) based on model order reduction (MOR). The electromagnetic characteristics and dynamic behavior model of the rotating machine are constructed by using the MOR based on proper orthogonal decomposition. First, the q-axis and d-axis currents and rotor angle of the motor are scanned to construct the magnetic field distribution snapshot matrix. Then singular value decomposition of the snapshot matrix is used to calculate the basis vectors. Finally, the order of the system is reduced by selecting an appropriate truncation order of the basis vectors. Compared with the finite element method (FEM), the calculation time of MOR for the BPMSM is significantly reduced. At the same time, it can provide accurate results of magnetic field distribution, electromagnetic force, levitation force and dynamic response. Through analysis and comparison, the results of the proposed method match well with the FEM simulations.

articleTitle: From thermographical data to 2D temperature maps: how to evaluate performance for magnetic hyperthermia experiments in phantoms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We unveil a novel method to generate 2D temperature maps for magnetic nanoparticle samples in magnetic hyperthermia experiments from infrared thermography measurements. It allows obtaining thermodynamic parameters such as energy, power and heat flux with spatiotemporal detail, in contrast with the conventional local probing. We tested it by analyzing polyacrylamide gel phantoms that have a viscosity near cytosol’s, with both dispersed and oriented nanoparticles. We tracked the temporal evolution of the temperature gradient of the phantom during ac field application and identified spatial inhomogeneities through the temperature maps, which highlights that a 2D analysis could benefit the interpretation of results obtained in biological and medical uses.

articleTitle: Influence of Phase Shift Angle on Performance of PMSM with Dual Three-Phase Star and Delta Connection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of phase shift angle on the performance of permanent magnet synchronous motor with dual three-phase star and delta connection (DSDC-PMSM). Firstly, the harmonic elimination principle of magnetomotive force (MMF) of machine stator under different phase shift angles is deduced. Secondly, the winding connection methods with different slot/pole combinations and different phase shift angles are analyzed. Then, the performances of 24-slot 10-pole, 48-slot 22-pole, and 72-slot 46-pole machines with different phase shift angles are analyzed by finite element method, including harmonic of MMF of stator, output torque, vibration noise and so on. It is found that two sets of three-phase windings with a phase shift angle of 15 degrees can maximize the performance of the machine. Finally, a 24-slot 10-pole DSDC-PMSM prototype with a phase shift angle of 15 degrees is manufactured, and the theoretical analysis is verified.

Author Keywords: Dual three-phase star and delta winding connection (DSDC)

articleTitle: Evaluation of magnetization response of magnetic nanoparticles internalized into cultured adherent cells
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To develop the biomedical application using magnetic nanoparticles, the magnetization properties associated with the magnetic relaxation with respect to magnetic nanoparticles internalized into cells were important. In this study, magnetization properties of magnetic nanoparticles internalized into the cultured adherent cells were measured by evaluating harmonic intensities derived from the magnetization response, which were compared to the magnetization of magnetic nanoparticles dispersed in liquid and fixed with epoxy resin. In particular, the nano-volt harmonic signals were obtained in intracellular magnetic nanoparticles. It is indicated that the particle aggregation reduced the magnetization, and the particle physical rotation was inhibited in the intracellular environment.

articleTitle: Holding Performance of an Adaptive Magnetorheological Fluid-Based Robotic Claw
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This study addresses the holding performance of adaptive magnetorheological fluid (MRF)-based robotic claws that can grasp a wider range of objects satisfying various grasping task requirements. To this end, a two-finger type of MRF-based robotic claw was proposed in this study. Two magnetorheological (MR) grippers with MR elastomer (MRE) bladders were configured at the end of each finger. An object was placed between these two MR grippers and was grasped by manually adjusting the distance between these two fingers. This distance adjustment of two fingers results in a change in the normal force applied to the object. The holding forces of the MRF-based robotic claw with respect to applied normal forces and applied magnetic field strengths were experimentally measured by using an Instron material testing machine. From the measured holding forces, the dynamic and static holding forces and holding coefficients were determined for the evaluation of the holding performances. The feasibility of the MRF-based robotic claw was experimentally confirmed.

articleTitle: Design of Microscale Magnetic Controls for Magnetic-Field Driven Actuation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic actuators require reproducible, small-scale approaches for controlling the magnetic field gradient and direction used to drive the actuation. Here a system of two control magnets is designed to generate the local magnetic fields that are required to actuate a magnetic system and elicit microscale, local deflections. The two control magnets are engineered to have magnetizations preferentially pointing along two orthogonal axes, leading to the coupling of the magnetic flux densities between them and the generation of a field (and gradient) localized with micrometer resolution. To demonstrate the ability of this field to exert an actuation force on a magnetic material, a system composed of the two control magnets and a microscale magnetic beam/cantilever is designed and simulated.

articleTitle: Study on Injection Molding IPMSM Using Sm-Fe-N Bonded Magnet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) that applies bonded magnets made of Sm-Fe-N magnetic powder, which can be directly injection molded into the rotor. First, Sm-Fe-N magnetic powders with high residual flux density and high heat resistance were prepared by developing a magnetic powder manufacturing process that enables uniform phosphoric acid coating on the surface of magnetic powders. the motor performance was evaluated by two-dimensional finite element analysis when the developed magnetic powder was adopted for injection molding into the motor rotor. It was shown that the proposed Sm-Fe-N bonded magnet IPMSM has can achieve performance equivalent to an IPMSM with N-Fe-B sintered magnets using the same stator.

articleTitle: Influence of air gaps between grain-oriented steel sheets on losses in the magnetic system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents results of investigations of the influence of air gaps in GO steel sheet inserts on magnetic losses. Classical iron loss measurements were performed using a single strip tester to magnetize material samples at 50 Hz. The samples included air gaps of various thickness and it is found that their presence led to the increase the losses up to 30%. It is concluded that if GO steel inserts are to be used in a magnetic system of an electrical machine, the sheets must be properly connected to reduce the effect of air gaps and thus to increase the overall performances of the machine.

articleTitle: Spin-wave dynamics in the multi-layered ferromagnetic crescent-shaped nanorod
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Since magnonic devices use spin waves they can operate at high frequencies with low-energy consumption, so they have the potential to be more efficient than CMOS devices. Thus, the study of the influence of the magnetic field on ferromagnetic nanostructures with different geometries is crucial for the development of modern technologies, in planar and particularly in the area of 3D-magnonic circuits, where geometric constraints create an intricate relationship between the fields of demagnetization, exchange, and bias fields. Our numerical research on single and bi-layered crescent-shaped nanorods (CSNs) in dependence on the magnetic field has revealed several exciting conclusions. In particular, we show that CSNs offer a rich spectrum of spin waves with frequencies, intensities of modes, and hybridizations between them strongly dependent on field magnitude and orientation. This makes them of great importance for future research and applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magnetization Reversal Process of Non-Oriented Electromagnetic Steel Sheet by Extended Landau Free Energy Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We analyzed the magnetization reversal process of non-oriented electromagnetic steel sheets using the extended Landau free energy model (eX-GL). The model is a new analysis approach that can connect the macroscopic function and the microscopic structure beyond the hierarchy by using data science technique. It can treat grain boundaries and defects, which frequently occur in actual magnetic materials, furthermore it can visualize the inhibiting factors of magnetization reversal back to the original image. As a result, we could draw the experimental energy landscape of an electromagnetic steel sheet for the first time, and the magnetic domain walls that contribute to magnetization reversal was selectively visualized.

articleTitle: Shape Observation by Local illumination Using Reflected Light from Magnetically Controlled Guanine Crystal Platelet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Biogenic guanine crystal platelets act as micromirror with the high reflectivity because their refractive index is ~1.83. The diamagnetic anisotory enables the guanine crystals suspended in water to control the reflected light by a magnetic field of several hundred millitesla. In this paper, we demonstrate the shape observation by reflecting the light which enters from the side of the sample on the broadest surface of guanine crystal just below the sample. Reflected light illuminates the sample locally from an oblique direction by adjusting the permanent magnet position. In this case, higher contrast image like a dark-field illumination is observed compared to bright-field illumination. For reducing the magnetic field amplitude required for guanine crystal orientation to improve the controllability, various magnetic nanoparticles are examined to bind the guanine crystal platelets. As a result, the orientation of the crystal direction by low magnetic field and the high reflection property of light are obtained for Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanoparticles with average particle size of 15 nm. The guanine crystal platelet can be oriented by a three axis Helmholtz coil. A high-contrast image comparable to that for guanine crystal without nanoparticles case is successfully obtained.

articleTitle: Electride and Magnetic Properties of Ternary Intermetallic Compounds LaTMSi
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We present a theoretical study of the electronic, spectral, and magnetic properties of ternary intermetallic LaTMSi (where TM = Mn, Sc) compounds within the DFT+DMFT method combining density functional theory with dynamical mean-field theory. It is demonstrated that compounds of the LaTMSi series are interesting for magnetic orderings and electride properties prospective for catalytic applications. The DFT+DMFT calculations for manganese compounds at 1000 K indicate a high-spin to low-spin crossover in Mn-3d ions with pressure. We find that scandium ternary compound LaScSi exhibits high interstitial density characteristics of electrides. Our calculations show that both lanthanum and scandium 5d orbitals contribute electrons to the strongly localized interstitial electron density, which can be considered an electride anion with pronounced s-symmetry.

articleTitle: Realization of large magneto-optical effect by diagonal permittivity change in epsilon-near-zero materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The Epsilon near-zero (ENZ) effect has been suggested as a method to enhance the magneto-optical (MO) effect; however, the enhancement of the MO effect in the ENZ materials has not been experimentally verified. Here, we measured the MO properties of ENZ materials and analyzed the correlation between the diagonal permittivity and MO effect. The Faraday effect is enhanced in the wavelengths where the real part of diagonal permittivity is almost zero and the Kerr effect is enhanced in the wavelengths where the diagonal permittivity is almost one. Our findings would lead to various potential applications, including on-chip isolators and one-way topological waveguides.

articleTitle: Single Domain Spin Orbit Torque Enabled Magnetic Field Sensor with Offset Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Reducing the zero-field offset is crucial for absolute field measurements. In this work we present a device that can be used to measure magnetic fields smaller than 1 mT and compensate the respective offsets. The device employs a modulated spin-orbit-torque (SOT) to reduce the offset. The sensor is sensitive to in-plane fields parallel to the current direction Ixx. Depending on whether a positive or negative current is applied, the damping like spin-orbit torque results in a positive or negative Mz component of the single domain state, respectively. This out of plane Mz component depends on the Bx field and it is measured via the anomalous Hall effect. The signal is obtained by subtracting the measured Mz components of the two opposing current directions. It is shown that bias fields applied orthogonal to the sensitive direction does not increase the offset but changed the sensitivity of the sensor.

articleTitle: A novel comb-shaped magnetoresistive sensor with magnetic flux concentrators for improved sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We investigate the impact of the geometric overlap between a current-in-plane giant magnetoresistive (GMR) element and magnetic flux concentrators (MFCs) on the performance of GMR sensors using the finite element method. The simulations revealed that while an overlap between the MFCs and GMR element can increase their magnetostatic coupling, it can also decrease the magnetic sensitivity of the GMR sensor due to a magnetic shielding of GMR element by MFCs. To avoid the adverse effects of GMR and MFC overlapping, we propose a comb-shaped GMR element with alternating notches and fins. Our simulations indicate that the fins of the comb-shaped GMR element provide a strong magnetostatic coupling with the MFCs while confining the electric current within the main body of the comb-shaped GMR element, leading to improved sensitivity.

articleTitle: Effect of Applied Stress on Magnetostriction of Amorphous Magnetic Microwires
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetostriction coefficient and its stress dependence are evaluated in Co- and Fe-Ni- based glass-coated microwires with different character of hysteresis loops and positive and low negative magnetostriction respectively. We found that the stress dependence of the magnetostriciton coefficient, λs, is linear for both families of studied microwires, however a decrease with applied stress is observed for Co-rich microwires with negative magnetostriction coefficient. In contrast, a linear increase of the magnetostriction coefficient with applied stress is observed for Fe-Ni- rich microwires with positive magnetostriction coefficient. Observed results are discussed in terms of influence of internal stresses and short range ordering induced by annealing.

articleTitle: Emergent inductance in ferromagnetic nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Several embodiments of emergent inductance in ferromagnetic nanostructures are theoretically presented. The emergent inductance is a universal phenomenon when an order parameter such as magnetization in ferromagnets is coupled with conduction electron spin based on a sequential action of spin torque and spinmotive force effects under ac current application. An original version of the emergent inductor using a spiral magnet can be extended to include the spin-orbit coupling effects. Materials are not limited to metallic systems but also insulators. A striking common feature over the emergent inductors is their size dependence of the effect; the inductance is inversely proportional to the sample cross sectional area, opening a way for integration of an inductor element. We also discuss key performance factors: the operation frequency and quality factor that represents the energy efficiency of the inductive response.

articleTitle: Energy loss and constitutive equation of soft magnetic materials for broadband applications in power electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Soft magnetic materials find applications in power electronics as cores of passive components, such as transformers and inductors. In these components, it is necessary to balance efficiency, volume, and operating temperature. New design methodologies use advanced magnetic modelling of the magnetic cores and the optimization of their properties. Therefore, one key area of research is the development of new methods for predicting iron loss under non-sinusoidal and DC-biased conditions and high frequencies. This approach includes loss decomposition theory to model soft ferrites and amorphous/nanocrystalline ribbons.

articleTitle: Antiferromagnetic domains distribution carried by stoichiometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We present a spatially resolved X-ray magnetic linear dichroism study of high quality micron-sized mixed nickel-cobalt oxide (NCO) crystals. Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf>O were prepared in-situ by high-temperature oxygen-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on Ru(0001) single crystal. To check the effect of incorporating Ni in the cobalt oxide films, three different composition were prepared. The element specific XMLD measurements reveal strong antiferromagnetic contrast at room temperature and magnetic domains up to one micron wide, reflecting the high structural quality of the islands. By means of vectorial magnetometry, the spin axis orientation of the domains was determined with nanometer spatial resolution, and found to depend on the stoichiometry of prepared crystals.

articleTitle: Improvement of Transmission Torque Characteristics of Strain Wave Gear with Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Lower limb exoskeletons with actuators aids disabled individuals in walking. However, the exoskeleton weight is greater than that of conventional medical devices such as orthoses and walking frames. In this study, we propose a novel strain wave gear for light exoskeletons, which is lighter than conventional commercial strain wave gears. The proposed gear uses magnets, rather than a mechanical cam. The thin-walled elastic cylinder is deformed by the magnetic force in the gear, and the torque is transmitted by tooth engagements. In this paper, strain wave gears with 4 pole- and 16 pole- magnets are designed. Next, we constructed dynamic analysis method. In this analysis method, the magnetic force distribution on the elastic cylinder at each deformation and posture conditions is obtained through static magnetic analysis with finite element method, and dynamic behavior is calculated through multi flexible body dynamics with the finite element method, the direct solver, and the obtained magnetic force distribution database. From analyzed and measured results, we clarified that the gear with 16 pole-magnets can transmitted larger torque than that with 4 pole-magnets.

articleTitle: Comparison of Fractional and Integral Slot Winding Configurations on the Position Error for A Conventional Wound-Rotor Resolver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Resolvers are feedback elements used in the control of electric motors for many years. They are highly preferred in many parts of industry. One of the most important reasons for using resolvers is that they are more reliable than other electronic feedback elements especially in harsh environments requiring shock resistance or high vibration. At the same time, its ability to work at high temperatures makes them preferred in demanding and harsh applications. Both integral and fractional slot windings are used in resolvers. However, no detailed comparison is given for the two types of resolvers in various features including position errors. This study focuses on the design and comparison of a conventional wound-rotor resolver with both winding configurations focusing on position errors.

articleTitle: Comparison of Simulation Methods for Angular Dependency when Modeling Demagnetization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Rare earth element free magnets, such as ferrites, are weaker than their more common alternatives and therefore more subject to demagnetization. Additionally, in electrical machines they are commonly tangentially magnetized and placed in a spoke-type geometry to enhance the magnetic field. In this geometry, the magnets are subject to inclined fields, which is normally not accounted for when evaluating demagnetization risk. In this paper, different methods for demagnetization of permanent magnets are applied to two separate motors under two distinct loading conditions and the results are compared. It is concluded that it is more important to consider inclined fields when studying ferrite magnets than rare earth element magnets. The common most simple model of omitting inclined fields is shown to be the most conservative method for evaluating demagnetization. However, more precise results can be reached with methods taking inclined fields into account, especially if the models are adapted for the specific magnet type.

articleTitle: Quantified spin-wave symmetry in rectangular permalloy microstrips investigated using TR-STXM, FMR and Mumax3
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The asymmetry quantification of spin-wave dynamics in confined rectangular permalloy microstrips is suggested and applied to the TR-STXM results and micromagnetic simulations. The excitation was done at a frequency of 9.43GHz using a uniform microwave magnetic field while the external static magnetic field is varied. The results show a higher asymmetry for the double microstrips indicating an influence of an additional microstructure placed in a close proximity to the analyzed structure.

articleTitle: Comparison of Permanent Magnet Vernier Motors with Evenly and Unevenly Distributed Modulation teeth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Permanent magnet vernier motor (PMVM) possesses the advantage of high torque density. In split-tooth PMVMs, the modulation teeth can be evenly or unevenly distributed on each stator tooth, which leads to the corresponding evenly and unevenly distributed slot vector diagrams. So, by selecting closer slot vectors into one phase, the winding factor can be improved, and the torque of PMVMs can be increased further by using the unevenly distributed modulation tooth structure. In this paper, two split-tooth PMVMs with evenly and unevenly distributed modulation teeth are compared. The simulation and the test results verify the correctness.

articleTitle: Spin-Dependent Photocarrier Generation Dynamics in Electrically Detected Nitrogen-Vacancy-Based Quantum Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Electrical detection of a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond is advantageous for developing and integrating quantum information processing devices and quantum sensors. However, the mechanism for the electrical detection of NV spins is not fully understood. In this study, we observe positive contrast in photoelectrically detected magnetic resonance (PDMR) despite the usually observed negative PDMR contrast. To discuss the sign of the PDMR contrast, we numerically analyze the dynamics of photocarrier generation by NV centers using a seven-level rate model. It is found that the sign of the PDMR contrast depends on the difference in the photocurrent generated from the excited states and the metastable state of NV centers. Furthermore, we demonstrate alternating-current (AC) magnetic field sensing using spin coherence with the PDMR technique using a phase-cycling-based noise-canceling technique to suppress the noise from a fluctuating magnetic environment. We obtained the sensitivity of AC magnetic-field of ${\sim}29{\text{nT}}/\sqrt {{\mathbf{Hz}}} $ with the PDMR technique.

articleTitle: A Study on Accelerating SP decoding by Neural Network in SMR System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have previously studied low-density parity-check (LDPC) coding and iterative decoding in shingled magnetic recording (SMR) system as a signal processing method to realize ultra-high-density hard disk drive (HDD). In addition, we have proposed the application of the neural network to improve decoding performance and realize the automation of iterative decoding. In this study, we apply a neural network to accelerate iterative decoding in the sum-product (SP) decoder. As the result, the SP decoder with the neural network realized "no errors" at the fewest times of the iterative decoding compared to our previous studies.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Method for Estimating the Position of Ferromagnetic Markers under Magnetization Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In the treatment of early-stage breast cancer, breast-conserving surgery is performed to remove only the tumor while preserving the original breast shape as much as possible. In a previous study by our research group, a hand-held magnetic probe [1] was developed to achieve high sensitivity by simultaneously measuring the magnetic field and enhancing magnetization with a permanent magnet in order to accurately determine the tumor location during surgery. However, the hysteresis curve of the magnetization of the magnetic marker to be enhanced changes from moment to moment in a complex manner according to the way the probe is moved and its history, making it difficult to estimate the position using the forward problem method. In this study, we propose a position estimation method that combines an inverse problem solution and a magnetization model, and show that the estimable distance can be extended within an error range of 1 mm in the presence of magnetization enhancement by a permanent magnet.

articleTitle: An Evolutionary Computation Approach for the Electromagnetic Field Assessment of Eddy Current Motion Dampers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Electromagnetic suspension and damper systems have recently emerged as valid alternatives to the traditionally utilized hydraulic systems. In the past, different analysis approaches were introduced for the performance assessment of active eddy current dampers and shock absorbers. This paper is to present an evolutionary approach for the solution of electromagnetic field problems related to permanent magnet eddy current dampers. Details of the proposed approach are given in the paper.

articleTitle: Anomalous Zeeman shift of defect-bound states in epitaxial FeSn films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We synthesize high-quality FeSn thin films on SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(111) substrates by molecular beam epitaxy. Using in situ low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy, we observe honeycomb lattice on the Sn-terminated films and close-packed lattice for the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn termination. In addition, we also directly visualize single Sn vacancy in the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn layer and di-vacancy in the Sn layer, as well as their response to applied magnetic fields. The bound states induced by these defects exhibit anomalous Zeeman shifts in out-of-plane magnetic fields, where the energy of the bound states shifts linearly towards higher energy independent of the direction of the magnetic field. A two-fold oscillatory response to in-plane magnetic fields is also observed. These findings provide critical insights into under-standing magnetism in Kagome magnetic materials.

articleTitle: Spin voltage gradient is the driving force for ultrafast demagnetization and Terahertz spin transport
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Laser-induced terahertz spin transport (TST) and ultrafast demagnetization (UDM) are central phenomena in femtomagnetism and terahertz spintronics, but so far disconnected. Here, we use broadband terahertz emission spectroscopy to reliably measure both processes in one setup. We find that the rate of UDM of a single ferromagnetic metal film F has the same time evolution as the flux of TST from F into an adjacent normal-metal layer N. This remarkable observation suggests that UDM in F sample and TST in F|N stack arise from the same force. An analytical model quantitatively explains our measurements and reveals that the driving force is a generalized spin voltage, i.e., an excess of magnetization which is defined for arbitrary, nonthermal electron distributions. Our observation indicates that contributions due to a possible temperature difference between F and N, i.e., the spin-dependent Seebeck effect, are minor. Based on these findings, one can apply the vast knowledge of UDM to TST to significantly increase spin-current amplitudes and, thus, open up new pathways toward energy-efficient ultrafast spintronic devices.

articleTitle: A sub-micrometric spintronic-based accelerometer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Accelerometers have widespread applications and are an essential component in many areas such as automotive, consumer electronics and industrial applications. Most commercial accelerometers are based on micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) that have limited scalability and power efficiency. Here we propose a novel spintronic-based accelerometer employing magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) as spintronic-diodes to develop compact and high-sensitivity accelerometers where the output voltage measured across the MTJs terminals is mapped directly into the external acceleration. The device exploits both mechanical and magnetic couplings and leverages the spin-diode effect for higher sensitivity at low-power input. The proposed technology represents a potentially competitive solution to current MEMS-based approaches.

articleTitle: Prediction of Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy Constant in FeCoNi Alloys Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Using Machine Learning, the possibility of predicting small K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> materials and exhaustive search, which is thought difficult with existing theoretical calculations, was verified for FeCoNi alloy systems. At the K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> ≠ 0 point for FeCoNi alloys of about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3~5</sup> (erg/cc), the results show that K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> can be predicted with an error of 0.5 order of magnitude for virtually unknown compositions and temperatures, indicating the possibility of predicting small K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> materials using machine learning. The results also show that it is possible to successfully predict how the K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> = 0 line changes by structure-ordering (annealing samples), and exhaustively search for points where the sign of K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> changes.

articleTitle: Large Tunnel Magnetocapacitance Effect in FeCo/MgAlO/FeCo(001) Magnetic Tunnel Junctions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We investigate the frequency characteristics and voltage dependence of tunnel magnetocapacitance (TMC) in FeCo/MgAlO/FeCo(001) epitaxial magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs). We have successfully observed a large TMC ratio of up to 456% at 140 Hz and 75 mV, which is the largest value ever reported for MTJs. The frequency characteristics and voltage dependence of the observed TMC characteristics can be reasonably explained by the calculation based on the extended Debye-Frölich model.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Hexaferrite-Based SrFe12O19/Fe-Co Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Hexaferrite-based nanocomposites were prepared by a powder metallurgical method using a mixture of SrFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> powder as a hard phase and Fe-Co alloy nanopowder as a soft one at a volume fraction of SrFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf>:Fe-Co= 90:10. X-ray diffraction measurements showed that heating a mixture of the two powders in a vacuum at 773 K for 3 h leads to fabricating SrFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf>/Fe-Co nanocomposites without severe reaction between the two phases. Elemental mapping using a scanning electron microscope with an energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy devise confirmed a uniform mixture of the SrFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> powder and Fe-Co nanopowder. The room-temperature magnetization measurements gave rise to a slight increase in saturation magnetization (53.2 emu/g) compared to the value obtained from pure SrFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> powder. The magnetic coercivity of the SrFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf>/Fe-Co nanocomposites was 2.0 kOe, comparable to that of the pure SrFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> powder.

articleTitle: Research on A Transverse-Dislocated Magnetic-Field Modulated Brushless Contra-Rotating Machine Adopting Different Core Material Combinations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The transverse-dislocated magnetic-field modulated brushless contra-rotating machine (TDMFM-BCRM) is a novel contra-rotating machine for the contra-rotating propeller propulsion. It has the advantages of no brushes and slip rings, equal and opposite torques at any time. However, due to the geometrical complexity of the TDMFM-BCRM, there are some challenges about its manufacturing. In this paper, first, the structure and operating principle are introduced. Second, the performance of TDMFM-BCRM adopting different core material combinations including electrical steel (ES) and soft magnetic composite (SMC) is investigated. Third, a prototype is manufactured and tested to verify the analysis. Finally, more manufacturing methods for the TDMFM-BCRM are studied.

Author Keywords: transverse-dislocated magnetic-field modulated brushless contra-rotating machine (TDMFM-BCRM)

articleTitle: Novel Stator Slot Opening to Reduce Electrical Machine Bearing Currents
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Ball bearings are largely used in electrical machines, where high frequency parasitic currents affect their life time. This document presents a novel Zig-Zag stator slot opening geometry to reduce the winding-to-rotor capacitance C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">wr</inf> with the consequent reduction of Bearing Voltage Ratio and Electric Discharge Machining bearing currents. This digest focuses on an improved analytical model to permit the calculation of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">wr</inf> for unusual slot opening geometries, validated via Finite Element Analysis. Complete electrostatic and electromagnetic Finite Element Analysis comparisons between the Zig-Zag, oblique and original (classical slot opening configuration) machines will be proposed in the full paper. These comparisons suggest that the Zig-Zag geometry yelds the best performance in terms of Bearing Voltage Ratio reduction, while keeping torque performance close to the original machine. An additional comparison between the novel Zig-Zag model and the classical one with reduced slot opening to have the same C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">wr</inf> values will be proposed, showing an higher degradation in terms of torque performance for the latter. The study will show that the Zig-Zag model could be a good candidate to reduce effectively electrical machine bearing currents. Moreover, the improved analytical method can be helpful for engineers and researchers to calculate C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">wr</inf> with a good accuracy for unusual slot opening geometries.

articleTitle: Hysteresis Effect Induced Inductance Change and Power Loss for Boost Converter during the Voltage Conversion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Based on the Jiles-Atherton (J-A) model, the differential equation of hysteresis has the different signs at the positive-going and negative-going magnetic fields (H), which is +1 if dH/dt > 0 and is -1 if dH/dt < 0. This implies that an inductor has the different inductances at the current ramp-up time and ramp-down time due to hysteresis sign and remanence magnetization changes. However, this phenomenon is never reported until now. In this paper, the inductance of an inductor larger than the intrinsic inductance at the current ramp-up time and smaller than that at the current ramp-down time are found in a boost converter during the voltage converter.

articleTitle: Mechanisms and Control of Inter-Skyrmion Attractions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To commercialize stable, highly-integrated, and low-power-consuming magnetic memories of skyrmions, stable control of their motion are crucial. The key is to manipulate the inter-skyrmion interactions. However, conventional circular skyrmions have only isotropic repulsion and the mechanism of inducing attraction has been unclear. We theoretically find two such mechanisms, distortion of skyrmion shape and formation of magnetic domains. Remarkably, the latter induces strong attraction which can be tuned by two orders of magnitude, by tilting the external magnetic field.

articleTitle: Magnetization reversal and Gilbert damping in Co2FeAl0.5Si0.5 (CFAS) quaternary Heusler alloy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, study of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>/M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>, resonance field (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) and linewidth (ΔH) as functions of the magnetic field angle for the CFAS films of varying thickness (t) by longitutional magneto-optical Kerr rotation (L-MOKE) and ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) techniques establishes the presence of in-plane uniaxial anisotropy. The observed variation of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> with the azimuthal field angle is well described by the two-phase model. In the CFAS films with t = 12 nm, 25 nm and 75 nm, magnetization reversal occurs through the formation of ripple domains, while for t = 50 nm CFAS films, the reverse 180° domain nucleates and grows by domain wall movement with increasing external magnetic field. The contributions to the FMR linewidth from the inhomogeneity, two-magnon scattering and Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) damping are estimated. The lowest (intrinsic) LLG parameter (α) of 0.002 is deduced for the film with t = 50 nm. Our results provide crucial information about the magnetization dynamics and damping in CFAS thin films which will be usefull for applications in spintronics devices.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation and Experiment of 3-D Electromagnetic Force of Permanent Magnet Electrodynamic Suspension System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The electromagnetic module is essential for the stability of the permanent magnet (PM) electrodynamic suspension (EDS) system, and the accurate calculation of the electromagnetic force is the premise of studying the dynamic performance of the Halbach array. To establish an accurate and effective dynamic model of the PM EDS, considering the translational and vertical motions of the magnet, an analytical model (AM) of the linear Halbach array is established in this research. According to the Biot-Savart law and the surface current method, the 3-D magnetic flux density expression is derived. When the linear Halbach array translationally and vertically moves, the magnetic vector potential equations are formulated using the Fourier transform and are solved using truncated region eigenfunction expansion.
