Then, compared with the 3-D finite element model in steady state, the average errors of lift force and drag force only are 0.87% and 3.96%, respectively. The accuracy of the AM satisfies the requirements of dynamic modeling and analysis of the PM EDS system. Furthermore, considering the translational and vertical motions, the validity of the AM is verified by comparing the analytic calculations with the dynamic experiment data on the high-speed rotating experiment platform.

articleTitle: Experimental Determination of Anisotropy Fields, First and Second Anisotropy Constants, and Remanent Magnetizations in Self-Polarized Zn-Ti and Co-Ti Equally Co-Substituted BaM Ferrites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: M-type hexagonal barium ferrites Ba(M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12−2x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> (M=Co or Ti, x=0-0.5) are synthesized by chemical topotactical reaction. Both randomly oriented and self-polarized samples are prepared. Experimental values of the anisotropy fields, first and second anisotropy constants, and remanent magnetizations are extracted by combining hysteresis loops and microwave measurements. A salient result of this study is that, comparing with K1, K2 cannot be disregarded for these co-doped BaM hexaferrites, even at low doping levels. Results show that the compositions Ba(CoxTix)Fe12−2xO19 are more suitable for microwave applications that operate at frequencies between 30GHz and 40GHz.

articleTitle: Defect-driven antiferromagnetic domain walls in CuMnAs films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Antiferromagnetic (AF) materials offer a route to realising high-speed, high-density data storage devices that are robust against magnetic fields due to their intrinsic dynamics in the THz-regime and the lack magnetic stray fields. The key to functionality and efficiency is the control of AF domains and domain walls. Although AF domain structures are known to be sensitive to magnetoelastic effects, the microscopic interplay of crystalline defects, strain and magnetic ordering remains largely unknown. Here, we reveal, using photoemission electron microscopy combined with scanning x-ray diffraction microscopy and micromagnetic simulations, that the AF domain structure in CuMnAs thin films is dominated by nanoscale structural twin defects, which determine the location and orientation of 180° and 90° domain walls. The results emphasise the high sensitivity of the AF domain structure to the crystallographic nanostructure and provide a route to optimisng device performance.

articleTitle: Magnon dynamics in a Skyrmion-textured domain wall of antiferromagnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We theoretically investigate the interaction between magnons and a Skyrmion-textured domain wall in a two-dimensional antiferromagnet and elucidate the resultant properties of magnon transport. Using supersymmetric quantum mechanics, we solve the scattering problem of magnons on top of the domain wall and obtain the exact solutions of propagating and bound magnon modes. Then, we find their properties of reflection and refraction in the Skyrmion-textured domain wall, where magnons experience an emergent magnetic field due to its non-trivial spin texture-induced effective gauge field. Based on the obtained scattering properties of magnons and the domain wall, we show that the thermal transport decreases as the domain wall’s chirality increases. Our results suggest that the thermal transport of an antiferromagnet is tunable by modulating the Skyrmion charge density of the domain wall, which might be useful for realizing electrically tunable spin caloritronic devices.

articleTitle: Non-Conventional Computing using thermal and driven Skyrmion Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Skyrmions are magnetic whirls which exhibit quasiparticle-behavior, respond strongly nonlinear to external stimuli and have recently been shown to exhibit thermally activated dynamics. These properties open up possible future applications in computing architectures beyond von-Neumann computing. We propose and demonstrate experimentally a conceptually new approach to skyrmion reservoir computing that exploits the thermally activated diffusive motion of skyrmions. By confining the thermal and energetically low, electrically gated skyrmion motion, together with employing spatially resolved input and readout, we find that already a single skyrmion in a confined, triangular geometry suffices to realize non-linearly separable functions, which we demonstrate for the XOR gate along with all other Boolean logic gate operations. Beyond reservoir computing, we design and experimentally realize token-based and stochastic computing devices which also greatly benefit from thermal skyrmion dynamics.

articleTitle: Magnetic-field-assisted photocatalysis of N-TiO2 nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Nitrogen doped TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles were synthesized through solvothermal method employing Ti (IV) butoxide and HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as precursors. Structural and optical characterizations confirm their nanometer nature (sizes around 10 nm) and the band-gap energy values in the UV range (3.2 eV). Nitrogen doping enhances the occurrence of optical Urbach tails extending towards the visible region. Visible photocatalytic performance (degradation of methyl orange) is correlated with maximum values in the magnetic susceptibility linked to a magnetic polarization of the anatase structure via defects (oxygen vacancies). The application of magnetic field provides a positive effect (acceleration in reaction kinetics) within the UV-Vis range.

articleTitle: Current-induced Néel order switching facilitated by magnetic phase transition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Antiferromagnetic materials (AFMs), which have zero-stray field and the THz-range magnetic resonance frequency, are promising candidates for the next-generation magnetic memory technology. Here, we report an electrical writing of antiferromagnetic orders through a record-low current density on the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> A cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> facilitated by the unique AFM-ferromagnetic (FM) phase transition in FeRh. The spin-orbit torque can switch the AFM order parameter by 90° with a reduced writing current density by introducing a transient FM state via current-induced Joule heating. This work demonstrates the exciting possibility of writing operations in AFM-based devices with a lower current density, opening a new pathway toward pure AFM memory applications.

articleTitle: Four-terminal sensing of laser-induced anomalous-Nernst voltages
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report four terminal sensing of the anomalous Nernst effect of a Co/Pt thin film induced by perpendicular thermal gradients locally formed by a focused laser beam. We observed that transverse and longitudinal electrical voltages individually detect the projection components of the magnetization via the laser-induced anomalous Nernst effect. This scheme would be potentially applied to vector sensing of local magnetization under a focused laser beam.

articleTitle: Magnetite/copolymer Nanosphere Added Soft-magnetic Carbonyl Iron Based Magnetorheological Fluid And Its Damping Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetite/copolymer (Fe3O4/copolymer) nanosphere was synthesized via chemical oxidative polymerization and utilized as an additional ingredient in soft-magnetic carbonyl iron (CI) microsphere based magnetorheological fluid (MRF) to improve its magnetorheological and damping performance. MRFs with a monodisperse phase (CI-based MRF) and with a bidisperse phase (CI/nanosphere-based MRF) were prepared using polyalphaolefin as an oil medium. Magnetorheological performances of CI-based MRF and CI/nanosphere-based MRF were analyzed by the steady shear model and oscillatory dynamic model under gradient magnetic field. Flow curves are well fitted to the Hershel-Bulkley model, and dynamic, elastic and static yield stresses were confirmed to follow a universal scaling equation. The dispersion stabilities of MRFs were measured using an optical analyzer of Turbiscan. The CI/nanosphere-based MRF were further injected into a custom designed magnetorheological damper (MRD), and its damping force characteristics including damping force as a function of magnetic field, displacement and velocity, were investigated for vibration damping applications in mechanical system. Results shown that the CI/nanosphere-based MRF exhibited improved dispersion stability, magnetorheological and damping performance, which is attributed to the nanosphere filling the free volume among the CI, inducing stiffer chain structures and improved magnetorheological and damping performance.

articleTitle: Electronic Structure and Curie Temperature Change in Ti or Al Doped GdFeSi Compound
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The ternary GdFeSi compound doped with Ti or Al as the GdFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Si and GdFeSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf> series is investigated theoretically and experimentally in this work. The parent and Ti doped compounds are found to crystallize into the tetragonal structure, in the Al doped compounds, the cubic and hexagonal phases are also found in addition to the original tetragonal phase. GdFeSi is interesting for the presence of a magnetocaloric effect with a maximum -ΔSM(T) value of 5.0 J/kgK. With increasing Ti content, the Curie temperature T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> is found to increase quickly for x = 0-0.1 and then, more moderate change is observed, similar to the Al doping. The electronic structure and magnetic moments for GdFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Si and GdFeSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf> are calculated theoretically within DFT+U taking into account strong electron correlations in 4f Gd shell. The calculated electronic structure demonstrates a significant increase of the density of electron states at the Fermi level for some compositions which accompanied by the rapid growth of T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> in the GdFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Si system.

articleTitle: Global Biasing Using a Hardware-Based Artificial Zeeman Term in Spinwave Ising Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A spinwave Ising machine (SWIM) is a newly proposed type of time-multiplexed hardware solver for combinatorial optimization that employs feedback coupling and phase sensitive amplification to map an Ising Hamiltonian into phase-binarized propagating spin-wave RF pulses in an Yttrium-Iron-Garnet (YIG) film. In this work, we increase the mathematical complexity of the SWIM by adding a global Zeeman term to a 4-spin MAX-CUT Hamiltonian using a continuous external electrical signal with the same frequency as the spin pulses and phase locked with with one of the two possible states. We are able to induce ferromagnetic ordering in both directions of the spin states despite antiferromagnetic pairwise coupling. Embedding a planar antiferromagnetic spin system in a magnetic field has been proven to increase the complexity of the graph associated to its Hamiltonian and thus this straightforward implementation helps explore higher degrees of complexity as the technology evolves.

articleTitle: Torque Performance Enhancement for Hybrid PM Motor Considering Magnet Characteristic Difference and Variation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, for the hybrid PM (HPM) motor using multi PM materials with different characteristics, considering the characteristic difference and coupling effect between magnet materials, a preliminary design of the hybrid PMs is presented to improve the PM utilization and the superposition rate of torque components. Besides, according to the magnet characteristic variation under different working modes of the motor, a multi-objective variable condition weighted optimization design method is further proposed to improve the torque performance, efficiency and anti-demagnetization capability of HPM motor under multiple operating conditions.

articleTitle: Field-Induced Spin Nematic Phase of a Magnet on the Shastry-Sutherland Lattice with the Anisotropic Ferromagnetic Interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A spin-1/2 magnetic system with the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice is investigated using the numerical diagonalization of finite-size clusters. The easy-axis anisotropy is introduced at the ferromagnetic bond of the present system and the magnetization process in the external magnetic field parallel to the axis is studied. As a result, the field-induced two-magnon bound phase is found at higher magnetization region than half the saturation. Base on the analogy to the previous study on the spin ladder system, the spin nematic order perpendicular to the external field would be expected to appear in this two-magnon bound phase.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Practicality for Fully Dense Isotropic Sm-Fe-N Magnets Made by Shock-Wave Consolidation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Fully dense isotropic Sm-Fe-N magnets were successfully fabricated using the shock-wave consolidation method. Deterioration of the hard magnetic properties of the Sm-Fe-N by the impact load during the consolidation process was not observed, and consequently the fully dense magnet showed high (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of 116-144 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (14.5-18 MGOe) which is the highest level as the isotropic magnet. Its temperature coefficient of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> was 0.066 %/°C, and that of coercivity was 0.36 %/°C. The irreversible flux loss of the sample with L/D of 0.78 after exposed at 150 °C was small value of 5-10 %. The fully dense Sm-Fe-N magnet without coating showed a good corrosion resistance, and it had enough mechanical strength. From these results, the practicality of the fully dense Sm-Fe-N magnet made by shock wave consolidation has been confirmed.

articleTitle: Magnetization State and Magnetic Structure of Wiegand Wire Evaluated by External Magnetic Field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We analyzed the magnetization state and magnetic structure in Wiegand wire by measuring a magnetic field from the wire. The Wiegand wire exhibits a unique fast magnetization reversal feature in an externally applied alternating magnetic field. The mechanism and magnetization states that yield a large Barkhausen jump have not been sufficiently elucidated. We defined a three-layer magnetic structure of the Wiegand wire, as well as analyzed the magnetization state and magnetization process of these layers in the applied alternating magnetic field. We determined a switching field of each layer and specified the magnetization states that resulted in the large Barkhausen jump.

articleTitle: Polarized neutron transmission spectroscopy on an ultrafine grained steel
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Neutron transmission spectroscopy has attracted much attention as a promising operando characterization method for multi-phase composite materials with various crystallographic textures. For further advances, we have studied contributions from magnetic scatterings for polarized neutrons using an ultra-fine grained high carbon steel as an example. The results suggest that the information derived from the magnetic scatterings is helpful to evaluation of the complicated fine structure in magnetic and structural materials.

articleTitle: Switchable Frequency Response Based on Electropermanent Magnet Actuator for Wide-range Operation of Electromagnetic Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a linear oscillatory actuator (LOA) that can switch its degree of freedom (DOF) for the purpose of improving its frequency response. Electropermanent magnet (EPM) is utilized as an energy-saving solution to switch DOF by absorbing and desorbing secondary mass with primary mass. EPM is a magnetic circuit which uses two different magnets: NdFeB magnet (high coercivity) and AlNiCo magnet (low coercivity). We derive two motion equations under absorption and desorption of the masses. The operational principle of the EPM is described. We evaluate absorption and desorption of the masses through numerical calculation through MATLAB/Simulink and JMAG-Designer. The primary mass successfully absorbed the secondary one due to the electromagnetic attractive force of the EPM generated by a short-time pulsed current. The desorption motion was also successful because the short-time pulsed current demagnetized the AlNiCo magnet and eliminated the attractive force of the EPM.

articleTitle: Wireless Magnetoelectric Neural Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In the study of human physiology, the brain remains the last frontier. Wired electrode interfaces first developed in the 1960s endure to today as treatments for Parkinson’s, depression, paralysis and other neurological diseases and injuries. Unfortunately, the risks involved with implanting and replacing the electrodes in the brain confine it to niche, last resort cases for patients without functional drug-based treatments. In the effort to replace wired interfaces, magnetic fields have emerged alongside ultrasound and optogenetics as one of the leading paths forward. However, modern magnetic methods such as magnetomechanical and Transcranial Magnetic stimulation have tradeoffs with temporal and spatial resolution. Magnetoelectric nanoparticles (MENPs) can offer the best of both worlds, obtaining both spatial localization and temporal rapidness with particles small enough to pass the blood-brain barrier. MENPs efficiently convert non-tissue interacting magnetic fields into short range, stimulating electric fields. In this work, we demonstrate that MENPs can wirelessly modulate neuron firing in vitro and govern motor behavior in vivo in a controllable and reversible manner.

articleTitle: Control of spin currents and antiferromagnetic moments via topological surface states for ultralow energy consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The efficient electrical detection and manipulation of antiferromagnetic moments is challenging. We show that the spin current and antiferromagnetic moments in the topological insulator/antiferromagnetic insulator bilayer (Bi,Sb)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/α-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> can be controlled via topological surface states. The spin current can control the moment rotation in the antiferromagnetic insulator by means of a giant spin-orbit torque (SOT) generated by the topological surface states, where the switching is detected by the magnetoresistance signal at the interface, named as Rashba-Edelstein magnetoresistance (RE-MR). The required threshold switching current density is 3.5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> A cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> at room temperature, which is one order of magnitude smaller than that required in heavy-metal/antiferromagnetic insulator systems, exhibiting the potential for ultralow energy consumption. Notably, the topological surface states of (Bi,Sb)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> can be modulated by applying a gate voltage, giving rise to electrically controllable RE-MR and SOT switching. Consequently, when the Fermi-level location of (Bi,Sb)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is tailored by electric fields, the signal of RE-MR is enhanced and the threshold switching current density is further decreased.

articleTitle: Investigation of Electromagnetic Formulations for Efficient Analysis of MFTs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper concerns with enhancing the efficiency of Medium Frequency (MFT) analysis accounting for the inductive, capacitive, and resistive phenomena in MFTs connected to high dv/dt power converters. A formulation using EQS, MQS, and the so-called Darwin approximation of electromagnetic Maxwell equations is implemented. The numeric stability, computational complexity, accuracy, and validity of the various quasi-static formulations are detailed.

articleTitle: Minor Loop Position and Area Measurement of Inductors for DC-DC converter Considering Excitation Process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Power conversion circuits based on switching operations are used in automobiles and home appliances to achieve higher eﬃciency and its miniaturization. The power conversion circuits have to connect use inductors, which are characterized by the fact that DC current is superimposed on the inductor. In this circuit, the evaluation of losses assuming the actual environment has become an issue in the design of inductors. This paper proposes a measurement procedures of minor loop due to differences in the excitation process of inductors used in actual power conversion circuits.

articleTitle: Impact of the Capacitance Cancellation on Attenuation Characteristic of Common-Mode Inductors Based on MnZn Ferrites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The impedance of inductors based on manganese zinc (MnZn) ferrites decreases in the high-frequency (HF) range because of the winding stray capacitance and the drastic decrease in complex permeability. Thus, the improvement of insertion loss by the capacitance cancellation on the common-mode inductors (CMIs) based on MnZn ferrites may be limited. This digest evaluates the impact of the capacitance cancellation on the insertion loss of CMIs based on MnZn ferrites. The measurement results validate that the MnZn ferrite-based CMI limits the improvement by the capacitance cancellation on the insertion loss in the MHz range.

articleTitle: Design of a Reaction Wheel with MRF-encapsulated Magnetic Ball
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, a novel design of reaction wheel used as attitude indicator/controller for satellites is proposed and examined through numerical finite element (FE) studies. Utilizing characteristics of magnetorheological fluids (MRF) being able to change state from liquid to solid when subjected to magnetization, a MRF-encapsulated magnetic ball is employed in this design to generate angular momentum in the reaction wheel. Through parametric studies in FE, best placement of coils is obtained in which the coils are concentrically placed and arranged sequentially around the circular tube of the reaction wheel. With the design, inertia of the reaction wheel is reduced and contact and friction issue of its moving parts are resolved. The proposed system can be ideal for indicating and controlling satellite’s attitude in space.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Optimization of the Interior Permanent Magnet Motor for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This research carries out the optimization design and analysis experiment of the existing design of the IPM motor for electric vehicles. In this paper, three optimization methods are designed for the torque ripple value, namely the Taguchi method, the fuzzy Taguchi method and the reaction surface method, and the reaction surface method has the highest optimization rate. The optimization rates are 84.58% and 38.47%, respectively. Finally, a single-layer magnet IPM motor with a high optimization rate and low production cost is selected to make a prototype, and the verification and comparison between the physical and the simulation are carried out. The error values between the load and no-load measurement results and the simulation results are 4.35% and 3.95% for average torque, 14.49% and 75.98% for torque ripple, and 17.21% and 15.07% for efficiency. The measurement results of the load test show that the torque ripple value of the prototype is better than the original design, so it is verified that the above optimization and simulation methods are suitable for torque ripple optimization.

articleTitle: The effect of annealing temperature on grain boundary structure and magnetic properties of Nd-Ce-Gd-Fe-B sintered magnet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Post-sinter annealing plays an important role in optimizing grain boundary phases of Nd-Fe-B magnets. The sintered magnet is usually processed by two-step annealing, which consists of a high-temperature annealing (first-step annealing) followed by a low-temperature annealing (second-step annealing). In this work, the magnetic properties and microstructure of Nd-Ce-Gd-Fe-B magnets have been investigated by different second-step annealing temperature at 420 °C and 460 °C, respectively, since differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) analysis revealed that the phase transition temperature was approximately at 436 °C. As the second-step annealing temperature was increased from 420 °C to 460 °C, the intrinsic coercivity (Hcj) of the magnets was increased by 20.0 kA/m, and the squareness factor was improved significantly from 0.85 to 0.98. Microstructural analysis showed that the thickness of grain boundary layers in annealed magnets increased from 13.0 nm to 21.1 nm, which is helpful to decrease the exchange-coupling between RE2Fe14B (RE: rare earth) grains and therefore enhance the coercivity.

articleTitle: Rotor Auxiliary Slot Design Optimization for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Double-layer Rotor Structure for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPM) for electric vehicle drive has the disadvantages of high torque ripple and high vibration. Auxiliary slots on the rotor surface can improve the air gap magnetic density sinusoidality by changing the magnetic permeability at different positions of the air gap. The IPM uses a double-layer permanent magnet (PM) rotor structure, and the shape, position, and number of different auxiliary slots affect the torque performance and vibration of the IPM. In this paper, we optimize the rotor auxiliary slot structure of three IPM rotor structures with torque ripple and air gap magnetic density deformation rate (MDDR) as the optimization objectives and summarize the influence of rotor auxiliary slot on the torque performance and vibration of double-layer permanent magnet IPM.

articleTitle: Martensite transition and room temperature magnetocaloric effect in Ag doped Ni50Mn37In13 alloy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Ni-Mn-In based Heusler alloys have excellent magnetocaloric properties and have been subjected to chemical modification for more than a decade to enhance their entropy change. This work is a novel try where Ni is doped with Ag, a non-magnetic element, and as a result, martensite transition temperature has been tuned close to the room temperature. Further silver doping has considerably reduced magnetic and thermal hysteresis. Overall, a large room temperature inverse magnetocaloric effect has been observed in Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">48</inf>Ag<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">37</inf>In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</inf> alloy with an appreciable reversibility.

articleTitle: Axial Flux Switched Reluctance Machine Modelling by a Quasi-3D Reluctance Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Switched reluctance machines find applications in numerous sectors such as electric vehicles, mechanical presses, pumps, conveyors, compressors, fans, washing machines… and can replace classical induction machines in situations where operating conditions do not suit them. The axial flux version of these machines is characterized by its high-speed capability and high power density making it especially suited for traction applications. Design of electrical machines could be highly time consuming for structures having 3D main magnetic flux as the axial flux machines and especially when using 3D finite element method which is not suitable for the early stages of the design process. In this paper, an alternative quasi-3D reluctance network (Q3DRN) modelling method is proposed combining both an acceptable precision and a reduced computation time in one package, and it is applied to a 24-pole segmented rotor, 36-slot per stator topology of an axial-field double stator switched reluctance machine (AFDSSRM) fed with a 3-phase current. The proposed modeling approach is validated by comparing obtained results to the 3D finite elements ones for the magnetic flux density in the air gap and the electromagnetic torque in nonlinear permeability conditions. The proposed method is 20 times faster than 3D finite elements with an error not exceeding 8% on total torque.

articleTitle: Magnetic MXene: A Machine learning model with small data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: MXenes, comprising of atomically thin layers of transition metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides, exhibit properties which are not found in their corresponding bulk materials. Interestingly, because of the presence of transition metal, MXenes may also provide the candidate materials for observing low-dimensional magnetism. This can be of interest to various applications such as spintronic devices, data storage, and electromagnetic interference shielding. Here, we focus on the magnetic MXenes which are only a few in number out of known MXenes. We propose a machine learning model for the prediction of magnetic MXenes using a carefully designed descriptor.

articleTitle: Analytical Model for Electromagnetic Field in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Considering Stator Slotting and Rotor Eccentricity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In order to quickly and accurately predict the air-gap flux density under stator slotting and rotor eccentricity, in this paper, a two-dimensional analytical model of the loaded magnetic field of a permanent magnet synchronous motor(PMSM) is established based on conformal mapping and fractional linear mapping. Firstly, the separation variable method is used to solve the two-dimensional air-gap flux density of the ideal model. The conformal mapping is used to analyze the complex relative air-gap permeance function and the armature reaction magnetic field under the stator slotting. Then the fractional linear mapping is introduced to calculate the relative permeability function when the rotor is eccentric. Finally, a 32-pole 36-slot PMSM is used as a prototype. The comparison between the analytical model and the finite element method (FEM)results proves the accuracy and the effectiveness of reducing the calculation time. The results show that the two-dimensional analytical model can take the slotting and rotor eccentricity into account, and can quickly calculate the loaded air-gap flux density and electromagnetic properties under different winding current inputs. The analytical model can reveal the mechanism of the motor design parameters on the flux density. The research shows that the complex relative air-gap permeance function is only related to the slot opening width and the number of stator slots. The slot opening width determines the magnitude of the permeance, and the relationship is reverse. The slots number determines the spatial order of the permeance. Rotor eccentricity distorts the air-gap flux density by changing the air-gap permeance. With the increase of the static eccentric distance, the amplitude of the eccentric permeance will increase, but the spatial order will not change.

articleTitle: Conformally Conical Coil Design in Wireless Power Transfer for Emerging Unmanned Electric Vessels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Coil design plays an important role in wireless power transfer (WPT). Conformally conical coils are presented in this paper for wireless charging electric vessels to meet the mechanical requirement of vessels. The conical coil is adopted on the receiver side to install on an electric vessel, while spiral coils are used as transmitter coils. Moreover, load-independent constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) are analyzed through circuit analysis to charge battery-based electric vessels.

articleTitle: Approximation of nonlinear properties of soft-magnetic materials with Bézier curves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Adequate mathematical description of magnetization curves is indispensable in engineering. The accuracy of the description has significant impact on design of electric machines and devices. The aim of this paper was to systematically analyze the capability of Bézier curves to describe the nonlinear properties of soft-magnetic materials. Bézier curves were compared with most used sigmoid functions. The conclusion was that Bézier curves have the flexibility needed to describe discussed nonlinear properties, whereas an in-depth analysis and comparison versus state-of-the-art functions for description of nonlinear magnetization curves will be presented in the full-paper.

articleTitle: PLD-fabricated Fe-Co films prepared by using different spot size of laser beam
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Fe-Co films prepared by using a PLD (Pulsed Laser Deposition) method with several diameters of a laser beam. It was found that the usage of a Fe-Co alloy target together with a small spot size, which means that a laser beam was focused on the surface of a target, enables us to reduce the number and/or size of droplets and improve the surface roughness of samples. The transfer of composition from a target to the corresponding film deteriorated as diameters of a laser beam decreased. Furthermore, an as-deposited Fe-Co film prepared by using the small spot size had the magnetization of approximately 2.4 T at the applied magnetic field of 1400 kA/m.

articleTitle: Functional magnetic nanoparticles: from synthesis design to in-depth characterization and nano-labelling for ultrasensitive magnetic biosensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The detection of disease specific biomarkers such as proteins and nucleic acids has recently received increased attention with the outbreak of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. One of the innovative medical sensing nanotechnologies is based on the change in dynamic magnetic behaviour of magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) upon binding to a specific biological target. Here, we present and analyze tricomponent MNPs for magnetic immunoassays (MIAs). The MNPs remain monodisperse before and after coating with a functional polymer and exhibit suitable magnetic properties for MIAs.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Dual-Stator Permanent Magnet Machines With Squirrel Stator Teeth Designed in Hypotenuse
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The new dual-stator permanent magnet machines with squirrel stator teeth designed in hypotenuse (SSTH-DSPMM) are designed and analyzed, which are suitable for the demand of high torque quality in electric vehicle application. The hypotenuse in SST is designed for regulating the harmonic distribution and suppressing harmonic distortion of airgap flux density to achieve the merits of low cogging torque and low torque ripple. The designed SST can be considered as combinations of rectangle and triangle, which form trapezoid- and parallelogram-shaped stator teeth. The paper forces on the comparative analysis of three representative SSTH-DSPMM and the conventional DSPMM with rectangle squirrel stator teeth using finite element analysis (FEA). For a fair comparison, the investigated four machines are designed with identical key parameters. The FEA-analyzed results of cogging torque, steady torque at rated state and torque ripple can verify the superiority of the designed SSTH-DSPMMs.

articleTitle: Modeling the Impact of Laser Powder Bed Fusion on Nd-Fe-B Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Statistical modelling was successfully applied to Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) of Nd-Fe-B permanent magnets to identify the potential impact of different process parameters and their interactions on resulting magnetic properties. Process models for the magnetic properties coercivity H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>, remanence J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> as well as for the shape of the demagnetization curve are obtained. The model quality for H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> is excellent (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.99). The model for J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> only allows a rough statement on the impact of the LPBF process due to a weaker quality of the model (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.77). It will not be possible to maximize H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> and J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of LPBF manufactured Nd-Fe-B magnets at the same time due to their contrary dependencies on different LPBF parameters. We have predicted an optimized parameter set with a resulting high H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> of 816 kA/m and a maximized J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of 0.65 T. From these properties and the calculated shape of the demagnetization curve we predict a (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of 60.77 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> for a magnet processed on a LPBF machine AconityMINI using MQP™-S powder.

articleTitle: Anisotropic FMR Peak Widths in Fe-Co Single Crystal Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We investigated Q-band (f=35 GHz) and X-band (f=9 GHz) ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) spectra of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> single crystal thin films (x<0.5) in the (001)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe-Co</inf> film plane in terms of magnetostriction. The FMR peak width ΔH(f) and the magnetostriction λ had the maximum and minimum values at the 〈100〉 and the 〈110〉 directions of the specimens. The periodic variations of ΔH(f) were due to the anisotropic variations of the frequency independent part ΔH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> in ΔH(f). The linear relationship existed between ΔH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and λ.

articleTitle: Magnetic and magnetocaloric properties of arc-melted and melt-spun TbNi1.5Fe0.5
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Polycrystalline Laves phase intermetallic compound TbNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> with x = 0.5 (Cubic, MgCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) has been prepared by arc-melting as well as melt-spinning techniques. The crystallite size of melt spun TbNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf> has been found as ~ 46 nm from powder X-ray diffraction data. Transmission electron microscopy images on melt-spun sample show the formation of spherical particles of size ~ 62. Magnetization data reveal ferromagnetic ordering at 323 K and 319 K respectively for the arc-melted and melt-spun samples. Nearly constant magnetocaloric effect has been observed in the temperature range of 250 to 340 K indicating that the magnetic moments align over a broad temperature range and not completely near Curie temperature.

articleTitle: Application of Oleic acid functionalized Fe3O4 magnetic nanoparticles for adsorption of oil from emulsified solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, magnetite was synthesized via co-precipitation method and modified with different amounts for oleic acid (x=0.5 and 2 mL) in seeking to understand the adsorption capability of oil for potential wastewater treatment usage. The morphology and chemical structure of the OA-coated Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanoadsorbents were characterized by FT-IR, XRD, SEM, TEM, VSM, ASAP and MTT assay for the cytotoxicity test. Successful coating was confirmed by FTIR and showed COO- groups within the spectra. An increase in the amount of OA leads to the decrease in magnetization but still demonstrated a superparamagnetic property for an easy recovery. Grain size was evaluated, and was found out to be in the range of 8-10nm. The adsorbent is well fitted on the Langmuir model suggesting a monolayer adsorption. Regarding the adsorption kinetics, the adsorbent follows the pseudo second order with high R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.98. The nanoadsorbent exhibited a high cell viability rate signifying low toxicity. Therefore, the synthesized nanoparticle is a good candidate for broad environmental applications as such for oil/water emulsion separations as shown in this study.

articleTitle: Measuring spatially resolved phase of nanoscale spin waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report on spatially resolved phase measurements of nanoscale spin waves with sub-50 om spatial resolution. We performed micro-focused phase-resolved Brillouinlight scattering experiments utilizinga weaklyinteracting array of Mie- resonators patterned by electron beam lithography on the top of a magnetic thin film. This allowed us to detect nanoscale spin waves and at the same time to achieve a spatial resolution in the order of tens of nanometers, one order of magnitude belowthe optical resolution of the used microscope objective. We were able to measure full dispersion relation for the spin waves in the range from 1 rad/μm to 30 rad/μm. These results demonstrate the feasibility of all-optical phase-resolved characterization of nanoscalespin waves.

articleTitle: Dynamical switching properties and downsize scalability in Perpendicular Shape Anisotropy MTJ
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The novel Perpendicular Shape-Anisotropy Spin-Transfer-Torque Magnetic Random-Access Memory (PSA-STT-MRAM) is shown to increase the thermal stability factor ∆ of the storage layer through modulation of its shape anisotropy, surpassing the scalability limitation of conventional magnetic tunnel junctions to below sub-20 nm technological nodes. However, for large aspect-ratio, the magnetization reversal becomes non-uniform and less controllable. Thus, it is necessary to reduce the total thickness of the storage layer, while keeping an appropriate ∆. We show that, making use of micromagnetic simulations, making use of a capping layer to promote an additional surface anisotropy leads to a lower thickness requirement, compatible with lower switching voltage and faster reversal. These results are backed with experimental evidence, as STT reversal is shown without field. However, this capping layer shows less efficient for very small diameters, down to 5 nm, in the limit where ∆ is limited by the energy of the domain-wall created in the layer. It is shown that it would be possible to avoid this stability capping while maintaing a single PSA layer, with an induced uniaxial anisotropy.

articleTitle: Structure, Magnetism and Electrical Transport of Electron Doped SrCo0.5Nb0.5O3
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A-site nominal doping of disordered perovskite SrCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> with La<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>, Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> showed a shift in transition temperature to lower temperatures. Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf>A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>(CoNb)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (A=La, Nd) forms in the cubic structure with Pm-3m symmetry. An increase in unit cell dimensions for La doped sample is observed. Whereas, the Nd doped samples show a decrease in unit cell volume. Electron doping introduces 2+ oxidation state for Co ions, with the Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> state still present in the system. The samples are highly insulating, with the doped samples showing higher resistivity. The high resistivity in the doped samples is consistent with the increase in antiferromagnetic interactions in those.

articleTitle: FePd Single Layer and Synthetic Antiferromagnet with Low Damping and Crystalline Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy on Amorphous Si/SiO2 Wafers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: (001)-textured L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-phase FePd possesses strong crystalline perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) and low Gilbert damping constant and thus, is considered a promising material choice for scalable spintronic devices. To date, however, well-textured L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-FePd(001) thin films can only be prepared on a few expensive substrates, which directly impedes their industry compatibility and application prospect. In this digest, we report the deposition of L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-FePd(001) single layer and synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF) on industry-ready Si/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> wafers with large PMA, low damping, and strong antiferromagnetic interlayer exchange coupling. The microstructures of L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-FePd(001) single layer and SAF were imaged using scanning transmission electron microscopy. We observed sharp and flat interfaces between each layer as well as the heteroepitaxial growth of sample stacks, which explains the high performance of the samples.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis and Comparison of In-Wheel Outer Rotor Consequent-Pole Flux-Switching Permanent Magnet Machines with Different Magnet Arrangements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Due to the inherent flux-focusing effect as well as the elimination of the flux-barrier effect, consequent-pole flux-switching permanent magnet (CP-FSPM) machines have attracted growing attention in recent years. Furthermore, the simple and robust salient-pole rotor structure of CP-FSPM is suitable for in-wheel traction applications when the outer rotor (OR) layout is adopted. In order to investigate the applicability of OR CP-FSPM machines in traction applications, three typical machines with II-shaped, V-shaped, and U-shaped permanent magnet (PM) arrangements and a proposed machine with an improved inclined U-shaped PM arrangement are comprehensively analyzed and compared in this study. A simplified semi-analytical magnetomotive force (MMF)-permeance model is established to analyze the flux modulation effect of different PM excitations. In addition, the global optimization of these machines is conducted, and the on-load performance of the optimized machines is investigated and compared. As a result, the proposed inclined U-shaped PM machine exhibits the highest torque density among various CP-FSPM machines with the same PM volume, while the torque ripple is kept at a low value.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Shielding Method with Single-source Active Topology and Efficiency Stability for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Single shielding methods, especially single-active and single-ferrite, are known to suffer from insufficient comprehensive performance in wireless power transfer (WPT) system. To complement each other single method, a novel hybrid shielding method along with a parameter optimization strategy (POS) is proposed in this paper. The hybrid shielding system is composed of the single-source topology-integrated active suppression coils and adjustable ferrites. Two planar suppression coils are integrated into the compensation topology without an additional source. The ferrites channel the main magnetic flux, enhancing the coupling. The suppression coils generate a canceling flux whose path is opposite to the leakage flux from the ferrite pads. The principles of the POS are explained and discussed based on the analysis of magnetic field and circuit theory. A 1.5 kW/85 kHz scaled-down WPT prototype based on the proposed shielding method is fabricated, and its performance is experimentally verified. With a minimum transmission efficiency of 91.5%, the proposed method improves the shielding performance by 23.47% and 24.67% on the transmitting and receiving sides, respectively.

articleTitle: High Torque Density Toroidal Winding Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine with Dual Rotor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a new type of permanent magnet vernier machine (PMVM) with double rotor toroidal winding (TW). The design of double rotor and TW can effectively improve the utilization of armature winding, which makes the proposed machine torque density significantly improved. In addition, the TW can effectively reduce the end-winding length, so as to reduce the copper loss of the machine. The electromagnetic performances of the existing and proposed machines are analyzed and compared by using the time-stepping finite-element method, verifying the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Generation of Spin-wave Soliton using Magnetostatic Surface Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In recent years, as electronic devices have become more integrated and miniaturized, heat generation in electronic devices has been a big problem to be solved. Spin waves are considered as the next-generation information carrier, since a spin wave is the stream of angular momentum and accompanies no charge flow. To develop magnonic device using spin wave, the obstacle is the magnetic damping and distortion. A promissing solution to this problem is the use of spin-wave soliton. In this experiment, we observed the generation of spin-wave solitons of magnetostatic surface spin waves.

articleTitle: FEA Verification and Analyses for the Attraction Cases Between Magnetic Like Poles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A novel phenomenon of attraction between unequally sized like magnetic poles has been discovered experimentally, wherein the two magnets have different permeance coefficient (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) values. The attraction occurs only when a localized region of the low |P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>| magnet reverses its polarity and forms an unlike-pole region with respect to the high |P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>| magnet. The attraction of like-pole magnets is caused by the localized demagnetization (LD) and influenced by several factors such as geometry and alignment of magnets. In this paper, finite element analysis (FEA) simulation and verification of the experimental results are reported, along with the FEA simulation results for other unexperimented unequally sized magnet pairs with various geometries. The factors affecting the LD level based on the field/force map from FEA results are demonstrated. The FEA simulation results for various unequally sized like-poles have the potential to help in developing novel devices to be used in vast applications.

articleTitle: Winding Magnetization Design of Single-phase Capacitor-run Induction Motor for Submersible Pump Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper provides a systematic stator winding design scheme that can improve the operational efficiency of commercial single-phase capacitor-run induction motors effectively. Without changing the circuit components and structural constraints, the motor’s stator windings will be rearranged based on the devised theoretical basis and design objectives. The design scheme supported by the finite-element emulations will be supplied to show the efficiency improvement of a commercial single-phase 2-pole induction motor. In addition, experimental hardware validations will be accomplished from the motor with rewound stators, and evident performance advances from measurements confirm the design.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Electrical Conduction Property at Conductive Shield Layer to Improve Performance of Magnetically Shielded Rooms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To improve a performance of conductive shield, which is constructed in magnetically shielded rooms (MSRs) with high shielding performance, we introduce an evaluation method for electrical conduction property at joint part of conductive plates (e.g., Cu, Al). Some actual resistance sensors are developed via numerical analysis to evaluate the conduction property. We measure the resistance value at joint part of a simple conductive-shield box and its shielding performance on high frequency magnetic noise, and the results reveal that they have a correlation.

articleTitle: Multiband Periodic Metamaterial Antenna Design for Radar Sensor Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Design, simulation, and implementation of a periodic multiband metamaterial antenna design operating within 29-50 GHz frequency range for radar sensor applications is presented. Effect of metamaterial periodic surface on resonance frequency, directivity, and beamwidth has been studied and beamforming characteristics of the proposed design for radar sensors is analyzed in detail by integrating harmonic suppressed feed model for patch antennas. The prototype of multiband periodic metamaterial antenna is then built and measured. Simulation and measurement results are compared and verified to be in an agreement.

articleTitle: Iron and gold thin films: first-principles study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Using density functional theory, we carried out systematic calculations for a series of ultrathin iron layers with thicknesses ranging from one atomic monolayer to eleven monolayers (up to about 1.5 nm). We considered three cases: (1) iron layers both on a gold substrate and coated with gold, (2) iron layers on a gold substrate but without coverage and (3) free-standing iron layers adjacent to a vacuum. For our models we chose initial bcc Fe(001) surfaces and fcc Au(001) substrates. Based on the calculations, we determined the details of the geometry and magnetic properties of the systems. We calculate lattice parameters, magnetic moments, Curie temperatures and magnetocrystalline anisotropy energies. From the thickness dependence we determined the volume and surface contributions to the magnetic anisotropy constant. The further analysis allowed us to determine the thickness ranges of the occurrence of perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, as well as the effect of thickness and the presence of a substrate and cap layer on the direction of the magnetization easy axis.

articleTitle: Giant Magnetoresistive Biosensing Platform for Point-of-Care Gene Expression Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Influenza viruses are among the most common causes of respiratory viral infections globally. Detection and quantification of the host transcriptional response to influenza viruses can serve as a tool for timely diagnosis, triaging, and clinical management. However, use of gene expression analysis for clinical applications has traditionally been limited due to elaborate instrumentation requirements and slow turnaround-times. Using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and giant magnetoresistive (GMR) biosensors, we present a highly automated and multiplexed point-of-care (POC) platform that quantifies the expression of 4 genes related to influenza infection within ~35 min. Further, we demonstrate that this platform may serve as a useful clinical tool for POC influenza diagnostics by showing that, in a study of 21 subjects, those infected with influenza viruses had higher overall expression when compared with influenza-negative subjects (p < 0.0001, n=21).

articleTitle: Graphene-Supported Atom-Sized Magnets for Data Storage: What Can We Learn from First-Principles Calculations?
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Doping the graphene lattice with transition metal (TM) atoms has been identified as an effective strategy for obtaining high magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE), preventing thermally induced reorientation of magnetic moments between the easy and hard magnetization axes. Lattice imperfections such as atomic vacancies can anchor TM atoms or their clusters, preventing them from diffusing and agglomerating on the surface, ultimately allowing high MAEs of 170 meV for an OsPd dimer bound to a single nitrogen-decorated vacancy (NSV) in the graphene lattice. Importantly, the lighter TM dimers, FeMn bound to two separate double-vacancy (DV) defects, can also exhibit a significant MAE of 120 meV when interacting with each other through the graphene lattice. The presence of Mn impurities associated with DV defects in the graphene lattice has been confirmed experimentally and can form anchors for the formation of FeMn dimers. For practical applications of graphene-supported magnetic dimers, the carbon sheet must be deposited on a solid support. A properly selected substrate can, to a large extent, allow for the preservation of a large MAE of dimers.

articleTitle: Current-induced nonreciprocal dynamics and nonlinear Hall effect of a magnetic hopfion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A magnetic hopfion with torus-like spin structure hosts swirling emergent magnetic field and naturally gives rise to emergent magnetomultipoles. We show that the hopfion dynamics is determined by its emergent magnetomultipoles, specifically the emergent toroidal moment and the emergent magnetic octupole component. Under an ac driving current, the emergent multipoles give rise to intriguing hopfion dynamics via the spin transfer torque effect. When the current is applied along (perpendicular to) the hopfion’s symmetry axis, hopfion exhibits nonlinear nonreciprocal dynamics (nonlinear hopfion Hall effect) with corresponding translation and rotation mode. The nonreciprocity and nonlinear Hall angle can be controlled by the chirality and polarity of hopfion. These results provide an alternative approach for the potential implementation of hopfion in three-dimensional spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Study the Optimal Duty Cycle of a Coaxial Magnet for a Rotary Type Magnetic Refrigerator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In a design of rotary type magnetic refrigerator, a high field of coaxial magnet is desired . Typically, a high field design can be achieved with a small duty cycle which might not be optimized from the viewpoint of the thermal hydraulics of a magnetic refrigerator. Numerical simulation analysis of a coaxial magnet-designed using COMSOL program for rotary type active magnetic refrigeration (AMR) system has been performed for magnet structures based on neodymium-iron-boron permanent magnets. The AMR material considered was thin gadolinium plates. For a rotary type magnetic cooling system, from the thermal hydraulic point of view, the best duty cycle of coaxial magnet should be 50% if the magnetic field can be kept as constant during the period of duty cycles. However, the simulation calculation shows that a serious reduction of the magnetic field strength at higher duty cycles resulting in lower magnetic cooling efficiency. After considering the thermo-hydraulic part, the optimized duty cycle is around 30% if temperature drop is 10 K between hot and cold ends on a rotary type magnetic cooling system.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Soft Magnetic Powder/Epoxy Composite Sheet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper describes the development of a composite resin magnetic sheet of soft magnetic powder and epoxy resin used in the beyond 10MHz band magnetic devices. Magnetic powder and epoxy resin were mixed, dispersed and formed into a sheet shape by the bar coating method. Fe-Si based polycrystalline powder, Fe-Si-Cr based amorphous powder and Fe-Si-Nb-Cu-B based nanocrystalline powder with an average particle size of 3 μm were used as the soft magnetic powder. In addition, submicron Fe-Si-Cr based powder was used to further increase the packing density of the magnetic powder. As the evaluation of the magnetic sheet, saturation magnetization, coercivity, relative magnetic permeability and loss-tangent in 10MHz – hundreds MHz were measured. A magnetic sheet using the nanocrystalline powder and submicron powder showed high relative permeability of 13 and low loss-tangent of 0.05 at 100MHz.

articleTitle: A new method for emitting spin-polarized electron
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The development of field emission electron source is beneficial for its wide and important applications including material science, nanotechnology, biological, etc. in decades. In recent year, the research for "spin-polarized" field emission electron source have attracted much attention due to the development of spintronic devices creating more demands on the measurements of spin. In this report, a new method for emitting spin-polarized electron is provided greatly influencing the development of field emission source and being a rising research direction. The model of this method is that hybrid interfaces between magnetic and carbon materials are used as emission source. When charge current flows through a magnetized magnetic material, anomalous Hall effect occurs and spin current is provided flowing to the thin films of carbon material. Because of the excellent field emission property from the thin films of carbon material, the spin-polarized electrons are field-emitted to the vacuum environment. The spin-polarized field emission source can offer more effective, convenient and reliable spin-polarized measuring technologies from the interactions between samples such as diffraction, interference and scattering.

articleTitle: Importance of SAF Stability against Temperature and Magnetic Field in Automotive-Grade-1 STT-MRAM Wafer Electrical Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We investigate the automotive grade 1 temperature response of different MTJ stack designs based on the state-of-the-art GlobalFoundries 22FDX® Embedded-MRAM technology. An anomalous reference system reversal occurred in some devices as a response to external magnetic fields at operating temperatures as high as 150 °C. The strength of the external magnetic field, temperature and degree of magnetic moment mismatch of the synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF) reference system all affect the severity of the reference system’s instability. By careful stack optimization of the SAF reference system, the anomalous reversal was successfully suppressed in the investigated external magnetic field and temperature regime.

articleTitle: Demonstration of PtMn-based Field-free Switching SOT MRAM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In the group of Mn-based antiferromagnetic materials, PtMn shows high enough thermal stability to fit the requirement of high temperature in BEOL. We worked on a field-free switching device with the application of PtMn, which can be integrated into perpendicular MRAM stacks and processes of BEOL. With help from ferromagnetic coupling from SAF which is pinned by PtMn, we can get field-free switching, which can further increase the pillar size compared with traditional stray-field MRAM.

articleTitle: Magnetic Anisotropy Studies of FeyN Nanocrystals Embedded in GaN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Doping of GaN with Fe atoms above 0.4% concentration leads to crystallographic phase separation and to the self-assembly of Fe-rich nanocrystals (NCs) with stoichiometry and magnetic characteristics imposed by the growth conditions. Here, we report on the studies of magnetic anisotropy of GaδFeN layers with Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>N embedded nanocrystals controlled by strain engineering via Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf>N buffers with different Al concentration 0 ≤ x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Al</inf> ≤ 41%. Already for x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Al</inf> < 5% the structural properties: phase, shape, orientation - as well as the spatial distribution of the embedded NCs are modified in comparison to those of the NCs stabilized in GaδFeN on GaN. Our study shows that although the magnetic easy axis of the cubic γ’-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4−y</inf>N nanocrystals lies in-plane of the layer, the easy axis of hexagonal ε-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N NCs formed in all samples with x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Al</inf> > 0 coincides with the [0001] growth direction. This leads to a sizeable out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy and opens wide perspectives for perpendicular recording based on nitride-based magnetic nanocrystals. Our study yields the first direct determination of the temperature dependence of magnetocrystalline anisotropy parameter ε-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N.

articleTitle: Experimental and Theoretical Evaluation for Pressure Effects on Spin Hall Effect in Pt
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have experimentally evaluated the influence of pressure on the spin Hall effect for the Pt by using a laterally configured Pt/CoFeB hybrid nanostructure. Experimental results suggest that the spin Hall angle for the Pt is almost constant under the pressure up to 2 GPa. We have also developed the theoretical evaluation method for the pressure dependence of the spin Hall angle by using the first-principles calculation. The theoretical results also show the spin Hall angle for the Pt is insensitive to the pressure up to 75 GPa. These results imply that the enhanced spin Hall signal in the dynamical spin injection due to the pressure application is caused by the modification of the spin mixing conductance at the Pt/CoFeB interface.

articleTitle: Experimental assessment of the performances of an anisotropic magnetoresistive sensor after exposure to strong magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: On-chip magnetometers are already integrated within long-term implants such as cardiac implantable electronic devices. They are also good candidates to be integrated within the next generations of brain stimulation electrodes to provide their position and orientation. In all cases, long-term implants are expected to be at least certified as MRI conditional. We investigated the resilience to the exposure to 3 T and 7 T of an anisotropic magnetoresistive sensor integrating a set/reset function. The sensitivity, non-linearity, and offset of a batch of 63 identical sensors were not affected by the exposure. These preliminary results provide new insights on the usability of magnetoresistive sensors for biomedical applications requiring MRI conditionality.

articleTitle: Tuning the coercivity of permanent magnets by the combined effect of field angle and defect thickness
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A combined effect of defect thickness and externally applied field angle is studied for physics based modelling of coercivity. A single cubic grain with intrinsic properties of Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf> B surrounded by a soft magnetic defect is used. Finite element based micromagnetic modelling is used to compute coercivity and magnetic microstructural parameters. A novel magnetic reversal process is reported, which is primarily driven by defect thickness. This work provides implications for future work to design better grain boundary engineered permanent magnets for applications in green technologies.

articleTitle: Downsizing of High-Power Open-end Coil with Pure Water
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes an open-end coil using pure water to reduce the size of the high-power coupler used in the Inductive Power Transfer system. A conventional open-end coil tends to have larger size at lower operating frequency. On the other hand, the proposed open-end coil uses pure water with high dielectric constant to achieve lower operating frequency and higher power without changing the coil size. First, the features and structure of the proposed coil are described. Next, the proposed open-end coil is evaluated using the finite element method. The results show that a factor of about 1/3 reduces the operating frequency compared to the conventional type.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Torque Ripple Suppression Method Using Coriolis Force Generated by Electromagnetic Oscillatory Actuator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental system to verify the torque ripple suppression method using the Coriolis Force. The method of suppressing torque ripple is understood as the parametric excitation. The control logic of the experimental system uses zero-crossing detection of the pendulum angle to generate the parametric excitation. The effectiveness of the torque ripple suppression method is experimentally verified by suppressing the vibration of an elastic pendulum using a solenoid actuator.

articleTitle: Antiferromagnetic Tunnel Junctions for Spintronics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Antiferromagnetic (AFM) spintronics has emerged as a subfield of spintronics, where the AFM Néel vector is used as a state variable.
