An efficient electric control and detection of the Néel vector are critical for device applications. This invited talk features an AFM tunnel junction (AFMTJ) as a spintronic device where such control and detection can be realized. The critical requirement for efficient AFMTJs is AFM electrodes exhibiting a spin-split Fermi surface and thus momentum-dependent spin polarization. Such AFMTJs can support a giant tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) effect exceeding that in conventional magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs). In addition, the AFMTJs can generate sizable spin-transfer torques (STTs) capable of Néel vector switching. Overall, AFMTJs have potential to become a new standard for spintronic devices providing a few orders of magnitude faster switching speed than conventional MTJs.

articleTitle: A new class of ferromagnetic semiconductors and quantum heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To integrate ferromagnetism and topological properties into mainstream semiconductors is highly challenging but potentially useful for new ultralow-power electronics and topological quantum computing. By doping Fe in narrow-gap III-V semiconductors such as InAs, GaSb and InSb using molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), we realized a new class of N-type and P-type ferromagnetic semiconductors (FMSs) with high Curie temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> > 300 K) for the first time. Furthermore, heterostructures of these new Fe-doped FMSs exhibit various new phenomena such as giant proximity magnetoresistance and odd-parity magnetoresistance, all induced by a long-range magnetic proximity effect. These results suggest that the Fe-doped III-V FMSs are promising materials for high-performance spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Research and Analysis of Toroidal and Conventional Windings in permanent magnet synchronous machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The winding arrangement has an important impact on the performance of permanent magnet synchronous machine According to the characteristics of the toroidal and tooth-coil windings, the phase relationship of the two winding forms is analyzed, and the accuracy of the analysis is verified by the finite element method. In view of the combined use of the two windings, the calculation method of the winding factor and the law of the winding factor considering the harmonic weakening ability are studied. Finally, the method of improving the machine performance by using different combinations of the both windings is researched.

articleTitle: Ferromagnetic resonance hysteresis in hybrid magnetic trilayers with combined in-plane and perpendicular magnetic anisotropies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We present an experimental study on hybrid magnetic systems based on hardmagnetic NdCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> films with weak perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, which are dipolar coupled to a softmagnetic layer with in-plane magnetic anisotropy, such as permalloy, via a nonmagnetic Al spacer. Using broadband ferromagnetic resonance, we have investigated the magnetization dynamics in this sample system, which exhibits a host of unique magnetic properties including a frequency hysteresis. We provide an explanation for the origin of this hysteresis, which is intimately related to the regular magnetic hysteresis, by accounting for the switching between acoustic and optical resonances, that naturally occur in unsaturated systems with different magnetic domains. Our model is ultimately supported by a simple expression relating the frequency difference between these two types of modes at their transition field to the periodicity of the stripe domain pattern imprinted into the permalloy film. Moreover, we show that these unique features in the FMR spectra can also be observed when substituting the ferromagnetic metal permalloy for a ferrimagnetic insulator such as yttrium iron garnet.

articleTitle: Complex shaped magnets for an efficient use of rare earths in synchro-reluctant machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In order to maximize the torque of Permanent Magnet assisted Synchronous Reluctance (PMaSynRel) machines, sintered magnets should ideally exhibit curved shapes. Standard process fails to produce such geometries without large critical material loss during machining. The Powder Injection Molding technique has been assessed in this work as an efficient process for producing complex shaped magnets while minimizing the environmental impacts and improving the recyclability of end-of-life products. A case study suited for the automotive sector is presented.

articleTitle: Control of Information Flow in Arrays of Spin-Torque Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Arrays of spin-torque oscillators (STOs) can be used in neural networks. Adjacent STOs can be synchronised via magnetostatic interactions. In this work we show that by varying the diameter of the STOs it is possible to control the flow of information. Unidirectional information flows can be enabled by a consistent change in diameter along a row of STOs. A switch to control the direction of information flow can be constructed using rows of STOs with different diameters.

articleTitle: Analysis of A New Bidirectional Field Modulation Machine with Separated Type PM Excitation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, a new bidirectional field modulation machine with separated type PM excitation (STPM-BFMM) is proposed and analyzed. The STPM on rotor is composed of one external PM and two internal PMs, which a surface mounted PM is divided into three pieces along the radial centerline and circumferential centerlines. The external and internal PMs can form a triangle PM excitation for flux concentrated effect. The magnetic fields excited by STPM and stator-PM are modulated by stator teeth and rotor teeth, respectively, for high torque production. Then, the electromagnetic performances of STPM-BFMM with different slot-pole combinations are analyzed using finite element analysis (FEA), back electromotive force, cogging torque, and steady torque at rated state. The FEA-calculated results show that the 12-slot/10-pole STPM-BFMM performs high torque density with low torque ripple.

articleTitle: Monitoring Ionic Diffusion from CoB in Molecular layers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have studied the thermal diffusion of Boron in C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf>/CoB/C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf> trilayers using Polarised Neutron Reflectometry (PNR). Monitoring the diffusion of boron in carbon is a difficult problem using electron or X-ray based techniques. On the other hand, boron can be easily detected in neutron spectroscopy due to its strong absorbance. Comparing PNR measurements taken before and after in-situ annealing for 10 hours at 300°C shows significant changes in the nuclear and magnetic structure. Fits to the data suggest that Boron migrates from the CoB alloy into and through the adjacent 20nm C60 layers and aggregates at the very top and bottom interfaces of the trilayer. This demonstrates ionic diffusion in a fullerene layer, suggests that molecular thin films may be used for ionic-control of magnetism and as ionic reservoirs in ultra-thin electrical devices.

articleTitle: Unconventional Emergent Hall Effect Phenomena and its Modification in a van der Waals Ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The discovery of two-dimensional (2D) magnetic van der Waals (vdW) materials and the stabilization of magnetic order down to the monolayer limit have ushered in a new venture, important from a fundamental viewpoint leading to development of novel spintronics devices. 2D vdW ferromagnet (FM) Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>GeTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (FGT) is an interesting candidate owing to high Curie temperature, uniaxial magnetic anisotropy, and realization of an unconventional chiral magnetic ground state. Here, we investigate an unexplored route towards manipulation of the exotic ground state of FGT via chemical doping at the magnetic (Fe) and non-magnetic (Ge) site of (Fe,Co)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(Ge,As)Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Interestingly, Cobalt (Co) and Arsenic (As) doping results in an unconventional Hall effect whose strength can be considerably modified by increasing concentration, arising from emergent electromagnetic behaviour from underlying complicated spin configurations.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Two-Dimensional Magneto-Static Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A physics-informed neural network (PINN) for solving two-dimensional (2D) magneto-static fields is proposed. The magnetic field intensity and the magnetic vector potential are solved using a neural network. The computation of the spatial derivatives of media constitutive parameters, which negatively impacts the training of PINN, is eliminated. The proposed PINN is verified in a 2D magneto-static case study by comparing its results with those of a finite element method. It is expected that this work will promote applications of PINN in the numerical analysis of electromagnetic devices and systems.

articleTitle: Passive Components for Advancement of Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents the necessity of miniaturization and high efficiency of transformers and inductors used in power electronics equipment, and the research topics necessary to realize this. Firstly, the difference in electrical circuit theory between transformers and inductors used in power electronics equipment is explained, and the characteristics required for the magnetic materials used in each is be explained. In the next, we show that the Steinmetz equation, a well-known loss description method for magnetic materials, may not be suitable for accurate loss calculations of magnetic cores of transformers and inductors used in power electronic circuits. In order to solve these problems, we introduce the loss map method and the accurate iron loss measurement method developed by the authors, and show some calculation examples to prove their validity.

articleTitle: Analysis of Efficiency Maps of Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this contribution the efficiency maps of synchronous machines are analyzed. The tool developed to draw these efficiency maps allows considering the synchronous machines electromagnetic parameters and related losses. It will be exploited to analyze the effects of the different parameters on the efficiency maps. The developed tool is based on the synchronous machines electrical circuits models in the Park’s referential frame. The adopted modeling approach allows considering all types of classical synchronous machines: wound field synchronous machines, permanent magnet synchronous machines, hybrid excited synchronous machines and synchronous reluctance machines. It can even indirectly consider the effect of magnetic saturation. These analyses will help identify parameters sets allowing optimizing the energy efficiency of synchronous machines for a given application, as electrical traction.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Noise Suppression Sheet Embedded in Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To provide a solution for future electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues in highly densified electronic circuits in which electric components and its interconnections are integrated in proximity, effectivity of integration of noise suppression sheet (NSS) inside printed circuit boards (PCB) was investigated. For this purpose, NSSs compatible to PCB embedding was fabricated, and noise suppression performance of PCB integrated NSSs was evaluated systematically. Using newly proposed measurement jig to imitate PCB embedded NSS, mitigation of conduction noise was observed. NSSs were also embedded in PCBs used in actual product, and validity of PCB integrated NSS for the mitigation of radiation noise was also observed around the frequency range of 700MHz to 1GHz which is widely used for telecommunications.

articleTitle: NV center-coupled Magnetoelastic Waves: Modelling and Experiment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Surface acoustic waves have been shown to be a power efficient technique for exciting magnetic dynamics in thin films, and such dynamics have been shown to couple efficiently to the Nitrogen-vacancy defect center in diamond. However, prior demonstrations have operated in nonlinear regimes, and are poorly modelled and understood. In this work, we show that SAW-driven dynamics can directly drive the NV-center resonance, and propose a model for the mechanism of interaction with randomly oriented NV ensembles.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Laser Induced Magnetization Switching in Amorphous TbCo and the Role of Element Specific Damping on HI-AOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The optical control of magnetization has immense importance in high-speed low-power data storage applications. The present study focuses on the optical control of magnetization using linearly polarized ultrashort laser pulses. Here, we demonstrate the Helicity Independent All-Optical Switching(HI-AOS) in TbCo RE-TM Alloys with the help of the Atomistic Spin Dynamics Calculations. The Tb composition is varied from 18% to 36% and the possibility of HI-AOS is investigated by applying a wide range of input laser fluences. The results show that HI-AOS is possible for the range of composition 20% to 32%. Further, an element specific damping is applied to both Tb and Co sublattices to illustrate the role of the damping parameter on HI-AOS.

articleTitle: Universal Set of Magnon-Mediated Quantum Gates
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We propose a universal set of magnon-mediated quantum gates applied to a hybrid quantum system of mutually noninteracting qubits coupled to an ancilla magnonic mode. The gates are realized through dynamic manipulation of the frequency of the magnon mode and control of its initial state, without directly changing any qubit parameters. We present protocols for arbitrary single-qubit gates and two-qubit controlled phase gate, which together form a universal set and can be combined to perform any unitary transformation on the qubit subsystem. Our results demonstrate principal possibility of realizing a universal quantum computer controlled solely through manipulation of magnon-qubit interactions.

articleTitle: Study of interplay between magnetic/electric fields and Cr-doped effect in Mo1-xCrxSe2 (x=0, 0.5) nanosheet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The Cr-doped effects on 2D MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanosheet and the interplay between external magnetic and electric fields are studied. The MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> changes its magnetism from diamagnetism to paramagnetism as Cr ions substitute the Mo ones. Vacancies at the Mo site in pure MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> also result in the paramagnetism below 10 K. A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1g</inf> mode of Raman spectra display two at characteristic temperatures, 150 K (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>) and 210 (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>) for x=0, and 180 K (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>') and 260 K (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>') for x=0.5. All of the anomalies disappear as an external magnetic field is applied. This observation implies that the two abnormalities at A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1g</inf> mode correlated to the magnetic fields but were irreverent to the interplane distance. A similar effect does not find when an external electric field is subject to the Cr-doped sample, but the peak width of pure MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> will gradually broaden as the external electric field increases and will not narrow down again as removed the field. These observations imply that the smaller Cr ions reduce the interplane distance and enhance the coupling strength along the c-axis. This effect resists the influence of an external electric field and increases the characteristic temperatures in A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1g</inf> mode.

articleTitle: An Electroplated Magnetic NiFe Film Based Electromagnetic Targeting for Interlocking-Nail Broken-Bone Surgery
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report a novel interlocking nail onto which magnetic NiFe film is electroplated, for electromagnetic targeting system for screw-hole locating in interlocking-nail broken-bone surgery. The system consists of a C-shaped silicon steel core with emitting and pick-up coils, an intramedullary interlocking nail which the high-permeable magnetic NiFe is electroplated onto two locations of the nail, and measurement electronics. An AC voltage is applied to the emitting coil to generate an AC magnetic flux. Subsequently, by electromagnetic-induction, an AC voltage signal is induced in the pick-up coil. When the electroplated nail is moved axially or rotated in air-gap between the emitting and pick-up coils, the AC magnetic flux between them is affected, resulting in a change in the output voltage of the pick-up coil. This voltage change is further analyzed to determine the location and orientation of the screw holes. Based on this principle, we fabricated above parts and conducted targeting test (also an adhesion/scratching test). According to results, axial and angular targeting errors are 1 mm and 9.5°, respectively. Also, the electroplated film shows an acceptable against-scratching property.

articleTitle: Achieving 2.8 T coercivity in Nd-Fe-B sintered magnets subjected to DyCu and PrCu grain boundary diffusion process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: There has been a concern about the over-consumption of scarce and expensive heavy rare-earth elements (HREs), such as Dy and Tb, in achieving high coercivity in Nd-Fe-B magnets. This work reports an approach to achieve a high coercivity of 2.8 T by sequentially diffusing Dy<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">70</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</inf> and Pr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">68</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">32</inf> eutectic alloys in fine-grained sintered magnets fabricated by a press-less process. The coercivity of 2.8 T was achieved for its low Dy content of only 0.9 wt.%. The Pr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">68</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">32</inf> diffusion facilitated the infiltration of Dy towards the center of the magnets, resulting in uniform Dy-rich shell formation in the whole sample. Such a unique shell structure increased the anisotropy field of the shell to realize the 2.8 T coercivity.

articleTitle: Challenges to High Magnetic Flux Density and Low Loss Magnetic Materials and Devices for Next-Generation Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: High-saturation magnetic flux density and low iron loss soft magnetic materials as passive components in modern power-electronics systems has attracted much attention due to the compelling global demand of carbon neutrality. For this purpose, many elemental studies on iron loss have been undergone, such as multi-dimensional iron loss map, iron loss component analysis, broad-band iron loss measurement, data science driven material development, and so on. In this paper, our recent results on iron loss analyses and material developments are introduced.

articleTitle: Discrete Anomalous Hall Resistance-based Quantized Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spintronic devices have shown promise for energy-efficient storage and neuromorphic computing. In this abstract, we present the realization of a spintronic device exhibiting discrete anomalous Hall resistance states. We attribute this discrete resistance behavior to the magnetic domain wall pinning and depinning and gradual switching of different magnetic layers. The number of resistance states is a function of the temperature. Furthermore, this discrete resistance behavior of the device allows us to employ these resistance states as weights in a quantized convolutional neural network. The network is trained and tested on the CIFAR-10 data set and the system achieves an accuracy of around 86.95%.

articleTitle: Semi-analytical modeling for linear motors with conductive media in high-dynamic applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Linear motors in high-dynamic applications contain conductive surfaces which generate losses and parasitic forces due to eddy-currents. While FEA models can be implemented to estimate these effects accurately, longer computing time makes them unfavorable for a parametric analysis of the motor. Therefore, a computationally faster and accurate tool using semi-analytical techniques is developed for a linear motor delivering high-dynamic motion. One such example is a superconducting linear motor. To produce a reliable and cost-effective design, it is considered to house the superconducting coils in a conduction-cooled assembly with several conductive media to operate at a cryogenic temperature. However, cooling efficiency at this temperature is low and therefore, accurate estimation of the eddy-current losses is crucical for an economical design of the motor. The modeling technique is applied to a benchmark model of such a motor, delivering high-dynamic motion. When compared to FEA, the method shows a major improvement in computation speed with a relative error in instantenous loss and force under 3%. For these reasons, the developed method is suitable for a parameteric analysis of the motor.

articleTitle: Sub-Harmonic Synchronous Machine Using a Dual Inverter and a Unique Three-Layer Stator Winding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A dual inverter sub-harmonic synchronous machine having a distinct three-layer stator winding topology is presented. The two inverters provide two sets of balanced three-phase currents to the three-layer stator winding. These three-layer windings are arranged in such a way that they can generate both fundamental and sub-harmonic magnetomotive force. Furthermore, the fundamental MMF component of this machine is four times the sub-harmonic MMF component used for the brushless operation. In contrast, the subharmonic magnetomotive force is used for field excitation, which leads to brushless operation. An 8-pole 48-slot 2-inverter 3-layer subharmonic machine is designed to validate the concept through a 2-D finite element analysis of this new topology, showing a better overall torque profile and performance.

articleTitle: Magnetic Hammer Testing with Tunnel Magnetoresistive Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: For the nondestructive inspection for infrastructures required both high accuracy and energy conservation, the tunnel magneto-resistive (TMR) sensors with high sensitivity have the potential to meet the requirements. In this study, the magnetic hammer test (MHT) technique was developed using TMR sensors that detect very weak magnetic signals generated by the eigen-oscillation of steels. TMR sensor detected the weak signals below 1 nT by natural vibration and the size of steel plates was accurately evaluated from the eigen-frequency. In addition, a finite element method (FEM) simulation analysis was conducted to confirm the validity of experimental results. We concluded that the MHT technique using TMR sensors can be applied to a novel nondestructive inspection for detecting small fractures and corrosion in steel materials.

articleTitle: Design and Performance of a Compact 3D-Printed Magnetorheological Fluid Damper
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, a magnetorheological fluids (MRF) was encapsulated in a compact 3D-printed fluid damper, and the field-dependent mechanical properties, such as stiffness and damping, of the MRF damper were experimentally evaluated. To this end, an MRF prepared with 40% volume fraction of iron particles and silicone oil was injected into the 3D-printed Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) encapsulant with elastic thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) compression layer. A fluid channel was fabricated between the top and bottom reservoirs and a field-induced magnetorheological (MR) effect was controlled in the channel, resulting in enhanced stiffness and damping. The bottom side adjacent to the bottom reservoir has a circular opening and a membrane was bonded to its perimeter so that the pressurized MRF could flow and be accumulated in the lower reservoir. An external magnetic field (i.e., 0 and 32 kA/m) was applied to the 3D-printed MRF damper at the time of a uniaxial dynamic test. The 3D-printed MRF damper was characterized via force-displacement tests at a 2.5 mm/sec displacement rate. The effect of the channel and accumulator on the mechanical properties of the 3D-printed MRF damper was investigated.

articleTitle: External bias field control of skyrmion dynamics in a magnetic nanotrack
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Evolution and tunable control of skyrmion dynamics in a magnetic nanotracks are crucial for the next generation skyrmion based racetrack memory (RM) devices. Here, using micromagnetic simulation we present the precise control of skyrmion motion in a magnetic nanotrack consisting of three narrow and a wider nanochannels under the influence of spin transfer torque (STT) and out of plane bias field. We find that the application of out of plane magnetic field results in efficient conversion of Domain wall (DW) pair to skyrmion as well as assists in achieving the uniform velocity of each skyrmion. Importantly, the thorough analysis of individual and total energy terms during the DW pair to skyrmion conversion provides in-depth insight into the role of bias field in overcoming the pinning potential present at the junction of the narrow and wide nanochannel. The precise control of skyrmion motion stabilized from a DW pair under the influence of external bias field is significantly important for the development of skyrmion based memory devices.

articleTitle: Parameter Analysis and Multilevel Design Optimization of a Permanent Magnet Claw Pole Machine with Hybrid Cores
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The permanent magnet claw pole machine (PMCPM) with hybrid cores investigated in this paper is a new claw pole machine (CPM) with the modular design where its stator is composed of stator yoke made by silicon sheet and stator claw pole teeth made by soft magnetic composites (SMC). As the PMCPM is with very complex 3D structure and there is a great number of design parameter needs to be determined, optimizing the PMCPM is very time consuming and using the traditional multilevel optimization strategy (MOS) is an effective way. In this paper, the parametric analysis is proposed as a pre-design to the MOS, and a parameter-oriented grouping (POG) method based on parameter analysis is proposed to improve the optimization speed of MOS. Specifically, the objectives and design parameters are streamlined and grouped by using inter-objective correlation analysis (CA), parameter-to-objective sensitivity analysis (SA), and inter-parameter correlation analysis (RA) method, then the MOS is performed based on the parameter analysis results. The traditional MOS method are employed for the benchmark comparison, and the effectiveness of the proposed MOS based on POG is verified by the experiment.

articleTitle: Skyrmion vs. antiskyrmion Hall angles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We observe significant, 6.5% - 12%, differences between skyrmion and antiskyrmion Hall angles in existing experimental data. To account for them, the Thiele equation is generalized with the transverse velocity component in the collective coordinate of magnetization vector. The corresponding generalized Hall angle is formulated, and its consequences are compared to the data. A plausible physical origin is provided for explaining the Hall angle differences.

articleTitle: Ion Irradiation Effects on Crystal Structure and Magnetic Properties of Iron-Nickel Binary Alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Iron-based alloys are used widely in the structural components of fission and fusion reactors. Since the change in magnetic properties during neutron irradiation can cause harmful effects on the components, the irradiation effects on magnetism and their mechanisms merit attention. This study focuses on the role of structural and magnetic phase stabilities and investigates the effects of ion irradiation on the magnetic properties of Fe- x%Ni <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(x=16,24,29$</tex> and 36) films. After 2. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\text{MeV Cu}^{2+}$</tex> irradiation up to 0.9 dpa, an increase in saturation magnetization occurs in FCC Fe-29<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>Ni film, but almost no effects appear in the other specimens. This relates to the structural and the magnetic instabilities of the alloys.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Wide-bandwidth Actuator for Haptic Controller with Novel Magnetic Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This study proposes a new actuator for a haptic controller that has a wider bandwidth than that of the prototype. The acceleration on the dummy jig of the prototype is analyzed using the electromagnetic-mechanical coupling method and verified using the experimental results. Several new designs have been proposed to provide higher accelerations on the dummy jig and a wider bandwidth. The new magnetic circuit, called the sandwich structure, includes one top plate, two permanent magnets, and two yokes. Response surface methodology is employed to perform the optimal analysis to find the maximum force factor while maintaining a magnet volume similar to that of the prototype. The predicted values (force factor and magnet volume) are confirmed by analysis results of the optimal type. Compared with the prototype, the optimal type has a higher force factor (77.74%) and 417.24% improvement in bandwidth with the same outer dimensions.

articleTitle: Broadband Integrated Magneto-Optical Isolators on Silicon Nitride Platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report ultra-broadband integrated magneto-optical isolators on silicon nitride platforms based on the dispersion compensation method. The device achieved 2.7 dB insertion loss with 29 nm (3.48 THz) 20-dB isolation bandwidth.

articleTitle: Simple design for magnetic field energy harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a simple design for magnetic field energy harvesting. Drawbacks of the free-stand harvester are the limitation of the harvesting power and production cost. Although several researchers proposed magnetic core designs with a magnetic concentration technique, it makes the production cost high. First, the simple design of the harvester is explained with three key points. According to the previous reports, the target value of magnetic field to be harvested is set to 7 μT at 50 Hz. Example values of the estimated harvesting power and induced voltage are 5.57 mW and 7.84 V, respectively. This simple design could be the mass production cost in low.

articleTitle: The transition from soft to hard exchange bias and oscillation of biasing field with the variation of IrMn thickness
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The exchange bias (EB) in thin films with compensated AFM-FM interfaces is explained at the microscopic level with the support of experimental results. In the article, we varied the thickness of IrMn deposited above Co and have observed that, for small thickness the system has shown soft EB and as the thickness increases the EB has shown oscillation nature. As the thickness increases, the soft EB has transformed into hard EB. Also for the AFM deposited below the FM layer, the soft EB has enhanced by 5 times (20 Oe to 100 Oe).

articleTitle: Power and Phase Profiles in Nano-constriction Based Synchronized Spin Hall Nano-oscillators near Threshold Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) demonstrate self-sustained magnetization auto-oscillations, that have recently received much attention due to their potential for cutting-edge applications. In this work, the power and phase profiles, i.e., the complex quantized propagation dynamics of nano-constriction-based spin hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) near the threshold current have been investigated. The SHNO generates a 12 GHz microwave frequency upon application of 2 mA direct current in presence of a 0.6 T external bias magnetic field. Power profile reveals that spin wave (SW) modes are quantized along x-axis. The phase profile reveals a complex nature of the SW modes at the dominant frequency (mostly localised at the nano-constriction region and additionally propagates from centre to the edges). Whereas SW mode of other frequencies mostly propagate towards the edge from the central nano-constriction region having a complex spiral nature. The SHNO devices, which are operational at high-frequencies, can be useful in energy-efficient tuneable microwave oscillators and neuromorphic computing.

articleTitle: Toward Low Soft Error Sensitivity and Latency Near Memory Computing with EB MRAM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic random-access memory (MRAM) suffers from reliability issues subject to the harsh industrial environment and applications with limited hardware resources. Thus, we propose the new spin-orbit torque MRAM (SOT-MRAM) scheme called exchange bias (EB) MRAM for error-tolerant application. EB MRAM enhances reliability from its immunity to external magnetic and higher endurance. In addition, this paper presents near-memory computing (NMC) with EB MRAM to further achieve low soft error sensitivity and latency implementation. In the proposed scheme, the NMC controller exploits the accelerated design to reduce data movement, and EB MRAM as the computation memory is performed with subword-level compression. The experimental results show that the access time and energy of EB MRAM is only 0.9ns and 0.113pJ/bit while the data compressed rate is up to 75% with 2.05% loss over the state-of-the-art designs.

articleTitle: Helicity-Dependent Terahertz Emission from a Weyl Semimetal Mn3Sn
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, we present the experimental observation of helicity-dependent ultrafast photocurrents in a Mn3Sn film using optical pump-Terahertz emission spectroscopy. The magnitude and direction of photocurrents depend on the polarisation of the pump pulse and the optical incidence angle, but have no dependence on the magnetic field. We combine experimental results with a thorough symmetry analysis to argue that the helicity-dependent photocurrents arise predominantly from the circular photon drag effect.

articleTitle: Band engineering of magnetic semiconductors by phosphorus doping
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Impact of P and Mn incorporation into GaAs layers on their electronic- and band-structures as well as their magnetic and structural properties has been studied. A set of the homogenous (Ga,Mn)(P,As) layers with 8% of Mn and 0-32% of P contents of high structural perfection have been grown by the low-temperature molecular-beam epitaxy technique. Post-growth annealing treatment of the layers results in an improvement of their structural and magnetic properties and an increase in the hole concentration in the layers. Hard-x-ray angular-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (HARPES) reveals that a strongly dispersing band crosses the Fermi energy in the highly doped samples. This is a consequence of the high concentration of Mn-induced itinerant holes residing in the valence band of the III-V semiconductor host. We find an increased density of states near the Fermi level for higher doping levels, which one may attribute to additional localized Mn states. The spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) results confirmed the modification of the valence band of the epitaxial layers.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of the Magnetic and Magnetotransport Properties of FINEMET Thin Magnetic Wires
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A comparative analysis of the magnetic and magnetotransport properties of FINEMET glass-coated, glass-removed, and cold-drawn microwires subjected to various stresses is presented. Major differences are noticed between their magnetic properties, depending on the preparation method and microwire diameter. The effect of the applied tensile force on the evolution of the magnetic permeability, coercivity, and magnetoimpedance response was analyzed, considering also the stresses induced during preparation, their relief following annealing and the annealing-induced structural transformations. The coercivity dependence on applied force is more sensitive in the glass-removed microwires, while the magnetic permeability and magnetoimpedance dependence on applied force is found to be more significant in the cold-drawn samples. The results of this comparative analysis will enable an enhanced material selection process for various applications in miniaturized magnetic and stress sensors with increased sensitivity.

articleTitle: Effective Performance Improvement Designs of a Hybrid Permanent-Magnet-Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: By inserting ferrite magnets into the rotor of a synchronous reluctance motor (SynRM), it is expected that the related operational performance of this motor can be improved. However, for those SynRMs with a higher number of poles, the rotor physical spaces for flux path adjustments and performance improvements are restricted. An assessment index is proposed to evaluate the volume of the optimal magnets based on the specified operational objectives and structural constraints, with the manufacturing convenience considered. In addition, to enhance the motor performance with more fluxes passing through the rotor available spaces by combining with the spoke-type NdFeB permanent magnets, a hybrid permanent-magnet-assisted SynRM structure is proposed.

articleTitle: Low-Coercivity Perpendicular Spin Transfer Torque Magnetic Tunnel Junctions as Nanoscale Magnetic Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents the use of the spin transfer torque effect in perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions to operate the devices as magnetic sensors. The junctions, specifically designed for sensing applications exhibit close to low-coercivity, allowing the sensitivity to be as high as 25 mV/mT for a large dynamic range of 20 mT. In addition, the junctions have diameters ranging from 20 to 100 nanometers, making them among the smallest magnetic sensing elements ever reported to our knowledge. A single operational amplifier operates the junction and outputs a voltage proportional to the external magnetic field. This paper opens the way to a monolithic integration of both the conditioning electronics and the perpendicular magnetic tunnel junction.

articleTitle: Spin Hall Switching Enabled by Uniaxial In-Plane Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, we examine spin-orbit-torque magnetic random-access-memory (SOT-MRAM) devices stabilized by in-plane uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy, enabling switching without shape constraints or external fields. We investigate the interaction between uniaxial in-plane anisotropy and the spin-Hall effect in this device – an interaction whose fundamental behavior is currently unknown. We examine switching behavior by performing time-resolved simulations based on the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation, and find strong and tunable dependence on the polarization angle of the incoming spin current, as well as boundaries between stochastic and deterministic switching. Furthermore, we demonstrate an extension of this concept to enable out-of-plane field-free switching.

articleTitle: Axis-Shifted Machines with Hybrid Rotors Considering Forward and Reverse Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, a permanent synchronous machine with hybrid rotors is designed to increase the torque density of the machine. The hybrid rotor consists of two axially parallel parts. One provides the reluctance torque of the machine and the other increases the permanent magnet torque of the machine. By offsetting the permanent magnet torque part of the hybrid rotor, the permanent magnet torque and reluctance torque of the machine is maximized at the same current angle so that the total electromagnetic torque is increased significantly. A slider was further added to the hybrid rotor to improve the reverse rotation torque performance. By using the slider, the electromagnetic torque in the forward operation conditions is further strengthened, and the reverse torque is also improved with at all current angles. Finally, by using finite element analysis, it is found that the proposed hybrid rotor structure with slide is capable of providing better torque performances in both forward and reverse operations compared to the traditional interior rotor.

articleTitle: Impact of Pulse Amplitude on Voltage-Driven Precessional Switching Dynamics Using Macrospin Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In Voltage-Controlled Magnetic Anisotropy (VCMA) switching of magnetic random-access memory (MRAM), the precessional dynamics of the magnetization is behind the writing mechanism. This work aims to give a fundamental understanding of VCMA-induced precessional switching dynamics through macrospin modeling. We start investigating the effects of different voltage pulse amplitude and pulse shapes on the precessional dynamics of the magnetization. We show that high voltage does not necessarily result in a faster and a more consistent switching and that adding a few hundreds of picoseconds ramp times will have an important impact on the switching dynamics and its final state. Moreover, we perform the analysis considering two damping parameters, an unrealistically high Gilbert damping parameter for CoFeB thin films (α = 0.2) and a realistic parameter for CoFeB (α = 0.01), showing how they impact the precession dynamics.

articleTitle: Enhanced tunneling electroresistance effect by interface engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A high and stable tunneling electroresistance (TER) effect is critical for the storage application of multiferroic tunnel junctions (MFTJs). A large interface dipole can significantly modulate the effective barrier height, producing metallic-insulating transition of barrier, which can be used to obtain a high TER effect. Our first-principles calculations of Co-TiO2-(BaO-TiO2)m-CoO-Co (m = 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) MFTJ [1], Co-(TiO2-BaO)m-Co MFTJ [2] and Co2MnSi/BaTiO3/SrRuO3 MFTJs [3] demonstrate that the large interface dipole can be obtained by means of interface oxidation or designing interfaces with large difference in ionic radius. And the TER effect can indeed be greatly enhanced through the large interface dipole. These provide guidance for further improving TER effect through the interface engineering. (Note: These three works have been published in references [1] - [3].)

articleTitle: Coupled Field–Circuit Modeling and Analysis for Interturn Short-Circuit Faults in an Onboard Traction Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Onboard traction transformers are essential electrical equipment in high-speed railway systems, and their interturn faults can seriously threaten the safety of rail transportation. In this digest, a coupled field–circuit model of an onboard traction transformer with interturn short-circuit (ITSC) faults is built, in which the magnetic field is calculated together with the external circuit through transient data exchange. Moreover, a cybernetic arc model is adopted for the simulation of the time-varying conductance of the fault arc, and the effect of the traction rectifier control system is also considered in the circuit domain. As a study case, a typical 6.5 MVA/25 kV onboard traction transformer on a China Railway Highspeed (CRH)-1 electric multiple unit (EMU) was modeled and simulated in a 25 kV traction system. With fault occurrence, the flux distribution is markedly distorted, and the short-circuit current reaches 7.8 kA at its maximum. The proposed method and representative findings enrich fundamental studies on the internal faults of the onboard traction transformers.

articleTitle: Magnetic Domain Observation of Milled Nanocrystalline Alloy Powder
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Fe-based nanocrystalline alloys have high magnetic flux density and low loss. So, in this study, the magnetic domain structure of ball-milled magnetic powders of these nanocrystalline alloys was observed using a Kerr effect microscope. The effect of strain removal heat treatment on the magnetic properties of the powder was also investigated by observing and comparing the magnetic domain structure of the milled powder before and after heat treatment during the preparation process of the nanocrystalline milled powder. Our findings showed that the strain removal heat treatment changed the size and shape of the magnetic domains to a simple structure. In addition, the magnetic wall motion was found to occur quickly, resulting in soft magnetic properties.

articleTitle: Magnetic imaging by the anomalous Nernst effect using atomic force microscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report a method to visualize magnetic domains based on the anomalous Nernst effect in a nanowire of Co2MnGa using atomic force microscopy. The touching AFM tip creates a temperature gradient in the sample, whereby the generated voltage due to the anomalous Nernst effect is measured by lock-in technique. Our method works at room temperature and atmosphere with a high spatial resolution on the magnetic domain compared to similar techniques.

articleTitle: Interpretation of spin-wave modes in Co/Ag nanodot arrays probed by broadband ferromagnetic resonance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) and the measurement of magnetization dynamics in general have become sophisticated tools for the study of magnetic systems at the nanoscale. In this work, we present a detailed investigation of Co/Ag nanodots with a 200 nm diameter arranged in a square pitch array with a periodicity of 400 nm, which, due to their size, can support standing spin-wave modes with complex spectral responses. To interpret the experimentally measured broadband FMR, we compare the spectra of the nanoarray structure with those of the unpatterned Co/Ag film of identical thickness, which serves as a baseline for obtaining the general magnetic parameters of the system. Using state-of-the-art simulations of the dynamic response to identify the nature of the excitation modes allows us to assess the boundary conditions for the nanodots. We then proceed to calculate the spectral response of our system, for which we obtained good agreement. A full description of the theoretical framework and its application to our system is provided and the novel frequency domain, matrix-free simulation method used is described in detail.

articleTitle: Magnetic study of Cobalt three dimensional nanonetworks: First Order Reversal Curves, hysteresis loops and first magnetization curves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Three-Dimensional (3D) magnetic nanostructures will be the next generation of functional magnetic nanostructured metamaterials. In this work, we report some of our recent results on the synthesis and characterization of different interconnected Co nanowires forming a dense and ordered magnetic system: Co 3D Nanowire Networks (3DNN). The 3DNN presents anisotropic magnetic responses. We used first magnetization curves, hysteresis loops, and first order reversal curves techniques to characterize the systems, which provide information about the key magnetic properties of the 3D nanostructure.

articleTitle: Magnetism meet microelectromechanical systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The integration of magnetic materials in conventional micro electromechanical systems (MEMS) is becoming a hot topic for various applications. Integrated micromagnets are used for magnetic actuation or energy harvesting, due to the sizable forces they allow to produce on movable parts without friction. On the other hand, movable micromagnets can be exploited for reconfiguring the functionalities of integrated magnetic devices exposed to their stray field. Soft magnetic layers are instead used to confine or create magnetic field gradients to be used for sensing applications. In this talk I'll present three specific applications (i) the realization of MEMS magnetometers based on magnetic microresonators interacting with the gradient of a magnetic field produced by a magnetic flux concentrator or a superconductive coil, (ii) the implementation of a magnetic plucking technology for frequency up-conversion in energy harvester and (iii) the development of hybrid magnonic-MEMS devices where the bias field for the propagation of spin waves in spin-textures is provided by some movable micromagnets integrated in a MEMS.

articleTitle: A Novel Magnetic-Geared Motor Combining Magnetic Gear and SR Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A direct-drive permanent magnet (PM) motor and a conventional magnetic-geared motor have the advantage of high torque density. Therefore, these motors are expected to be applied as in-wheel motors for electric vehicles (EVs). However, they have a problem that it is difficult to achieve the wide speed-torque characteristics required for EVs. This paper presents a novel magnetic-geared motor that consists of a flux-modulated type magnetic gear and a switched reluctance (SR) motor. The proposed magnetic-geared motor has the wide speed-torque characteristics.

articleTitle: Formation of bct structure and high magnetic anisotropy in Fe-Co films with added V and C elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A high amount of 0-20 at.% of C was added into an Fe-Co-V film by sputtering method, and the crystal structure transformed from body-centered cubic (bcc) to face-centered cubic (fcc) through body-centered tetragonal (bct) structure. In the Fe-Co without V, with increasing C content, the crystal structure changed discontinuously from bcc to fcc not through bct structure. On the other hand, in the Fe-Co with added 10 at.% of V, a single bct phase with the axial ratio c/a of ~1.2 formed in samples with added 5-10at.% of C. The saturation magnetization of these samples (Fe-Co-V-C) were approximately 1200-1500 kA/m and the uniaxial magnetic anisotropy constants were approximately 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> J/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: High Resolution Enlarged Open-Bore Narrow-band Magnetic Particle Imaging Based on Double-layer Linear Scanning Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We developed a novel high resolution open-bore magnetic particle imaging (MPI) system for big animal and future clinical usage. In the MPI system, the gradient field and linear scanning trajectory were formed by 16 square coils independent from excitation field, by which the gradient magnetic field strength reached 4T/m, and the open field of view (FOV) was 15cm×15cm×10cm. Further, a new differential pick-up structure was proposed in order to suppress the system noises, consisting of multi Helmholtz excitation and pickup coils away from the FOV, which was very important for the limited open bore structure. The new differential structure contributed significantly to improve the signal-to-noise ratio as high as about 100dB. Several home-made resonant circuits, filters and lock-in amplifier was used to form the so-called narrowband MPI system. Experimental results showed that the detection limit of the system was 1ug Fe of Resovist sample with a spatial resolution of 1mm after reconstruction, satisfying many clinical needs such as drug delivery bedside-monitoring.

articleTitle: Flexible thermoelectrics based on 3D interconnected magnetic nanowire networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)

authors.preferredName: T. da Camara Santa Clara Gomes

abstract: 3D networks of ferromagnetic (FM) nanowires fabricated by direct electrodeposition into the crossed nanopores of polymer templates are effective thermoelectric materials. The interconnected nanowire networks are formed from pure metals, alloys, and FM/Cu multilayers. Giant magneto-Seebeck effects in multilayer nanowires allow the determination of key parameters in spin caloritronics such as spin-dependent Seebeck coefficients and can be exploited to design flexible thermoelectric switches with optimal magnetic field-induced control of the sign and magnitude of the thermoelectric power output. Homogeneous nanowire arrays exhibit extremely high thermoelectric power factors that make them effective materials as flexible active Peltier coolers for thermal management of hot spots.

articleTitle: Design of Non-Isolated Modulation Code with Minimum Hamming Distance of 3 for Bit-Patterned Media Recording Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In the bit-patterned media recording (BPMR), to increase the areal density, the magnetic islands are adjusted closer together. This makes the bit-error rate performance of BPMR become worse by inter-symbol interference (ISI) and inter-track interference (ITI) from cross- and down-track directions, respectively. To solve the ISI and ITI, the data is modulated into non-isolated patterns before storing on the medium of BPMR systems. Therefore, we introduced a method to create the non-isolated patterns with a minimum Hamming distance (MHD) of 3. In our proposed method, firstly, we exploit the generator matrix of the Hamming code to create one-dimensional codewords with an MHD of 3. Then, these codewords are converted into two-dimensional codewords without isolated pattern. Finally, to create a fast encoder and decoder, we used the multi-layer perceptron to encode the original data into the non-isolated codewords with an MHD of 3. The results show that our proposed model improved the BER performance of the BPMR system.

articleTitle: 3D Modeling of High-Temperature Superconducting Rotating Field Electrodynamic Maglev Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: High-Temperature Superconducting (HTS) Rotating Field Electrodynamic Maglev Motor (RFEMM), which 3D finite element method is time-consuming and analytical model has insufficient accuracy, is presented in this paper. Based on magnetic field reconstruction method (FRM) and second order vector potential (SOVP), a 3D calculation model of the motor, which the expression of magnetic field in the air gap, the lift force, torque and power losses were derived respectively, was proposed and verified by 3D transient finite element model. Finally, a small-scale prototype is manufactured, and experiments are carried out to verify the predicted results.

articleTitle: Electrical switching of insulating antiferromagnet/heavy metal bilayers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Efficient and reliable electrical writing and reading of the Néel vector in antiferromagnetic insulators is a key prerequisite in view of using this class of materials as active elements in future spintronic devices. Here, we study the current-induced switching of the Néel vector in NiO/Pt and CoO/Pt bilayers. We compare the signal read out electrically, via the spin Hall magnetoresistance effect, with the imaged magnetic domain structure and from this comparison we identify the switching mechanisms that lead to the reorientation of the Néel vector in the thin films.

articleTitle: Multitrack Recording and Two-stage Decoding Schemes for Heated Dot Magnetic Recording with Double-layered Bit Patterned Media
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In previous work, a two-stage signal processing scheme for a heated-dot magnetic recording (HDMR) system using double-layered bit-patterned media (BPM) was proposed [1]. This two-stage signal processing scheme can be applied or extended to an advanced HDMR system combined with multi-track recording and simultaneous detection. Consequently, the two-stage signal processing scheme is capable of detecting data sequences recorded on double tracks simultaneously in an order which progresses from the top layer (upper layer) to the bottom layer (lower layer). In addition, the two-stage signal processing scheme is able to produce a fourfold increase in the effective transmission rate of the HDMR system with two-track simultaneous detection and double-layered BPM compared to the HDMR system with single-track detection and single-layered BPM. The purpose of introducing multi-track recording and simultaneous detection schemes causes further to further increase the effective transmission ratio. Using multi-track recording and simultaneous detection in this way, this research shows how significant of an effect can be expected in terms of improving the error rate performance.

articleTitle: Magnetooptics of higher order in magnetization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetooptic Kerr effect (MOKE) is often considered to be proportional to magnetization direction. However MOKE may also depend on higher orders in magnetization direction, such as quadratic or cubic MOKE. There are two distinct contributions to higher order MOKE, (i) the relation between material permittivity and material magnetization direction, described by magnetooptic tensors of higher orders, G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ijkl</inf>, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ijklm</inf> (material property) and (ii) the relation between the permittivity and MOKE (optical property). Here, we present spectral investigation of quadratic MOKE on Fe and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnSi, and investigation of cubic MOKE on Ni(111).

articleTitle: Radio-Frequency Spintronic Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spintronic nano-synapses and nano-neurons are complex cognitive devices that have high accuracy due to their reproducible and controllable magnetization dynamics. They have the potential to revolutionize artificial intelligence hardware, but currently, there is no scalable way to connect them in multilayers. We show that magnetic tunnel junctions can be used to connect spintronics components in multilayer neural networks, allowing them to function as both synapses and neurons. We build a two-layer hardware spintronic neural network using nine magnetic tunnel junctions and found that it could classify nonlinearly-separable RF inputs with an accuracy of 97.7%. We also demonstrate that a larger network of these junctions could identify drones from their RF transmissions while consuming minimal power. This study lays the foundation for the development of deep, dynamical, spintronic neural networks [1].

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Phase Transformation of Sm-Fe-Co-X (X = Ga, V, B, Si, and Ti) Permanent Magnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetic properties and phase transformation of Sm(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>X (X = Ga, V, B, Si, and Ti) were investigated. The Sm(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>X ribbons were produced by rapid solidification process, and their phase transformation and magnetic properties were analyzed using DSC and VSM. It was confirmed that the melt-spun amorphous phase was converted to the ɑ-Fe phase, then to TbCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>-type phases, and finally to the ThMn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>-type phase. Magnetic property measurements show that the coercivities of the Sm(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>X ribbons vary with the compositions. The Ti substituted sample has the highest concentration of ThMn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>-type phase across all annealing temperatures and the corresponding coercivity is also the highest among the samples. The squareness, M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>/M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>, of the samples shows that the trends follow the degree of crystallinity of the ThMn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>-type phase, so that higher concentrations of hard magnetic phase result in the enhanced squareness.

articleTitle: Frequency Characteristics Analysis of Remote Field Eddy Current Testing on Ferromagnetic Pipes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Eddy current testing (ECT) method is widely used for defect detection in heat exchangers in steel and petrochemical plants. In practical usages, the remote ECT method is effective on external defect detection of ferromagnetic pipes. To clarify the detailed detection mechanism of the remote field ECT method, the frequency characteristics of the remote field ECT method on detecting an artificial external defect made on a ferromagnetic pipe specimen are measured and analyzed in detail by using the nonlinear eddy current analysis. Peak occurs directly under the defect under the same optimal frequency range in both analysis and measurement.

articleTitle: Multiphysics modeling and optimization of PMSM for high speed operation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In many modern applications like aerospace and automotive, maximizing the power density of an actuator is required to ensure lighter systems. This can be achieved by increasing the rotational speed of electrical machines, which leads to face many constraints, particularly from a mechanical and thermal points of view. Developing multiphysics modeling tools associated to optimization methods is then necessary for sizing high speed machines. The paper presents electromagnetic, mechanical and thermal analytical models of surface mounted PMSMs to ensure pretty precise pre-sizing. Numerical simulations that use the finite element method (FEM) are conducted to validate the analytical findings.

articleTitle: Effect of sputtering process parameters on tungsten structural phases and its spin Hall angle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) plays a crucial role in spin-to-charge interconversion. SOC correlates structural phases of heavy metals (HM) and its spin Hall angle. Here, we report a systematic investigation of the growth of tungsten (W) by tuning sputtering process parameters, and its influence on spin Hall angle (θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SH</inf>). Surface topographical measurements suggest that nucleation and growth of polycrystalline W follow the Volmer-Weber mechanism. The X-ray diffraction and resistivity results reveal that W exhibits a structural phase transition from mixed (α + β)-W to β-W as a function of Ar deposition pressure (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ar</inf>) for a constant thickness. The kinetic energy of sputtered atoms and the adatom's surface mobility determines the phase formation. W deposited with different deposition rates (D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) at constant P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ar</inf> suggests that relative phase fraction is tunable by D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> where the resistivity measurements confirm the same. From spin-pumping technique, the maximum spin-mixing conductance is found to be 10.1× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>. The estimated θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SH</inf> from inverse spin Hall effect measurements is found to be −0. 24 (± 0.08) at D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=0.08 nm/s. Our systematic investigation may improve the understanding on the evolution of W crystalline phases via controlling sputtering process parameters.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties Evaluation of a Compacted Soft Magnetic Composite Core for Permanent Magnet Claw Pole Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Soft magnetic composite (SMC) cores exhibit different magnetic properties at different mass densities and heating process, meanwhile the further mechanical processing on a compacted SMC core can deteriorate its magnetic properties. Therefore, in the development of electrical machines with SMC cores, using the compacted SMC core is very important. However, the required SMC core for electrical machine is normally with irregular shape and its magnetic properties is determined by the corresponding manufacturing process. Currently, the measurement of the magnetic properties of SMC cores are generally carried out based on ring, sheet or cubic samples, and few evaluations of the magnetic properties of compacted SMC cores with actual irregular shape have been performed. In this paper, a magnetic characteristic measurement system for the compacted SMC stator claw pole teeth is constructed, meanwhile the error source in the measurement system is analyzed and the corresponding finite element model (FEM) is established for verifying the measured results. It can be seen that the actual magnetic characteristic of the compacted SMC stator claw pole teeth is close to that obtained from the ring sample.

articleTitle: Dry-type phantom emulating quadrupole-like magnetic field distribution for evaluation of magnetoneurography
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A dry-type phantom for evaluating the accuracy of magnetoneurography (MNG) is presented in this work. The phantom emulates the quadrupole-like pattern of the typical magnetic field distribution observed in MNG. It is composed of print circuit boards patterned with long rectangular coils, whose short and long edges measure 5 and 400 mm, respectively. The magnetic field distribution from the dry-type phantom is obtained using a 132-ch MNG system equipped with an array of vector-type superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) flux sensors, and it shows a clear quadrupole-like pattern. The dry-type phantom is easier to handle, and provides the comparable or higher accuracy than that of the previously developed wet-type phantom in terms goodness-of-fit.

articleTitle: Effect of cross-saturation on the performance of synchronous reluctance machine operating as autonomous generator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper deals with the cross-saturation effect on the performance of self-excited reluctance synchronous generator. Such machine is well known for its non-negligible saturation due to its air gap of small width that can be accounted for in different ways when using d-q diphase analytical model. On the basis of a test synchronous reluctance machine, the magnetizing inductances with respects to the current along both d and q axis are identified using 2D-FE. The model is then used to study the performance of the test machine as a stand-alone generator operating. Results obtained when the cross-saturation effect is considered are compared to the ones when the saturation effect is taken into account along the only d-axis or along both axes independently showing significant differences.

articleTitle: Modeling the Dependence Hysteresis Characteristics of Thin Films Pd/Co/CoO on Cobalt Oxidation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The influence of cobalt oxidation on the hysteresis characteristics of Pd/Co/CoO films was studied. The oxidation of thin cobalt film was carried out within the framework of three models: layer-by-layer island oxidation, "growth" of islands in the form of cone-shaped structures deep into the film, and the combination of these models. The calculations showed that independently from thickness of the antiferromagnetic layer, the hysteresis loops of the Pd/Co/CoO films have a rectangular shape. The saturation magnetic moment Ms, and the remanent magnetization Mr decrease with increasing percentage of cobalt oxide. The rate of decrease in Ms during layer-by-layer oxidation turned out to be significantly lower than in the "growth" model of islands.

articleTitle: Ac Susceptibility Measurement Using a Vibrating Sample Magnetometer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We propose the addition of an ac susceptibility measurement capability to the vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM) method. By applying an ac magnetic field to the vibrating sample, asymmetric sidebands appear at the mixed VSM and ac frequencies. We analyze these sidebands to obtain the complex ac susceptibility, simultaneously with the dc magnetization of the VSM method. We verify our method on a permalloy thin film sample.

articleTitle: Epitaxial Co2FeSi/LiNbO3 multiferroic heterostructures with a low damping constant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Piezoelectric LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> has been widely utilized to generate and detect spin waves in surface acoustic wave devices. Here we demonstrate an epitaxial Co-based Heusler alloy on a LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> 128° Y-cut (LN-128Y) substrate by molecular beam epitaxy. Although there is no matching between the lattice length and symmetry, the insertion of a bcc metal buffer layer enables to grow L2<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> - ordered epitaxial Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>FeSi films on the LN-128Y substrate. The epitaxial Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>FeSi/LN- 128Y multiferroic heterostructures show a high saturation magnetization of ~1235 emu/cc and a low damping constant of ~6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. This study will open a way for an efficient electric-field control of the spin waves in surface acoustic wave devices.

articleTitle: PAC Code Construction for Spin-Torque Transfer Magnetic Random Access Memory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate, for the first time, the design and optimization of the polarization-adjusted convolutional (PAC) code for the spin-torque transfer magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM) channel. A crucial problem for the application of PAC codes to the STT-MRAM channel is to optimize the index set of the non-frozen bits of the PAC codes. Hence, a rate-profile optimization method based on the genetic algorithm assisted bit-swapping is proposed. Simulation results show that the PAC code with the optimized rate-profile outperforms both the polar code and the PAC code with existing generic rate-profiles.

Author Keywords: Spin-torque transfer magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM)

articleTitle: Anisotropic Magnetoresistance Effect in Bulk Single-Crystal Half-Metallic Heusler Alloys
