publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Crystal orientation dependence of the anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) of bulk single-crystal of Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGe and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>FeSi Heusler alloys was investigated. Negative AMR was observed in all crystal orientations [100, 110], and [111] for Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGe, which has been predicted to be a half-metallic ferromagnet. On the other hand, both positive and negative signs of AMR were observed for Co2FeSi. For the interpretation of these behaviors, theoretical prediction based on the s-d scattering taking into consideration not only the spin-orbit interaction and exchange magnetic field but also the crystal field is required.

articleTitle: Spin pumping with heavy metals, topological insulators and antiferromagnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spin current-based electronics, referred to as spintronics, is the promising technology to replace charge current-based technology. Spintronics-based devices allow for the minimization of the size of the device and faster response. The study of spin current efficiency in different materials is one of the emergent research topics in modern days. Spin pumping and inverse spin Hall effect (ISHE) are popular tools for studying the spin current efficiency in materials. In this regard, high spin-orbit coupling (SOC) materials are very useful for such studies. Heavy metals, topological insulators, and Antiferromagnets are used as high SOC layers in this work.

articleTitle: Eddy-Current Reduction Structure of Copper Foil Winding for Medium-Frequency Transformer in DC-grid Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: As a differentiating technology from the conventional technology utilizing a Litz wire, a low-cost and simple structure that reduces in-plane eddy-current loss due to the leakage magnetic flux generated in the copper-foil windings of a medium-frequency transformer (MFT) was devised. An MFT based on this structure was prototyped by processing a tapered cross-section at both ends of the copper foil. The frequency-versus-AC-resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ac</inf>) performance of the winding was evaluated by short-circuit test. According to the results of the test, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ac</inf> of the prototyped MFT can be reduced by up to 8% at around 1 kHz compared that of an MFT with conventional copper-foil winding.

articleTitle: Boron-induced magneto-optical Kerr spectra and dielectric tensors in ferrimagnetic antiperovskite thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Boron-induced electronic states of antiperovskite nitrides such as ferrimagnetic Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>N were investigated via a combination of polar magneto-optical Kerr effect (p-MOKE) spectroscopy and spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE). The boron content in the Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>N film varied from 0 to 4.3 at.%, for which the crystal structure was maintained. The amplitude of p-MOKE spectra and the diagonal and off-diagonal dielectric tensors decreased with increasing boron content, which is in agreement with magnetic properties such as magnetic anisotropy and saturation magnetization. These results were related to the lattice expansion and displacement of the charge density in Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>N by boron doping. However, the peak energy of Lorentz oscillator in the diagonal elements of dielectric tensors suggests that a dominant inter-band transition was independent of boron content.

articleTitle: Assessment of Directionally Solidified Eutectic Sm-Fe(Co)-Ti Alloys as Permanent Magnet Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Sm-Fe-Ti and Sm-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>-Ti alloys were prepared via arc-melting and directionally solidified on a water-cooled copper hearth. The alloys featured cells of the Sm(Fe,Co,Ti)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>- Ti(Fe,Co)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-(αFe) lamellar eutectic, with the lamellae of Sm(Fe,Co,Ti)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>phase (crystal structure of the ThMn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>type) less than 0.2 μm thick and with their [001] directions oriented along the temperature gradient of the solidification. Although this eutectic microstructure also led to an increased coercivity, the latter reached only a modest value of 0.07 T (0.7 kOe), which is believed to be insufficient for utilization of the directionally solidified alloys as anisotropic permanent magnets.

articleTitle: Atomic Layer Deposition of Perpendicularly Magnetized Co Layers Showing Current-induced Domain Wall Motion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Successful preparation of perpendicularly magnetized Co thin layers on Pt seed-layers using atomic layer deposition (ALD) technique with Co(PF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>H as a precursor is reported. The residual phosphorus content in the samples, due to low deposition temperatures to realize ALD, was reduced effectively by tuning ALD parameters. Spin-orbit-torque driven current-induced domain wall motion was observed in the strip containing ALD Co layer prepared with the low phosphorus condition.

articleTitle: Evolution of magnetic interactions from non-magnetic amorphous NiCu@SiO2 composite
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report on the structural and magnetic properties of disordered Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">72</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</inf>@SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> composites synthesized by modified sol-gel method with varying silica content. The nanocrystallites of Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">72</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</inf> evolved from amorphous composite on heat treatment. Magnetic measurements indicate that the interaction effects can be controlled by varying the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> content. The temperature and field dependent magnetization measurements indicate that particle size distribution and interparticle interactions lead to evolution of ferromagnetic character from weakly magnetic amorphous composites.

articleTitle: Influence of Magnetic Field on Evaporation of Water and Ionic Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The evaporation of water in half-filled beakers and sessile droplets is studied in the presence and absence of a static magnetic field produced by permanent magnets. The main difference between the two is that water in beakers in the steady state evaporates into a reservoir of air loaded with its own its own fresh vapour. The ratio of otho to para nuclear isomers, which behave effectively as independent gasses is 39:61, whereas water in droplets evaporates into open ambient air where the ratio of the triplet to singlet is 3:1. The isomeric ratio of fresh vapour is deduced from the change of evaporation rate in a magnetic field, whose principal effect is to equalize the isomer populations due to dephasing of nuclear Larmor precession in a magnetic field gradient. The field increases the evaporation rate of 2M or 4M LiCl, NaCl and KCl are comparable to that in water. 1M NaCl is anomaloua. The field decreases the evaporation rate and the isomeric ratio is 60:40. A similar field effect found for a 1 M NaCl sessile droplet confined in a 1mL cuvette.

articleTitle: Magnetic Nanoparticles: from the Nanostructure to the Physical Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Some of the synthesis methods and physical properties of iron oxide-based magnetic nanoparticles such as Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3- x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and CoxFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> are reviewed because of their interest in health, environmental applications, and ultra-high density magnetic recording. Unlike high crystalline quality nanoparticles larger than a few nanometers that show bulk-like magnetic and electronic properties, nanostructures with increasing structural defects yield a progressive worsening of their general performance due to frozen magnetic disorder and local breaking of their crystalline symmetry. Thus, it is shown that single-crystal, monophasic nanoparticles do not exhibit significant surface or finite-size effects, such as spin canting, reduced saturation magnetization, high closure magnetic fields, hysteresis loop shift, or dead magnetic layer, features which are mostly associated with crystallographic-defective systems. Besides, the key role of the nanoparticle coating, surface anisotropy, and inter-particle interactions are discussed. Finally, the results of some single particle techniques -magnetic force microscopy, X-ray photoemission electron microscopy, and electron magnetic chiral dichroism- that allow studying individual nanoparticles down to sub-nanometer resolution with element, valence, and magnetic selectivity, are presented. All in all, the intimate, fundamental correlation of the nanostructure (crystalline, chemical, magnetic…) to the physical properties of the nanoparticles is ascertained.

articleTitle: Magnetic Relaxation effects on Magnetoelastic Resonance Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The phenomenon of magnetic relaxation in amorphous ferromagnetic alloys produces a time-dependence of the magnetization, and other magnetic related properties, that can be a source of error when these materials are used in sensor applications. The present work studies the influence of the magnetic relaxation on the performance of an amorphous ferromagnetic ribbon of composition Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">73</inf>Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> as the main element of a magnetoelastic resonance (MER) sensor. The relaxation behavior was observed through the evolution of the MER signal, in particular through the variation experienced by the resonance frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>, which is the most commonly used parameter in sensing applications. It was found that, after the application of the bias field, and under constant measurement conditions, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> increases with time in a typical relaxation behavior. The amplitude of the excitation magnetic field (h) turned out to be a key factor on this phenomenon, since larger excitation field amplitudes (h ≥ 100 mOe) reduce considerably its effect, decreasing the relaxation time (τ) and reducing the temporal variation of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> (Δf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) experience by the sensor. The influence of this relaxation on the sensor performance and the approaches to overcome this problem are evaluated and applied to the case of a real-time monitoring of a precipitation reaction.

articleTitle: Micromagnetic Simulations of CoFeB/MgO Perpendicular Stacks for Sensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: CoFeB/MgO thin films are popular materials materials for application in magnetic storage and spintronic devices. In this study, we use micromagnetic simulations to characterize the magnetic properties of CoFeB/MgO thin films devices with perpendicular anisotropy, aiming at optimizing the structures for detection of magnetic fields perpendicular to the plane. We simulate various experimentally achievable combinations of exchange stiffness, interfacial anisotropy, the thicknesses of the CoFeB film and dimensions and aspect ratio of the devices in order to see how is their impact on the magnetic performance. Furthermore, we numerically show that obtaining a low coercivity and low saturation field for thin films in an out-of-plane (OOP) sensing application is impossible without a strong interfacial anisotropy, even if its volumic anisotropy in the OOP axis is arbitrary. These findings provide valuable insights into the magnetic behavior of OOP magnetic systems, in particular based on CoFeB/MgO thin films and could aid in the design of improved sensorial devices.

articleTitle: Initial Rotor Position Estimation for an Ultra-low Inductive Saliency Machine Based on Eddy Current Loss
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Initial rotor position detection is essential to ensure the accuracy of sensorless control for surface permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) drives. In order to extract position information for SPMSM with an ultra-low inductive saliency, this paper presents the estimation method of rotor position based on eddy-current-reflected resistive saliency. This method separated high-frequency (HF) eddy-current-reflected resistance from HF impedance and extracted the HF voltage vector corresponding to the resistance. To recognize accurate subtle position signatures in the extracted HF voltage, the method harnessed the convolutional neural networks (CNN) to establish the relationship between the HF voltage image and the rotor position. Finally, the proposed method is experimentally evaluated and proven to have a promising performance on initial position estimation for an ultra-low saliency machine.

articleTitle: Metal Influence Suppression Method for Rotating Wireless Power Transfer System Based on Toroidal Double-D Coil
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The wireless power transfer technology provides a feasible solution for scenarios where there is a demand for rotating power transfer. However, the rotating power transfer system is located in a small space and the design of each part is too compact, and when it is too close to the surrounding metal parts, the influence of the metal will cause the system parameters to change and reduce the energy transfer efficiency, and the eddy current loss generated in the metal will lead to temperature rise and affect the safe operation of the system. In this paper, we take an electrically excited motor as the application scenario, establish the equivalent influence model of the system lateral to the metal of different spacing and material, conduct circuit parameters and magnetic field analysis, and propose a toroidal DD structured coil for the design of wireless power transfer system according to the need to suppress the influence of metal and anti-rotation deflection.Based on the finite element method, a simulation model is established to analyze the transmission performance and the surrounding magnetic field of the toroidal DD coil under metal disturbance and to compare the metal influence and rotational offset resistance of the wireless power transfer Finally, an experimental platform of the rotating wireless power transfer system with a toroidal DD coil under the influence of metal at the end of the simulated motor is built to experimentally verify the theoretical and simulation models. The experimental results show that the proposed toroidal DD coil structure has better resistance to metal influence and rotational offset than other power transfer coil structures.

articleTitle: Effect of isothermal aging process on the microstructure of grain boundary regions in Sm(Co, Fe, Cu, Zr)z magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: 2:17-type SmCo permanent magnets have been widely applied in applications under elevated temperature due to their good magnetic properties and excellent thermal stability [1]- [5]. It is confirmed that complete cellular nanostructure in grain boundary regions is very important for improving the magnetic properties of the magnets. In this study, the effect of isothermal aging process on the microstructure of grain boundary regions is systematically investigated. As the isothermal aging duration increases from 30 to 720 minutes, the number of 1:5H cell boundary phase in grain boundary regions is reduced, which leads to incomplete cellular nanostructure. However, the grain size is getting increase, results in the decrease of grain boundaries, which has a positive effect on the squareness. Meanwhile, the coercivity is enhanced with the isothermal aging duration increase. The above findings deepen our understanding of the correlation between isothermal aging process and cellular nanostructure of grain boundary regions, and is beneficial to provide potential considerations for the preparation of high performance magnets.

articleTitle: Exchange bias, magnetic fluid hyperthermia, and cellular uptake by endothelial cells in core-shell Fe@Fe3O4 nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, a well-defined system of spherical monodispersed superparamagnetic core-shell Fe@Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanoparticles has been synthesized by a thermal decomposition reaction. Before surface functionalization, the mean particle size was 14.1 nm ± 1.2 nm with a bright shell of a thickness of 1.3 nm ± 0.4 nm. After ligand exchange surface functionalization, the shell thickness has more than doubled to 2.7 nm ± 0.4 nm. The appearance of the Verwey transition TV=125K confirms the presence of magnetite "Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>" as a shell around the magnetic core "Fe", which was verified with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM). The exchange bias (EB) associated with exchange anisotropy between the shell and the core has been observed. After incubating the human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) with Fe@Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> overnight, a complete uptake of the particles at low and high concentrations (50 and 400 µg/ml) was observed. The specific absorption rate (SAR) values of core/shell iron/iron oxide nanoparticles are higher than the conventional iron oxide nanoparticles, which highlights their promising application as heating agents for magnetic fluid hyperthermia.

articleTitle: Stator Optimization for a Novel Magnetic Levitation Actuator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A novel planar actuator that utilizes mechanically driven stator magnet arrays to levitate a permanent magnet mover is proposed. A state of levitation and actuation is obtained by mechanically altering the orientation of the stator magnets to control the forces and torques on the mover. In this study, a stator design method is proposed, allowing decoupled sinusoidal traveling magnetic fields to be created. The decoupled magnetic fields are important for independent linear translations in the plane and allow for a conventional permanent magnet mover to be used in the actuator. This study obtained an airgap-dependent mean total harmonic distortion of 1.64%.

articleTitle: Novel FeCoBPSiCr Amorphous Alloy Powder with High Bs of 1.61 T and High Corrosion Resistance

High DC-Bias characteristic and the excellent corrosion resistance was recognized also in the inductive device using the (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">82</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> amorphous alloy powder compared to the conventional Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">79</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</inf>C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> amorphous alloy powder.

articleTitle: Design of Wrist Rehabilitation Exoskeleton Device with Magnetic Serial Elastic Actuator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, axial magnetic coupling is employed as an elastic body to develop a serial elastic actuator for the development of a wrist exoskeleton rehabilitation robot that can control strength and stiffness in real time. With the design of dual driving degrees of freedom, four wrist movements, namely flexion, extension, radial deviation, and ulnar deviation, can be performed. In addition to achieving control of the output force, the proposed method can be used to quantify and evaluate patient's recovery status for more precise automated medical rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Magnetic Bionic Hair Array for Sliding Tactile Sensing and Object Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Tactile sensing is one of the indispensable ways for human beings to perceive the external environment. In addition to the skin surface, hairs covering a large area on human skin are extremely sensitive to external contact. With the popularity of household robots, the precise grasping and human-machine safe interaction of robots have become increasingly considerable. A crucial way to solve these problems is to endow the robot with the ability of large-area tactile perception and sliding perception. With the idea of bionics, we apply the hair structure of human skin to tactile sensing, and a magnetic hair array is developed by using a demoulding method. The magnetic hair array is then applied to sliding tactile sensing and object recognition. It can realize precise detection of the size, direction and sliding of external force, and achieves a success rate of 97% in object recognition. In addition to recognizing the shape of objects, the magnetic hair array can identify whether the object has magnetism inside, which has great application potential in intelligent robots and rescue relief in the future.

articleTitle: Blocking phenomenon of hard/soft bilayer FePt grains in granular film
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The structural inhomogeneity of an L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>–FePt grain in a granular film was investigated, and its blocking phenomenon was simulated. It was confirmed that 1) structural analysis reveals that both lattice distorted disordered portion at near the interface with MgO underlayer and ordered potion at the upper region exist inside one FePt grain in a granular film, 2) simulation of blocking phenomenon for FePt grains with structural inhomogeneity, hard (order)/soft (disorder) bilayer grains, shows that switching field (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sw</inf>) increases steeply near T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> of the disorder layer with decreasing temperature. To generalize blocking phenomenon of the hard/soft bilayer structure, it was found that matching the Curie temperatures of the hard and soft layers leads to high H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sw</inf> near the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>, which means high robustness against thermal field in random direction. These are useful findings for the design of cap-layer media for HAMR to realize the high spatial resolution.

articleTitle: Spin Dynamics at Interfaces on Femtosecond Timescales
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The interaction of femtosecond laser pulses with ferromagnetic metals and their heterostructures drives a range of dynamic magnetic phenomena including ultrafast demagnetization and spin-dependent charge transport. Controlling these dynamics might pave the way to future ultrafast spintronics applications. This however requires gaining microscopic insight into the underlying processes. Time-resolved magneto-optical and x-ray spectroscopies provide such insight in combination with ab initio theory, revealing the competition of femtosecond spin transfer with spin-orbit coupling as well as the influence of local correlations on the transient band structure of the 3d ferromagnets.

articleTitle: Magnetization and Spin Dynamics in Two-Dimensional Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The discovery of magnetism in two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) materials has flourished a new endeavor of fundamental problems in magnetism. In this talk, we will discuss the magnetization and spin dynamics in two types of 2D magnets: a room-temperature vdW magnetic crystal Fe5GeTe2 with a Curie temperature Tc = 332 K and Cu(1,3-bdc), a quasi-2D magnet with a Kagome lattice. Ferromagnetic resonance was performed with external magnetic fields applied along the c-axis (H║c) and the ab-plane (H║ab). We have found a sizable Landé g-factor difference between the H║c and H║ab cases for both Fe5GeTe2 and Cu(1,3-bdc). The FMR measurements have also revealed that Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>GeTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> has a damping constant comparable to Permalloy. Our experiments highlight key information regarding the magnetic state and spin scattering processes in 2D magnets, which can lead to implementations of 2D magnets based spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Thermal Decay and Read-Write Characteristics Depending on the Structure of Sputtered Tape Media
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A magnetic recording simulator considering thermal agitation was created by assuming probabilistic switching of the magnetization according to the Arrehenius-Neel equation. In the sputtered perpendicular media for magnetic tape recording, the effect of a Capped and a H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>-Graded media were analyzed. The simulation results agreed well with the measurements in both M-H curves and read-write characteristics. A clear relationship was shown between the writeability and the high-speed sweeping H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cr</inf>. On the other hand, no clear relationship was confirmed between the media SNR decay and the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cr</inf> decay over time, suggesting that the magnitude of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cr</inf> after being affected by thermal agitation may also affect the SNR decay.

articleTitle: Significant effect of carrier concentration on spin lifetime at low temperatures in strained Si0.1Ge0.9
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Using lateral spin transport measurements, we experimentally estimate the spin diffusion length (λ) and spin lifetime (τ) in strained n-Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf> with two-different carrier concentrations (n) of ~1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> and ~5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> in the temperature range from 8 K to room temperature. We find a marked difference in τ depending on n at temperatures less than 100 K. We propose that, in the degenerate regime, the intravalley spin-flip scattering mechanism should be considered in the strained n-Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf>.

articleTitle: Magnetic domains and flexomagnetism in Cr2O3
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Antiferromagnets, which possess nearly zero magnetic moment and consist of a few magnetic sublattices connected by the symmetry operation of their permutation, represent a perspective material platform for technology and fundamental science. Among a variety of such materials, Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is a unique example of the easy axis magnetoelectric material at room temperature. Here, we discuss measuring and manipulation of domain walls in single crystal and polycrystalline Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> samples, and respective applications including electric access to the texture state: pinning at grain boundaries, elastic degrees of freedom of a domain wall and detection of an uncompensated magnetization, which originates from the spatial distribution of the Néel temperature and is coupled with the strain gradient.

articleTitle: Ultrafast time-resolved spectroscopy of spin precession by an asynchronous optical sampling based on a dual-comb system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We developed an asynchronous optical sampling measurement (ASOPS) system based on a dual-comb fiber laser. This measurement system enables us to significantly accelerate a time-resolved measurement using the optical pump and optical probe method. We demonstrated the time-resolved measurement of laser-induced spin precession dynamics in a ferromagnetic permalloy thin film. The time resolution of the system was sub-picoseconds, the time window was 16 nanoseconds, and the overall measurement time was tens of seconds. This technique is expected to be useful for the temporal characterization of spin dynamics, taking advantage of high-speed measurement.

articleTitle: Automatic MTPA Control Method for Magnetic-Geared Motor Using Sensorless Control Based on Extended Electromotive Force Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper describes an automatic MTPA (Maximum Torque Per Ampere) control method for a magnetic-geared motor using sensorless control based on the extended electromotive force model. The magnetic flux due to the permanent magnet appears in the q axis as well as in the d axis in a magnetic-geared motor when a load is applied to the low-speed rotor. Therefore, it is difficult to apply a MTPA control method to a magnetic-geared motir. In this paper, an automatic MTPA control method for a magnetic-geared motor using sensorless control is proposed. The electric circuit equation of a magnetic-geared motor is shown, and mathematical sensorless control model based on the extended electromotive force model is described. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed MTPA control method is investigated by the comparison of the mathematical simulation, finite element analysis, and measurements on a prototype.

articleTitle: Effects of the external disturbances on rotational stability of the HTS magnetic bearings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The rotational characteristics of the entire HTS magnetic bearing system under influence of the external disturbances is studied. This is intended to apply the HTS magnetic bearing device as a superconducting flywheel for power storage in vehicles and other moving objects. The HTS magnetic bearing system consists of the rotor and the HTS. In this system, the rotor is used as the rotor and the HTS is used as the stator. The rotor levitates stably by the pinning effect of the HTS. The flux distribution of the rotor has large influence on stability. The yoke-equipped cylinder-type rotor is introduced. This rotor consists of the cylinder-type permanent magnet and the yoke. The flux from the top of the rotor interlinked the HTS by equipping the yoke. This increases the flux-use rate of the permanent magnet. And the stability of the rotor is increased.In this study, the stability of the rotating rotor is evaluated under vibration. At start of vibration, the rotor was affected by the vibration and the resonance frequency changed. However, even when vibration was applied, there was little effect of vibration on the rotational attenuation. Therefore, the rotor can be levitated stably under vibration.

articleTitle: Estimation of Anomalous Portion in Gray Cast Iron using Non-contacting Electromagnetic Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The gray cast iron is used in pulleys for power transmission in industrial machinery, etc., since its excellent wear resistance and castability. However, this cast iron material may become brittle during the manufacturing process. In the brittle cast iron, the ferrite content is increased and the pearlite content is decreased. The electromagnetic properties in the cast iron are affected by the proportions of these components. In this paper, an electromagnetic sensor that detects the brittleness of the cast iron from changes in electromagnetic properties within the cast iron is proposed. The electromagnetic FEM analysis using a play model method and the verification experiment show that the brittle cast iron is discriminated from the difference in hysteresis magnetic curve and conductivity between brittle and normal cast iron.

articleTitle: High-performance Type-y Spin-orbit Torque MRAM Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We demonstrated in-plane field-free-switching spin-orbit torque (SOT) magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) devices capable of low switching current density, fast speed, high reliability and most importantly, manufactured uniformly by the 200 mm-wafer platform. The SOT-MTJ devices are integrated on 200 m-wafers using two-metal-layers back-end-of-line (BEOL) process. The performances of the devices are systematically studied, including magnetic properties, endurance, data retention and switching dynamic of the devices. Specifically, the devices exhibit low critical switching current density J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>~160 MA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 0.3 ns, high tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) ratios exceeding 100%, ultra-high endurance over 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> cycles, and excellent thermal stability Eb > 100 k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>T. The research provides flexible solutions for high-speed and energy efficient memory applications. As a prospective, it is expected to obtain excellent performance of the devices through further optimizing the MTJ film stacks and corresponding fabrication processes.

articleTitle: Growth-Induced Order by Site-Preference in Anisotropic Mixed Rare-Earth Iron Garnet Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic properties of rare-earth iron garnets can be dramatically changed by mixing different ions on a single site in the crystal structure. We observe and characterize ordering of rare-earth ions due to site-preference in mixed europium-thulium iron garnet (EuTmIG) thin films grown by pulsed laser deposition (PLD) on (111) gadolinium gallium garnet (GGG). EuTmIG thin films with increasing Eu fraction (x) show linear strain variation from tensile to compressive due to lattice mismatch on GGG. In addition, a large anisotropy in the form K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf> = K(x)(1-x) is observed and identified as growth-induced anisotropy (GIA), which is great enough in intermediate Eu:Tm compositions to overcome shape and magnetoelastic anisotropy and generate perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA). Spin-Hall magnetoresistance measurements show that GIA in PLD films (80 kJ/ m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) is five times greater than that observed in liquid-phase grown garnets. Atomic resolution h scanning transmission electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) prove that GIA is caused by local atom ordering described by site symmetry reduction due to the projected face view during growth (site-preference model). This work shows that modern growth and characterization techniques enable understanding and control of atomic matter enabling one to engineer magnetic properties in complex oxides.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Various Slot Pitch for 2-Pole 6-Slot Ultra-High Speed Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The 2-pole 6-slot permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is an attractive option for ultra-high-speed (UHS) applications due to their high manufacturability and balanced magnetic force. UHS PMSM should be designed with short stack length and end coil height due to rotor dynamics issue. Also, due to its high frequency, it must be designed considering stator iron loss, rotor eddy current loss, and AC copper loss. With the same pole-slot combination, the performance varies greatly depending on the slot pitch, so we compared the efficiency and power density of the 2-pole 6-slot UHS PMSM according to the winding arrangement. For a reasonable comparison, an optimal design was performed for each slot pitch, and to reduce computation time, the optimization was conducted in two stages: axial size minimization and efficiency maximization. It was confirmed that in terms of total axial length, 1-coil pitch was the shortest due to the advantage of short end coil height, even with the lowest winding factor. On the other hand, 2-coil pitch has good trade-off relationship in terms of efficiency and axial size.

articleTitle: MagPure Chip: a microfluidic device to isolate viable circulating tumor cells
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) could be interesting biomarkers to assess the severity of cancer, monitor the evolution of the disease in real-time, and guide therapeutic strategies. However, their study is challenging as they are present in an ultra-low concentration in blood, at about 1 ppm to the most. Besides, CTCs share common physical properties with some white blood cells (WBCs), which limits the performances of physical-based isolation. On the other hand, sorting CTCs from biological surface markers does not allow for obtaining sufficiently high throughput. In this context, we have developed an immunomagnetic microfluidic device, named MagPure Chip, to purify in CTC a pre-treated blood sample. Here we show that this device preserves the integrity of the recovered CTC and the relatively fast operation is compatible with the timescale of clinical workflows.

articleTitle: Effect of Humidity on Head Smear Generation in Head-Assisted Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The causes of head smears deposited on the magnetic head surface due to laser heating in heat-assisted magnetic recording need to be investigated to achieve higher recording densities for hard disk drives. Factors that affect smear formation in hard disk drives include outgassing from components and humidity. In this study, we focused on the effect of relative humidity in the environment on smears generated due to laser heating. The lubricant films (dipped, UV-treated, and rinsed) were deposited on the samples using three different methods, and the amount of smear generated on a glass pin was evaluated using a pin-on-disk tester with a laser heating system. As a result, it was confirmed that the amount of smear increased as the humidity increased. The lubricant film with a higher chemical bonding fraction showed less smear generation and a smaller dependence on humidity.

articleTitle: A complete optomagnonic logic set
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The discovery of new methods of purely optical ultrafast excitation of spin waves led to the creation of the first optomagnonic gate XNOR. However, with the help of XNOR alone, it is not possible to perform all types of logical operations. In this work we demonstrate the way to realize an optomagnonic NOR gate. Micromagnetic simulations are used to estimate the requirements for such type of logic gates. The resulting NOR gate forms a complete set of logic gates and has the same advantages as XNOR while not much more complicated than its predecessor.

articleTitle: Non-linearities in Driven Spin-Wave Active Ring Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have studied the interaction between external microwave signal and the magnetostatic surface spin-wave modes generated in the active ring oscillator. By tuning the strength of the injected signal, the spin-wave ring oscillator can be moved from a non-linear operation region to a linear one and vice-versa.

articleTitle: Logic operations of magnetic-skyrmion chirality via a branched nanowire
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report on AND operation using magnetic-skyrmion chiralities for realizing binary logic circuit device via micromagntic simulations. The AND operation is confirmed by two skyrmions with independent chiralities move and disappear at a branched nanowire under the application of spin-orbit torque (SOT) and spin-transfer torque (STT). The circuit can be operated at various branch angle (ϕ) where the magnitude of spin Hall angle (θ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Η</sup>) and current density (j) are 0.15 rad and 0.5~0.6 TA/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively, regardless of the chiralies of skyrmions. The maximum AND operating margin is obtained at θ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Η</sup> = 0.11~0.12 rad and j = 0.6~1.0 TA/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at ϕ = 60°. Our method can be used as a fundamental building block for fully electrical operation in logic devices using the chirality of skyrmions as a data bit.

articleTitle: 3D Wireless Power Transfer System with Three-Phase Skewed Cylindrical Coil
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a wireless power transfer system with a three-phase skewed cylindrical transmitter coil. The transmitter has three-phase coils wounded around cylinder, which are skewed. The skew gives an additional angular freedom to the receiver. Magnetic field analysis and experiments are performed to examine the magnetic field distribution generated by the transmitter and power transfer performance. From these results, the effectiveness of the transmitter is validated.

articleTitle: Electronic Structure and Exchange Bias of a Compensated Ferrimagnet Mn2PtAl
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>PtAl alloy has been investigated for its electronic structure properties along with structural, magnetic and exchange bias properties. It crystallizes in hexagonal structure with lattice constants of a = b = 4.34 Å, and c = 5.47 Å at room temperature. Theoretical calculations reveal a ferrimagnetic arrangement of the magnetic moments of Mn with a small value of total magnetic moment in good agreement with the experimental magnetization measurements. Magnetization isothermal curves in the ambient of a cooling field H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cool</inf> = 70 kOe, show asymmetric hysteresis with a negative shift along H-direction. The estimated exchange bias in Hcool = 70 kOe is giant (2.73 kOe) at 3 K which is attributed to the unidirectional anisotropy associated with ferromagnetic clusters.

articleTitle: Magnetotransport properties of Mn2CoSb
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetotransport properties of melt-spun ribbons of Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CoSb Heusler alloy were investigated. Electrical resistivity ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">xx</inf> does not obey the Mooij correlation. Calculation of normal Hall coefficients R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> revealed a dominant role of electrons in electrical transport of the alloy until 200 K. At room temperature, the hole-like conductivity predominates. R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is of about ~ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> – 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> and the anomalous Hall coefficient RS is of about ~ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Dependence ${{\text{R}}_{\text{s}}}\sim {{\rho}_{{\text{xx}}}}^2$ points to the mechanism of the anomalous Hall effect, independent of the concentration of the scatterers. Pronounced hysteretic features of ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">xx</inf> were observed upon application and removal of the magnetic field. The hysteresis width decreases with increasing temperature and completely disappeared above T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>. It was suggested that the observed hysteresis of ρ is related to a magnetic after-effect in the region of randomly frozen spin states.

articleTitle: Exploration of functional properties of all-3d transition metal Heusler alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Heusler alloys are known to have a large number of applications ranging from spintronics to solid-state cooling devices. In this work, we study a new sub-class of Heusler alloys in which all constituent elements belong to 3d transition metals alloys using a combination of density functional theory and Monte Carlo simulations of the Heisenberg model. Potential candidate alloys are selected by performing a high-throughput search of the available electronic structure database of materials based on pre-defined criteria; these criteria depend on applications of materials which we study. Here we focus on magnetic alloys which are potential candidates either as permanent magnets or for magnetocaloric applications. We calculate magnetocrystalline anisotropy energy as well as Curie temperature for a few selected alloys. Based on our studies we find Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>NiZn, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>NiTi and Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CoFe as potential candidates for permanent magnets. We further observe a structural phase transition in Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnCu and Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnZn which deserves more attention for potential caloric applications.

articleTitle: A Brushless Hybrid Excited Motor based on Field Modulation Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel brushless hybrid excited (HE) motor, in which both armature and field windings are located on the stator, and PMs are housed on the rotor. The key difference is that a special consequent-pole rotor structure is adopted, in which each two PMs is separated by a rotor tooth. So, when DC current is fed into the field winding, the produced stationary wound field can be modulated by the rotor teeth to generate rotary wound field harmonics. Thus, an effective HE operation can be achieved due to the interaction between the synchronous rotating PM field and the wound field harmonics. The motor configuration is introduced firstly. Then the operating principle is discussed by the magnetic field modulation theory. By finite element analysis, the electromagnetic performances are calculated and analyzed. The results verify the validity of theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Field Modulation Effects On Consequent-Pole PM Machines with Different Stator Slot Configurations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of the field modulation effects (FMEs) on consequent-pole permeant magnet (CPM) machines with different stator slot configurations, i.e., open-slot, semi-closed slot and close-slot. Due to the asymmetrical PM magneto-motive force (MMF) distributions and double-side slotting effect, the CPM machines exhibit more air-gap field harmonics for the torque production. In order to quantify the torque contributions of the various effective harmonics, the Maxwell stress tensor method (MSTD) is adopted. The torque proportions due to various air-gap field harmonics in the CPM machines with different stator slot configurations are subsequently investigated by finite element (FE) method, which confirms that the stator slot configurations have a great influence on FME. It can be found that the highest and the lowest torque proportion contributed by the modulated field harmonics can be observed in closed-slot and open-slot structures, respectively. Finally, some experimental measurements on a 12-slot/14-pole CPM machine prototype with a semi-closed slot configuration are carried out to validate the theoretical and FE analyses.

articleTitle: Estimation of Material Characteristics of Film-Type Noise Suppressor Using Equivalent Circuit Modeling and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: An estimation method for material characteristics of a magnetic film-type noise suppressor on the microstrip line was investigated. First, the electrical equivalent circuit of the MSL with magnetic film was obtained. A resistance due to the ferromagnetic resonance loss was calculated by using a magnetic circuit. A resistance due to the eddy current loss was estimated by the least squares method for regression prediction. Next, the material parameters of the film were estimated by using a genetic algorithm in order to obtain high noise suppression effect at 3 GHz and low insertion loss at 1 GHz. The conductive noise suppression effect by magnetic film with estimated parameters was calculated by using electromagnetic field simulator. In result, the noise suppression was maximized around 3 GHz and low insertion loss at 1 GHz was successfully obtained. The results indicate that the proposed estimation method has the potential for material and geometry design of magnetic noise suppressor in order to obtain required noise suppression effect at the circuit design stage.

articleTitle: Giant Magnetoimpedance effect at GHz frequencies in amorphous microwires
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic properties and GMI effect of amorphous Co- rich microwires reveal that they present GMI effect at GHz frequencies. Frequency dependence of maximum GMI ratio has been evaluated. Magnetic field dependences of GMI ratio and frequency dependence of maximum GMI ratio are affected by the post-processing conditions. In particular, we observed that stress-annealing allows improvement of magnetic softness, GMI ratio and affects the frequency dependence of GMI ratio.

articleTitle: Realization of Soft Magnetic Properties in Precipitation Hardening Stainless Steel
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A precipitation hardening type soft magnetic stainless steel that has both workability (at low hardness during machining process) and durability (at high hardness during practical use) while maintaining good soft magnetic properties was developed. Precipitation strengthening by NiAl intermetallic compound shows the highest hardness after aging treatment at 550°C, and soft magnetic properties are obtained for compositions in the single phase of ferrite ( δ; bcc structure) region on the Schaeffler diagram. The compositional design of precipitation-hardenable soft-magnetic stainless steels was made possible by using the parameter obtained from the δ limit line in Schaeffler diagram for the microstructure and magnetic properties. And also by using the parameter obtained from the contribution of solution strengthening elements to material strength, the compositional design for hardness after solution treatment and aging treatment was made possible.

articleTitle: Magnetic Order in Wurtzite (Ga,Mn)As
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Here we report on detailed studies of the magnetic properties of the wurtzite (Ga,Mn)As cylindrical shells. Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.94</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.06</inf>As shells have been grown by molecular beam epitaxy at low temperature as a part of multishell cylinders overgrown on wurtzite (Ga,In)As nanowires cores, synthesized on GaAs (111)B substrates. Our study clearly indicates the presence of a low temperature ferromagnetic coupling, which despite a reasonably high Mn contents of 6% is limited only to below 30 K. A set of dedicated measurements shows that despite a high structural quality of the material the magnetic order has a granular form, which gives rise to the dynamical slow-down typical to blocked superparamagnets. The lack of the long range order has been assigned to a very low hole density, caused primarily by numerous compensation donors, arsenic antisites, formed in the material due to a specific geometry of the growth of the shells on the nanowire template. In a broader view our results constitute an important contribution to the still ongoing dispute on the true and the dominant form(s) of the magnetism in this model dilute ferromagnetic semiconductor.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependence of Wideband Losses in Fe-Co and Fe-Si Steel Sheets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We show that the temperature dependence of the magnetic losses, measured up to 5 kHz in non-oriented 0.20 mm thick Fe-Si and Fe-Co laminations follows two distinct trends. While the total loss in Fe-Si decreases at all frequencies upon increased temperature, a phenomenon well exploited in electrical machines, a substantial increase is observed in Fe-Co. The moderate softening of Fe-Si with temperature is well understood in terms of decreased anisotropy and increased resistivity, while a further temperature-induced mechanism must be invoked for the opposite behavior of Fe-Co. Such a mechanism is identified with the different thermal expansion coefficients of the coexisting ordered and disordered regions and the ensuing internal strains. These induce local unfavorable anisotropies, chiefly affecting the quasi-static hysteresis and loss.

articleTitle: Propulsion and Control of Microrobot using a Multiple Wireless Power Transfer Coil
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Microrobot can be used for a various kind of applications. To maximize the utilization of microrobot, the mobility as well as providing electrical energy is necessary. Therefore, by using a time-varying magnetic field, which is accompanies on wireless power transfer system, the magnetic force and torque is applied to the magnetic material have been researched. In this paper, a multiple wireless power transfer coil based microrobot control is analyzed. The transmitting coil is selectively activated to generate the impulsive magnetic force and torque on a magnetic material based microrobot. The 3D FEM electromagnetic simulation was conducted to validate this idea and the results showed that the magnetic force and torque can be varied according to the incident magnetic field direction by using a multiple transmitting coil.

articleTitle: Near Zero Magnetostrictive Nanocrystalline Fe-Si-B-Cu-Nb Alloys with a High Heating Rate Annealing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A nanocrystalline Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">73.5</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15.5</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.0</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.0</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.0</inf> alloy has near zero magnetostriction (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>), a high saturation magnetic flux density (B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) of 1.23 T and a low coercivity (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) of about 2.5 A/m. Higher B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> than 1.23 T maintaining near zero λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> has been researched with a high heating rate annealing. Near zero magnetostriction with a high heating rate is found in Fe-based nanocrystalline alloys having Si/Fe ratio of about 0.21. Moreover, nanocrystalline Fe-based alloys having about 18at%Si in the α-Fe phase show near zero λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> which is close to that of a nanocrystalline Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">73.5</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15.5</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.0</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.0</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.0</inf> alloy. Saturation magnetic flux density of 1.38 T having near zero λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> is realized with a nanocrystalline Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">76.4</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16.6</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6.0</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.0</inf> alloy. However, nanocrystalline Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">76.4</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16.6</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6.0</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.0</inf> alloy has a crystalline grain size of about 30 nm which is considerably larger than 13 nm of a nanocrystalline Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">73.5</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15.5</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.0</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.0</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.0</inf> alloy and, thus, further research to decrease the coercivity with a high heating rate annealing is needed.

articleTitle: Goos-Hänchen effect for the inelastically scattered spin waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The lateral shift of a spin-wave beam undergoing inelastic scattering on an edge spin wave propagating along the permalloy film's edge is studied. This effect is a counterpart of the Goos-Hänchen effect for the inelastically scattered wave beams, which has not been demonstrated for spin waves. Scattered beams resulting from both the confluence and stimulated splitting processes are analyzed, and their amplitudes are in the range of several percent of the amplitude of the primary reflected beam. The obtained values of the lateral shifts of the inelastically scattered beams to the incident beam spot could be as large as several wavelengths, which is much bigger than the value of the Goos-Hänchen shift for the reflected beam. We believe our findings are an important contribution to nonlinear magnonics, particularly nonlinear spin-wave optics.

articleTitle: Prediction of High Tunnel Magnetoresistance Ratios in (111)-Oriented Junctions with a SrTiO3 Barrier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We theoretically study the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect in novel (111)-oriented magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) with SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> barriers X/SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/X(111) (X = Co, Ni). Our ballistic transport calculation combining the density-functional theory and the Landauder formula obtains high TMR ratios of ~ 500% for the Co-based MTJ and ~300% for the Ni-based MTJ. By analyzing band structures in each region of the MTJs, we find that the high TMR ratios originate from the coherent tunneling of the half-metallic Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> state in Co (Ni), where the Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> state is the rotationally symmetric electronic state along the Λ line corresponding to the [111] direction. Since the in-plane lattice periodicity of SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is twice as long as that of fcc Co (Ni), the original band structures of Co (Ni) are folded in the k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>-k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf> plane, leading to the half-metallicity in the Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> state. The band-folding-driven high TMR ratios found in this study is a novel mechanism of high TMR ratios in (111)-oriented MTJs, in sharp contrast to the interfacial-resonance mechanism reported in our previous works.

articleTitle: Soft-Landing Mechanism Design driven by Electromagnetic Repulsion Force with Application to Bypass Switch
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Bypass switch is an important component to protect power electronic devices in flexible DC transmission system. Due to the fault current rises rapidly, bypass switch must complete the operation quickly in milliseconds. However, the bounce caused by high-speed contact motion will lead to bypass failure. Therefore, design a high-speed soft-landing mechanism based on electromagnetic repulsion, and analyze its dynamic characteristics. Compared with the traditional Solenoid electromagnetic mechanism, it can effectively reduce the contact closing speed to only 1/4 peak value. Finally, the influence of the buffer coil operation on the closing speed is analyzed and discussed. Too early or too late buffer initiating time is not conducive to soft-landing closing. Specific analysis is required for specific structural parameters.

articleTitle: Intrinsic Orbital and Spin Hall Effect in Bismuth Semimetal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We investigate the intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity (OHC) and spin Hall conductivity (SHC) in Bismuth semimetal, by employing sp-orbital tight-binding model. We report a substantial difference between anisotropy of OHC and SHC whose orbital and spin polarization lie within the basal plane. We do not observe substantial correlation between the orbital and spin Berry curvature via spin orbit coupling (SOC) at Fermi energy, disproving the correlation between OHC and SHC in strong SOC regime. We argue the huge SHC in Bi semimetal attributes to its gigantic SOC which strongly affects the hybridization of the p-orbitals, despite its relatively small magnitude of OHC. We hope the distinct anisotropy of OHC and SHC provides a feasible mean to differentiate the two effects in experiments.

articleTitle: Microscopic magnetic properties of two-dimensional magnetic FexGeTe2 films on graphene
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Scalable fabrication of magnetic 2D materials and heterostructures constitutes a crucial step for scaling down current spintronic devices and the development of novel spintronic applications. With this prospect, we have recently succeeded in growing high quality and large area Fe3GeTe2 (F3GT) and Fe5-xGeTe2 (F5GT) epitaxial films via molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) on graphene/SiC(0001) templates. This 2D magnet is extremely promising for such applications, given its highly tunable properties and large potential for room temperature ferromagnetism (FM). Morphological and structural characterization of the films confirmed the realization of large-area, continuous layers with stable interfaces with graphene, and good crystalline quality. Magneto-transport and x-ray magnetic circular dichroism investigations confirmed a robust out-of-plane FM in the layers of F3GT with a Curie temperature of around 220 K. More interestingly, our most recent XMCD findings suggest that F5GT layers exhibit FM up to around 320 K. These results are comparable to state-of-the-art exfoliated flakes from bulk crystals and are highly relevant for further research on wafer-scale growth of van der Waals heterostructures combining FGT with other layered crystals such as transition metal dichalcogenides for the realization of multifunctional, atomically thin devices.

articleTitle: Spin Revolution breaks time reversal symmetry of rolling magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The classical laws of physics are usually invariant under time reversal. Here, we reveal a novel class of magnetomechanical effects rigorously breaking time-reversal symmetry. These effects are based on the mechanical rotation of a hard magnet around its magnetization axis in the presence of friction and an external magnetic field, which we call spin revolution. The spin revolution leads to a variety of symmetry breaking phenomena including upward propulsion on vertical surfaces defying gravity as well as magnetic gyroscopic motion that is perpendicular to the applied force. The angular momentum of spin revolution differs from those of the magnetic field, the magnetic torque, the rolling axis, and the net torque about the rolling axis. The spin revolution emerges spontaneously, without external rotations, and offers various applications in areas such as magnetism, robotics and energy harvesting.

articleTitle: Thickness-dependent SOT effective fields and magnetization control in Topological insulator/2D-ferromagnet Bi2Te3/Cr1+δTe2 Van der Waals heterostructures with PMA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Second harmonic Spin-Orbit Torques (SOT) evaluation has been used to quantify amplitudes of Field-like (FL) and Damping-like (DL) in Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1+δ</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Van der Waals (VdH) heterostructures grown by Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE). Although the FL effective field was found to be larger than the DL component, as expected for interfacial mechanisms for SOT generation, the FL/DL torque-ratio exhibits a non-monotonic dependency on the thickness of the ferromagnet layer. At 10 repetitions of the CrTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> VdH trilayer, the ratio displays its maximum value with the FL field being about 100 times larger than DL field. The amplitudes of DL field are on par with values for Spin-Hall materials. We also report current-induced magnetization reversal in Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1+δ</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA).

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Noise and Vibration for Dual Three-phase IPMSM under Healthy and Multi-phase Open-circuit Fault Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The dual three-phase interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) exhibit excellent fault-tolerant capabilities due to the multiphase winding configuration. Under certain winding failure circumstances, the machine can still provide the expectedly comparable torque as the healthy mode using the fault tolerant control (FTC) to reconstruct the normal rotating magnetomotive force. However, limited attention was paid to the noise and vibration (NV) problems of the dual three-phase IPMSMs in FTC operation. This digest conducts a quantitative comparison on the NV performance of a laboratory dual three-phase IPMSM under healthy and multiphase open-circuit fault conditions controlled by our newly proposed FTC algorithm. The comparative studies involve radial electromagnetic force, acceleration distribution, sound pressure level as well as stator deformation, which are analyzed under both conditions. Based on the research, after applying the FTC, the maximum deformation and sound pressure level of the IPMSM can be mitigated by 6.9% and 12.5%, respectively, compared to ones under fault condition.

articleTitle: A New Observation System for Nonlinear Localized Oscillation Using Commercially Available Magnet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper proposes an Intrinsic Localized Mode (ILM) observation device using a magnetic spring made of a ring-shaped NdFeB magnet. Utilizing magnetic springs composed of ring-shaped magnets in equipment improves the availability of nonlinear springs. We made a holder to obtain the desired nonlinear spring characteristics. The relation between the magnetic repulsive force acting on the magnetic spring and the displacement of the magnetic spring was found to be a cubic function from magnetic field analysis and measurements. This result is equivalent to the lattice interactions in the Fermi Pasta Ulam (FPU) -β lattice. The excitation of ILM using the proposed magnetic spring is found to be theoretically feasible. Numerical simulation of ILM in MATLAB/Simulink using measured magnetic repulsive forces successfully observed localized vibrations. The simulation results show that the ILM can be observed with the proposed system.

articleTitle: Experimental and Theoretical Investigation of Cation Site Occupation and Magnetic Ordering in Co-Ferrite Spinels
