publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Phase pure cobalt ferrite of spinel structure (CoFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) is experimentally synthesized using bulk powder processing methods and characterized using neutron diffraction methods to quantitatively characterize cation site occupation, magnetic moment, and magnetic ordering as a function of temperature. Novel computational techniques based upon a combination of density functional theoretical calculation, machine learning, and Monte Carlo methods are applied to calculate the same quantities for direct comparison with experiments. The obtained results show excellent agreement, and the combination of experimental and theoretical methods enables the unambiguous extraction of exchange bond energies between A-A, B-B, and A-B sites in the spinel structure with excellent agreement to theoretical predictions, as compared to traditional empirical fitting methods using average magnetization as a function of temperature. The proposed methods offer an opportunity to further explore spinel ferrite systems for a deeper understanding of bonding and exchange interactions within these complex and interesting ferrimagnetic systems.

articleTitle: Large Magnetocaloric Effect of PrNi Compound at Liquid-hydrogen Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In the work, polycrystalline PrNi compound was synthesized by the arc-melting method. The Curie temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>) is determined to be 21 K according to the maximum absolute value of first derivative of magnetization. The slope of the Arrott plots is positive around phase transition temperature, indicating of the SOPT characteristic. The magnetic entropy change (-ΔS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf>) was obtained from the isothermal magnetization data based on the Maxwell’s relationship. The maximum value of -ΔS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf> is calculated to be 7.4 and 13.0 J/kg K for the magnetic field changes of 0-2 T and 0-5 T, respectively. The large MCE around 21 K with SOPT feature indicates that PrNi is a possible candidate in the application of magnetic refrigeration for hydrogen liquefaction.

articleTitle: Grain Boundary Engineering of Nd-based ThMn12 Magnets and Their Nitrides
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Grain boundaries in rare earth (RE) permanent magnets are of major importance for magnetically decoupling and sintering densification. In this work, we investigate the grain boundary engineering of the Nd-based ThMn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> magnets and their nitrides. First, we demonstrate the possibility to form a RE-rich grain boundary by adding excess Nd <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Nd}_{\mathrm{x}}\text{Fe}_{10.5}\text{Mo}_{1.5}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{x}=1.2$</tex> and 1.4) in micro- and nanostructured samples. We show that the grain boundary phase is dhcp-Nd and is paramagnetic, being beneficial for magnetically decoupling the grains and optimizing the coercivity. In addition, this phase promotes the liquid-phase sintering process, and we successfully obtained a bulk <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Nd}_{1.2}(\text{Pe}_{2}\text{Mo})_{12}$</tex> sample with a relative density of 95 % using Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS). With adding small amounts of Cu or Ga elements, we were able to tune the grain boundary phase properties in lowering its melting point by forming eutectic phase. Next, we focus on the effect of grain boundary in nitrides. We show that during the nitrogenation process, the dhcp-Nd grain boundary phase reacts with nitrogen to form NdN grain boundary phase, which is paramagnetic at room temperature. However, magnetic characterization suggests that the NdN grain boundary does not influence the magnetic coupling of grains resulting in no further improvement of the coercivity. In addition, NdN inhibits liquid-phase sintering of the nitrided compounds, due to its high melting point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(> 1500^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$</tex>, limiting the relative density to 65% after SPS.

articleTitle: Spacer-less Free-Layer for High-TMR Double Magnetic Tunnel Junction MRAM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The Double Magnetic Tunnel Junction (D-MTJ) is a promising approach to lower the required switching current of Spin Transfer Torque Magnetic Random Access Memory (STT-MRAM). However, one of the primary challenges is that two MgO barriers are required, reducing the Tunnel Magnetoresistance Ratio (TMR) due to both a competing magneto resistance and increase Resistance Area product (RA). In this work, a spacer-less Free-Layer (FL) is proposed to remove the competing TMR, while maintaining the switching current benefit. Device performance demonstrates this with J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sw</inf> = 2.3 MA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 50 ns, for a retention of Δ = 50k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>T while maintaining a TMR = 120%. However, the Spin Torque Efficiency (STE) is still less than that promised in the literature. Micromagnetic simulations are used to show that this is likely due to a competition of a gradient in A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf>, M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> and an anti-symmetric coupling strength across the MgO barriers.

articleTitle: Emergent Magneto-Inductance Effect in Ni45Fe55 Thin Films on Polycarbonate Substrates
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We fabricate Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">45</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">55</inf> thin films on polycarbonate (PC) substrates by using thermal evaporation and investigate their structural and magnetic properties. Atomic force microscopy reveals that the surface roughness is small at 0.96 nm in Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">45</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">55</inf> thin films on PC substrates. Magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements indicate that Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">45</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">55</inf> thin films on PC substrates are magnetically soft. In the Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">45</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">55</inf> thin films on PC substrates, we have successfully observed the emergent magneto-inductance (ML) effect at room temperature. The ML ratio increases at lower frequencies, and it reaches 218% at 2 kHz. The observed emergent ML effect can be explained by spin motive force originating from the motion of domain walls under a stepwise external magnetic field.

articleTitle: Vertical long pillar magnetic memory with two magnetic junctions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A vertical ferromagnetic (FM) pillar is proposed for use as magnetic memory with high thermal stability. The current-induced magnetization reversal of long pillars is a significant challenge in spintronic applications. We propose a novel magnetization reversal method for long pillars, based on spin injection and spin-polarized current. The magnetization direction of the pillar was controlled by the direction of the current flowing through the pillar. The magnetized direction of the pillar was determined from the two magnetoresistance values in the proposed structure. The magnetization reversal was demonstrated by a micromagnetic model simulation. A domain wall (DW) was produced during magnetization reversal. We also propose that a three-value magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) can be developed by maintaining the DW in the pillar. Consequently, the proposed memory writing scheme paves the way for next-generation spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Heat and current annealing effects on magnetic properties of Fe-rich glass-coated amorphous microwires with different radius
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: For Fe-rich glass-coated microwires to be a competitive option for magnetic technologies, the enhancing and tuning of their properties is necessary, and therefore, a better understanding of these processes is also needed. In this work, two Fe microwires with different geometries are subjected to both conventional and current annealings to study their effects. Results show a general enhancement of magnetic softness and domain wall dynamics after both treatments, also suggesting an earlier onset of crystallization in thin samples.

articleTitle: Surrogate-Based Modeling of Induction Machines to Reduce the Computational Burden of Robust Multi-Objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: One of the main obstacles to robust design optimization of induction machines (IM) is the high computational burden, which is mainly due to time-intensive nonlinear finite element (FE) simulations. The large multivariable design space of electric machine optimization typically requires running thousands of simulations taking many hours, if not days which is quite prohibitive. To overcome this bottleneck, hybridization of FE-based optimization with approximate models can lead to expedite the process. This paper is focused on accelerating the typical FE-based optimization scenarios by implementing and systematically studying an ensemble of surrogate models of IMs in terms of computational burden and performance. In this regard, after adopting the most significant surrogate model, a two-step surrogate-based optimization approach is developed. Compared with direct FE-based robust optimization, competitive results are achieved by adopting the proposed hybrid surrogate-based approach and the overall runtime is reduced by 69%. Furthermore, as a case study, an optimization problem for an 11-kW IM is considered by applying the typical FE-based optimization task followed by the proposed hybrid technique. Hence, the achievable speed improvements, as well as further possible enhancing means are discussed. The detailed comparison of the presented surrogate models makes a comprehensive source for engineers and designers to follow.

articleTitle: Skin effect in Iron-Silicon steel sheets: from low inductions to saturation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: High frequencies are ubiquitous in power applications: most electrical equipment such as electrical machines are supplied by Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) switching inverters, often working at tens or hundreds of kilohertz. PWM is responsible of minor cycles along the major hysteresis loop, lasting a few microseconds. Such minor loops can cause deep skin effect, even if the thinnest laminations (0.20 mm thick laminations or even lower) provided by steel sheets manufacturers are used. Moreover, common mode currents in the megahertz range, flowing from electrical machines windings to the machine’s chassis through capacitive effects, can be responsible of strong electromagnetic disturbances and bearing damages. A correct prediction of these high frequency phenomena is necessary for an accurate calculation of the common mode filter, requiring a magnetic model of the laminated cores adapted to high frequencies and low inductions. For power conversion applications, such as the transformers embedded in planes, the necessity to reduce the core volume, often made of high-permeability grain-oriented (HGO) materials, has increased the conversion frequency from a few hundreds of hertz to several kilohertz. However, the peak induction remains very high, to reduce the cross-sectional area of the laminations. Consequently, HGO materials can be subjected to high induction values in the kHz range. Although the problem is quite different from the low induction case, skin effect must be considered. This case is made especially complex by the material non-linearity and calls for specific models and experimental methods. In this work, we summarize recent modeling advances we have achieved in this field. We treat first the low induction case, with focus on the behavior of thin non-oriented (NO) sheets. We consider then the case of high-permeability grainoriented (HGO) sheets magnetized at high polarization values, which requires non-linear models, and we validate our predictions by magneto-optical observations of the domain wall dynamics.

articleTitle: Effect of Annealing Temperature on Structure and Magnetic Properties of Ultra-thin High-Purity Iron Ribbons
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper reports the effect of annealing temperature on structure and magnetic properties of ultra-thin high-purity iron ribbons. The grains of the ribbons decreased and increased as the annealing temperature increased. The preferred orientation of the ribbons changed from (100) and (111) to random orientation as the annealing temperature increased. These structural changes with annealing might be due to the secondary recrystallization. Magnetic properties such as the coercivity and complex permeability of these ribbons, were dependent on the annealing temperature, suggesting that these parameters were related to the change in grain size and crystal orientation with annealing. Therefore, these results demonstrate that the ultra-thin high-purity Fe ribbons with high-temperature annealing are one of the candidates for soft magnetic materials for the next-generated power electronics devices.

articleTitle: Silicide formation at lower temperatures for cobalt and nickel on √3 x √3R30°-Ag/Si(111)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Because of the ease of formation, and good lattice match with Si, metal silicides often result in the formation of high-quality epitaxial layers and have established themselves over the years as important technological materials for use in industrial processes. To pave the way for industry applications of silicides, a concrete understanding of different transition metal/silicon interfaces is crucial. In this report, we propose a molecular-incident reaction effect (MoIRE) model that successfully explains the different chemical reactions for Co/Si and Ni/Si interfaces by the introduction of a $\sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 R{30^o} - {\text{Ag}}\,{\text{layer}}$. The interaction transfer of silicon atoms forms a Co silicide for ${\text{Co}}/\sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 R{30^o} - {\text{Ag}}/{\text{Si}}(111)$ with a thickness of a few nanometers, thus greatly reducing the temperature needed for the formation of a layered CoSi2 silicide compared to that for typical CoSi2 silicide formation at a Co/Si interface. Based on the MoIRE mechanism, the introduction of the $\sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 R{30^o} - {\text{Ag}}\,{\text{layer}}$ as an intermediate layer permits the silicidation temperature needed to produce a NiSi layer to be reduced to 400 K from typically above 600 K. This approach is advantageous for the formation of a silicide at the Ni/Si interface at low temperature and opens a possible way of fabricating Si-based spintronic devices at lower temperatures.

articleTitle: Tuning Spin-Orbit Torque Generation Via Seed/Heavy Metal Interface Modification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Investigations of spin generation and accumulation at the seed layer/heavy metal interface have remained elusive. In this study, we systematically investigate spin-orbit torque (SOT) switching efficiency with different seed layers X={dielectric MgO, metal Ti} beneath the heavy metal Pt, in the substrate/X/Pt/Co perpendicularly magnetized heterostructures. An enhancement of SOT efficiency has been observed in the heterostructure with Ti seed layer, compared to that of inserting MgO. This is attributed to the high spin absorption in Ti seed layer, less spin reflection from Ti/Pt interface, resulting in more net spin accumulation on Pt/Co interface. Moreover, the SOT-induced Co magnetization switching at zero external magnetic field has been observed in the heterostructure with MgO seed layer, due to the strong spin reflection from the insulating MgO layer. This work provides an in-depth understanding of the impacts of the spin reflection from the X/Pt interface and spin transport with different seed layers, which paves an additional way to tune the spin generation in terms of both magnitude and orientation for pursuing high-performance SOT devices.

articleTitle: Mechanical, electrical and optical control of magnetization reversals and spin dynamics in extrinsic multiferroics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Galfenol thin films have attracted a large amount of interest in the last two decades. Indeed, it is of interest to understand the fundamental mechanisms driving the strain and magnetic coupling in thin films. This study focuses on thin Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.81</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.19</inf> (FeGa) films of thickness 5, 10, 20, and 60 nm deposited by sputtering onto glass substrates, PMN-PZT substrates and Aluminium foils. FeGa magnetostrictive properties were characterized using optical deflectometry. This first study reveals a remarkable thickness dependence, with an effective magnetoelastic coefficient decrease with an a thickness increase. A 10 nm Fe-Ga thin film was grown on Al kitchen foil and then mechanically strained under an isotropic configuration using spherical optical lenses. The FeGa MR properties under such a mechanical strain were determined. The results indicate the development of a random anisotropy character due to the bending. Under an electric field, a large converse magneto-electric effect for the Fe-Ga/PMN-PZT layered structure is observed. This effect is shown to be angular dependent. Finally, light control of static and dynamic magnetic properties in the Blue region is demonstrated. It is achieved with a CW laser or a LED.

articleTitle: Control of Magnetization Precession Frequency Using Current Density of Spin-Orbit Torque Applied to Local Area
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We numerically study current density dependence of magnetization dynamics in a local area induced by the spin-orbit torque as a source of spin waves. The precession frequency of magnetization dynamics shows large change at a critical current density, which controls the wave length of spin waves. The origin of the change is due to the increase of exchange field caused by the magnetization torsion at the interface between SOT-applied and non-applied regions. Our new finding gives a way to manipulate spin wave’s properties by controlling the magnetization direction in a local area.

articleTitle: Nd-Fe-B Hydrogenation-Disproportionation-Dehydrogenation-Recombination (HDDR) magnet for variable magnetic flux motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The variable magnetic flux permanent magnet synchronous motor (VMF-PMSM) is one of the next-generation technologies to improve the efficiency of PMSM. VMF-PMSMs require the magnets with high magnetizability and minor curve flatness that are difficult for conventional Nd-Fe-B magnets to acquire. In this work, we developed (Nd-Sm)-Fe-B HDDR magnet with much improved magnetizability and minor curve flatness compared to conventional sintered magnets, by densifying HDDR powders while maintaining sub μm-sized main phase grains, and also observed the feature of microstructure unique to this magnet.

articleTitle: Application of all-optical switching for a high-speed optical memory. Proposed scheme of high-speed demultiplexing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Optical recording and demultiplexing are two essential functions of a high-speed optical memory. The mechanism of the all-optical switching in an external magnetic field and the toggle switching are based on a heating and cooling of magnetic lattices and, as a result, are relatively slow. In contrast, the spin-transfer optical switching does not rely on the heating/ cooling and, therefore, can be fast. We proposed and demonstrated experimentally the spin-transfer demultiplexing at a speed of 2.2 TBit/sec. We discuss possibilities of improving efficiency of the spin-transfer optical switching to fit requirements of the high-speed optical memory.

articleTitle: A Novel Winding Connection Sequence of Dual Three-Phase Series-End Winding PMSM Drive for Speed Range Extension
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Series-end winding motor drives double the dc-link voltage utilization compared with the conventional star-connected winding counterparts, which indicates that series-end winding motor drives are suitable for high-speed applications with limited dc-link voltage. To further improve the dc-link voltage utilization and extend the speed range of the dual three-phase series-end winding permanent magnet synchronous motor (DTSW-PMSM) drive system, this paper develops a novel winding connection sequence (WCS) for DTSW-PMSM drive, and the dc-link voltage utilization is further improved by 36.6% compared with the normal WCS. The dc-link voltage utilizations of different WCSs are analyzed through the phasor relationship between the phase and leg voltages. In the experimental tests, the speed range of the DTSW-PMSM drive with the proposed WCS is extended significantly. Therefore, adopting the proposed WCS can be an effective means for further speed range extension of DTSW-PMSM drives without additional hardware.

articleTitle: Influence of Free Layer Surface Roughness on Tunnel Magnetoresistance in 300 mm CMOS-compatible MTJ Stacks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) is a highly versatile device widely used in magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM), magnetic sensors and prospective as a read device in racetrack memory. Tuning the MTJ stack to match the desired properties, such as tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR), magnetic anisotropy or coercive field of the free layer, requires careful optimization of the deposition parameters as well as precise thickness control. Here, the deposition of individual layers in a wedged manner across 300 mm wafers is proposed to engineer the thicknesses within the stack more efficiently. Furthermore, this technique provides detailed insights into effects related to surface roughness, magnetic anisotropy and TMR.

articleTitle: Nucleation, stabilization, annihilation, and transformation of topological spin textures for reservoir computing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Topological spin textures have been considered as one of the prominent candidates for low power consumption physical reservoir computing. In this work, we fabricated a micro-sized symmetry breaking multilayered disk composing of stacks FeCo/CoNi/Pt as a reservoir for topology spin textures. We found the nucleation, stabilization, annihilation of topological spin textures in the disk can be controlled by a current in a ring outside the disk. We also found the transformation between skyrmions and bimerons can be achieved by simply tailoring the amplitude and frequency of the AC current. The phenomenal can be explained by the concurrent effects of oersted field, joule heating, and magnetostriction of the current. Due the concurrent effects, we find an abnormal dependance of magnetization on the applied current at low current frequency. Namely, the films keep perpendicular magnetization at low applied currents but transition to in-plane magnetization with sufficiently large current. Photo-elastic microscope observations show a sufficient large stress is created if we apply a current to the ring coil. Nucleation, stabilization, annihilation, and transformation of the topological spin textures provided a robust, nonlinearity, and memory physics system for carrying out reservoir computing.

articleTitle: Spin-fluctuation induced enhancement for pure spin current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, we study the interplay of pure spin current and spin fluctuation in ferromagnetic NiCu alloys. By tuning the compositions of the alloys, we shift the Curie temperature in a wide range. We demonstrate a significantly enhanced spin current through spin fluctuation at the Curie temperature. Most importantly, in the specific composition of Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>, we obtain an unprecedentedly large spin Hall angle of 46%, about 5 times larger than that of Pt at room temperature. The 3d magnetic alloys function as higly efficient spin Hall materials.

articleTitle: Using magnetic tunnel junctions as unconventional computing devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Hardware for specialized computing tasks is becoming more and more relevant in computational research due to the nearing intrinsic physical limitations of Von Neumann architecture. Most of the industrially relevant problems belong to the combinatorial optimization class and require a nondeterministic approach to be solved efficiently. To this end, magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) are one of the best candidate devices as building blocks to implement unconventional computation paradigms thanks to their tunable stochasticity, their size, and their compatibility with current CMOS technologies. Here, we present an MTJ-based implementation of two state-of-the-art paradigms, evaluate them and compare them over relevant computational problems.

articleTitle: Quantifying the magnetic anisotropy of individual nanomagnets embedded in biological entities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Nanomagnets can nowadays be found in a myriad of applications as diverse as data storage, tissue engineering or cancer theragnostic. All these applications rely on the magnetic properties of the nanomagnets which are mostly determined by their magnetic anisotropy. Despite its importance, the magnetic anisotropy of the individual magnetic nanostructures is unknown. Indeed, the implementation of magnetic nanoparticles relies on average values obtained by measuring a plethora of dissimilar entities. Here we present a method capable of working out the magnetic anisotropy constant and the magnetic easy axis of individual magnetic nanostructures embedded in biological entities by combining scanning transmission X-ray microscopy using an axi-asymmetric magnetic field with theoretical simulations based on the Stoner−Wohlfarth model. This method may be considered general and be applied to any nanomagnetic system.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Magnetic Geared Permanent Magnet Machine to Improve Electromagnetic Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a design and analysis method for magnetic geared permanent magnet machines (MGPMMs), which improve driving performance and loss reduction. First, an initial design model with outstanding operating characteristics (wide operating range and low torque ripple) has been developed according to the pole-slot combination selected and gear ratio. Based on the initial model, the loss reduction method of MGPMMs is presented. Finally, this paper discusses several ways for reducing losses and thereby improving the electromagnetic performance of MGPMMs.

articleTitle: Generalised Form of the Magnetic Anisotropy Field in Micromagnetic and Atomistic Spin Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A general approach to the derivation of effective anisotropy fields for Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics is presented. The approach is based on the gradient in spherical polar coordinates with the final results being expressed in Cartesian coordinates as usually applied in atomistic and micromagnetic model calculations. The approach is generally valid for all orders of anisotropies including higher order combinations of azimuthal and rotational anisotropies often found in functional magnetic materials especially permanent magnets. The anisotropies are represented in terms of spherical harmonics which have the important property of rational temperature scaling.

articleTitle: Dynamic Performance Analysis of The Variable Speed Ratio Magnetic Gear
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic characteristics of a variable speed ratio magnetic gear (VSRMG) by using a dynamic performance analysis method, which is based on the torque look-up table model of the VSRMG obtained by finite element analysis (FEA). The dynamic characteristics under different conditions such as start-up, the abrupt load changes and speed regulated are studied. It is found that the VSRMG exhibits speed oscillations on the loaded rotor during star-up, speed regulated and under load disturbances, but it stabilizes quickly under the influence of system damping. The experimental results verify the reliability of this dynamic performance analysis method.

articleTitle: FeNi-based Nanocomposite Soft Magnetic Alloy Magnetic and Mechanical Property Tailoring Through Flash Annealing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Tailoring details of thermal processing, including controlled heating rates and annealing time, plays a key role in the enhancement of soft magnetic properties of amorphous and nanocrystalline soft magnetic materials. In particular, rapid thermal processing also known as flash annealing has shown potential for grain size refinement, tailoring of phase identity, and tuning of magnetic properties. This work explores the differences between conventional furnace annealing and isothermal annealing with flash annealing techniques for a range of detailed thermal processing conditions (temperature, time, cooling method) in an FeNi-based alloy. As compared to conventional annealing, flash annealing results in dominant FCC γ FeNi phase with refined grains. Microstructural refinement due to flash annealing showed improved soft magnetic properties with reduced coercivity and improved ductility for improved core manufacturing at scale.

articleTitle: Computationally Efficient Estimation of PWM-induced Iron Loss of PMSM using Deep Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: As the demand for increasing the efficiency of traction motor for increasing the mileage of electric vehicles, it is necessary to accurately estimate the efficiency of traction motor at the early design stage. Since the iron loss of the traction motor is highly affected by the pulse width modulation (PWM) frequency, the PWM current should be considered when designing the motor. However, it is difficult in considering the PWM current at early design stage because of its high computation cost. Therefore, we propose a method to reduce the computation cost for the calculation of PWM-induced iron loss using deep transfer learning. The proposed method can be achieved by training a neural network that can predict PWM-induced iron loss accurately using a large amount of sinusoidal current-based iron loss and a small amount of PWM-induced iron loss. As a result, the PWM current can be practically considered in design stage of traction motor because the computation cost can be decreased by using the proposed method.

articleTitle: New versatile instruments to measure element-specific and macroscopic hysteresis at ID12 of the ESRF
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this contribution we will present two new instruments implemented at the beamline ID12 of the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF) in the framework of the ULMAG – "Ultimate MAGnetic characterization" collaborative project. These instruments offer the ESRF users a unique possibility to measure under strictly the same experimental conditions the element-specific X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS)/X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD), and X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) simultaneously with various macroscopic properties (magnetization, magnetostriction, magnetocaloric, magnetoresistance), as a function of magnetic field (up to 17 T) and temperature (5-325 K). To demonstrate the potential and features of these scientific instruments, we will present two case studies: (1) FeRh, which has a first-order anti-ferromagnetic to ferromagnetic transition around room temperature and (2) HoCo2, which exhibits a first-order ferrimagnetic to paramagnetic transition. These two cases demonstrate new horizons for studying the physics of magnetic materials, where the interplay between the magnetic, structural, and electronic subsystems of the solid is essential.

articleTitle: Compositionally magnetostrictive response of perpendicularly magnetized Ta/CoFe(B)/MgO films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetostriction effect in Ta/Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</inf>(B)[CoFe(B)]/MgO for alloy compositions spanning Fe-rich (x=20) to Co-rich (x=80) films has been studied in order to investigate the relation between magnetostriction and the onset of perpendicular magnetic anisotropy at the Ta/CoFe(B)/MgO interfaces. By considering the Ta/CoFe(B) and CoFe(B)/MgO interfaces as atomistic volumes with in-plane (ip) and out-of-plane (op) orbital magnetizations, respectively, the relative ratio of ip to op orbital magnetization in the atomistic volumes is found to be closely related to the dependence of magnetostriction constant (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) on Co composition. The findings suggest that the composition dependence of ip and op orbital magnetization at the CoFe(B)/MgO interface caused by the relative population of op (ip) orbital moment, plays an important role in controlling the interfacial anisotropy and magnetostriction property at the interface.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Spin-Orbit-Torque-Induced Coherent Magnetization Switching with Picosecond Current Pulses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spin-orbit-torque (SOT)-based magnetization switching offers the promise of fast switching speed at low current density. However, recent SOT switching studies show an incubation delay in the ~ns range due to stochasticity in the nucleation of a magnetic domain during the domain-wall-driven magnetization switching. Here, we experimentally observe ultrafast SOT-induced coherent magnetization switching dynamics with no incubation delay primarily driven by an ultrafast thermal anisotropy torque. We employ an ultrafast photo-conducting switch and a co-planar strip line to generate and guide a ~9 ps current pulse into the heavy metal/ferromagnetic layer stack and thereby induce ultrafast SOT. The magnetization crosses zero in ~70 ps and complete switching occurs in ~250 ps. A good agreement between our experimental results and a macro-spin simulation model confirms that the switching dynamics are coherent and ultrafast heating-induced thermal anisotropy torque is responsible for the coherent switching. These results show a new way to dramatically increase the writing speed of SOT-induced magnetization switching within a coherent regime.

articleTitle: DEM simulation of the single-directional pressed and double-directional pressed Nd-Fe-B compacts
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, the differences between single-directional pressed (SDP) and double-directional pressed (DDP) Nd-Fe-B compacts were investigated by using discrete element method (DEM) simulation, especially the difference in alignment degree distribution of compacts. The results show that the DDP compact has a higher alignment degree than the SDP compact since the difference in movement distance between particles in different sections of the DDP compact was smaller during the pressing process. And the distribution of the alignment degree of the DDP compact is more uniform than that of the SDP compact. In both of the DDP and SDP compacts, the central section has a higher alignment degree in the direction of the applied magnetic field, and particles close to the punch had a lower alignment degree because they traveled a longer distance than middle particles and were subjected to a larger compressive force.

articleTitle: Resonant Magnetoelastic Coupling Between Magnetic Vortex and Lattice Breathing Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Optical photons are ideal carriers for long-distance transmission, while state-of-the-art quantum processors, such as supercon-ducting qubits, operate at microwave frequencies. An important requirement for networked quantum computation is therefore the ability to coherently convert the quantum information from microwave to optical frequencies and vice-versa. We theoretically address a scheme to achieve this via an intermediate conversion to magnons that enhances the weak direct magneto-optical coupling. We wish to demonstrate the feasibility of such a scheme by employing the magnetoelastic coupling between the modes of a magnetic vortex (vortex breathing mode, VBM) and that of the lattice (elastic breathing mode, EBM), which requires no additional external bias field. In our setup all but the opto-mechanical coupling can be made resonant. We propose an alternative Mumax3 simulation post-processing procedure for semi-classical normalization, where we use regression analysis of the the internal energy dependency on excitation amplitude in a limit cycle motion. We provide estimates for direct resonant coupling between the VBM and the EBM.

articleTitle: Extraordinary magnetoresistance in a 2-terminal structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Extraordinary magnetoresistance (EMR) is a phenomenon discovered by Solin et al. at the interface between a metal (high conductivity material) and a semiconductor (high mobility material). EMR is a much larger effect than the other magnetoresistive phenomenon, reaching values up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> %. In this work, we present simulation results to determine if it is possible to realize EMR-based power limiters, by defining more clearly the differences between 4- and 2-terminal geometries in term of performance for power limiter applications, as well as the dependence of the EMR with different material properties and different shapes.

articleTitle: Hybrid precorrected FFT - Poisson solver method for the magnetostatic field in finite element micromagnetic modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A hybrid integral evaluation – differential equation approach is introduced for the computation of the magnetostatic fields in finite element method based micromagnetic solvers. The approach calculates the magnetostatic field at the boundary of the computational domain or any additional surfaces by direct superposition via a fast approach, such as precorrected fast Fourier transform and uses this surface values to formulate a Poisson equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions to compute the field in the bulk of the structure. The benefits of this hybrid approach are a significant reduction of the sparse matrices used in the accurate integral evaluation with the associated memory reduction as well as the ability to subdivide the problem into a set of smaller problems for parallelization.

articleTitle: Observation of Magnetoresistance Caused by Orbital Angular Momentum Accumulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report a sizable angular dependent magnetoresistance (ADMR) in a Tm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>/oxidized Cu (CuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) heterostructure, which cannot be attributed to the spin Hall magnetoresistance in lack of elements with large spin-orbit coupling. Different from the orbital Rashba-Edelstein magnetoresistance proposed previously, the ADMR depends on the magnitude of magnetic field rather than the magnetization of magnetic layer. Based on contrast experiment, we conclude that the ADMR originates from the electrically induced orbital angular momentum (OAM) accumulating at the interface of insulator/CuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x.</inf> Our findings not only reveal the transmission and accumulation of OAM in insulator/CuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> heterojunction but also provide important experimental evidences towards the microscopic understanding of the OAM interaction with magnetic field.

articleTitle: Improved Detectivity in Tunnel Magnetoresistance Sensors by Controlling Free Layer Thickness and Annealing process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Detectivity is an important figure-of-merit for evaluating the magnetic field resolution of a magnetic sensor. In this work, MgO based tunnel magnetoresistance sensors with an amorphous-CoFeSiB free layer were fabricated. A two-step annealing technique was utilized to achieve good linearity with a small magnetic hysteresis. The dependances of magnetic and noise properties of these sensors on the free layer thickness and annealing process have been studied. An improvement in the sensitivity and a lowest detectivity of 1.06 nT/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sup> at 10 Hz was obtained for devices with free layer thickness of 80 nm and annealed at 180 °C. The detectivity value further decreased to 0.9 nT/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sup> for the devices for which the second annealing was performed at 225 °C. Another set of devices annealed at the same temperature, but after the microfabrication process, exhibited a minimum detectivity of 0.4 nT/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sup>.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Segment Method to Reduce PM Eddy-Current Loss in Axial Flux PM Wheel Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The high permanent magnet (PM) eddy-current loss will cause the risk of irreversible demagnetization. To reduce the PM eddy-current loss, the PM complete segmentation method (CSM) is a widely applied. However, the PM CSM will increase the cost and assembly process especially for axial flux PM (AFPM) motors. To address this problem, a new arc incompletion segmentation method (AISM) is proposed to reduce the PM eddy current loss and cost, including double-side AISM and single-side AISM. Then, some of the key parameters are optimized. In addition, the PM eddy current loss, cost and torque performance are compared with different segmentation methods under different conditions based on 3-D finite element method (FEM). Finally, two different 25kW prototypes are manufactured and tested to validate the proposed method and analysis.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Wound Laminated Cores for a Dual-Axial Gap Induction Motor under PWM Excitation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We are developing a high-speed high-efficiency 3-phase 8-pole dual-axial gap induction motor. Since this motor is driven by a PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) power supply that operate at high modulation and carrier frequencies, stator cores and a rotor core with particularly low eddy current loss are required. We have developed a new wound laminated ring core for this motor by winding a 0.08 mm thick ultra-thin electrical steel strip. The newly developed core was called a "wound laminated core". This wound laminated core had extremely small eddy current loss at high frequency in both sinusoidal excitation and PWM excitation. Therefore, it was an excellent material for the stator core for high-speed high-efficiency motors.

articleTitle: Optical Profiling of Surface-Acoustic-Wave Absorption due to Elastically Driven Ferromagnetic Resonance in Nickel
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We optically characterized the local changes in the amplitude and phase of a surface vibration that are associated with the magnetoelastic effect. Pulsed laser interferometry was used to directly probe the amplitude and phase of a surface acoustic wave (SAW) propagating on a nickel thin film in a magnetic field, and a conversion from the angular momentum of the SAW to that of the macroscopic spin system was clearly observed. Pulsed laser interferometry opens the door to local probe and spatial mapping of magnon–phonon conversion in various magnetic materials, which can lead to further progress in fundamental and applied research related to magnetism.

articleTitle: Dual Induction Eddy Current Probe for Vibration Noise Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Eddy current testing is widely used in manufacturing processes of bars and tubes to detect cracks on the product surface. In eddy current testing, signals originating from product vibration and cracks are detected. This paper quantitatively describes the performance of a dual induction eddy current probe that selectively suppresses only the vibration signal from detection signals. The probe employs the dual induction method that simultaneously performs self and mutual inductions. Simulation and measurement results show that suppression of the vibration signal improves the signal-to-noise ratio of crack signals.

articleTitle: Enhanced soft magnetic properties in N-doped amorphous FeCo thin film
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Here we report, highly resistive FeCo thin films with enhanced soft magnetic properties (low coercivity and magnetic anisotropy) by incorporating nitrogen (N) in the amorphous system. N-doped FeCo films (FeCoN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, x= 15, 17.5 and 19%) are deposited in N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>+Ar environment with N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flow rate up to 19%. Systematic magnetic and microstructural studies reveal optimum level of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flow (17.5%) to obtain minimum coercivity (~7.8 Oe) along hard axis of the film.

articleTitle: Novel Stator Multi-Tooth Hybrid Permanent Magnet Memory Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, the stator multi-tooth structure is introduced into the traditional stator flux-concentrating permanent magnet memory machine (SFCPM-MM), and a novel stator multi-tooth hybrid permanent magnet memory motor(SMTHP-MM) is proposed. The space occupied by the armature winding can be solved by placing the magnetized winding and permanent magnet between the adjacent stator teeth. Compared with the traditional DSPM, the multi-tooth structure can shorten the distance between adjacent stator teeth, reduce the amount of permanent magnets, and improve the utilization rate of permanent magnets while improving the torque. Due to its low coercive force(LCF), AlNiCo magnet provides flexibility for in-line application of transient current pulses to the controllability of air gap fluxes. Finally, experiments are conducted to verify its good electromagnetic characteristics.

articleTitle: Design of two-dimensional magnonic crystals using yttrium iron garnets and non-magnetic metals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Two-dimensional magnonic crystals (2D MCs) for forward volume spin waves were designed using the finite integration technique. The calculated model consisted of a 170 mm × 170 mm × 0.6 mm substrate with two microstrip lines (MSLs), and a 15 mm  × 15 mm × 10 μm yttrium iron garnet (YIG) film placed on top of the MSLs. The 2D MCs consisted of Cu dots with a diameter of 300 μm and a thickness of 1 μm periodically located on the YIG film. Two types of periodic structures, a square configuration and a hexagonal configuration, were fabricated. The reflected spin waves from the edge of the YIG film were suppressed by placing 30-nm thick Au films, and a magnonic bandgap of 2D MCs was observed. In addition, the shift of the magnonic bandgap was obtained when the incident angles of spin waves to 2D MCs were varied.

articleTitle: Spin Swapping Effect of Band Structure Origin in Centrosymmetric Ferromagnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We show the spin swapping effect originated from band structure in centrosymmetric ferromagnets. Without breaking inversion symmetry or introducing spin-orbit impurities, the effect is attributed to anticrossings at which bands with different spin and different orbital are nearly degenerate, and thus has no analogue in nonmagnets. First-principle calculations for centrosymmetric 3d transition metal ferromagnets support the analysis based on analytic and tight-binding models and demonstrate the sizable spin swapping conductivity of band origin ~ 2500 (ħ/e)(Ωcm)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. Our theory generalizes the understanding on the transverse spin currents of ferromagnets and highlights the role of orbital degree of freedom in spin-orbit-coupled transport.

articleTitle: Write-error rate estimation of voltage-controlled magnetization switching in a magnetic-topological-insulator-based device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We theoretically investigate influences of electronic circuit delay, noise and temperature on write-error-rate (WER) in voltage-controlled magnetization switching operation of a magnetic topological insulator (MTI) device by means of the micromagnetic simulation. This device realizes magnetization switching via spin-orbit torque (SOT) and voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) which are derived from 2D-Dirac electronic structure. As a result, this device is not easily affected by peripheral electrical circuits and is extremely robust against circuit delay and signal-to-noise ratio. The WERs as a function of temperature are extremely low due to steep change in VCMA. Furthermore, the larger SOT can improve thermal stability factor. This study provides a new perspective for developing voltage-driven spintronic devices with ultra-low power consumption.

articleTitle: The Pulse Magnetic Field Controls the TNF-α of the BALB _ C Mice Injected with LPS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Among diverse mechanisms for treatment of chronic inflammatory diseases, reducing the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines is most effective. In this study, the anti-inflammatory effect of the pulsed magnetic field(PMF) was confirmed in vivo by measuring the amount of pro-inflammatory cytokine <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TNF-}\alpha$</tex> according to the presence or absence of PMF stimulation, after inducing inflammation in the mouse by injecting LPS. Also lung histopathological studies demonstrated protective effects of PMF against LPS-induced lung injury.

articleTitle: Wireless Inductive Displacement Sensor 3D Printed using Additive Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents an application of 3D printing technology for the production of a flexible inductive displacement sensor. In order to achieve wireless measurements, the sensor is designed in the form of an Archimedean spiral, which has two electrical contacts: a central inner and an outer one. When displacement is applied to the spiral center, an increase in the distance between the adjacent windings of the spiral is achieved. As a result, there will be a decrease in inductance, i.e. an increase in the sensor’s self-resonant frequency. The change in resonant frequency is detected using an external coil (antenna) mounted close to the sensor. The resonant frequency of the system (sensor and antenna) is determined by finding its phase dip minimum. This way the resonant frequency vs. displacement characteristic is obtained. The displacement measurement range is up to 30 mm. The calculated sensitivity of the proposed system design is 0.27 MHz/mm.

articleTitle: Propagating Spin-Wave Spectroscopy at Millikelvin Temperatures Using Arbitrary Magnetisation Orientations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Large-scale integrated magnonic circuits for quantum applications require the operation of nanostructured magnetic materials, such as yttrium-iron-garnet, at cryogenic temperatures. To initialise, manipulate and read out these circuits, different technological challenges must be overcome. One of these challenges is the precise orientation of external magnetic fields at millikelvin temperatures, for example to align the magnonic circuits precisely or to generate different spin-wave modes. Based on recent results, we discuss in this manuscript propagating spin waves in a 100 nm-thin yttrium-iron-garnet film at millikelvin temperatures, using arbitrary magnetisation orientations.

articleTitle: Synthesis and characterization of single phase γ-Co47Ni22Al31 Heusler alloy nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Off-stoichiometric single phase γ-Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">47</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</inf> nanoparticles have been synthesized by a facile template-less chemical method. The nanoparticles could be obtained in a single secondary cubic (γ) phase crystal structure with average particle size of 68±1 nm and average crystallite size of 36±1 nm for the first time. These nanoparticles exhibited soft ferromagnetic behavior with very high magnetic moment of 87.99 emu/gm at 5 K and Curie temperature 705 K.

articleTitle: Investigating magnetocrystalline anisotropy in the system Au/Co-Staircase/Au(788) by using XMCD
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Here, we report the investigation of the influence of the magnetocrystalline anisotropy (MCA) in Cobalt ultrathin films grown on the vicinal surface Au(788), through the anisotropy of the orbital magnetic moment. The aim of this study was to apply the X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) technique to probe the spin magnetic moment and the orbital magnetic moment anisotropy within the spin reorientation transition (SRT) range in the system Au/Co-Staircase/Au(788). The influence of increasing Co film thickness on SRT, from easy out-of-plane magnetization axis to in-plane magnetization was investigated by means of the magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE). The preparation and surface quality of the Co films were characterized using LEED and STM surface experimental techniques. Analysis of XMCD measurements as a function of the film thickness for Au/Co-staircase/Au(788) shows the anisotropic orbital magnetic moment during the SRT regime (8 to 12 ML range) indicating a decreasing influence of MCA with the increased thickness and nearly isotropic orbital magnetic moment above 12 ML, with a small MCA influence.

articleTitle: Preparation of Fe-B/epoxy composite films by the LbL-assisted composite plating method using epoxy-coated Fe-B fine particles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Metal-insulator composite films, including Fe-B particles and insulating epoxy films, were synthesized by the layer-by-layer (LbL)-assisted composite plating method. In this method, charged magnetic particles are attracted to the cathode by electrostatic force simultaneously with insulating epoxy thin film deposition. To suppress the oxidation of Fe-B fine particles in the reaction aqueous solution for Fe-B/epoxy composite film deposition, Fe-B fine particles were coated with epoxy by using the electroless plating method. It was clear that epoxy coating on Fe-B fine particles effectively prevents oxidation of the fine particles. It was also found that the epoxy coating rate on the Fe-B fine particles could be controlled by adjusting the concentration of the water-dissolved epoxy in the reaction solution. The film deposited using epoxy-coated Fe-B fine particles exhibited a smoother film surface than those obtained using uncoated Fe-B fine particles. However, the highest amount of Fe-B content obtained in the deposited film was approximately 36 wt.% using Fe-B fine particles with a concentration of 1.0 g/L.

articleTitle: Cold Workability and Magnetic Properties of FeCo-V Alloys with the Addition of a Small Amount of Aluminum
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Aluminum oxide films on alloy surfaces are selectively formed on surfaces of FeCo-V alloys with the addition of a small amount of aluminum by annealing under a low partial pressure of oxygen. The thickness of the oxide films increases with increasing aluminum content and temperature. The transition temperature and magnetic properties of the FeCo-V alloys with the addition of a small amount of aluminum are further investigated. The addition of a large amount of aluminum is shown to increase the order-disorder transformation temperature from the B2 to the A2 structure and deteriorates cold workability. In addition, a large amount of aluminum is shown to reduce magnetic flux density.

articleTitle: Proximity effects in molecular beam epitaxy grown van der Waals ferromagnet Cr2Te3 on two-dimensional layers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Achieving the large-scale growth of 2D ferromagnetic materials with high Curie temperature and perpendicular magnetic anisotropy is highly desirable for the development of future ultra-compact magnetic sensors or magnetic memories. In this context, van der Waals (vdW) Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> appears as a promising candidate. It exhibits strong perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and a Curie temperature in bulk of 180 K. In this work, we will demonstrate the growth of quasi-freestanding few layers of Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> on various 2D, which exhibit strong variation in terms of magnetic anisotropy with the crystal structure and exotic magnetotransport properties with of charge transfer from the 2D substrates.

articleTitle: Toroidal Field Excitation for Axial-Field Double-Rotor Flux-Reversal DC Motors with Magnetic Differential
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In order to provide differential action for electric vehicles performing reliable cornering, the axial-field (AF) double-rotor (DR) flux-reversal (FR) motor shows a good ability of torque output along with magnetic differential (MagD) control on its two rotors. Apart from using permanent magnet (PM) excitation which suffers from high PM cost and risk of accidental demagnetization, this paper proposes the toroidal DC (TDC) windings for field excitation to avoid the problems associated with PMs. The TDC windings not only serve as the source of the magnetic field but also regulate the flux on two rotors to produce MagD action. By using three-dimensional finite element analysis, motor performances between using the TDC windings and the conventional concentrated DC (CDC) windings are quantitatively compared, which validates that the proposed AF-DR-FR-TDC motor takes definite advantages over the CDC counterpart, while offering the desired MagD action.

articleTitle: Dynamics of an Antiferromagnetic Bloch Line Driven by Spin Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We demonstrate that a Bloch line in a bi-axial antiferromagnet driven by a spin current is a close analog of a fluxon in a long Josephson junction. We propose a scheme that allows to create, move, read, and clear such Bloch lines. Compared to superconductors, this transmission line operates at room temperature and can be dynamically reconfigured.

articleTitle: Effects of Magnetic Field and Magnetic Force on Proliferation and Differentiation of Osteoblast cells
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This study investigated the effects of moderate static magnetic fields (moderate SMFs) with the high field gradients on proliferation and differentiation of mice osteoblast MC3T3 cells to clarify whether the magnetic field or the force contribute to the biological effect. Cells were exposed to SMFs of 75–239 mT with the field gradient (0.95–4.75 T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/m). No significant effect was observed in cell proliferation by moderate SMFs exposure. However, Osteocalcin (OC) productions, which is known as a biomarker of differentiation of osteoblasts, were significantly suppressed in the exposure group with the correlation between exposed magnetic field levels. Magnetic force had no effect on the cell proliferation or OC production. These results indicate that moderate SMFs affect the differentiation of osteoblasts without modifying the cell proliferations and the magnetic field itself, not magnetic force, may be the cause of the biological effects.

articleTitle: Optimization of Magnetic Coating for Improved Electromagnetic Wave Absorption in Bi-layered Nano-hollow Spheres
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: With the increase of electronic device usages, the necessity of efficient electromagnetic (EM) wave absorbing material has been rising significantly. We have already reported the lightweight ferrite nano-hollow spheres (NHS) to exhibit enhanced electromagnetic (EM) wave absorption. Herein, the deposition of the magnetic CoFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (CFO) layer on MnFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (MnFO) NHSs is observed to be an effective strategy to improve EM wave attenuation for a high reflection loss along with larger bandwidth. EM wave absorption properties of as-synthesized bare and CFO coated MnFO NHSs with different coating thicknesses are examined within a widely-used microwave frequency domain.

articleTitle: An Inductive Power Transfer System with Multiple Receivers Utilizing Diverted Magnetic Field and Two Transmitters for IoT-level Automatic Catering Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Automatic catering vehicles (ACVs) are increasingly adopted in restaurants to save expensive human resources. Especially in special situations such as a pandemic, ACV offers a wise choice to keep social distance. A wireless power transfer (WPT) system is proposed to charge four ACVs at the same time. With the help of ferrite cores, the flux can be guided through all four receivers while the leakage magnetic field can be reduced simultaneously. Two transmitters are used to confine the flux path further. Both areas #A and #B can charge UAVs with the consideration of the mechanical structure of the food preparation area and charging standby area (Areas #A and #B). the presented system can also realize zero phase angle (ZPA) to degrade the volt-ampere (VA) rating and improve the overall efficiency. Finally, an experimental setup is constructed, and the overall dc-dc efficiency is 87.6% when delivering 117W to four loads.

articleTitle: Automated Characterization of Time-Resolved Switching Dynamics in MRAM Magnetic Tunnel Junctions Writing Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Evaluating the switching properties of MRAM technologies under Spin Transfer Torque (STT) or Spin Orbit Torque (SOT) is critical to optimize MRAM performances in the context of embedded memories such as SRAM in last level cache applications [1]. The operating conditions of magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) result from the compromise between writing current level, retention and stability during read operation and external perturbations like magnetic field. To optimize the operating conditions for a given application, and to tune the physical parameters of the MTJs, we propose a fully automated system that allows to extract efficiently the writing error rate as well as the dynamics of magnetization switching in real-time under varying conditions (pulse duration and amplitude, magnetic field).

articleTitle: Magnetization Process of Stadium-Shaped Magnetic Tunnel Junction Cells for Artificial Spin Ice
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Artificial spin ice (ASI) consisted of submicron-sized magnetic cells, which showed emergent behavior of the magnetizations in the cells. To apply the magnetization dynamics of the ASI to spintronics devices, it is important to understand the magnetization process of the cells. In the ASI samples, stadium shaped (SS) cells were widely used, however, whose magnetization process has not been well understood. In this study we investigated the magnetization process of the SS cells by magnetoresistance measurement in magnetic tunnel junctions as well as micromagnetic simulation. It was found that the SS cells showed magnetization switching at a low field, which was triggered by the annihilation of the magnetic vortex.

articleTitle: Development Acoustic Device using Giant Magnetostrictive Material: Fundamental Consideration on Output Performance Due to Differences in Material Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The ultra-compact electric vehicle EV uses an electric motor instead of a gasoline engine. This vehicle has the problem of interior space which is the noise input into the vehicle mainly consists of road and wind noise. Therefore, we propose an active noise control system using wall vibration generated by the giant magnetostrictive actuator (GMA). In this system, GMA is able to generate a high output by boundary wall surface vibration. In this paper, we created an analysis model of the GMA and considered output performance due to differences in material properties of the proposed GMA by electromagnetic field analysis.

articleTitle: Heat treatment effect on magnetic properties of Sm-Co nanopowder prepared by induction thermal plasma process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The Sm-Co alloy nanopowder was successfully prepared by the low oxygen-induction thermal plasma (LO-ITP) process. In order to improve the magnetic properties of the Sm-Co nanopowder, the heat treatment effect on the phase transformation and magnetic properties of the Sm-Co nanopowder was investigated. The Sm-Co nanopowder was annealed at 873, 973, 1073, and 1173 K in Ar flow. According to the X-ray diffraction (XRD) profile, the uniform Sm-Co nanopowder the major phase is SmCo5 was created when the annealing temperature was higher than 1073 K. The coercivity of Sm-Co nanopowder was measured as 0.5 MA/m at 300 K. After annealing at 1073 K, the coercivity enhanced to 1.4 MA/m due to the increase of the SmCo5 phase.

articleTitle: Algebraic decay of non-local spin transport in NiO
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Long-distance and low-dissipation spin transport is a crucial goal for spintronics where flow of spin angular momentum is considered as an information carrier. It has been theoretically predicted that when magnetization dynamics is confined in a two dimensional space and undergoes a rotational symmetry, spin angular momenta can be transported in a low dissipative mode, which is the so-called spin superfluidity. In this study, we investigated the spin transport in a magnetic easy-plane of an antiferromagnetic NiO thin film where magnetization dynamics is confined while satisfying the requirements for spin superfluidity.

articleTitle: Magnetotactic Bacteria: Biorobots for Targeted Therapies and Model Nanomagnetic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) are aquatic microorganisms that biomineralize chains of membrane-enclosed magnetic nanoparticles called magnetosomes. Taking advantage of their self-propulsion capability provided by their flagella and the guidance capabilities ensured by their magnetosome chain, MTB are envisaged as biorobots. These can be guided and manipulated by external magnetic fields and are naturally attracted toward hypoxic areas, such as the tumor regions, while retaining the therapeutic and imaging capacities of the magnetosomes. In addition, MTB exhibit a series of characteristics that also make them very attractive for studies on fundamental magnetic properties. In fact, the arrangement of the magnetosomes in a 1D assembly already presents a great opportunity to better understand self-assembled nanostructures, and the high quality of magnetosomes also enables them as ideal candidates to study the change of the magnetic properties at the nanoscale. In this work, we will review the latest progress in the use of the MTB biorobots for targeted therapies and model nanomagnetic systems.

articleTitle: Magneto-transport properties and magnetization switching in perpendicular magnetized Mn-rich Heusler alloy Mn2.5CoAl
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The temperature dependence of resistivity and the negative magneto-resistance (MR) as well as spin-orbit torque (SOT)-induced magnetization switching behaviors have been investigated in perpendicularly magnetized Mn-rich Heusler alloy Mn2.5CoAl (MCA) films with the different thicknesses (tMCA). The MCA films with excessive Mn partial substitution for Co are subject to compressive strain, resulting in a tunable perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) behavior. Moreover, the resistivity of the MCA film increases with decreasing temperature, showing a semiconducting-like transport behavior. Furthermore, the SOT-induced magnetization switching has been demonstrated in a Pt/MCA heterostructure-based Hall device under an in-plane external field. These results suggest that perpendicularly magnetized Mn-rich Heusler alloy MCA may be a promising candidate material for spintronic devices.

articleTitle: A Rare-Earth-Free Linear Motor Replacing Coreless Linear Motors with Neodymium Sintered Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Neodymium sintered magnets are often used in coreless linear motors for miniaturization and improvement of thrust force density. Since using Nd sintered magnets, which contain rare earth elements, has a problem of material risk, it is required to make them rare-earth-free. In this research, we have developed a rare-earth-free linear motor that can replace coreless linear motors with Nd sintered magnets. The developed motor has higher thrust force density than the coreless motor and acceptable cogging force characteristics.

articleTitle: Electric Potential-Induced Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance of Fe3O4/Ag Composite Magnetic Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, we investigated the effect of an electric potential on localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) properties of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/Ag composite magnetic nanoparticles. The nanoparticles were synthesized using the co-precipitation methods and deposited on BK7 hemispherical prisms coated in an Au thin film. The light source used is A He-Ne laser beam with a wavelength of 632.8 nm using the Kretschmann array consisting of a prism, Au thin film, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/Ag composite NPs, and an air medium. Electric potential generated by varying voltages of 2, 4, and 6 volts were applied to a prism/Au thin film/air layer structures and a prism/Au thin film/Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/Ag composite NPs/air layer structures. The result showed that the greater the applied electric field, the more significant the shift in the LSPR angle.

articleTitle: Magnetization Dynamics in FePt Nano-Granular with Thermal Heating Observed by All-Optical Pump-Probe Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Heat assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) is used to switch the magnetization of FePt nano-granular film in hard-disk-drive. To understand the magnetization switching behavior, magnetic damping constant is used as an important material parameter. However, the observation of magnetization dynamics and evaluation of magnetic damping constant for FePt thin film is technically difficult because its precession frequency reaches several hundred GHz. All-optical pump-probe technique have been used to detect such high frequency magnetization dynamics.
