Here, fast magnetization dynamics in FePt thin films with thermal heating was investigated to clarify the temperature dependence of magnetic damping constant. The effective magnetic damping constant for the FePt nano-granular thin film exhibit minimum at 620 K, and its value was evaluated to 0.064.

articleTitle: Frequency Demultiplexing of Spin Waves by Inverse-designed Magnetization Patterns, Experimentally Realized by FIB Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We present the spatial separation of spin waves with distinct wavelengths when traveling through machine-learned magnetization landscapes, which can be used to demultiplex the corresponding excitation frequencies. Focused ion beam irradiation is used to modify the magnetization of YIG locally, and the maximum achievable magnetization change is used as a training basis to generate a binary 2D magnetization profile. The pattern is created with an inverse design approach using a micromagnetic solver embedded in the PyTorch framework. Subsequently, the magnetization pattern is experimentally realized using the corresponding FIB dose and its performance is demonstrated using time-resolved MOKE microscopy.

articleTitle: Robust Design of Permanent Magnet Motors for Electric Traction Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology enabling robust design of permanent magnet motors constituting a favored choice in electric traction applications, particularly promising in high speed ranges. Appropriate permanent magnet grade and configuration selection ensuring satisfaction of standard design criteria such as high efficiency and high power density over a wide range of operating conditions are considered in conjunction with fault risk avoidance offering enhanced robustness and drive viability. Higher harmonic phenomena introduce increased stray losses in high speeds such as eddy current losses in surface mounted permanent magnets and are taken into consideration through an appropriate coupled field and circuit approach. The proposed modeling techniques are validated by measurements in prototype linear machine experimental set-up.

articleTitle: Coherent magnetization dynamics in strongly quenched systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The remagnetization process after ultrafast demagnetization can be described by relaxation mechanisms between the spin, electron, and lattice reservoirs. Thereby, collective spin excitations in form of spin waves and its angular momentum transfer play an important role on the longer timescales. In this work, we address the question whether the strength of demagnetization affects the coherency of the excited spin waves. We present a study of coherent magnetization dynamics in thin nickel films after ultrafast demagnetization using the all-optical, time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr-effect (tr-MOKE) technique. The largest coherent oscillation amplitude was observed for strongly quenched systems, showing the conservation of coherency for demagnetizations of up to 90%. Moreover, the change of the spin-wave phase with pump power shows a delay of the precession, which is related to the remagnetization time.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Magnetostrictive and Elastic Properties of Polycrystalline Co70Fe30 Alloy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetostrictive property of Fe alloys is generally correlated with their elastic property, which is referred as the magnetoelastic effect. However, the correlation is not necessarily clarified in practical polycrystalline Fe alloys with texture. To understand the properties of polycrystalline Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">70</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</inf> alloys, the properties in alloys with texture must be studied. In this study, the anisotropy of the properties of the alloy sheets was investigated by measuring the magnetostriction and Young’s modulus of the alloy sheets. The results showed that the magnetostriction of the sample with (001) texture component was high, which was fairly consistent with the values of the Young’s modulus of the alloy sheets.

articleTitle: Spin-Wave Frequency Comb and Penrose Superradiance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: An optical frequency comb consists of a set of discrete and equally spaced frequencies and has found wide applications in the synthesis over a broad range of spectral frequencies of electromagnetic waves and precise optical frequency metrology. Here, we investigate quantization effects of the nonlinear magnon-vortex interaction in ferromagnetic nanodisks. We show that the circular geometry twists the spin-wave fields with spiral phase dislocations carrying quantized orbital angular momentum (OAM). Meanwhile, the confluence and splitting scattering of twisted magnons off the gyrating vortex core (VC) generates a frequency comb consisting of discrete and equally spaced spectral lines, dubbed as twisted magnon frequency comb (TMFC). It is found that the mode spacing of the TMFC is equal to the gyration frequency of the VC and the OAM quantum numbers between adjacent spectral lines differ by one. By applying a magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of a thick nanodisk, we observe a magnonic Penrose superradiance inside the cone vortex state, which mimics the amplification of particles scattered from a rotating black hole.

articleTitle: Revisiting a hidden order at an ferromagnet/antiferromagnet interface and its switching dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Study on the exchange bias (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf>) switching in a ferromagnet (FM)/antiferromagnet (AFM) bilayer driven by the spin-orbit torque (SOT) has been an explicit research field and current focus has been devoted to determining the approaches to drive the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf> switching along with specific SOT applications. H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf> is magnetically dominant but only reveals the partial facet of IrMn, which is only responsible for the ferromagnetic component at the interface of AFM. Therefore, the complete facet of AFM and its interaction with SOT at an FM/AFM interface is still not fully uncovered. This research reports an SOT-driven hidden order transition behind H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf> in a heavy metal (Pt)/FM (Co)/AFM (IrMn) trilayer along with the issue of switching activity at Co/IrMn interface. The exchange coupling across Co/IrMn interface allows a long-range spin order in the form of an exchange-spring configuration, yielding two kinds of order in IrMn: a canting-induced ferromagnetic order for hosting H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf> and a hidden Néel order for preserving the antiferromagnetic nature. The former appears to be strongly coupled to the magnetization state of Co during the SOT switching, so it can be reversibly switched with Co on the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf> switching. On the contrary, the hidden Néel order transition re-orientated to the current direction appears to be irreversibly driven by SOT and independent on the current polarity, which can reflect on the magnetoresistance (MR) measurement and X-ray magnetic linear dichroism (XMLD) spectroscopy. Finally, a micromagnetic simulation reveals the dynamic IrMn spins are mainly based on a canting type interface instead of an uncompensated type via an exchange-spring coupling with Co.

articleTitle: All-optical switching in a 2D van der Waals magnet CrI3
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The discovery of magnetism in two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) materials presents an unprecedented opportunity to understand the fundamental interactions between light and spins and develop novel device architectures. However, little is known about how laser pulses can affect the magnetic properties of 2D magnets. Here, we demonstrate laser-induced manipulation of magnetic domains within CrI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> flakes. By fabricating CrI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> vdW heterostructures, we can additionally achieve full all-optical switching (AOS). The dependence of the AOS upon the polarization of the laser pulses agrees with the valley-dependent optical selection rules for WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, implying that spin-dependent interfacial charge transfer is the underpinning mechanism for the switching.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Properties of Agglomerates of Fe Nanoparticles Fabricated by Cold Spray Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The development of soft magnetic devices requires high-performance soft magnetic materials and high degree of design freedom. We aim to obtain high soft magnetic properties and high degree of design freedom in molding by molding high-performance soft magnetic powders using additive manufacturing. Fe nanoparticles are attracting attention as a soft magnetic material because of their high saturation magnetization and low coercivity. Achieving high packing density without lowering soft magnetic properties is a challenge when nanoparticles are used as the starting material. A bulk-like structure with high packing density, comprising pure Fe nanoparticles were sucessfully fabricated by the cold spray deposition technique. The packing density of the particles was estimated to be 96%, which was 31% larger than that of conventional compression molded samples at room temperature. Although the size of the Fe nanoparticles slightly increased in the post annealing process, the grain growth was limited after cold spraying. The coercivity of the cold sprayed sample was lower than that of the compression molded samples because of the higher packing density of the nanoparticles. These results indicate that the cold spray technique is suitable for fabricating bulk-like structures using nanoparticle materials.

articleTitle: Iron Loss Analytical Prediction of IPMSMs Considering Multi-factor Effects Over the Drive Cycle of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: It is difficult to accurately calculate the iron loss in electric propulsion systems for electric vehicles (EVs) with traditional models due to the complicated effects of temperature variations and supply current harmonics on magnetic material properties. In order to improve the performance of interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) drive system in EVs, this paper proposes an improved iron loss analytical model for IPMSM, aiming to consider the multi-effects of iron loss versus temperature and harmonics, as well as to reduce the huge computational costs compared with finite-element method. To guarantee the modeling accuracy, the influences of temperature variations and various supplies on silicon steels are investigated carefully by the developed magnetic measurement platform. Moreover, considering that the frequency, power and temperature of drive systems would vary continuously in the operating mode, the proposed models are also applied to an IPMSM prototype for analyzing the iron loss during a dynamic drive cycle, rather than at a stable working point. Experimental comparative results show the satisfactory accuracy and less computational burden of the proposed model, even in a dynamic drive cycle of EV.

articleTitle: Data-driven optimization of FePt heat-assisted magnetic recording media accelerated by deep learning TEM image segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Areal density increase of heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) media to 4 Tbit/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> requires further optimization of microstructure and magnetic properties of FePt-X granular media. This has been hindered due to the large space of processing parameters and selection of optimum segregant. In this study, we demonstrate how data-driven approach can accelerate development of media with desired microstructure and magnetic properties. This approach consists of automatic harvesting of microstructural data from transmission electron microscopy images, and training regressor models capable of predicting optimum processing conditions leading to the desired combination of microstructure and magnetic properties in the FePt granular media. The feasibility of this routine is demonstrated on a series of FePt-C media samples and optimized processing conditions proposed by machine learning were verified experimentally. Such a data-driven workflow offers a promising way to realize 4 Tbit/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> areal density in hard disk drives using HAMR.

articleTitle: A Novel Flux Concentrated Stator Consequent-pole Permanent Magnet Machine with Non-uniform Stator Modulation Teeth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents a novel flux concentrated stator consequent-pole permanent magnet (FCSCPM) machine with non-uniform stator modulation teeth (SMT) design, which provides a relative lower magnetic reluctance circuit for low-order working harmonics and hence resulting a higher torque capability. To confirm the merits of the proposed design, a conventional FCSCPM machine is selected and compared by finite element (FE) analysis. The simulated results show that the proposed design exhibits a higher torque capability, better field-weakening ability and a relative larger high-efficiency (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq$</tex> 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) region than conventional FCSCPM case. It validates the feasibility of the proposed design with performance improvement.

articleTitle: Topology-Dependent Brownian Gyromotion of a Single Skyrmion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Non-interacting particles exhibiting Brownian motion have been observed in many occasions of sciences, such as molecules suspended in liquids, optically trapped microbeads, and spin textures in magnetic materials. In particular, a detailed examination of Brownian motion of spin textures is important for designing thermally stable spintronic devices, which motivates the present study. In our recent work, through using temporally and spatially resolved polar magneto-optic Kerr effect (MOKE) microscopy, we have experimentally observed the thermal-fluctuation-induced random walk of a single isolated Néel-type magnetic skyrmion in an interfacially asymmetric Ta/CoFeB/TaOx multilayer. Interestingly, a nonlinear temperature-dependent diffusion coefficient and topology-dependent gyromotion are obtained and further formulated based on the stochastic Thiele equation. The experimental and numerical demonstration of topology-dependent Brownian gyromotion of skyrmions can be useful for understanding the nonequilibrium magnetization dynamics and implementing unconventional spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Is there theoretical upper limit of coercivity?
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Coercivity analysis was performed using Landau theory. In this framework, coercivity was given by differential of energy landscape. It has been shown that this calculation result is equivalent to the Kronmuller formula. Therefore, the coercivity is generally suppressed by the magnetic anisotropy field. However, we take advantage of special switching between two types of energy landscape. Here, we transform the functional form of the energy derivative by special switching to tailor the two energy landscapes. Specialized switching is designed to be completed in a region named stitching area. As a result, it has been possible to design a coercivity that exceeded the limits of magnetic anisotropy fields.

articleTitle: Spatial Resolution and Sensitivity of GMR Sensors with Magnetic Flux Concentrators used for Magnetic Field Microscopes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spatial resolution and sensitivity of GMR sensors used in magnetic field microscopes are investigated by estimating the sensitivity distribution function. Sensors are used together with magnetic flux concentrators (MFCs), and detects local magnetic field with the typical sample-sensor distance of 5 mm. For the full-bridge type sensor unit, the spatial resolution was roughly determined by the distance of the GMR elements. Sharing the central MFCs is effective for improving the spatial resolution without losing sensitivity. It is found that the MFC loses its gain with decreasing sample-sensor distance because the MFC size is comparable with or larger than that distance. The half-bridge arrangement is found to be effective for obtaining small spatial resolution with high sensitivity.

articleTitle: Gate-Controlled Charge Rectification in Elemental Tellurium
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Chiral conductors exhibit spin-related charge rectification but its controllability is still limited. In this contribution, we report gate-controlled enhancement of charge rectification in chiral semiconductor Te under magnetic field. As gating shifts the chemical potential to the valence band maximum of Te, the charge rectification efficiency is enhanced hundredfold. By combining model calculations, we attribute the charge rectification to the asymmetry of the chiral band structure which is caused by the Zeeman effect. We also find that the carrier density subject to this asymmetry is increased by a camel-back structure near the valence band maximum, which further enhances the gate-controlled charge rectification.

articleTitle: Ferrite Pads Gap Thermal-Magnetic Evaluation and Mitigation for 11.1-kW Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Local overheating and airgaps magnetic leakage are severe due to the distributing inter-tile airgaps in wireless power transfer (WPT) ferrite pads. In this paper, a thermal-magnetic multi-objective optimization function (MOF) is proposed to evaluate and mitigate the thermal-magnetic deterioration caused by the distributing airgaps. The effects of the airgaps on temperature and leakage distribution are analyzed based on the magnetic-thermal coupling finite element method (FEM) simulation. It is found that the trend of the local temperature is opposite to that of the magnetic leakage following the increase of the airgaps width. An interesting range can also be found by using the proposed MOF strategy. When the airgaps width within the range, the gap thermal-magnetic problems can be mitigated effectively. Subsequently, a full-scale prototype with 11.1kW at 85kHz is fabricated to validate the effectiveness of MOF strategy and the accuracy of evaluation. The WPT pads with optimized airgaps achieve an excellent comprehensive performance which is superior to that without the optimization.

articleTitle: Acoustic spin transport in s-wave superconductors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We theoretically study the generation of spin current due to a surface acoustic wave in an s-wave superconductor. We model an s-wave superconductor as the mean-field Hamiltonian and calculate spin current generated via spin-vorticity coupling based on quantum kinetic theory. The results suggest that the spin current can be driven in a single-superconductor layer. Our proposal may contribute to the advancement of spin transport in superconductors from application and fundamental physics aspects.

articleTitle: Optimisation of Ga-doped τ-MnAl for use as a permanent magnetic material
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: 8 samples within the composition range Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(52.5–60)</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(31.5–47.5)</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(0–11.5)</inf> were heat treated into the τ-MnAl phase in order to assess the impact of Ga-doping on critical magnetic variables defined by J.M.D Coey in "Permanent magnets: plugging the gap" and determine suitability for further development in order to see industrial applications. Ga-doping was seen to increase observed M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</inf> and affect k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">uniaxial</inf> such that all but one composition could theoretically meet BH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Max</inf> requirements for Type A Gap Magnets and thus warrant further development to increase observed values of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf> and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>.

articleTitle: Magnetic structural analysis of Pt3Fe antiferromagnet by single crystal neutron diffraction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Single-crystal neutron diffraction measurements for a Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Fe antiferromagnet were performed to determine the detailed magnetic structure below T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N2</inf> = 100 K, where the magnetic structure characterized by the propagation wave vector q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> = (1/2 1/2 0) and q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> = (1/2 0 0) are formed. We found that magnetic domain model where both (1/2 1/2 0)-type and (1/2 0 0)-type ordering coexist in a crystal well explains the observed magnetic neutron intensities, but, there is a large difference in the volume fraction of the magnetic domains. This suggests a large spin reorientation at T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N2</inf> where (1/2 1/2 0)-type domains are partially replaced by (1/2 0 0)-type domains.

articleTitle: Development of TbCu7-type Sm-Fe-N anisotropic magnet powder by low-temperature build-up process using molten salt
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Anisotropic TbCu7-type Sm-Fe-N magnet powder was developed using TbCu7-type Sm-Fe alloy powder synthesized by modifying low-temperature Ca reduction diffusion process. Using Sm metal powder instead of SmCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Ca, an almost single-phase TbCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>-type Sm-Fe powder was obtained. By nitriding the powder with an NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mixture gas, a TbCu7-type Sm-Fe-N anisotropic magnet powder was fabricated. Its magnetic properties of magnetization at field of 90 kOe σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">90kOe</inf>, remanence ratio σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>/σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">90kOe</inf> and coercivity were 138.5 emu/g, 0.64 and 6.3 kOe, respectively.

articleTitle: Demonstration of weighted sum using electrical manipulation and detection of magnetic skyrmions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)

authors.preferredName: Tristan Da Câmara Santa Clara Gomes

abstract: Thanks to their original properties, magnetic skyrmions have many promising applications, from memories, sensors to logic operations. In this study, we propose to use fully-electrical manipulation and detection of magnetic skyrmions in multilayer devices to perform a basic unconventional computation operation in hardware. The fabricated devices take advantage of the particle-like nature of the magnetic skyrmions: operations can be applied to a large ensemble of skyrmions using fully-electrical stimuli, while skyrmions can be counted individually by electrical means. Here, we show the nucleation and the motion of a controlled number of magnetic skyrmions in multilayer tracks using electrical current pulse parameters. Then, we show that the number of skyrmions can be directly summed and detected with non-perturbative Anomalous Hall resistance measurements. Magneto-ionic effects are used for the local non-volatile and reversible tuning of the magnetic properties of the tracks.

articleTitle: High saturation magnetization and high coercivity of Co substituted orthoferrite
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Rare earth orthoferrite with orthorhombic perovskite crystal structure normally show weak magnetization due to the antiferromagnetic superexchange between the nearest Fe ions. In this work, we show that orthoferrite thin films with saturation magnetization as high as 145 emu/cc and coercivity larger than 8 kOe can be obtained by the substitution of Co. The orthorhombic perovskite Eu(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films show preferential perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. A magnetic field of 24 kOe applied parallel to the film plane can not saturate the samples. Which means the large intrinsic magnetic anisotropy in the films. The substituted orthoferrite is expected to have strong bulk Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interactions (DMI) due to the centrosymmetry-breaking of the orthorhombic crystal structure. Those novel magnetic ordering make the films prominent candidates for the coexistence of ferroelectric and magnetism, and for the hosting of high density magnetic skyrmions at room temperature.

articleTitle: Spintronic logic: from transducers to logic gates and circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: While magnetic solid-state memory has found commercial applications to date, magnetic logic has rather remained on a conceptual level so far. Here, we discuss open challenges of different spintronic logic approaches, which use magnetic excitations for computation. While different logic gate designs have been proposed and proof of concept experiments have been reported, no nontrivial operational spintronic circuit has been demonstrated due to many open challenges in spintronic circuit and system design. Furthermore, the integration of spintronic circuits in CMOS systems will require the usage of transducers between the electric (CMOS) and magnetic domains. We show that these transducers can limit the performance as well as the energy consumption of hybrid CMOS-spintronic systems. Hence, the optimization of transducer efficiency will be a major step towards competitive spintronic logic system.

articleTitle: Placement of Electromagnets for Edge-supported Maglev Systems: Fundamental Consideration on Tilting Angle of Electromagnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In the manufacturing process of thin steel plates, the surface quality deteriorates due to contact with rollers. Therefore, it is necessary to convey thin steel plates without contact by magnetic levitation. However, when thin steel plates are levitated by electromagnetic force, deflection of the plate occurs, and stable levitation of the steel plate is difficult. Therefore, an edge support type magnetic levitation method was proposed for stable levitation. However, this method has the disadvantage of low suspension force, although sufficient attractive force can be obtained. In this report, the method that electromagnets are tilted was proposed. It is possible to levitate by low steady current using the method. Moreover, the horizontal and vertical attractive forces when the electromagnets are tilted were investigated by electromagnetic field analysis.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Analysis on Ringing Phenomenon of Inductor Driven by Inverter Considering Stray Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In recent power electronics equipment applying GaN semiconductor, etc., the ringing phenomenon, which is the oscillation in the waveform of current due to the short rising and falling time, increases noise and loss. To design magnetic devices in such power electronics equipment, the ringing phenomenon is tried to be simulated using the electromagnetic field analysis taking account of the stray capacitance in this paper. The stray capacitance of the windings is modeled by taking account of the displacement current, and its effect on ringing phenomenon is examined. It is shown that the ringing phenomenon can be represented by taking account of the stray capacitance.

articleTitle: Electrical Determination of Magnetization Switching in In-plane Anisotropy Spin-orbit Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Electrical determination of magnetization switching is essential in the development of spintronics devices. However, for in-plane magnetic anisotropic systems, electrical readout of magnetization is challenging on simple Hall bar devices. Here, we propose a simple method based on DC measurement to probe magnetization switching on the spin-orbit Hall bar devices. The observed resistance-field relation is highly coincidental with the magnetic hysteresis loop measured at sheet films. Our result provides an effective method to evaluate the magnetization switching of the in-plane anisotropic systems on the Hall bar devices.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Fe-based nanocrystalline powder-pressed magnetic core with low coercivity and small iron loss
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, to decrease coercivity and iron loss for the pressed magnetic core, a reduction process for the residual stress induced through the pressing magnetic powder was investigated, and two types of the powdered magnetic core using Fe-Si-B-C-Cr amorphous powder and Fe-based nanocrystalline powder were fabricated. It was found that the Fe-based nanocrystalline powdered magnetic core exhibited about 30 % lower coercivity and 42 % smaller iron loss than that of Fe-based amorphous one when 1MHz, 50mT.

articleTitle: Faraday effects of magneto-dielectric nanogranular films with various particle shape
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic-field control of polarized light via magneto-dielectric nanocomposite system is an important step in seamless implementation of nano-scale magneto-optical device. In this report, magneto-dielectric nanogranular films with “non-sphere shaped” magnetic nanoparticles, wherein (prolate, chained, and oblate)-shaped nanoparticles was investigated regarding to induce the magneto-optical anisotropy. We demonstrate that both optical transmittance and Faraday rotation angle at optical communication bands were successfully improved when the prolate shaped nanoparticle perpendicularly aligned in the film.

articleTitle: Characterization of Néel relaxation time in multicore magnetic nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic nanoparticles are developed for the biomedical applications such as hyperthermia and magnetic particle imaging. Magnetic relaxation determines the performance of magnetic nanoparticles in these applications. The magnetic relaxation was divided into two types as the Néel relaxation and Brown relaxations. In this research, the magnetization response associated with the Néel relaxation was observed by applying a pulse magnetic field in magnetic nanoparticles of the multicore structure. The measured Neel relaxation were roughly divided into fast and slow responses. The slow response was dominant compared to the fast part, which is consistent with the distribution of the particle core size of measured magnetic nanoparticles. Elucidating the Néel relaxation time of magnetic nanoparticles guide the design of particles suitable for the biomedical applications and determines the optimal magnetic field conditions.

articleTitle: Understanding the Coercivity of Ga-containing Nd-Fe-B Sintered Magnets from Feature Extraction and Selection of X-ray Diffraction Patterns by Dimension Reduction and Sparse Modelling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Coercivity enhancement of Ga-containing Nd–Fe–B as-sintered magnets driven by the microstructural change during post-sinter annealing was studied by feature extraction and selection based on the data science methods such as principal component analysis (PCA) and a linear model with the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), respectively. PCA and LASSO modeling of X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns objectively identified the microstructural changes contributing to coercivity. Furthermore, quantitative evaluation of the contribution of microstructural changes to the coercivity of the magnet revealed a preferred direction of the contribution even in an identical phase. The validity of our findings was qualitatively confirmed by the results of previous studies, indicating that sparse modeling accelerates materials research and development by automated decision-making.

articleTitle: Effect of Cu Addition on Magnetic Properties and Microstructures of SmFe11Ti Alloys Prepared by Melt-Spinning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The effect of Cu addition on the magnetic properties and microstructures of SmFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>Ti alloy ribbons has been investigated. In this study, the cooling rate of melt-spinning process and post heat treatment have been carried out to control the final microstructures. It was found that the Cu addition brought significant coercivity enhancement of the SmFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>Ti ribbons fabricated at low cooling rate. In particular, the coercivity of the Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>TiCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf> alloy reached 6.1 kOe at a wheel speed of 20 m/s. This increase in coercivity could be due to the formation of Sm-Cu rich intergranular phase in the alloy.

articleTitle: Growth and magnetoelectric effect of epitaxial Co3Mn films on piezoelectric Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-PbTiO3(001)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We explore epitaxial growth of metastable ferromagnetic Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Mn films on piezoelectric Pb(Mg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-PbTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (001) (PMN-PT) substrates by molecular beam epitaxy. By tuning the termination of the PMN-PT surface and the growth temperature, thermodynamically metastable bcc and stable fcc/hcp phases can be distinctively formed. We find that the bcc-Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Mn/PMN-PT structure expresses a relatively large converse magnetoelectric (CME) coupling coefficient (α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</inf>) of 8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> s/m while the fcc/hcp-Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Mn/PMN-PT one shows a small value less than 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> s/m. This provides a possibility for achieving simultaneous demonstration of large CME effect and tunneling magnetoresistance one.

articleTitle: Equivalent Magnetic Network Modeling of Grain-Oriented Silicon Steel Sheets Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to accurately and rapidly compute the performance of permanent magnet linear synchronous motors with grain-oriented silicon steel sheets for initial design procedures. Therefore, an equivalent magnetic network model with considering the anisotropy of grain-oriented silicon steel sheets is proposed, and the uneven magnetic density distribution of the primary tooth is also considered. The equivalent magnetic network makes it possible to evaluate the influence of core saturation by iteration, from which the flux linkage, the back electromotive force and the thrust of the motor are calculated. Finally, the accuracy of the equivalent magnetic network model is verified by finite element method results.

articleTitle: Development of Magneto-Optical Diffractive Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We propose a magneto-optical diffractive deep neural network (MO-D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>NN). We simulated MO-D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>NNs, each of which consists of five hidden layers made of a magnetic material that contains 100 × 100 magnetic domains with a domain width of 1 µm and an interlayer distance of 0.7 mm. The networks demonstrate a classification accuracy of > 90% for the MNIST dataset when the light intensity was used as the detection signal. The accuracy was > 80% even for a small Faraday rotation angle of π/100 rad when the angle of polarization is used as the detection signal. The MO-D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>NN allows rewriting of the hidden layers, which is not possible with previous implementations of D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>NN. Furthermore, we fabricated a prototype of the MO-D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>NN with two layers consist of Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>GaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> thin film. The magnetic domain pattern recorded by the MO recording technique was 1 µm and the hidden layer was formed with high precision.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependence of Magnetic Anisotropy and Domain Wall Width Tuning in a BaTiO3(111)/CoFeB Heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Composite multiferroics consist of two types of ferroic materials, typically a ferroelectric and ferromagnet, often coupled interfacially by strain induced by the lattice elongations in the ferroelectric. In BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (BTO) substrates the magnitude of the strain is strongly temperature dependent, varying greatly between each of the polar crystal phases and exerting a huge influence over the properties of a coupled magnetic film. In this work we determine the temperature dependence of the strain-induced magnetoelastic anisotropy within ferromagnetic domains in a CoFeB film coupled to the ferroelectric domains from a BTO(111) substrate. Using our measurements of this anisotropy strength we then micromagnetically determine the scaling of magnetic domain wall widths as a function of temperature, demonstrating an increase of 100% across the entire range with the most significant changes occurring around the BTO phase transitions.

articleTitle: Development of Dy-free sintered NdFeB magnet through grain boundary engineering by diffusion of PrCu alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Dy-free sintered magnets were fabricated by blending Neo powder with different amount of PrCu powder. With increasing PrCu from 0-10 wt.%, Hcj of the magnets gradually increases from the original 14.5 kOe to 18.6 kOe. The highest (BH)max achieved was 35.0 MGOe with 7.5 wt.% PrCu. It was found that PrCu was mainly distributed at grain boundary and triple junctions, leading to a reduced coupling among grains, thus an enhanced Hcj. The grain boundary engineering by the diffusion of PrCu alloy is an effective method to improve Hcj of Dy-free magnets.

articleTitle: Evaluation of magnetic flux density change for vibration energy harvesting: Comparison between direct and indirect measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The evaluation of magnetic-flux-density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta B$</tex> due to the inverse magnetostrictive effect is important to develop superior inverse magnetostrictive materials for the application to vibration energy harvesting. In this study, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta B$</tex> value of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}-70$</tex> at.%Co alloy was directly measured by applying dynamic stresses <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta\sigma$</tex> under constant magnetic fields. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta B$</tex> value in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta\sigma=160$</tex> MPa increased with increasing magnetic fields and showed a maximum. The maximum value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta B$</tex> was approximately 0.35 T. This value is about 19% less than that evaluated indirectly from magnetization curves under constant stresses. Consequently, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta B$</tex> values obtained by the direct measurement indicate different behaviors from that obtained by the indirect measurement.

articleTitle: Feasibility study of reduction in sound-pressure induced vibration in hard disk drives using an adaptive feed-forward control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Recently, the sound-pressure induced positioning error is the most important issue in HDDs for data centers. Because the sound-pressure induced positioning errors often contains higher frequency components than servo bandwidth, we considered to apply an adaptive feed-forward controls as a possible solution of the issue. A sensor is used to detect the vibration of a location on the HDD, that is correlated to the head vibration. The HDDs to apply the adaptive FF control are assumed to have dual-stage actuator system and the secondary actuators are used to compensate the sound-pressure induced positioning errors. The simulation results confirmed that the sound-pressure induced vibrations are well suppressed by the proposed method.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Pavlov associative memory by implementation of rate coding using magnetic tunnel junction neurons
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A fully functioning Pavlov associative memory system is designed by a basis of rate coding. In order to implement rate coding characteristics to the system, a neuron signal is constructed by utilizing telegraphic switching characteristics of the magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ). Binary neural signal created by the MTJ is used as a weight update method for AgSi memristor synapses. The proposed Pavlov associative memory conducts not only basic associative memory characteristics such as learning and forgetting, but also conducts complex characteristics such as contrived/natural forgetting, consolidation learning, rate variation, etc.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Minimum-Frame-Error-Rate BCJR Detector for Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We propose an adaptive minimum-frame-error-rate (AMFER) BCJR detector for the read channel in magnetic recording. Compared with the recently proposed AMFER soft-output Viterbi algorithm (SOVA), the AMFER BCJR detector not only produces more accurate soft information, but it also offers improved convergence performance and better robustness to parameter initialization.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of Asymmetric Multi-layer Barrier Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In order to reduce the torque ripple of the vehicle motor and increase the range of high-efficiency working area, this paper proposes an Asymmetric Multi-layer Barrier Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (AMBPMSM). The equivalent magnetic circuit model is established, and the characteristics of flux leakage, air gap flux density and inductance are analyzed, and the parameters affecting the magnetic density of air gap are determined. The influence of each parameter on the performance is analyzed by using the response surface method (CCB), and the parameters are optimized and analyzed by MOGA. Through Finite Element Analysis, it is proved that the proposed motor has lower torque ripple, less back EMF harmonics and a wider range of high-efficiency regions.

articleTitle: High Coercive Force Sm2Fe17N3 Magnetic Materials by Phosphate Surface Modification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, in the process of forming phosphate film on the surface of Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> magnetic powder particles, we stirred a slurry containing Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powder, water, and phosphoric acid compounds while adding inorganic acid to keep the pH of the slurry at 2 to promote a continuous film formation reaction. As a result, the phosphate coated Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powder with a relatively uniform thickness film was prepared with very few insufficiently coated areas. The magnetic powder prepared by this method was confirmed to have almost disappeared the αFe peak in XRD measurement and showed an intrinsic coercive force of 1400-1800 kA/m (1.3 times higher than that of conventional magnets). The irreversible flux loss of the bonded magnet obtained by injection molding using the improved phosphate coated powder after 8,000hours of immersion in 393 K hot aqueous solution was about 2.3%.

articleTitle: Magnetic Domain Observation of Grain-oriented Electrical Steel Sheet under Two-dimensional Excitation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The authors have constructed a magnetic domain observation system for grain-oriented electrical steel sheet using a magnetic optical sensor. The system uses a camera, coaxial illumination and a polarizer, and observation can be performed simply by placing the sensor on the sample surface. No processing of the sample, such as insulating coating removal, is required. In this paper, we will report the results of magnetic domain observation of grain-oriented electrical steel sheet and the changes in magnetic domains under DC excitation in arbitrary direction combined with a magnetizer by generating contrast images using Otsu's method of magnetic domain images obtained with the constructed system.

articleTitle: Dynamic Magnetic Network Modeling and Electromagnetic Analysis of An External Rotor PMSM for Electric Hub System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A dynamic equivalent magnetic network (EMN) model of 36 slots 8 poles external rotor permanent magnet synchronous hub motor (ERPMSHM) considering the distributed winding with fractional slot and the nonlinearity of the iron core material is established in this paper. Reluctance network (RN) consisted of diamond grid cells is adopted to deal with the air gap. The rationality of the EMN and the accuracy of the calculation results are verified by the finite element method (FEM) and EMN.

articleTitle: Modelling in-device inference and classification of binary digits using nonlinear dynamics of spin Hall oscillator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work, we employ micromagnetic modelling of a spin Hall oscillator for a direct inference and classification of binary digit inputs. The spectral characteristics of the oscillation is utilized for the classification. We observed a direct inference of binary digit inputs up to a sequence of four binary digits. Subsequently, handwritten digit image recognition is tested with the Modified National Institute of Standards and Testing (MNIST) handwritten digit database and acquired an accuracy of 88.6% with a linear classifier network.

articleTitle: Spinterface formation of sexithiophene (6T) on ferromagnetic surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Interfaces between organic molecules and ferromagnetic materials play a critical role in a variety of remarkable spin-related effects. In order to employ such spinterfaces in next-generation molecular spintronic devices, it is crucial to characterise and control these spin effects. Here, we report the features of prototypical spinterfaces comprised of sexithiophene 6T (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">24</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>) deposited on ferromagnetic metal and ferromagnetic oxide surfaces. We have investigated the controlled coverage of 6T monolayers on an Fe surface using a variety of advanced characterization techniques and show that adsorption leads to the formation of monodisperse conjugated solid islands. AFM results show that a 0.5 ML 6T deposition leads to solid islands, while with an increased thickness of 1.25 ML the material is deposited in the form of aggregated islands. XPS and UPS data reveal the orientation and electronic structure of the 6T/Fe system. Comparisons are also made to 6T adsorption on the more inert Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>(001) surface revealing the importance of adsorption geometry, molecular packing and surface reconstruction in determining spinterfacial electronic structure and associated device performance.

articleTitle: Application of Fe-based Alloy Powder to Noise Suppression Sheet for GHz-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The communication frequency band for small communication terminals are shifting to the Super High Frequency (SHF) band (3 GHz – 30 GHz) by the 5th generation mobile communication system (5G). Accordingly, a Noise Suppression Sheet (NSS), which have been used to solve electromagnetic interference problems inside small communication terminals, are required to have effective noise attenuation characteristics in the SHF band. The NSS is a composite sheet of flat magnetic powder and polymer. Noise attenuation characteristics of the NSS is mainly determined by the imaginary part (μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>´´) of the complex specific permeability. In this study, the design guideline of the NSS for SHF band was verified by measuring μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>´´ spectra of NSS to which flat powders obtained from Fe-based alloy powders with different phases were applied. Fe-based alloy powders with multiple crystalline phases tend to become flat powders with low aspect ratio by micro-forging. It is shown that powder design with high saturation magnetization and low aspect ratio is important to realize effective NSS in the SHF band.

articleTitle: Experimental detection of magnon noise enhancement near spin reorientation in Sm0.7Er0.3FeO3
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Antiferromagnets are one of the most promising candidates for high-speed spintronic applications in the future. The growing interest in thermal spin effects demands for experimental schemes that allow for the investigation of the dynamics of incoherent spin noise at ultrafast time scales. Here, we demonstrate a novel technique enabling time-domain detection of sub-THz-magnon noise dynamics in antiferromagnets with unprecedented time resolution. By measuring the correlation of the pulse-to-pulse polarisation fluctuation of femtosecond probe pulses, we successfully resolved the incoherent magnon noise dynamics in the orthoferrite Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Er<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf>FeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Due to the critical effects near the spin reorientation transition, the noise dynamics show strong enhancement. Our concept provides a universal ultrafast means to explore noise properties in a variety of correlated spin systems in the future

articleTitle: Integrating magnetic tunnel junctions with femtosecond laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spintronic MRAM is highly promising towards a next-generation “universal” memory paradigm. As its key building block, perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (p-MTJs) have been an active field of research, aiming at a high access speed with low power consumption. However, state-of-the-art p-MTJs are still fundamentally limited by the spin precession process, resulting in a sub-ns speed limitation. Recently, manipulating or even switching the magnetization of ferrimagnets in a highly non-equilibrium regime has been realized by a single femtosecond (fs) laser pulse, leading to a plethora of opportunities for device applications. In this presentation, we report our recent experimental progress on integrating p-MTJ with fs lasers. First, we introduce fs laser-assisted switching in a high-performance p-MTJ device using a direct electrical readout. Reconfigurable switching operations and a switching phase diagram are shown by the interplay of the laser and synchronized field. Second, we demonstrate fs laser-induced all-optical switching of a p-MTJ, by using a composite free layer structure employing interlayer RKKY coupling. All-optical switching speed within 10 ps is demonstrated, with a high energy efficiency and a decent TMR ratio. We believe our hybrid research approach might pave the way towards a new category of integrated photonic memory, as well as an alternating scheme for next-generation MRAM design.

articleTitle: A study of stable levitation conditions considering propulsion of a carrier in the magnetically levitated conveyance system using the linear stepper motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetically levitated conveyance system has been developed. Currently, most systems use separate systems for levitation and propulsion. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to levitate and thrust with the same system. In a conventional system, a carrier didn’t levitate stably because of large fluctuations in mutual inductance of the track (primary) side and carrier (secondary) side caused by gap fluctuations of a carrier. In this study, the optimal gap and primary and secondary current values, which were less affected by mutual inductance fluctuations, were obtained by analyzing attractive force acting on a carrier. As a result of levitation experiments, stable levitation was achieved considering the propulsive motion.

articleTitle: Independent Control of Spin-Orbit Torque
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Since the discovery of current-induced domain wall motion (CIDWM), a lot of attention has been paid due to its promising applicability for memory device. In the CIDWM, the spin-orbit torque (SOT) and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) are important for the efficiency and direction of the CIDWM. However, because these two parameters share the common origin of the spin-orbit coupling, it is hard to control just one independently of the other. If one can independently control one of these parameters, it is possible to freely control the movement of magnetic domain walls. Here we show the strategy to control the SOT independently of the DMI. Two groups (A and B) of samples are prepared for testing controllability of the SOT. We focus on the diverse materials in the group A and we focus on the thickness of material in the group B. In the group A, both SOT and DMI changed with the material choice. On the other hand, in the group B, only the SOT could be controlled independently of DMI by thickness adjustment.

articleTitle: Permeability Control of Ferromagnetic Wires for Time-varying Spintronic Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We study permeability (μ) variation of a lithographically-prepared magnetic wire consisting of Ta/NiFe:Py/Pt trilayers by means of spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR). By an injection of a direct current up to ±20 mA together with an alternating current in GHz frequencies, the meta-atom under external magnetic fields shows significant changes in position and width of ST-FMR signals due to a massive spin-current injection. The changes in the ST-FMR signals indicates a μ variation, which is verified by analytical calculation based upon the experimentally obtained resonance field and Gilbert damping parameter. The present study paves a way to time-varying spintronic metamaterials with a high modulation frequency for realizing microwave sources toward the 6th generation mobile communication system.

articleTitle: Effects of High-Pressure Environment on Deep-sea Fe-Co-V Alloys Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: An advanced deep-sea permanent magnet synchronous motors design method is proposed in this study. The high-pressure environment will seriously deteriorate the magnetic properties of the traditional soft magnetic material silicon steel sheet used in the motor, which will lead to a decrease in motor efficiency. As a kind of soft magnetic alloy with high saturation magnetic density, Fe-Co-V alloy instead of silicon steel sheet is used in the motor to significantly improve the torque density of the motor. However, the variation law of its magnetic properties in a high-pressure environment is blank. Through the study of Fe-Co-V alloy, it is found that at high pressure, the magnetic properties of the material change much slightly than that of silicon steel sheet. Accordingly, the use of Fe-Co-V alloy to manufacture deep-sea motors is proposed in this study. Compared with the motor made of silicon steel sheet, the advantages of the efficiency and torque of deep sea Fe-Co-V alloy permanent magnet synchronous motors are verified.

articleTitle: 3D printing of multipolar bonded SmCo permanent magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The use of permanent magnet in electrical machines and actuators makes it possible to get high performances in terms of torque or force density and efficiency. Permanent magnets can be manufactured either by sintering or bonding methods. Bonded magnets have smaller magnetic performances than sintered ones, but they are more flexible in terms of manufacturing. In this paper, we explore the use of 3D printing to speed up and reduce the cost of permanent bonded magnet manufacturing. We present in a first part the production of the filament material based on a mixture of SmCo powder and PA12 polymer. In a second part we present a customized commercial 3D printer that can print permanent bonded magnets with specific magnetization patterns in the plane of the heating plate. The adopted strategy is to apply an in-situ magnetic field during printing in order to reorient the magnetic particles toward the flow direction. With this machine, we have been able to print unipolar and multipolar bonded SmCo permanent magnets with special magnetization patterns (alternating poles, Halbach, …).

articleTitle: Improvement of Spin-Orbit Torque Efficiency for High Speed Operation of Tb/Co-Based Skyrmions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have investigated spin-orbit torque (SOT) efficiencies in (Pt/Co/Tb)10 and (Pt/Co/Tb/W)10 multilayers which are expected to have skyrmions. We improved the effective SOT by inserting a W layer between Tb and top Pt to prevent SOT from top Pt through thin Tb. As a result, the SOT efficiency was improved more than 5 times by W insertion, and moreover the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) required for stable skyrmions was maintained. It is one of candidates to realize the stable skyrmion transport with high speed by low current density.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Maximum Energy Product by α-Fe Coating on the Side of Rectangular Sm(Fe0.8Co0.2)12 Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The demagnetization process of exchange-coupled Sm(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>/α-Fe nanocomposite magnet particles with α-Fe phase coated on the sides of rectangular Sm(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> nanoparticles and the effect of Fe phase arrangement on their (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> are systematically investigated from micromagnetics calculations. The (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of the reference model Sm(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> particles without Fe layer was 630 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. On the other hand, the (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of the nanocomposite magnet particle model, in which the four sides of the hard phase are coated with a soft phase, was found to have the highest (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of 678 kJ/m3. This result may provide a guideline for designing high-performance magnet particle materials while reducing the use of rare metals.

articleTitle: Effect of Crystallinity on Magnetic Properties in Manganese-Doped Indium Tin Oxide Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Epitaxial and polycrystalline Mn-doped indium tin oxide (ITO) films were deposited by rf magnetron sputtering. Room-temperature ferromagnetism was observed both in epitaxial and polycrystalline Mn-doped ITO films. The origin of the magnetic properties of the Mn-doped ITO films suggested to be the carrier mediated ferromagnetic interaction.

articleTitle: Micromagnetics Simulation of Highly Efficient Oscillation of Magnetization in a Ferromagnetic Local Areas via Spin Waves Induced by Spin-Orbit Torque
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We study numerical simulation of highly efficient oscillation of magnetization in a ferromagnetic local region using the spin-orbit torque. It is found that in the presence of multiple SOT regions, the precession motion can be excited at a lower current density through the interaction. This interaction is caused by spin waves, and as a result, phase control between the precession motions is possible through the gap between the areas. Our new finding indicates that the interaction between the wave source and the spin wave is very complex in devices that utilize the interference effects of spin waves.

articleTitle: Influence Studies of the Flux-Barriers and PM Arrangements on High-Speed Flux-Intensifying Interior Permanent Magnet Motor Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of the multi-flux barriers and PM arrangements of FI-IPM motors in high-speed operation for spindle application. A 9 kW conventional FI-IPM motor is used as the fundamental for the investigation. First, characteristics of the air gap flux density, inductances, and saliency ratio variations under the effect of the muti-flux barriers and PM arrangement. Then, the performance of FI-IPM motors, such as torque ripple, CPSR, and demagnetization ability in high-speed operation, will investigate and compare with the original FI-IPM motor. The analysis results reveal that, with the multi-flux barriers and proper PM arrangement, the performance and constant power speed range (CPRS) of the FI-IPM motor will be significantly improved. Finally, a 9 kW FI-IPM motor prototype with multi-flux barriers is made and tested. The experiment results validated the analyses.

articleTitle: Fabrication of L10-FeNi from compositional optimized amorphous alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-FeNi hard magnetic ribbons were fabricated by annealing Fe-Ni-based amorphous alloys. The phase transition mechanism and the origin of L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-FeNi during the annealing process had been analyzed. By adding Si into the low stability Fe-Ni-P amorphous alloy, the resulted coercivity had been greatly enhanced to 912 Oe. The addition of Si was also found stabilizing the L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-FeNi since the high Si content samples could withstand 400 °C for prolonged annealing time without any deterioration of magnetic hardness. The reason of such beneficial effects would be discussed. By exploiting such composition design strategy, the recent progress has raised the coercivity beyond 1100 Oe.

articleTitle: Improved high permeability CoZrTaB laminated thin films with novel CMOS compatible dielectric material
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper present an optimized CoZrTaB-based laminated thin films with a novel wet etch-able oxide dielectric material. Wet etching capability was studied on the stack material exhibiting a narrow and clean undercut. Good uniaxial anisotropy with low coercivity was achieved via in-situ magnetic alignment during magnetron sputtering. Permeability of 432 and Q-factor of 23.4 at 100 MHz were observed in high frequency permeameter measurement. Finally thermal annealing was carried out at various temperatures. Uniaxial anisotropy was maintained up to 300 °C, while an enhancement of permeability (by 25%) was observed.

articleTitle: Variable cross-section FeGa/quartz composite magnetic field sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A magnetic field sensing structure of FeGa magnetostrictive membrane and AT-cut quartz with variable cross-section shape is proposed. The variable cross-section shape can not only effectively reduce the demagnetizing factor in the magnetic film convergence region, but also converge the strain to the electrode region of the wafer. The simulation results show that the composite symmetric with variable cross-section can effectively improve the strain transfer coefficient between the magnetostrictive layer and quartz. Compared with the rectangular structure, the average strain change rate of FeGa/quartz with variable cross-section is 0.0198ppm/Oe under the applied magnetic field of 0-100Oe, which is 3.17 times that of the rectangular structure. The enhancement of effective magnetostrictive strain proves that the modified shape of variable cross-section has great advantages in improving the sensitivity of magnetostrictive film/quartz wafer composite resonant magnetic field sensor, which provides a feasible method for the preparation of high Q value and high sensitivity micro magnetic field sensor.

articleTitle: A Collaboration from High Frequency Soft Magnetic Materials to Integrated Circuit Design for beyond 10MHz Switching Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper reviews interdisciplinary collaboration from soft magnetic material engineering to CMOS integrated circuit design level aiming for high power density and high efficiency switching power supplies beyond 10MHz. The overviews of the Fe-based metal composite materials showing high permeability with very low loss up to more than 100MHz and high saturation magnetic flux density are provided. The high processability of this material allows forming a magnetic composite sheet that is highly compatible with the conventional low-cost interposer packaging process. This is important to reduce manufacturing cost to realize package-integrated magnetic components. Furthermore, circuit techniques for beyond 10MHz operation are also briefly presented.

articleTitle: Coupling of Terahertz Light with Nanometer-Wavelength Magnons
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)

authors.preferredName: Thales V. A. G. de Oliveira

abstract: Energy-efficient spin-based technologies require new prospects for the realization of nanoscale logic devices that are able to operate at terahertz (THz) frequencies. For instance, in the field of magnonics, spin waves are proposed for data transport and processing. In this regard, magnonic concepts rely on generation of nanometer-wavelength spin waves, confined in a nanostructure. Here, we propose a layered metallic system, based on a ferromagnetic film sandwiched by heavy metals that allows a highly efficient coupling of millimeter wavelength THz light with nanometer-wavelength magnon modes. Using single-cycle broadband THz radiation, we are able to excite spin-wave modes with a frequency of up to 0.6 THz and a wavelength as short as 6 nm. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the coupling originates solely from interfacial spin-orbit torques. A possible origin of the enhanced damping of THz spin waves will be discussed.

articleTitle: Microstructure and Electron Magnetic Circular Dichroism of Antiphase Boundaries in Magnetic Oxides
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: A novel antiphase boundary in spinel NiFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> with rock salt structure interlayers and crystal translation (1/4)a [011] is observed. The atomic configuration dependent magnetic property is comprehensively invesitaged thtough the combination of aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy, electron magnetic circular dichroism, and dynamical diffraction calculations. Inroduing of antiferromagnetic coupling and decreasing in magnetic magnitudes at antiphase boundary is confirmed though first principles density functional theory calculation.

articleTitle: Comparison of Torque Generation Capabilities of the Axial-Field Switched Reluctance Machine with Segmented Rotor for Four Winding Configurations under Sine Wave, Unipolar and Bipolar Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper deals with the comparison of several excitation modes for four different winding configurations in a 3-phase, 36/24, axial-field switched reluctance machine with double stator and segmented rotor. The topology of the axial-field double stator switched reluctance machine (AFDSSRM) is made of 2 stators connected in series and a segmented rotor in between. The first couple of winding configurations is that each stator tooth holds one coil dedicated to one phase.
