The other two winding configurations are of two successive teeth holding two coils dedicated to one phase. In previous works, two winding configurations were explored for the AFDSSRM, the classical winding for SRMs (+A- -B+ +C- -A+ +B- -C+) and the mutually coupled one (+A- +B- +C- +A- +B- +C-) in the one tooth for one phase configuration. In this paper, the two successive coils for one phase windings are also explored in the classical SRM configuration (+A- -A+ -B+ +B- +C- -C+) that will be fed with rectangular current and in the mutually coupled (+A- -A+ +B- -B+ +C- -C+) that will be fed by sine wave current and bipolar step current. The comparisons of torque generation and torque ripple are carried out using 2D finite element model (FEM) with the hypothesis of radial invariance of local quantities. That allows 2D modeling at the mean radius of the machine.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cross-Coupling Effect for Multi-Objective Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this paper, a quantitative analysis of the cross-coupling effect for multi-objective wireless power transfer (WPT) is presented and a relevant method to eliminate the influence is implemented. Based on the exemplified two-pickup and three-pickup WPT systems, the wirelessly transmitted power and efficiency are significantly affected by the cross-coupling effects among pickup coils. Meanwhile, the zero-phase angle (ZPA) operation of the primary side is deteriorated due to the existence of the cross-coupling effect. Accordingly, a cross-coupling cancellation method is proposed to regulate the primary exciting current back to its original value and recover the primary side back to the ZPA operation. Both the simulated and experimental results are provided to verify the feasibility of the proposed cancelation method.

articleTitle: Glioblastoma Cancer Cells Destruction by Mechanical Stimulation Using Magnetic Particles: In vitro versus In vivo Assays and Investigations in 3D Gels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The mechanical vibration of magnetic particles by low frequency magnetic field allows for the application of mechanical stresses at the cells level. Although proven to be very effective in triggering cancer cells death in vitro, the results obtained in-vivo with real glioblastoma tumors were so far not as successful. According to our observations, several differences between in-vitro and in-vivo situations explain these contrasted results, including the limited dispersion of the magnetic particles in the tumor and the difference in medium stiffness.After detailing the results obtained so far, we will show how the particles dispersion within biological tissue can be improved by functionalization and how 3D cell spheroids open new perspectives for these investigations.

articleTitle: High Spin-Charge Conversion Efficiency of Co3Sn2S2 Promoted by Transition from Paramagnetic to Ferromagnetic Phase
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Temperature (T) dependence of conversion from charge current to spin current was investigated for the Co3Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (CSS) thin film by measuring the spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR) for the sample with CSS / Cu / CoFeB. Above the ferromagnetic phase transition temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>), the sample exhibited the clear ST-FMR signal coming from the spin Hall effect in the paramagnetic CSS and the anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) of CoFeB. Below T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>, on the other hand, it is found that the ST-FMR signal involves the dc voltages not only through the AMR but also through the giant magnetoresistance. In addition, the spin Hall torque generated from the ferromagnetic CSS dominantly acts on the CoFeB magnetization. An increase in the spin-charge conversion efficiency is observed at T < T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>, indicating that the phase transition from the paramagnetic CSS to the ferromagnetic CSS promotes the spin-charge conversion.

articleTitle: Unconventional octupole dynamics of a non-collinear antiferromagnet driven by spin-orbit torque
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Spin-orbit torque (SOT) has been utilized for efficient electrical control of magnetic ordering structure. When discussing the SOT-driven dynamics of magnetic ordering in magnets with collinear spin orientations, the overall magnetic order parameters such as net magnetization and Néel vector are governed by the same law of SOT on individual magnetic moments, and this treatment has been naively extended to the magnets with non-collinear system. Here, we reveal unconventional dynamics of the overall magnetic order parameter of a non-collinear antiferromagnet, i.e., the octupole moment, which is in sharp contrast to those of previously studied collinear systems. Using ac harmonic and dc measurements on a Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn/Pt heterostructure, we reveal that the octupole moment undergoes an opposite rotation with respect to the individual magnetic moments, which stems from the interplay between the SOT and the chiral-spin structure of Mn3Sn. Moreover, we quantify the SOT efficiency in the heterostructure. Our study provides a guideline for understanding the electrical manipulation of non-collinear antiferromagnets, which substantially differs from the well-established collinear systems.

articleTitle: Structural and micromagnetic modeling of the magnetic binder phase in WC-Co cemented carbides
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The magnetic properties of tungsten carbide with cobalt as a binder have long been used in industry to characterize the microstructure of this hard metal. We present bottom-up structural and micromagnetic modeling of WC-Co, from which we obtain coercive fields that compare well to experimental data. Future work will use experimentally obtained microstructure information as input to the structural modeling.

articleTitle: Enhanced anomalous Hall and negative anisotropic magnetoresistance effects driven by p-d hybridization with carbon
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C thin films were synthesized via vacuum carburization of the host CoMn alloy films based on a conventional gas–solid reaction to demonstrate the effect of C, a common light element, on the magnetic and spintronic materials. The crystal structure transitioned from the disordered face-centered cubic CoMn to the L1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-like Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C, for which the lattice constant increased from 0.356 to 0.378 nm. The C 1s X-ray photoemission spectra of the Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C film indicated hybridization in C–Co and C–Mn and a homogeneous concentration of C in the film. The enhancement of both the saturation magnetization and the anomalous Hall conductivity (σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">xy</inf>) was induced by C, attributing to the magnetic transition to the ferrimagnetic spin order. The surface flatness and high σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">xy</inf> are promising characteristics for spintronic applications such as the spin-anomalous Hall effect. Furthermore, the sign of in-plane anisotropic magnetoresistance ratio changed from positive for the host CoMn to negative for the Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C, suggesting the inversion of dominant spins from majority-spin to minority-spin. The atomic- and spin-resolved density of states (DOS) via first-principles calculations revealed that face-centered Mn(II) and Co could be significantly influenced by C because of p–d hybridization, resulting in enhanced spin polarization of the DOS at the Fermi level of ~0.82. These results demonstrate that the use of C could be an essential way to boost material properties in the future.

articleTitle: Tunneling Magnetoresistance in Noncollinear Antiferromagnetic Tunnel Junctions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Antiferromagnetic spintronics has emerged as a subfield of spintronics driven by the advantages of antiferromagnets producing no stray fields and exhibiting ultrafast magnetization dynamics. The efficient method to detect an antiferromagnetic order parameter, known as the Néel vector, by electric means is critical to realize concepts of antiferromagnetic spintronics. Here, using fist-principles calculations, we predict a tunneling magnetoresistance effect as high as 100% in antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions with Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn electrodes which exhibit a momentum dependent spin polarization. Moreover, further studies demonstrate that in single-crystalline Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Pt/perovskite oxides/Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Pt antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions, tunneling magnetoresistance can reach over 800%. We argue that the spin-split band structure and the related tunneling magnetoresistance effect can also be realized in other noncollinear antiferromagnetic metals like Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ge, Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ga and Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>GaN. Our work may provide a robust method for detecting the Néel vector in noncollinear antiferromagnets via the tunneling magnetoresistance effect, which should be useful for their application in antiferromagnetic spintronic devices.

articleTitle: Voltage control of frequency and effective damping in nano-constriction-based spin Hall nano-oscillators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Using micromagnetic simulations, we study the tunability of strongly voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA), ΔK = ±200 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, in voltage-gated W/CoFeB/MgO based nano-constriction spin Hall nano-oscillators. The VCMA modifies the local magnetic properties such that the magnetodynamics transitions between regimes of i) confinement, ii) tuning, and iii) separation, with qualitatively different behavior. As a consequence, voltage control remains efficient over a very large frequency range, and subsequent manufacturing advances could allow SHNOs to be easily integrated into next-generation electronics for further fundamental studies and industrial applications.

articleTitle: Ferromagnetic Springs in Exchange Biased Trilayers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We present the fabrication of spiral spin configurations induced in exchange biased trilayer systems consisting of a single ferromagnetic layer embedded between two antiferromagnetic layers. Using He ion bombardment the exchange coupling between the ferromagnet and one antiferromagnet is modified leading to a trilayer system in which the unidirectional anisotropies at the two ferromagnet/antiferromagnet interfaces point in different directions. Angular-resolved vibrating sample magnetometry reveals the existence of a spiral domain state in the designed layer system during magnetization reversal.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Magnetic Gear-axial Flux Generator for Wave Power Generation Based on Halbach Magnetic Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To solve the problems of large volume and low power density of wave generator motors, two topologies of magnetic gear-axial flux generator based on Halbach magnetic circuit are proposed in this paper. The magnetic circuit of the magnetic gear and the motor part are coupled with each other, which improves the power density of the whole system. The permanent magnets in the motor section provide additional flux to the magnetic gear, which increases the instantaneous torque of the magnetic gear. The flux density, torque and back EMF of the two structures are compared and analyzed to determine the optimal generator structure.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal Parametric Magnon Excitation by Surface Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Microwave parametric pumping can generate magnons, quanta of magnetization precession dynamics. Here, we show nonreciprocal parametric excitation of magnons, where the magnon oscillation threshold depends on the field direction dependence, in a magnetic thin disk excited by nonuniform microwaves. It is attributed to the excitation of surface mode spin waves, leading to the field switching of magnon excitation.

articleTitle: Noninvasive sensor patch for internal magnetic core characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Real-time magnetic core condition monitoring is a promising technique for rapid fault detection. In this domain, significant progress is forecasted by achieving precise local measurements. In this study, we propose an innovative solution to measure local magnetic properties, which is well suited to real-time monitoring and magnetic circuit evaluation. The proposed sensor is a one-piece device that is flat enough to be placed noninvasively between the laminations at distinct positions in the magnetic core. It measures the magnetic excitation and induction fields in two dimensions, which can be used as local inputs for real-time condition monitoring.

articleTitle: Spin current generation in highly conductive Ru/Cu epitaxial heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Significant spin current generation from highly conductive materials is promising for spintronic applications, such as spin-orbit-torque magnetic random-access memories. In this work, we fabricated epitaxial Ru/Cu heterostructures with interface engineering where 1-nm-thick Ru and Cu layers were alternately deposited at the interface. The spin current generation in the heterostructures was evaluated by unidirectional spin Hall magnetoresistance and spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance. A sizable spin Hall efficiency (~−2%) was achieved in the Ru/Cu sample with a sharp interface which may result from the interface spin filtering effect. Increased spin Hall efficiency (~−4%) was observed in the interface-engineered samples which could be attributed to the intrinsic contribution from lattice distortion and local band structure near the interface. The effective spin Hall conductivity was estimated to be $3\sim 5 \times {10^5}\frac{{h}}{{2e}}{\Omega ^{ - 1}}{{\text{m}}^{ - 1}}$, which is comparable to that of Platinum.

articleTitle: Nd-Fe-B Thick-film Magnets on Si Substrates with Al-O Underlayers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Although we have prepared Nd-Fe-B thick-films on Si substrates with glass underlayers via pulsed laser deposition (PLD) for micro-magnetization, the glass layers were not suitable for the micro-magnetization due to inhomogeneous structure including voids because of the emission of large particles (droplets). Moreover, the film's squareness of a hysteresis loop deteriorated due to the presence of knick. This paper reports the fabrication of a Al-O film (target: Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) instead of a glass film on a Si substrate. The numbers and size of large particles (droplets) could be reduced in an Al-O film compared with those of a glass film. We also confirmed that the use of an Al-O underlayer enabled us to improve the squareness of a loop.

articleTitle: Optimisation of perpendicular magnetic tunnel junction structures using scanning transmission electron microscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Here, we report work on sputter deposited CoFeB/MgO/CoFeB magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) stacks with a CoFeB thickness ≤1.5 nm to obtain perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) and thin continuous layers, which are essential for good quality MTJs. Informed by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) analysis, improved MTJ structures have been grown at room temperature. These structures have improved characteristics through optimisation of the Ta seed layer deposition conditions, as reducing the roughness of the Ta layer results in higher-quality CoFeB and MgO layers. The thicknesses of the MTJ layers were determined using X-ray reflectometry (XRR), and the magnetic properties were investigated using vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM). We demonstrate tunnelling within the MTJ structures by performing current-in-plane-tunnelling (CIPT) measurements on as-deposited (unannealed) MTJ structures, producing a peak tunnelling-magnetoresistance (TMR) ratio of 4.3%. Furthermore, after annealing at 100 °C, the MTJ structure exhibits a strong interfacial PMA, demonstrating the importance of optimising the layer quality when growing such structures.

articleTitle: Dynamic properties of magnetic hopfions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We present an investigation of two important aspects of hopfions dynamics: spatial distribution of spin waves against the hopfion background and motion of hopfion in a nonuniform electric field. It is shown here by computer simulations that the hopfion confined to the discs has a rich spectra of spin-wave excitations, and that the velocity of hopfion moving in a gradient of electrical field in the ferromagnetic stripe is constant, which actualizes the still unsolved problem of determining the mass of localized magnetic textures. The knowledge of such peculiarities of hopfion dynamics is necessary for their spintronic and magnonic applications.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Influence of Eccentricity on the AC Copper Loss of High Speed Slotless Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: AC copper loss is the main loss of slotless permanent magnet motor. The armature winding is exposed to the air-gap magnetic field. During high-speed operation, the effective part of the winding is cut by the open-circuit magnetic field, which will inevitably cause a large AC copper loss. However, when the rotor is eccentric, severely distortions would be appeared in the air-gap magnetic field, resulting in a large amount of copper loss. Based on finite element analysis, the mechanism of AC loss of slotless motor is explained firstly, and then the influence of various eccentricities on AC loss is evaluated.

articleTitle: Performance Prediction of a FMaSynRM Considering MTPA, FW, and MTPV Operating Conditions Using Open-Source FEA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The modelling of electrical machine by finite element analysis (FEA) using free and open-source packages nowadays has become more and more feasible and reliable in the last few decades because of the continuous development of the open-source FEA and modelling techniques. In this paper, a modelling technique is introduced for the electromagnetic performance prediction of an adjustable speed ferrite-assisted synchronous reluctance machine (FMaSynRM) by using open-source FEA Elmer. The d-q model is utilized in this paper to compute the d-q inductance maps within a few time steps, which can take the nonlinearity and cross-coupling effects into consideration. The electromagnetic performances e.g. average torque and flux linkage considering maximum torque per ampere (MTPA), field weakening (FW), and maximum torque per volt (MTPV) operating conditions are further obtained by the post processing of the d-q inductance maps. The correctness of the proposed modelling method in Elmer is verified by the tested results.

articleTitle: Factors affecting Magnetic Particle Imaging: Frequency-sustained Hysteresis and Dipole-dipole Interactions. Challenges and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this work we study the factors affecting the magnetic response of realistic systems of nanoparticles of magnetite submitted to a sinusoidal driving field H(t) of magnitude and frequency appropriate to typical Magnetic Particle Imaging operations. Magnetic rate equations give the time-dependent magnetization M(t) over a wide interval of driving-field frequencies. The magnetic behavior of iron-oxide particles for biomedical applications is dominated by frequency-sustained hysteresis and by dipolar interaction which pose some challenges to the typical methods of analysis exploited to produce MPI maps.

articleTitle: Spin Dynamics with Inertia in Ferromagnetic Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Understanding spin dynamics on femto- and picosecond timescales offers new opportunities for faster and more efficient devices. On short time scales, the inertia term in the LLG equation becomes important, leading to the nutation of spins. However, experimental observation of nutation is still in its infancy. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a non-resonant excitation of inertial spin dynamics in ultrathin Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> films leading to nutation at a frequency of ∼ 0.1 THz, measured by time-resolved magneto optical Kerr effect (TR-MOKE). The inertial regime has a lifetime of more than 300ps.

articleTitle: Axial Force Negative Stiffness in Axial-Flux Electric Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper examines the axial force negative stiffness of induction and permanent magnet (PM) axial flux machines. First, simplified analytical models are used to identify the key normalised machine parameters which affect the variation of axial force with airgap length. For current-driven induction machines and PM machines, this is found to be the ratio of the effective magnetic length of the magnets and magnetic core divided by the nominal airgap. For voltage-driven (line-start) induction machines, it is the ratio of the stator leakage inductance to the nominal magnetising reactance. Next, the analytical results are validated against finite-element results and results from experimental axial force testing on induction and PM axial-flux machines.

articleTitle: Physical reservoir computing utilizing voltage controlled magnetic anisotropy effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Physical reservoir computing using spin-torque oscillator succeeded human-voice recognition with high accuracy. It accompanies, however, large energy dissipation because the magnetization dynamics in the oscillator is driven by electric current and an external magnetic field is also necessary. Here, we show that the magnetization dynamics driven by voltage controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) effect can be applied to physical reservoir computing. It does not accompany Joule heating because of the absence of current. An external magnetic field is also unnecessary because physical reservoir computing does not requires magnetization switching. Instead, a second-order magnetic anisotropy is required for a deterministic computing. Solving the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with the second-order magnetic anisotropy field, we find that the computational capability of a magnetic tunnel junction can be tuned by the VCMA effect.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Heating Rate of Ultrasmall Gold-coated Iron Oxide Magnetic Nanoparticles by Ferromagnetic Resonance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this study, we experimentally demonstrated an ultrafast heating rate of ultrasmall gold-coated iron oxide magnetic nanoparticles (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@Au NPs) by the ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) effect. Using the constructed setup, the ferromagnetic resonance and temperature increment of NPs under FMR were evaluated. The resonant frequency of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@Au NPs and their uncoated Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs was several GHz and increased with increasing DC field strength. The resonant frequency of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@Au NPs shifted slightly lower than that of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs. The initial temperature rising rate reached the maximum values at their corresponding DC fields for FMR (e.g. 1.294 and 3.894 K/s under H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</inf>=1200 Oe for RF field of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">AC</inf>=4 GHz and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">AC</inf>=4 Oe for Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@Au and Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> NPs, respectively). These values were two orders of magnitude higher than that of Néel and the Brownian relaxation for the conventional magnetic hyperthermia. The maximum value also increased with increasing RF field frequency. The obtained results also indicate that it is possible to control the temperature of NPs by adjusting the parameters of the RF field and DC field, suggesting their potential use for therapeutic temperature control in magnetic hyperthermia applications.

articleTitle: Switching Field Distributions and Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy Fields in Zn-Ti and Co-Ti Equally Co-Substituted BaM Ferrites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: M-type hexagonal barium ferrites Ba(MxTix)Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12−2x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> (M=Co or Ti, x=0-0.5) are synthesized by chemical route. Experimental values of the anisotropy fields HK are extracted from microwave measurements. It is shown that HK values are very close to the higher switching field. Results show that the shift through lower values both for HK and the switching field distributions are the largest for CoTi substitutions. A qualitative analysis based on the cations occupation sites is proposed.

articleTitle: Direct consolidation of Sm2Fe17N3 magnet and coercivity improvement by severe plastic deformation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> coarse powder was directly consolidated into a disc magnet by the high-pressure torsion technique. The huge superimposed hydrostatic pressure above several GPa enables to apply large plastic strain to the disc as well as the powder particles of the brittle Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> compound at room temperature. This large deformation successfully increased the relative density to 98% at room temperature, inducing the grain subdivision inside powder particles simultaneously. This led to the coercivity of 5.7 kOe enhanced from the coarse powder having the coercivity of 1 kOe without reducing the particle size. It was found that those grain subdivision events are accompanied by the motion of dislocations on non-basal planes. Synchrotron X-ray diffractometry was also performed and revealed that too large strain, however, results in the disappearance of the hard magnetic Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> phase and the loss of the coercivity.

articleTitle: Giant Magnetocaloric Effect by Low Magnetic Field Metamagnetic Transition in Eu4Ga8Ge16 Compound
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The Eu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf> is a homologous compound comparable with a cage-structured type-I clathrate Eu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</inf>. The crystal structure of the Eu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf> compound has an orthorhombic structure (Cmcm) with a unique one-dimensional arrangement of Eu atoms along the a-axis. The charge-balancing Ga/Ge framework encompasses the Eu atomic chains, resulting in the one-dimensional caged spin chain structure. The quasi-one-dimensional antiferromagnetic spin alignment along the a-axis shows low magnetic field metamagnetic transition at H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf> = 3.3 kOe at T = 2 K. The magnetic hysteresis curve at T = 2 K presents an unconventional inverse magnetic hysteresis (rapid spin saturation for increasing magnetic field and spin disordering for decreasing magnetic field) at intermediate magnetic field ranges, which may be related to the quasi-one-dimensional spin chain structure. The magnetocaloric properties of the compound exhibit high spin entropy change and adiabatic temperature difference, such as -ΔS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf>= 14.56 J kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and ΔT<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ad</inf>= 7.77 K at T= 7.9 K, which are superior values than those of previously reported type-I clathrate Eu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</inf> compound. The exceptionally high values of magnetocaloric properties in the antiferromagnetic ground state of the Eu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf> may originate from the low magnetic field metamagnetic transition. Therefore, the high magnetocaloric materials do not restrict to materials showing the first-order ferromagnetic ordering but can be extendable to an antiferromagnetic ground state with low-magnetic field metamagnetic transition.

articleTitle: Accessing Ultrafast Demagnetization Rates of Ferrimagnetic Thin Films through THz Emission Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We present a comprehensive characterization of the optically induced sub-picosecond demagnetization of GdFeCo thin films, done via a rigorous frequency-domain analysis of their THz emission. We extract the temperature and chemical composition dependences of the Gd and FeCo contributions to the measured THz pulses and map them to their demagnetization rates, finding in some instances a significant Gd component that has been neglected in previous studies. We detect a strong suppression and a change in the polarity of the THz signal, features that we ascribe to equilibrium properties of the samples, i.e., out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy and magnetization compensation. Furthermore, our measurements show that the observed dynamics are also affected by the antiferromagnetic interaction between the Gd and FeCo sublattices which varies with temperature and concentration. Our methodology is readily applicable to disentangle the THz emission from other ferrimagnets and can thus contribute to our understanding of the ultrafast response of these technologically relevant materials.

articleTitle: An Experimental-Analytical Approach for Condition Monitoring of Magnetic Cores with Predominant Focus on Axial off-set between the Short Circuit Points
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper presents experimental and numerical studies on laminated magnetic cores with GO electrical steels subjected to inter-laminar short circuit faults, with predominant focus on axial off-set between the short circuit points. Experimental works were performed on stacks of four Epstein size laminations under controlled sinusoidal induction at power frequency of 50 Hz and peak flux densities of 1.0 T to 1.7 T. To support the experimental results, accurate time-domain finite element (FE) models were also performed to visualise inter-laminar eddy currents caused by inter-laminar faults. Impact of each fault scenario on dynamic hysteresis loop, additional eddy current loss, and additional magnetic field was studied.

articleTitle: Investigation of Fault-Tolerant Performance and Inductance in a Modular Permanent Magnet In-Wheel Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper investigates the fault-tolerant (FT) performance and inductances in a modular permanent magnet (PM) in-wheel motor. First, according to the working mechanism and main faulty types of the modular FT motor, the slot-pole combination with high FT performance for the modular motor is developed. The relationship between the FT performance and the inductance parameters is linked through the magnetic coupling coefficient. Second, the electromagnetic characteristics of the modular in-wheel motor under open-circuit fault and interturn short-circuit (SC) are investigated respectively. The influence of inductance on FT performance under open-circuit faults and interturn SC fault are investigated respectively. The design requirement for the inductance of this kind of motors is proposed.

articleTitle: Geometry Optimization of Split Ring Resonator for Terahertz Photon-Magnon Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Photon-Magnon Coupling (PMC) has been studied to develop effective quantum transducers and long-lifetime quantum memories. In order to achieve PMC, a cavity structure named as a split ring resonator (SRR) has been used as a photon resonator. However, most of the studies so far has remained in the gigahertz frequency range, so that it is hard to achieve PMC in terahertz range which is essential for coupling with antiferromagnetic magnons. Here, we investigate the geometry optimization of SRR in terahertz frequency range by using simulation as well as the experiment. The simulation shows that the efficiency and resonance frequency are varied by adjusting the geometric length and gap of the SRR. The simulation results are confirmed experimentally by using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy. This work provides a design rule for terahertz photon resonator with high efficiency for future PMC experiments.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Synaptic Behaviour in a Spintronic Device for On-Chip Learning in Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In a heavy-metal-ferromagnetic-metal-hetero-structure-based spintronic device, which exhibits perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA), an experimental demonstration is presented here of multiple synaptic states being modulated electrically to obtain long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD). Next, on-chip learning is simulated in a crossbar-array-based Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network, where the model of each synaptic element in the crossbar array is based on the experimentally obtained LTP and LTD characteristics of the spintronic device and hence includes experimentally measured non-linearity, asymmetry, and cycle-to-cycle variations of LTP and LTD. Using the Airline Passenger time-series data set, we show that the LSTM can be trained successfully even in the presence of these non-idealities.

Author Keywords: Long Term Potentiation and Depression (LTP and LTD)

articleTitle: Development of Sm2Fe17N3 magnetic powder doped with La, W, and Ti
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The fabrication of 12-nylon-bonded magnets with high magnetic properties have not been achieved thus far. The improvement of the magnetic properties of Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> magnetic powder doped with La, W, and Ti was investigated by suppressing the fine powder generated in the dispersion process and inhibiting oxidative degradation. A prototype Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> magnetic powder was developed with σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 154 emu/g, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cj</inf> = 10070 Oe (801.8 kA/m), and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> = 5642 Oe (449.2 kA/m) by increasing the nitrogen concentration to 3.46 % via nitridation at 500 °C.

articleTitle: Development of a flexible sensor focusing on the excitation and search characteristics of planar coils
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The cast iron is the part that engines are important and is used in various environment. The cast iron is produced in complex shapes. Cavity defects called shrinkage cavities occur inside cast iron. The cast iron product that there are multiple kinds of a shape and the defect have difficulty in examination for all quantity. In this research, a flexible electromagnetic non-destructive inspection technology corresponding to the complex shape of castings was proposed. By changing the shape of the detection coil from a solenoid shape to a planar shape, it is possible to perform inspections on any plane. In addition, results of comparison experiments between solenoidal and planar shapes have been reported.

articleTitle: Analysis of Aluminum Eddy Current Effect for Planar Switched Reluctance Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this article, influence of aluminum eddy current in the PSRM stator array on the electromagnetic properties and control performance is investigated. The eddy current density distribution model is established based on Maxwell’s equations, and the inductance model is derived considering the eddy current effect. The effect of aluminum eddy current on the PSRM position control performance is qualitatively analyzed. The aluminum eddy current distribution and ohmic loss distribution characteristics with the mover at different positions are verified by finite element analysis. The validity of the developed inductance model is experimentally verified. A material replacement method is proposed to eliminate the aluminum eddy current. The experimental results show that the position control accuracy of the PSRM prototype is improved by 6.94% on average after the elimination of eddy currents, while the motor efficiency is improved by 6.51%.

articleTitle: A Dimension Reduction Transformation Method for the hybrid Axial-Radial Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: For the hybrid axial-radial machine, 3-D finite-element analysis (FEA) is required in the design process due to the asymmetry of the axial flux direction. However, 3-D FEA is computationally intensive and will consume enormous resources and time. A new dimension reduction transformation analysis method based on constant torque transformation and virtual permeability is presented in this paper. On the premise of constant torque and the principle of magnetic circuit equivalence, the concept of virtual permeability is proposed based on the principle that magnetomotive force and magnetic resistance are not changed. The complex 3-D model is reduced to 2-D model, and then the load characteristics are predicted by the 2-D equivalent finite element model proposed in the preliminary design stage, which greatly reduces the simulation time.

articleTitle: High-Speed Iron Loss Calculation of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Combining Reluctance Network Analysis and One-Dimensional Magnetic Circuit Models Considering Dynamic Hysteresis Behavior
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Quantitative analysis of the iron loss taking the dynamic hysteresis behavior into account is essential to the development of high-efficiency electric machines. In a previous paper, a novel magnetic circuit model incorporating a play model and a Cauer circuit was proposed. It was demonstrated that this magnetic circuit model can accurately and fast calculate the hysteresis loops and the iron loss considering carrier harmonics under PWM excitation for magnetic reactors made of several kinds of core materials. This paper describes that the iron loss of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) driven by a PWM converter is calculated with high-accuracy and high-speed by combining a reluctance network analysis (RNA) model of an entire PMSM and a one-dimensional (1-D) magnetic circuit model representing the dynamic hysteresis characteristics in each element of an RNA model.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Excess Loss of the Grain-Oriented Steel Sheets in A High-Frequency Range Considering Skin Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This paper discusses the relationship between the excess loss statistical parameter V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and the magnetization frequency f, which is beneficial to accurately predict the loss of electrical steel sheets in a wide frequency range. To clarify the effect of magnetization frequency on excess loss, the hysteresis loss and classical eddy current loss considering the skin effect is firstly determined via a time domain One-dimensional(1-D) lamination model where the constitutive hysteresis relation is described by an improved inverse J-A model with waveform scale factors. Then, the excess loss and the parameter V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> are calculated by subtracting the hysteresis loss and the classical eddy current loss obtained from the solution of the 1-D diffusion equation. Finally, a discussion about the frequency dependence on the statistical parameter V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is carried out by measuring the loss of grain-oriented(GO) silicon steel B30P105 up to 1 kHz and 1.6 T. Obtained results show that statistical parameter V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> can be regarded as a function of magnetization frequency and magnetic flux density level.

articleTitle: Design, Analysis, and Experimental Verification of a PM-Based Hybrid Brake System for Personal e-Mobility Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: In this research, a hybrid eddy current brake (ECB) system is proposed for use in electric kick scooters. The system utilizes a combination of friction, kinetic energy, and electromagnetic energy to improve braking performance and maintenance characteristics. The braking systems of three commercial electric kick scooters were benchmarked in order to retrofit the proposed ECB system onto an existing drivetrain. Additionally, a 3D finite element analysis (FEA) based design approach was used to maximize braking torque while meeting specific design constraints. To experimentally verify the proposed ECB model's braking torque, dynamometer measurements were conducted. The design approach presented in this research can be applied to other personal mobility applications with similar space constraints.

articleTitle: PLD-fabricated (Nd or Pr)–Fe–B Thick-film Magnets Applied to Small Stepping Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We have fabricated isotropic Pr–Fe–B thick-film magnets (thickness: 0.25 mm) on a stainless shaft using a pulsed laser deposition method. Subsequently, we applied these magnets to a small stepping motor (diameter: < 3 mm) by taking advantage of the Pr2Fe14B phase with a large anisotropic magnetic field at approximately 300 K. We focused on the fact that, compared with the linear expansion coefficient of Pr element (6.7 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> 1/K ), the expansion coefficient of Nd element (9.6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> 1/K ) is closer to that of stainless steel (10 – 11×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> 1/K). Moreover, we compared the temperature dependence of magnetic properties and the mechanical characteristic of Nd–Fe– B and Pr–Fe–B thick-film magnets on a stainless substrate (shaft).

articleTitle: Microwave absorption properties of Fe/Fe16N2 nanoparticles prepared from iron oxide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Fe/Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles was prepared from Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanoparticles by hydrogen reduction and subsequent low-temperature nitriding process. XRD analysis showed that Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> phase was fully transformed into α-Fe phase after hydrogen reduction at 400°C. Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> component was confirmed after nitriding of the Fe nanoparticles from 140°C to 160°C. Volume fraction of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> was increased by increasing nitriding temperature, leading to increase in coercivity. The electromagnetic properties showed that the resonance frequency of resin composite of reduced Fe nanoparticles was 6.9 GHz, and it shifted to 9.5 GHz for resin composite of subsequent nitridation nanoparticles due to crystal structure of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> with large anisotropic field. It suggests that the resin composite containing Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles is a promising microwave absorption material for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of eddy current testing signals’ frequency responses for conductivity-invariant crack sizing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The eddy current testing (ECT) signals of a crack depend not only on the geometry dimensions but also the electromagnetic properties, i.e., the electrical conductivity in the case of a non-magnetic test object. The conductivity of the test object, and the conductivity inside or around the crack are generally unknown but play an important role in crack’s ECT responses. This study aims to establish a conductivity-invariant method to determine a crack’s geometry dimension. Theoretical and numerical analysis showed that the intrinsic flaw impedance or the magnetic field density ECT signals varies little with frequency. By finding out conductivity independent features, we were able to construct a master-curve by using the relation between the characteristic feature and crack dimension. A crack of unknown conductivity can be sized by referring to the pre-constructed master curve.

articleTitle: The effect of temperature on the magnetic properties of Fe/SiO2/ferrite soft magnetic composites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Soft magnetic composites Fe/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/ferrite with low energy losses and high magnetic permeability are studied. The magnetic properties in composites with (a) 0 vol%, (b) 2 vol%, (c) 5 vol%, and (d) 10 vol% of ferrite at peak induction of 0.1 T are investigated in the temperature range of 20–140 °C. Further, loss separation as a function of ferrite content and temperature was studied. An increase in temperature in working conditions affects the magnetic properties of the SMCs, which requires consideration of the temperature effect in the process of predicting magnetic properties. The content of ferrite plays a significant role in modulating the magnetic properties of Fe/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/ferrite soft magnetic composites.

articleTitle: Synthesis and in-situ XPS study of U-Te thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Motivated by the discovery of unconventional superconductivity in the UTe2 single crystals, we have studied formation and properties of U-Te thin films. The films were synthesized by dc sputtering. Separate U and Te targets were used: Te was evaporated simultaneously with plasma sputtering of the U target. Thin films with the varied U:Te composition were obtained and studied in-situ by means of x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS).

articleTitle: Scaling the manufacturing of soft magnetic inductor cores for power conversion applications from 8-inch to 12-inch wafers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: On-chip voltage regulators employing high-frequency micro-machined power inductors based on integrated thin-film soft magnetic cores are a promising path for replacing the bulky, slow and inefficient off-chip voltage regulators. Yet, fabricating these inductors remains technologically and economically very challenging, since low-loss magnetic cores with thickness of at least several micrometers operating at very high frequencies (10-100 MHz) need to be integrated with a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) compatible process for power conversion applications. Based on our production proven solution for cost-effective deposition of soft magnetic multilayered thin films with tunable properties on 8-inch wafers, which was previously used for manufacturing ultra-low-profile magnetic-core inductors with a record inductance density of ~3500 nH/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and peak quality factor of 26, we have made the transition from 8-inch to 12-inch wafers, and we are now ready to offer a cost-effective solution to manufacturers of on-chip voltage regulators. In this work, we investigate the magnetic properties of CoTaZr/Ta<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>, CoTaZr/CoTaZrO and CoTaZr/AlN soft magnetic multilayers fabricated by a physical vapor deposition (PVD) process on 12-inch Si and Si/500-nm-thermal-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> wafers in an industrial multi-chamber magnetron sputtering system.

articleTitle: Microstructure of Nd2Fe17N3 Magnetic Powder Surface with Nano-α-Fe Phases Separated Surface Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We investigated the application of Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> magnetic powder with planar magnetic anisotropy to magnetic field amplification materials at several tens of MHz. Consequently, we succeeded in developing a magnetic property with µ′ ~ 8 and at 10 MHz using a phosphoric acid coating and a simple heat treatment process in air. In this study, microstructural analysis by transmission electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction revealed that the coating layer became thicker and the Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> surface was phase-separated into nano-sized α-Fe phases and Nd-rich phases, either oxide, oxynitride, or nitride. Additionally, the nano-sized α-Fe phases and the nano-sized Nd-rich phases were oriented over a wide area spanning several hundred nanometers. We concluded that these characteristic structures have led to improved properties.

articleTitle: Systematic study of the strength of VCMA effect in nanomagnets of small and large strength of spin-orbit interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The dependence of anisotropy field and strength of spin-orbit (SO) interaction is systematically studied in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Ta/FeB/MgO,W/FeB/MgO, Ta/FeCoB/MgO, [W/FeB]_{n}/MgO, [Ta/FeB]_{n}/MgO$</tex> nanomagnets. It is found that the polarities of gate-voltage dependence of the anisotropy field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{ani}$</tex> and the coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_{so}$</tex> of SO interaction are opposite in all studied nanomagnets. The magnitudes of the voltage dependence of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{ani}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_{so}$</tex> are comparable in a single-ferromagnetic layer nanomagnet, in which measured strength of SO interaction is small, and in a multilayer -ferromagnetic layer nanomagnet, in which measured strength of SO interaction is large.

articleTitle: Comparison Between Novel Pole-changing and Conventional Flux Switching Permanent-Magnet Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This article evaluates a novel pole-changing (PC) flux switching permanent-magnet (FSPM) motor, which can achieve high torque density and wide speed regulation range simultaneously. According to different operation conditions, the PC-FSPM motor can use different modulated field harmonics with different pole-pair number based on a PC winding for high torque and high speed conditions, respectively, namely, the PC operation can be achieved. To prove the feasibility of the PC-FSPM motor, the comparative study between the PC-FSPM motor and a conventional U-core FSPM motor is conducted. The operation principles of the two motors are introduced. Moreover, the electromagnetic performance comparison is carried out quantitatively by finite element analysis. Finally, a prototype of the PC-FSPM motor is built and tested to verify the FEA results.

articleTitle: Fabrication and evaluation of fully sputtered topological insulator/perpendicularly magnetized CoFeB/MgO multilayers for SOT-MRAM application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Topological insulator (TI) is considered as one of the most important candidates for a spin current source in spin-orbit torque (SOT) magnetoresistive random access memory (MRAM) with the spin Hall angle larger than 1. However, well-known TIs such as Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and (BiSb)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> have a low electrical conductivity and are usually grown by the molecular beam epitaxy method which is not suitable for mass production. In this study, we report on fully sputtered BiSb/perpendicularly magnetized CoFeB/MgO multilayers for SOT-MRAM application, where BiSb has a large spin Hall angle 1.7 and a high electric conductivity 1.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> Ω<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. We demonstrated SOT-induced magnetization switching of CoFeB by a small critical current density of 1.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> Acm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>.

articleTitle: Development of recycling friendly coatings for Nd-Fe-B magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Today’s critical raw materials in the field of hard magnetic materials are getting more and more attention by all the players involved in their usage. While recycling of Nd-Fe-B magnets on paper seem feasible with the low cost HPMS method, we see that still many obstacles have to be resolved to make the recycling of End-of-life magnets a viable source for new magnets. One of the problems is the sheer difference in compositions, coatings and availability on the market. We focused on the effect of the coating that it has on the recyclability of the magnet and a way to make recycling one step closer to realization by developing recycling friendly Nd-Fe-B coatings. We tested different polymer coatings on Nd-Fe-B magnets. The target was to achieve low cost, thin and easy to remove coatings with a good corrosion protection. For this we used Parylene coatings, plasma polymerization and Styrene-ethylene/butylene-styrene coatings. The first tests showed that a sufficient corrosion resistance is achievable with such coatings, with easy removability. For a more in-depth study we are planning to install these magnets in consumer products to evaluate their real-life expectancy.

articleTitle: Crystal Direction Dependences of Anisotropic Magnetoresistance Effects in Co2MnGa and Co2MnAl Heusler Alloy Epitaxial Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: The crystal direction dependences of anisotropic magnetoresistances in Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa and Co2MnAl epitaxial thin films grown on MgO(100) substrate were investigated experimentally and theoretically by changing the Co content. Both Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnAl films showed the maximum values in the AMR ratios at the Co content of approximately 50 at%. The AMR ratios of Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa showed the negative values for the current direction I // Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa[110] and positive values for I // Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa[100], whereas Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnAl showed only the positive AMR ratios independent of the current direction. The calculated AMR ratios from s-d scattering theory of the electrons, including the density of state (DOS) information from first principles calculations, well reproduced the experimental features. We found that the AMR ratios of Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnAl can be explained by s–d scattering depending on the current direction against the crystal axis.

articleTitle: Antiferromagnetically exchange coupled CoFe/MgO/CoFe stacks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Exchange coupling in as-deposited and annealed magnetic trilayers Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> (CoFe)/MgO/Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> (CoFe) for MgO thickness spanning 0.45 to 4.5 nm has been studied. Antiferromagnetic exchange coupling behavior was observed in annealed CoFe/MgO/CoFe with 2.7-nm MgO insulating barrier. Interestingly, a transition from antiferromagnetic to nearly paramagnetic response to applied magnetic field was found around 520 °C—conceptually called as Neel temperature. Based on grazing incidence x-ray diffraction study, oxide phases of Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, CoO, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, and CoFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> were found at CoFe/MgO interface. In the annealed CoFe/MgO interface, formation of CoO and CoFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> at the interface indicates they act as antiferromagnetic sources giving rise to the exchange-coupled antiferromagnetic/ferromagnetic (AFM/FM) interface.

Author Keywords: angle dependence of magnetic hysteresis loop

articleTitle: Efficient Modeling of Magneto-Elastic Media Using the Feedback Preisach Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Magnetic materials demonstrating relatively high magnetostriction are currently being widely employed in various applications. Several magnetostriction models that vary in quantitative accuracy, efficiency and identification approaches have been previously suggested. This paper presents an efficient approach for modeling magneto-elastic media by employing a single scalar feedback Preisach-type model. Details of the proposed approach, its identification procedure and experimental testing are given in the paper.

articleTitle: Magnetodielectric Material for VHF Antenna Devices Tunable by a Low DC Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: This study presents the performance of a magneto-dielectric material (MDM) specially developed to enable the tunability of antenna devices operating in the VHF band. The magnetic susceptibility variation of the MDM material is controlled by a current flowing through the sample which creates a DC magnetic field inside the sample with the same symmetry as the magnetic domains. By changing the magnetization state of the MDM with a low DC magnetic field of 740 A/m, a tunability of 40% can be observed. The MDM tunability at VHF frequencies is also verified by microwave measurements for different magnetization states.

articleTitle: Feature analysis on B-H curves of dust cores under the application of DC bias field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: To realize high-efficiency power converter, it is very important to reduce the loss of passive magnetic components of transformers and inductors in the high-frequency region. The iron loss behavior under a DC bias field is crucially important to characterize inductor performance. The iron loss behavior under a DC bias field should be reflected in the B-H hysteresis curve shape. In this study, B-H curve shape of a Sendust dust core has been analyzed by principal component analysis (PCA). The iron loss monotonically decreases with increasing DC bias field. PCA analysis extracts principal components corresponding to the slope, curvature, and non-linearity of the B-H curve shape. As a result, the reduction of iron loss under the application of DC bias field relates to the change in the slope and nonlinearity of the B-H curve shape.

articleTitle: Characterization and Magnetic Properties for Room Temperature Synthesis of Ni-doped Fe3O4/ZnS Core-Shell Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: Ferromagnetism is used in a wide range of applications such as electrical and electromagnetic mechanical devices. Ferromagnetic materials have strong magnetic fields like low coercivity, and high remanence. Here, Ni doped with iron Oxide nanoparticles with various doping values (x=0, 0.014, 0.041, 0.068) was successfully synthesized using the solvothermal reduction technique, and Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>@ZnS Core-shell nanocomposite was successfully constructed using the seed-mediate growth approach. The nanoparticles investigated using XRD confirmed the prepared Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>@ZnS was single phase and crystallized structure of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> with typical cubic inverse spinel structure. Alternating gradient magneto meter (AGM) at room temperature, the field dependence of magnetizations (Ms) for Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> and Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>@ZnS Core-shell nanocomposites revealed saturation fields of around 14000 Oe for prepared samples and dynamic light scattering indicate that average diameter of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> and Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>@ZnS Core-shell nanocomposites. FTIR shows the functional group of the prepared material. The PL spectrum reveals that the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> /ZnS coated nanocomposites contain a wide emission band between 350 nm and 500 nm with an emission maximum at 400 nm. AGM exhibit Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>@ZnS Core-shell nanocomposites have ferromagnetic behaviour in low saturation, suggesting that they could be used in electrical and magnetic properties.

articleTitle: Putative Quantum Critical Point in Doped Skyrmion Binary Alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
abstract: We report on Cr substitution triggered changes in the magnetic properties of a skyrmion binary alloy (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf>Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf>Si using x-ray diffraction and magnetization measurements. The x-ray diffraction patterns reveal an unaltered B20 cubic crystal stucture with increasing lattice constant. Magnetization analysis infers that the helical magnetic ordering of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf>Si is gradually suppressed to the absolute zero for the concentrations above x ≥ 0.4. Such a suppression is a clear indication of doping/substitution driven quantum phase transition with a quantum critical point to fall within 0.3 ≤ x ≤ 0.4.

articleTitle: Valence Band Dispersion in Mn, Bi and In doped GaAs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Magnetic Conference - Short Papers (INTERMAG Short Papers)
